# Orders: what guild bots do (M4)

Design and as-built notes of milestone M4 (the design log §2.4, §6 "M4 — Orders v1"): the guild bots act on the orders
the leader gives them. Code: `modules/mod-guild-adventure/src/OrderService.*` (the planner), `WorldIndex.*` (world
data), `BotDriver.*` (the only place that touches mod-playerbots internals).

Status: see [§ Status](#status) at the end. Evidence tiers as in the design log §9.

## Orders v1

| Order | What the bot does |
|---|---|
| `AUTO` (default for recruits, D16) | Picks its zone like a player would: it stays in its current zone while that fits its level and has work (eligible quests to pick up, or quests in the log the planner has a task for: a turn-in it can reach, an objective with a spot in the zone); otherwise it moves to a fitting zone with at least three eligible quests whose givers stand in it, however far: the nearest, with more quests weighing against a longer way, and zones it is two levels into before zones it has just grown into (a ship leg counts as 6000 yd). Without such a zone it stays and grinds. It keeps itself supplied (vendor/repair, class trainer), walks there and runs the quest planner; grinds when no quest is left. Re-evaluates the zone every minute and after each level-up. Limits: level cap (stops at the nearest inn), continent. `nd` (no dungeons) and `gcap` (gold per trip) have nothing to limit yet: the planner never enters dungeons and spends gold only on repairs, food and class spells. |
| `LEVEL_ZONE <zone>` | Same as `AUTO`, but in the ordered zone. When the bot out-levels the zone (level above the zone's maximum) it records `ZONE_DONE`; with auto-advance (`aa`, default on) the order moves to the zone `AUTO` would pick next (`ORDER` event "moves on to …"). Without auto-advance it stays and grinds. |
| `IDLE` | Walks to the nearest inn of its region and holds there (fights back when attacked). |
| `FOLLOW` | Follows the character the owner plays (leader or a controlled bot) and joins its party. While the owner is offline it holds its position. |

Orders the server does not accept yet stay listed as `later` in `docs/protocol.md` §8.1.

## Architecture

```
 OrderService (world thread, every second, every AI-driven guild bot)
   ├─ Reconcile        strategy profile, playerbots master, party        ─┐
   ├─ RunAdventure     AUTO / LEVEL_ZONE: zone, upkeep, travel, quests    │  BotDriver  ──>  mod-playerbots
   ├─ RunIdle          inn, hold                                          │   - non-combat strategies
   ├─ RunFollow        follow the owner's character                       │   - NewRpg status (rpgInfo)
   └─ why line, events, xp/h and copper/h samples                         │   - master, group
 WorldIndex (built at startup and on .ga reload)                           ─┘
   spawns by entry, quest starters/enders, zone quests, quest-item sources, service NPCs, mob spawns, zone hubs
```

**Responsibilities** (the design log §3.2): the module decides *what* a bot does; mod-playerbots carries it out. No
mod-playerbots patch is needed (D13 stays untouched): everything goes through public members of `PlayerbotAI`
(`ChangeStrategy`, `SetMaster`, `rpgInfo`, `lowPriorityQuest`).

### Executor: NewRpg as a remote-controlled body

mod-playerbots' NewRpg strategy is a state machine (`RPG_GO_GRIND`, `RPG_GO_CAMP`, `RPG_WANDER_NPC`, `RPG_DO_QUEST`,
`RPG_REST`, …) whose actions do the real work: long-distance movement with mmaps (`MoveFarTo`), talking to quest givers
on the way (accept/reward everything worth doing), working a quest objective at its spot for up to five minutes,
selling/repairing/buying at vendors. The "grind" strategy fights: quest mobs and attackers always, other mobs only while
wandering.

On a random-bot server NewRpg picks its next status at random. Here the module picks it: **every
`Playerbots.RpgStatusProbWeight.*` is 0** (written by `tools\configure-server.ps1`, the module warns at startup
otherwise), so an idle NewRpg falls back to `RPG_REST` until the planner sets the next status:

| Planner task | NewRpg status | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| Travel to a zone | `GO_CAMP` at the zone hub | the bot is in the zone (or at the hub) → `ZONE_CHANGE` event |
| Voyage (other region) | `GO_CAMP` at the dock, then hold on the pier, board, ride, go ashore (§ Travel) | ashore in the next region → `ZONE_CHANGE` event |
| Pick up quests | `GO_CAMP` at the giver's spawn, then `WANDER_NPC` with the giver as target | the quest is in the log |
| Work an objective | `DO_QUEST` with the planner's spot (nearest spawn of the target / item source in the zone, else NewRpg uses the quest POI) | objective complete, or NewRpg gives up (no progress for 5 min → failure rule) |
| Turn in | like a pickup, at the ender | the quest is no longer complete (rewarded) |
| Grind | `GO_GRIND` at the densest fitting mob cluster in the zone (then `WANDER_RANDOM`, 5 min) | NewRpg's wander phase ends |
| Vendor | like a pickup, at the nearest repairer/vendor | 10 s at the vendor (NewRpg sells junk, buys food/water, repairs) |
| Train | only with `GuildAdventure.AutoLearnClassSpells = 0`: like a pickup, at the nearest class trainer; by default (since 2026-11-12, the design log §7 D22) the bot learns the nearest class trainer's spells where it is and for free, on every new level and on its first plan after a login, and no Train task is planned | the module teaches every affordable spell through the core's `Trainer::TeachSpell` (real cost) |
| IDLE: safe spot | `GO_CAMP` at the nearest innkeeper | within 15 yd → hold |
| Hold | `REST`, strategy profile *hold* | re-planned every 30 s |

### Strategy profiles, master and party

| Profile | Non-combat strategies changed | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| adventure | `+new rpg,+grind`, `-follow,-stay,-rpg,-travel,-move random` | `AUTO`, `LEVEL_ZONE` while working quests or grinding |
| travel | `+new rpg`, `-grind,-follow,…` | walking to a zone, an NPC or the inn (no detours after quest mobs; fights back when attacked) |
| follow | `+follow`, `-new rpg,-grind,…` | `FOLLOW` with the owner online; a squad member that follows its squad leader (§ Squads) |
| hold | `-new rpg,-grind,-follow,…` | holds |

Everything else of playerbots' defaults stays (food, loot, gather, buff, mount, quest packets). The profile is checked
every tick and re-applied when it differs (playerbots resets strategies when a master leaves).

Only `FOLLOW` bots have a playerbots master (the character the owner plays) and sit in its party. Every other bot has
**no master and no party**: `GuildBotHolder` asks the order service's master policy before it makes the owner's
character a bot's master (at login and on every swap), so autonomous bots are never invited into the owner's party.
Before M4 every guild bot followed the leader and sat in its party; a party of six or more turns into a raid, in which
normal quests give no credit.

The leader (the owner's own character while the AI holds it during a swap) is not a guild bot and keeps the take-control
policy: master = the controlled bot, "stay" — unless it has an order (next section).

### The leader (2026-11-12)

the owner: the guild master shall level and quest in auto mode too. The leader can take an order like a guild bot:
`AUTO`, `LEVEL_ZONE`, `IDLE` or `FOLLOW`, or `HOLD`, its default (no order). It has no roster row (no slot, no `ga_bot`
row), so its plan lives beside the roster (`AdventureGuild::leaderPlan`, `leaderPlanned`); its order is a
`ga_bot_order` row with its guid, its quest blocks are `ga_bot_quest_block` rows with its guid, and `HOLD` deletes both.

| Leader's order | While the owner plays a bot | While the owner plays the leader | When the owner logs out |
|---|---|---|---|
| `HOLD` (default) | holds its position, the owner's character as master ("stay"), as before | The owner plays it; watch mode is refused (`NO_ORDER`) | logs out with the owner (D12) |
| `AUTO`, `LEVEL_ZONE`, `IDLE`, `FOLLOW` | the order planner plays it like a guild bot (master per order: only `FOLLOW` follows the owner's character; party as for bots, O2) | The owner plays it; watch mode lets the AI play it with its order (docs/take-control.md §5.12) | plays on in the offline window like the bots and logs out when the window ends; after a worldserver restart inside the window it logs in again with the bots; the owner's login takes it over (below). `GuildAdventure.Leader.OfflinePlay = 0`: logs out with the owner as with `HOLD` |

How it fits in:
- `OrderService::Update` plans `guild.leaderPlan` after the roster bots while `leaderPlanned` is set, through the same
  `Step` (AI-driven or watched, `GuildBotHolder::GetPlannedPlayer`); without an order the leader's runtime is dropped.
- `GuildBotHolder`'s leader policy (master = the owner's character, "stay") applies only to a leader without an order
  (`SetLeaderPlanPolicy`); a planned leader goes through the master policy like a bot. `OrderService::SetLeaderOrder`
  persists a change; back to `HOLD` it stops NewRpg and re-applies the leader policy (`ReapplyLeaderPolicy`), and the
  protocol / command ends watch mode of the leader (`ControlSwapService::EndWatchOf`).
- Offline (`ControlSwapService::SetLeaderStaysPolicy`): `OnLogoutDetach` hands a planned leader to the AI when the owner
  leaves while playing it (instead of the normal logout), and the D12 leader logout (`ProcessLeaderLogouts`) skips it;
  `OfflineService::EndWindow` logs it out with the bots. Without an order nothing changes (D12).
- After a restart (2026-11-12; the integration server restarts every half hour while builders work): a window that was
  running goes on (`OfflineService::BeginWindow`), its active bots log in again, and `RosterService::LoginPlannedLeader`
  logs a leader with an order in on a home session of the owner's account, also with `.ga admin login <leader>`. It
  does that only while the owner's account has no session at all (in the world, at the character screen or on the
  offline session of a closed connection), checked on the world thread where the core adds sessions, so the module and
  the owner never load the leader at the same time.
- The owner's own login always wins: picking the leader at the character screen attaches the running leader (Path R
  attach; while the module still loads it the attach waits for the load, `GuildBotHolder::IsLoggingIn`), and logging
  into another character of the account logs the AI-played leader out in the next update
  (`ControlSwapService::ProcessLeaderLogouts`, line "its leader ... stops playing on its own and logs out").
- A login does not interrupt the auto mode (the owner, 2026-11-12: [quote left out]): logging into a leader with an order starts in watch mode, the AI plays it on
  and the client watches, until the owner presses *Take over* on the control bar (or `/ga watch`, `.ga watch off`).
  `GuildAdventure.Leader.WatchOnLogin`: 1 (default) when the AI was playing the leader at the login (the offline
  window, after a restart: the Path R attach), 2 at every login into a leader with an order, 0 never. A reconnect
  within two minutes of a connection lost while the owner played the leader by hand is no return to the auto mode
  (the controls stay with the owner). `ControlSwapService::QueueWatchOnLogin` waits until the owner's session plays
  the leader in the world and then calls `RequestWatch`; a refusal (GM mode, a vehicle ...) is told in the chat and the
  owner plays the leader by hand.
- `GuildAdventure.Leader.OfflinePlay` (default 1) switches the offline part off: the leader then logs out with its owner
  whatever its order (D12) and plays its order only while the owner is online (the design log §7 O11).
- A level-up of a planned leader makes the planner look at the zones again (as for a bot); the leader still earns no
  renown and no `LEVEL_UP` event (the roster's progress is the guild's, the leader's own is not counted, as before).
- The leader keeps auto-advance on (it has no `ga_bot` row for the flag).
- Protocol: `ORDER_SET^g=<leader>` with `o=HOLD` or any order, the `LEADER` record (docs/protocol.md §7.17); the addon's
  Overview tab has the leader panel (order, why line, Watch / Take over).

### Travel and regions

Travel is on foot (NewRpg's `MoveFarTo`, mmap paths in steps of ~300 yd) inside a **region**, a walkable land mass:
Eastern Kingdoms, Kalimdor, Teldrassil (the top of the world tree with Darnassus), Rut'theran Village (its foot, with
the docks; Darnassus' portal leads down), Sardor Isle (Feathermoon Stronghold off the Feralas coast; the Feathermoon
Ferry), Azuremyst Isles (Azuremyst, Bloodmyst, the Exodar), Eversong Isles (Eversong,
Ghostlands, Silvermoon, Quel'Danas), Outland, Northrend. Regions come from positions, not zones (`GetRegionAt` in
`WorldIndex.cpp`): a bot on a beach of the Veiled Sea belongs to the island next to it, Rut'theran Village is told
from the tree top by height; a zone template's region is its hub's.

**Between regions bots take ships and zeppelins** (`ga_transport_route` in `GA_world`: the transport entry, the
faction that may use it, the ship's name). The docks are not hand-written: they are the stop frames of the transport's
path (`TransportMgr`), so a route is one leg per pair of consecutive stops; the region of each dock is looked up in the
terrain. The planner searches the shortest chain of legs the team may take (Alliance boats, Horde zeppelins, the
neutral Booty Bay-Ratchet boat) and, among equally short ones, the leg with the least walking (to the dock, and from the
arrival dock to the destination's hub). A voyage task then runs through five phases:

*Regions beyond the level cap; the walk to the next dock* (2026-11-24, thread "Testgilde spielen"). The teleporters
players click are travel links too, Dalaran's and Shattrath's portals to the capitals among them, so Northrend and
Outland were ways through: a level-16 orc in the Barrens on its way to Ghostlands took The Mighty Wind to the Borean
Tundra (two legs over Dalaran's portal to Silvermoon, as many as the zeppelin to Tirisfal and Undercity's orb, and its
tower was nearer), and stood there until its hearthstone took it home. A region no zone within the level cap lies in
(`WorldIndex::IsRegionBeyondCap`: Outland and Northrend at a cap of 60) is a destination of a route, never a way
through it. And for a first leg of two or more the walk from its arrival dock to the dock of the next leg counts: the
ship from Ratchet lands in Booty Bay, the zeppelin from Orgrimmar beside Undercity's orb.

| Phase | What the bot does |
|---|---|
| to dock | walks to the dock (profile *travel*; done within 60 yd, where the path ends at the pier) |
| wait | holds on the pier until the ship is docked (within 12 yd of its stop) and the bot is within 45 yd of it |
| board | steps on board: a short same-map hop onto the deck next to a crew member (the bot cannot path onto a moving model), then becomes the ship's passenger |
| ride | holds on deck; cross-map ships (Stormwind ↔ Auberdine) carry the bot to the other map |
| disembark | when the ship is docked at the other stop: leaves the ship and hops onto the pier (the first solid ground towards the nearest friendly harbour NPC), records `ZONE_CHANGE` |

A ship that leaves while the bot is still on the pier means waiting for the next one; a voyage that has not boarded
after 30 minutes is given up (5-minute pause).

**Teleporters players click** are travel links too (2026-11-24): a game object whose spell teleports, at once or through
the spell's DB script, to a spot 300 yd or more away on an open-world map (`WorldIndex::IndexTransports`). The Orb of
Translocation in Silvermoon casts Translocate (35376), whose `spell_scripts` row casts 25649 to the Undercity, and the
Undercity's orb casts 35727, whose row casts 35730 back. The bot walks to the object like to a portal's trigger and is
teleported to the spell's target (`StepVoyage`, the portal branch). Without them the Eversong Isles had no way out: a
blood elf levels to 20 in Eversong Woods and Ghostlands, and the zones of its next levels lie behind the orb.

**Flight paths.** A walk of more than 1500 yd (to a zone hub or a dock) becomes a flight when the bot knows a flight
path that saves at least half of the way: the nearest friendly flight master (its node is learned there, like a player
talking to it), a route over nodes the bot knows (breadth-first over the taxi paths), the landing node nearest to the
destination, enough money for the fare. A flight master more than 120 yd away is reached by the task's own walk first
(a route; live, NewRpg's single straight move to a flight master 2351 yd away was what the ground guard had to stop);
next to it the flight is booked: NewRpg talks to the flight master, pays and flies; the walk continues from the
landing spot. Bots learn flight paths like players: a bot that plans next to a flight master it does not know (within
120 yd) talks to it first (task *discover*). Looked at once a minute while walking. With the worldserver's
`AllFlightPaths = 1` (the owner's setting, the design log §7 L5) the core lets every character fly to every node of its team;
the planner then plans over all of them and discovers none (before 2026-11-12 it planned only over learned nodes, so
the setting had no effect on bots).

**Landing.** NewRpg ends its flight status when the taxi lands. With instant flight paths (worldserver
`InstantFlightPaths = 1`, the owner's setting, with `AllFlightPaths = 1`) the core puts the character at the last node at
once: it is never "in flight", NewRpg would walk it back to the flight master it left, and the planner used to log the
hop as a jump and plan again. The planner now remembers the flight master of a flight it booked (`TryFlight`) and treats
"stood within 30 yd of that flight master, and is now on the ground more than 120 yd from it (or on another map)" as the
landing: NewRpg's status ends, the walk goes on from the landing spot (activity log: `landed in <zone> ... after its
flight`), and no jump is counted. The check does not look at NewRpg's flight status, because with instant flights NewRpg
drops it in the tick it books the taxi. A normal, timed flight ends the same way. T2 on the `gaps` instance (no client):
Stormwind to Sentinel Hill with instant flight paths, `landed in Westfall`, `ends travel: arrived`, no jump.

**Portals** are travel links too: every area trigger that teleports from one open-world map to another, or more than
300 yd on the same map (in 3.3.5a the Dark Portal to Hellfire Peninsula and back, Darnassus down to Rut'theran Village
and back; triggers inside one region fall out). The bot walks into the
trigger and gets the teleport the client's area-trigger message would give it. `AUTO` considers zones in other regions too, each ship leg counted as 6000 yd
of walking, so a bot crosses the sea only when nothing at home fits (a Night Elf at level
11 moves on to Darkshore). The
Silvermoon-Undercity orb, the Dark Portal and portals in general are not used yet (§ Open points).

**Deaths.** Bots release, run back to their corpse and resurrect like players (playerbots' dead strategy). playerbots
also counts deaths since the last repair and, for a bot without a client master, revives it after five and teleports it
to a random grinding spot for its level (`RandomPlayerbotMgr::Revive`), after ten it takes a start-zone graveyard: a
random-bot convenience that is a teleport-for-level cheat for guild bots. The planner resets that count every second
while a bot lives, so it never gets there (seen before the fix: a Draenei, a Night Elf and the dwarf hunter, all forced
to higher levels with starting gear, dying often and ending up far away).

NewRpg has a built-in fallback for long walks: if `MoveFarTo` has not come 5 yd closer for 90 s, it teleports the bot
straight to its destination (stuck recovery). For a guild bot that is a teleport by order, so `BotDriver::HoldOffStuckTeleport`
holds that counter's clock back every second (the progress it measures stays), and the planner's own stuck tracker
decides instead (wowbot335 A20, extended): stuck means no 10-yard move in two minutes **or no 5 yards closer to the
target in three minutes** (a bot walking back and forth in front of an obstacle moves, but never arrives); fights and
death do not count (both clocks stand still meanwhile; before, every fight restarted them, so a bot attacked every
two or three minutes never counted as stuck; review M2). What happens then depends on the task: an NPC (giver, ender, vendor, trainer, flight master) is
skipped for 20 minutes, an objective or grind spot is avoided (100 yd around it) for 20 minutes and the planner picks
another spawn, a travel retries after 30 s, and three stuck travels in a row towards the same zone set the zone aside
for 30 minutes (AUTO picks another one, `LEVEL_ZONE` waits with "Cannot find a way to …"; a new order clears it). Seen
before the fix: a level-58 hunter teleported 1100 yd to Honor Hold, a Draenei 900 yd across Bloodmyst Isle.

The planner also notices every jump it did not cause (more than 120 yd in a second, or another map, outside a voyage,
while alive), logs it, counts it (`.ga bot plan`: "jumps") and plans again from the new place; a ghost's release to the
graveyard is no jump. A wrong region once sent a Draenei bot 14000 yd towards the Dark Portal this way before regions
came from positions.

**Zone hubs** come from the world database, not from hand-written coordinates: per zone and team, the quest giver (of
that zone's quests, not hostile to the team, **standing inside the zone**) with the most other quest givers within 80 yd.
For Elwynn Forest that is Northshire Abbey, for Westfall Sentinel Hill. Givers in a neighbour zone do not count: a
travel ends on entering the zone, and a hub outside it sent the bot there again and again (review H1: the Alterac
Mountains' quests start in Hillsbrad, Azshara's at the pier in Tanaris, the Horde's Western Plaguelands quests at the
Bulwark in Tirisfal). A zone without a giver inside is marked by its densest cluster of grind mobs instead (the Alterac
Mountains for the Alliance); pickups are not limited to the zone, so its quests are still picked up next door. A travel
that reaches the hub without being in the zone counts as a stuck travel. `.ga admin hub <zone id>` prints both teams'
hubs with the zone and region their spot lies in. The region of a zone is the region of the **team's own** hub
(review H2: Feralas has Feathermoon on Sardor Isle for the Alliance and Camp Mojache on the mainland for the Horde; the
Alliance's hub used to decide for both, so Horde bots could not reach Feralas).

**On board without a voyage.** A bot that finds itself on a ship or zeppelin with no voyage task (its order changed
during the crossing, or the owner played it on board and handed it back) rides to whichever dock of that ship comes
first and goes ashore there (review H3); a following bot stays with whoever it follows. Before, it rode back and forth
for good, because planning waits while a bot is on a transport.

### Paths through the ground (2026-11-12)

the owner watched a bot above the Fargodeep Mine walk straight down through the hill to a kobold in the tunnel under it.
The cause is in the core, not in playerbots' route choice:

- playerbots takes a grind target up to 5 yd above or below the bot, and the line of sight check knows buildings but
  not the terrain; a mob that attacks the bot from the tunnel is a target at any depth.
- `PathGenerator` gets as near as the navmesh allows. When that is the bot's own polygon (the spot right above the
  mob), the path has one point and the generator appends the real destination: a path of two points, typed
  "incomplete", that ends at the mob itself.
- `PointMovementGenerator` does not follow a path of two points; `MoveSplineInit::MoveTo` computes it again and runs
  it, because only "no path" makes it think twice: a straight spline through the rock. A player as the path's source
  also gets a straight "normal" path when no polygon is found at the start or the end.

`.ga admin path <character> <x> <y> <z> [<from x> <from y> [<from z>]]` prints what the core would do between two
points (`PathProbe`). Around the Fargodeep Mine, from the surface straight above each of the 61 kobold spawns: for six
of them a straight line through 20 to 36 yd of rock.

**The guard.** Core patch CP-10 asks a script before a point movement of a player starts
(`PlayerScript::OnPlayerCanStartPointMovement`, also when the start was put off because the unit was casting). For a
character the AI plays, `GroundGuard` probes the movement from where the character really stands: a sample every yard
and a floor looked for under each (terrain, buildings and caves; water counts). A stretch without a floor, a step from
one level to another without a slope, and a drop steeper than about 68 degrees count as off the ground, and each such
yard is either **through solid ground** (more than 6 yd below the surface or a roof: the hill over a mine, a tower) or
**through the air** (off a ledge, down a slope the navmesh does not cover). A movement is cancelled when more than
3 yd of it run through solid ground or more than 25 yd through the air; a jump off a ledge passes, as it does for a
player. (The first version, live on the integration server for an hour on 2026-11-12, cancelled every stretch without
a floor: a bot in Loch Modan stood at a 15 yd ledge until the guard was switched off.) A plain navmesh path is
trusted (the floor lookup misjudges stairs and upper storeys inside buildings); only the step onto it is probed when
the character stands more than 3 yd off the mesh. Anything else is probed along its whole length. Not checked: ships
and zeppelins, flying, swimming, ghosts, vehicles, moves under 3 yd, and characters their owner plays.
`GuildAdventure.Paths.StayOnGround = 0` switches it off. Other code that moves a bot with `MotionMaster::MovePoint`
(a flight from a fight) can ask first: `sGroundGuard.WouldCancel(player, x, y, z)`.

**What the bot does then.** It stays where it is. A walk to a quest giver NewRpg wanted to visit in passing makes
NewRpg skip that giver (it would try again for ever: its own one-minute give-up never comes while the walk is
cancelled). Three cancelled movements within 45 s towards the planner's own task (an NPC within 80 yd of the cancelled
destination, an objective or grind spot within 200 yd) set the target aside for 20 minutes and the planner picks
something else. Activity log: `does not walk from (..) to (..): the way leaves the ground (...)`, `cannot get to (..)
on the ground`.

**The way out.** NewRpg's long-distance walk follows the navmesh towards the destination as far as the search gets
and then runs into dead ends (a city wall, a root of the world tree): from there the core only offers the straight
line. So that the guard does not leave bots standing, a bot whose *travel* is cancelled three times, or that is stuck
on any task where the guard cancelled something, gets a way out: a teleporter within 40 yd is taken (the sanctum of
Stormwind's wizard tower has no other exit), else the guard is off for that bot for a minute and it walks the
straight line as it did before the guard (once per task when stuck). Any other movement that keeps being cancelled
(NewRpg's own approach to a target) gets the same way out after three rounds of three within three minutes, and a bot
in a fight after three cancelled movements within 45 s (the planner does not plan during a fight; live, a bot stood
16 yd above an enemy it was fighting): the guard never stops a bot for long. Routes (below) remove most of the dead
ends of long walks. A quest giver NewRpg gave up this way is tried again when the planner itself sends the bot there. Since 2026-11-12 "off" is limited: while it is off the guard still cancels a movement that runs more than 12 yd through solid ground or more than 40 yd through the air (a short cut through a wall's corner or off a ledge passes, a walk through a hill does not: those ended under the map), and a bot that stands off the navmesh is rescued instead (§ Rescue). The rescue's log line names the last walk the guard let through for that bot ("last walk the ground check let through 12 s ago from (..) to (..): ..."), so a bot found under the ground shows how it got there.

### Rescue: under the ground, stranded (2026-11-12)

On the live server two of eight bots made no progress for hours: one stood 94 yd under Azuremyst Isle, the other at
a spot in Elwynn Forest it never left. Every task of theirs ended "stuck" after two minutes and the next one started
at the same place. How they got there is not known (both before the ground guard was installed; a straight spline
through a hill that was cut short is the likely way). No task can get a bot out of such a place, so the planner
checks for it itself (`OrderService::CheckStranded`), whatever the task:

- **Under the ground:** no floor within 15 yd below the feet and the surface more than 10 yd above, for ten seconds
  (not while falling, swimming, flying or on a ship).
- **Stranded:** not moved 15 yd in five minutes although the tasks of that time walk (travel, the way to an NPC, an
  objective, a grind spot, a dock); time between tasks and while waiting does not count, fights and flights start the
  clock again.
- **Water is not "off the ground"** (live: a hunter working "Buzzbox 827" on the sea floor off Auberdine was pulled
  out twice, the second time by hearthstone, and a walk to threshers under water was "no way on the ground").
  `Player::IsInWater()` is set from the client's movement packets only and always says no for a bot; the planner, the
  guard and the probe ask the map (`IsSwimming`, `IsDiving`). A swimmer is neither under the ground nor off the
  navmesh, its movements are not judged by the ground guard, and a stretch straight down through water is a dive,
  not a drop.
- **Air**: playerbots does not watch a diving bot's breath (180 s, then it drowns; a live death "63 % to 0 % in 4 s,
  no fight"). After 75 s under water the bot swims straight up, breathes for 8 s at the surface and goes back to work
  (`OrderService::CheckBreath`; activity log `comes up for air at (..) after N s under water`).
- **Off the walkable ground** (Magefrost on a slope above Loch Modan, 2026-11-12): the bot stands where the navmesh
  does not reach (it slid there in a fight, or a straight line left it there). The path finder then answers every
  target with a straight line, NewRpg does not even start to walk, and each task ends "stuck" after two minutes.
  Checked after 30 seconds of standing with a task that walks, and whenever the ground guard has cancelled three
  movements in a row: when the way to each of the two nearest road map nodes is a straight line, the bot is off the
  navmesh (`OrderService::IsOffNavmesh`) and is rescued at once. The ground guard's way out (the straight line for a
  minute) is not given to such a bot: walking it through the hill is how bots end up under the map.

The bot is then put back on the ground at the nearest node of the road map within 1500 yd (a spot with walking
links; not the far side of a teleporter), and when that happened less than half an hour ago, or no node is in reach,
it uses its hearthstone (the planner sets the hour's cooldown and moves it to its bind point). Activity log: `is
under the ground at (..) ... it is put back on the ground at <node>`, `has not moved for 5 min ... it uses its
hearthstone`. Both lines, and the line of every stuck walk (`is stuck at (..), N yd from its target (task ..)`),
carry what the bot looked like: its height, the floor and surface there, what holds it (stunned, rooted, casting,
falling, ...), its movement type and NewRpg's status.

A route the bot does not get going on (not moved 10 yd within 40 s of taking it) is dropped for the straight walk.

### Routes (2026-11-12)

the owner: [quote left out]. A walk of a task used to be one NewRpg "go camp" to the destination: the navmesh search towards
it, step by step, across whatever lies in between. On the live server of 2026-11-12 a level-11 rogue sent from Elwynn
Forest to Westfall cut through the corner of Duskwood and died nine times to level-20 wolves and spiders, and long
walks ended at city walls and cliffs.

**The road map** (`RoadMap`). mod-playerbots ships a travel node graph in its playerbots database
(`playerbots_travelnode`, `_link`, `_path`): towns, inns, flight masters and every named area as nodes, walking links
between neighbours, and for each link the walked path as points about five yards apart. The module loads the
open-world part at startup (2585 nodes, 10866 walking links, 1.24 million points, three seconds) and adds what the
graph lacks: for every link and team the **danger**, the highest level of creatures hostile to that team within their
reach of its path (elites count four levels higher, three until 2026-11-14; bosses ten), from the world's spawns. A creature's reach is how
near a walker has to come to be attacked: 20 yd times the server's `Rate.Creature.Aggro`, half of what the creature
wanders, and 4 yd of slack (14 yd for a standing creature at a rate of 0.5, 19 yd for one that wanders 10 yd); beyond
it the creature counts a level less for every 4 yd, for four levels.

**A route** is the cheapest chain of links from a node within 800 yd of the start to one within 800 yd of the
destination (Dijkstra). A link costs its length (swimming counts double) times a factor for its danger relative to
the walker: since the owner's ruling of 2026-11-14 ([quote left out]) 1 up to three levels above the walker, 12 at four, 20 up to six,
30 up to ten, 60 beyond (`GuildAdventure.Roads.CostFromLevelsAbove`, 4); groups the walker cannot take cost 20 times by
the crowd check, camps it cannot take likewise. (Before: 1.5 from one level above, then since the level sweep 2 from
one level above and 6 from two; § After the sweep.) So a way
through a zone far above the bot is taken only when the way around is many times longer. Examples at level 11
(`.ga admin route`): from the east of Elwynn Forest to Sentinel Hill over Goldshire, Mirror Lake and the Jansen Stead
(2876 yd, creatures up to level 15) instead of the straight 1853 yd through Duskwood (level 29); from Stormwind's
wizard tower to Westfall through the city gate.

**Walking it** (`OrderService::WalkTo`, `OrderRoutes.cpp`). Every walk of a task (travel to a zone or to an errand's
ender, the walk to a dock, to a flight master, to an NPC, to the inn, and the way to an objective's spot until 150 yd
before it, where NewRpg takes over) longer than `GuildAdventure.Roads.MinDistance` (350 yd) asks for a route. The planner hands NewRpg a route point about 80 yd ahead of the bot and moves it on as the bot gets there, so
each step is a walk the navmesh search covers; past the last node the rest is a plain walk. A bot more than 250 yd off
its route (a death, a fight that led away) plans again. No route (no node near, a route four times the straight line),
or a walk under 1000 yd whose straight line is safe and much shorter: straight, as before. Activity log: `takes the
route <nodes> (<n> yd, <m> yd straight; strongest hostile creatures on it level <l>)`.

**Too dangerous.** A travel whose safest route still passes hostile creatures more than eight levels above the bot is
not walked (a flight was tried first): the errand is given up, the zone set aside for 30 minutes ("The way to ... is
too dangerous at level ..."), and AUTO picks another zone. Elwynn Forest to Loch Modan on foot is such a way (through
the Burning Steppes, level 58); with flight paths it is a flight. A bot that already stands among such creatures
walks any way out.

**Road links from the navmesh** (2026-11-24, thread "Testgilde spielen"). The graph has parts that no walking link joins
to the rest of their map. The start mesa of the Tauren (Camp Narache, Red Cloud Mesa, Kodo Rock, Brambleblade Ravine)
has links among its seven nodes and none down to the plains, so the road map had no route off it; and the worldserver's
path finder cannot see the way down either: it only knows the navmesh tiles of loaded grids, and a walk into a grid
nobody stands in is a straight line ("not using a path", `PathGenerator::HaveTile`), which the ground guard refuses. A
new test guild's two Tauren recruits stood on the mesa's rim with every walk to Bloodhoof Village refused ("finds no way
to walk to ...: no route of the road map for 716 yd, and the path finder has no whole way there"), until the guild left
the village's quest givers alone for a day. Now `tools/navpath` (the core's Detour on the mmaps folder, all tiles it
needs loaded, the filter the core gives bots: ground and water, no steep ground, lava or slime) finds walks offline, and
`tools/gen_road_links.py` asks it, for every part of a map that no walking link joins to the rest, for walks between the
part's nodes and the other parts' nodes (the 16 nearest pairs within 1800 yd), keeps the shortest that is at most three
times the straight line and 2600 yd long, one per pair of parts, and writes them to the world table `ga_road_link`
(`data/sql/db-world/base/ga_road_link.sql`, generated). `RoadMap::Load` reads each row as two walking links with the
navmesh's points every 5 yd, which get their danger, groups and camps like every other link. On the server's data of
2026-11-24 it found three: Camp Narache's inn to Bloodhoof Village's (1442 yd for 535 straight, the path down at the
mesa's north end), Moonglade to Timbermaw Hold, Winterspring to Felwood's Talonbranch Glade. Parts it leaves alone are
not joined on the ground: Acherus floats, Thunder Bluff and Freewind Post stand on mesas a lift joins (now a ride, below), the islands of
Blade's Edge are in the air, Teldrassil is a tree. Run the script again after a new playerbots or mmaps version.

*Links whose path jumps* (2026-11-24, same thread). Some walking links of the graph were recorded by a character that
fell or was carried: their walked path rises or falls 40 yd and more within a few points. The four links of the node
"Lady Sylvanas Windrunner" in the Royal Quarter of Undercity end at the surface of Tirisfal and Silverpine 90 yd above
it, so the road map's routes into Undercity led a bot to Cold Hearth Manor and from there straight down through the
ground, which the ground guard refuses: the test guild's undead could not reach Carendin Halgar or the city's other
trainers (the navmesh's walk from Brill is 1748 yd through the northern sewer). `tools/gen_road_links.py` now looks at
the walked path of every walking link first: where it jumps 40 yd or more (10 yd since round 272) and the navmesh has no walk between the two
points of at most four times their distance (200 yd at least), the link goes into the world table `ga_road_unlink`
(same generated file), which `RoadMap::Load` leaves out, and the navmesh's walk between the link's two nodes takes its
place in `ga_road_link` when it is at most four times their distance (400 yd more at least). On the server's data of
2026-11-24: 111 links left out (37 in the old world: Undercity's Royal Quarter, Swamp of Sorrows' Pool of Tears, the
Caverns of Time, the Thandol Span, Darrow Hill to the Dalaran crater, Demon Fall in Ashenvale, Naxxramas' and Acherus'
floating nodes) and 33 walks in their place (the Royal Quarter to Cold Hearth Manor 1402 yd, to Tirisfal 1605 yd, to the
Shining Strand 1452 yd; Waterspring Field to the Caverns of Time 1511 yd; Darrow Hill to the Dalaran crater 1028 yd);
the three bridges between parts are unchanged. A bot that had followed such a jump had its step refused and the nodes
around it blocked (`ga_road_block`): an undead recruit of the test guild took "Varimathras" and the Royal Quarter's
"Lady Sylvanas Windrunner" out at 03:45, and since the lifts are no walks and the other way out of the city leads
through the Scarlet camp north of the Ruins of Lordaeron, a level-11 Forsaken that had flown into Undercity found no
route out of it ("no route of the road map for 426 yd"). `RoadMap::Load` gives back the blocks of nodes within 60 yd
and 15 yd of height of an end of a link it leaves out (4 of the server's 5 blocks: those two and two at the Caverns of
Time); a node that is no way on the ground is blocked again when a bot is refused at it.

**Rides on lifts** (2026-11-24, same thread). The road map knew no lifts: Thunder Bluff and Freewind Post stand on mesas
only lifts lead up to, Undercity's lifts join the city to the Ruins of Lordaeron, the Great Lift joins the Barrens to
Thousand Needles, and NewRpg rides none of them (mod-playerbots leaves static transports alone). A Tauren recruit of the
test guild at the foot of Thunder Bluff had its hand-in at Hunter Rise refused ("no route of the road map for 191 yd")
and gave it up. `RoadMap::Load` now reads the travel node graph's transport links (type 3) whose object is a static
transport (`GAMEOBJECT_TYPE_TRANSPORT`) and whose two stops stand one above the other (within 10 yd, 12 yd or more of
height; not the doors of Undercity's lifts, which the graph joins by their object too): 80 rides, each costing its height
and 60 yd for the wait (`Link::lift`, `RoadRoute::lifts`; the route's `via` names them "(lift)"). `OrderService::WalkTo`
does not let a route's point be passed or walked to beyond the boarding stop of its next ride; at the stop (8 yd, 12 yd of
height: the stops are the platform's own positions, which for Thunder Bluff's lifts lie 8 yd above its floor)
`OrderService::StepLift` takes over: the AI is held, the platform is looked up among the map's transports (static
transports are not stored in the grid), and when it stands at the stop the bot hops onto it and becomes its passenger
(`Transport::AddPassenger`; the server's static transport carries its passengers), the planner does nothing else during the
ride, and at the other stop the bot hops onto the landing, a point of the route 5 to 20 yd beyond the stop (the platform
hangs beside the landing, off the walkable ground). It gives up after 150 s without a platform or 90 s on it, and the rest
of the walk goes without the road map; the stuck rules do not count the wait. Lines: `steps onto the lift`, `rode the lift
... in N s`, `gives up its ride on the lift`.

**The landing beside a lift's stop** (2026-11-25, the owner: [quote left out]). The guild leader of the test guild stood on the mesa of Freewind Post with its quest targets
in the canyon below. Its route went down the lift, but the walk to the upper stop went to the stop itself, which is the
platform's place over the shaft: with the platform at the bottom the path finder's only ground there is the shaft's floor
130 yd below, the ground guard refused the walk, the bot stood 15 yd from the lift, and the refusal took both lower stops
of the mesa's lifts out of the road map (`BlockNodesNear` blocks the nodes near a refused step). From then on no route
led down, and every task ended "objective spot not reached" until a restart gave the stops back. Yesterday's ride had
worked because the platform stood at the top. Now the walk to a lift's boarding stop goes to its landing
(`OrderService::LiftLanding`: ground of the map and the world's models, not the platform, at the stop's height 4 to
14 yd from it, the nearest with a path from the bot), the bot boards from there (within 3 yd of the landing, or 8 yd of
the stop as before) and waits there for the platform; and `BlockNodesNear` leaves a lift's stops alone (`Node::liftStop`:
a step to one is refused while the platform is away). An objective whose spot lies 20 yd or more above or below the bot
with no path of the path finder to it is walked by the planner at once (its route takes the lift), where NewRpg had walked
the mesa round for three minutes before each task ended "no progress at this spawn". Lines: `walks to the landing at (..)
beside the lift's stop at (..), N yd from it`, `has the spot of quest .. N yd away and N yd below it, where no path leads:
the planner walks it there itself`. On `j5`: the leader put on the mesa with quest 4841 "walks to the landing at (-5382,
-2483, 89) beside the lift's stop at (-5382, -2489, 89), 6 yd from it", waited 31 s for the platform, "steps onto the
lift", "rode the lift ... to (-5382, -2489, -40) in 14 s" and fought the centaurs below.
A squad member does not follow its leader onto a lift (2026-11-25): mod-playerbots' follow does not board one, and a
warlock that followed its leader off the Mesa Elevator's top at Freewind Post walked out over the canyon, stood 54 yd
above its floor and was rescued. While its leader waits for a lift or rides it the member stays where it is (`waits
while its squad leader .. rides the lift (it does not follow onto it)`), and catches up by its own way afterwards.

**A ride is not cut short, and a passenger without a ride gets off** (2026-11-25, round 226). Ashmire (26) went up the
Mesa Elevator to its leader on top of Freewind Post (`walks to it along the roads`); 13 s into the 14-s ride it was
within 20 yd of its leader on its level, the walk counted as done (`is back beside its squad leader`), its task was
cleared and the ride with it. It stayed the platform's passenger, the next ride took it back down into the mesa, and it
was rescued by hearthstone to Tranquillien. A member's walk back to its leader does not end while a lift of its route
carries it or it waits at the stop, nor while it stands on any transport, and none begins then; the walk ends after
the ride (`OrderService::UpdateSquad`). And a passenger of a lift without a ride of its own was waited out for good:
the planner waits out anything a bot rides, before its rescue checks, so the rule that took a passenger off when it
stood away from its platform never ran. Mojowind entered the world on the Mesa Elevator after a restart during its ride
and stood on it from 18:28 to past 19:22 (`task none`, `moved 0 yd`); Ashmire stood on it half an hour after it had
followed its leader onto it, and entered the world on it after the next restart. Such a passenger now gets off at the
platform's next stop (its height unchanged for 1.5 s) onto the landing beside it, at the height the platform carries it
at or else the platform's own; one far from its platform, or with no stop in two minutes, is taken off where it stands
as before (`OrderService::StepStrayLiftPassenger`, before the planner's wait). Lines: `is a passenger of the lift ..
without a ride of its own .. it gets off at the platform's next stop`, `gets off the lift .. at its stop at height N
after N s: onto the landing beside it at (..)`.

**A service is chosen by its walk** (2026-11-24, same thread). A vendor, trainer, innkeeper or flight master was the
nearest as the crow flies that the risk rules let through (`NearestService`). The test guild's level-8 druid, bags full,
stood on the plateau beside the Valley of Trials 187 yd from Kzan Thornslash; the road there was 4683 yd through the
Razormane Grounds and Razor Hill and back into the valley, the next vendor (Rarc, beside him) 4386 yd, and the druid
died to a Venomtail Scorpid on the way. Now a service's walk counts: the path finder's walk (`WalkReaches`, its length),
else the road map's route; one whose walk is at most twice the straight line plus 100 yd is taken at once, else the
shortest walk of the first four with a good way; one with no way at all is none.

**What the first day on the live server changed** (2026-11-12). Bots were found under the map with the ground guard
on. One way there, seen on the test instance: from Stormwind's inn to the harbor the route was the single node
"Stormwind Stockade entrance", a node of playerbots' teleport links down the stairs to the instance, where the
navmesh of the world ends; the guard cancelled the step, the way out switched the guard off for a minute, and the bot
walked the straight line. Since then:

- nodes at instance portals and teleporters (names ending in "entrance" or "exit", or with "portal") are not part of
  routes or rescues;
- a walk off the graph, to the first node and from the last, costs 1.3 times its length for the first 150 yd and three
  times beyond, so a route ends at the node next to the destination when there is one (from the inn to the docks:
  "Stormwind City > Ship (The Bravery)", 1230 yd down the ramp, instead of 815 yd straight to the cliff above them);
- the rule "a short safe walk goes straight" applies only when the core's path finder has a whole path for that walk;
- a step of a route the guard cancels three times takes the nodes within 25 yd of it out of the graph (until the next
  restart or `.ga reload`) and the task walks on without a route: `leaves its route at (..): no way on the ground to
  its next point (..); out of the road map: <nodes>`. The guard stays on.
- when a route is given up, NewRpg is sent to the destination at once (it kept walking to the route's last point).

**Second day of live rounds** (2026-11-12, rounds 15 and 16). Every Alliance bot that wanted to fly from Stormwind
stood below the flight master, who stands on the wall 27 yd above the gate, for five minutes until the rescue:

- **The walk to a flight master ends at the flight master**: a flight is booked (handed to NewRpg, whose own walk to
  the master is one straight move) only when the bot stands within 20 yd of it on its level (6 yd); until then the
  task walks there (`WalkTo`). It was booked from 120 yd on the map.
- **Short walks get a route when the path finder has no whole path for them** (the destination is on another level):
  `WalkTo` probes walks under `Roads.MinDistance` once per destination.
- **The ends of a route are checked with the path finder**: a node is the first or last node of a route only when
  the walk between it and the start or destination is one the path finder has (not "no path", not a straight line,
  not a path that ends where it starts). The flight master's own node is 37 yd from the gate below and no walk; the
  route from there is "Stormwind City innkeeper" (313 yd for 32 yd as the crow flies) and the flight leaves two
  minutes later. This replaces the rule about the share of walks off the graph.
- **The next step of a route is about 80 yd ahead, by distance**: it was 16 points ahead, and the points of a link
  lie 5 to 60 yd apart, so one step could be 280 yd (the cancelled step above Loch Modan that took "Stonesplinter
  Valley" out of the graph).
- **Nodes taken out are remembered** in `ga_road_block` (world database; delete a row to give a node another chance).

`GuildAdventure.Roads.Enable = 0` switches routes off. Fights on the way, and whether a single mob is fought or
avoided, stay with playerbots and the behaviour work (the design log §7 L4).

### Level sweep 20 to 60 (2026-11-12)

the owner's live bots were level 11 to 16, so everything above the low twenties was untested. On the `gaps` instance
(integration round 2 plus this branch) copies of six of his bots were set to level 20, 30, 40, 50, 58 and 60
(`.ga admin boost`: level, uncommon gear, bags, money; spells, skills and talents from the level-up as in play) and
five fresh Horde recruits to 20, 30, 40, 50 and 58 in their start zones. Four runs of 16 to 25 minutes on autopilot,
fixes between the runs.

| | Run 1 (25 min) | Run 3 (25 min) | Run 4 (16 min) |
|---|---|---|---|
| "does not walk" (movements the ground guard cancelled) | 216 | 18 | 4 |
| "is stuck" | 41 | 0 | 0 |
| rescues | 0 | 3 | 1 |
| deaths | 8 | 4 | 2 |
| bots that gained experience | 5 of 13 | 11 of 13 | 12 of 13 (the 60 gains none) |

In run 1 every bot above level 30 spent the whole run travelling or standing. What was wrong, and what the fixes do:

- **Long routes were thrown away.** A route more than four times the straight line was "not worth it", and the bot
  walked the straight line into the mountains instead (Mulgore to Feralas, Redridge to the Swamp of Sorrows: ten
  minutes at a dead end, then the zone set aside). A route is a way and the straight line is a guess: the cap is
  twelve times now.
- **The ends of a route were guesses too.** The walk to the first and from the last node is followed with the path
  finder path by path, as NewRpg's long walk does (`WalkReaches`): its search covers a limited stretch, so a far
  target is "incomplete" whether or not there is a way, and only following it shows which.
- **A travel step with no way at all** (hundreds of yards through a hill or the air) counted as "stuck" only after
  two minutes of standing with the ground check "off". It counts at once now (`finds no way on foot towards ..`),
  and a bot that the path finder leads to none of the three nearest road nodes is `cut off from every road` and
  put back on one at once.
- **The flight master was the nearest on the map**: two Horde bots in the Valley of Trials walked towards Ratchet's,
  behind the cliffs, for the whole run. It is the nearest the bot can walk to, with the real length of the walk
  (`WalkLength`); the mage then walked to Orgrimmar and flew.
- **A zone entered at its far end had "nothing left to do"**: quest givers count within 2500 yd, and a mage that landed
  at Zoram'gar Outpost had Ashenvale's quests 3600 yd away at Splintertree Post. With nothing in reach, the givers
  of the zone's quests anywhere in the zone count.
- **An objective NewRpg leaves at once was planned again every five seconds** for ever ("Egg Hunt", 55 times in eleven
  minutes). After four times within a minute its spot is set aside like one the bot could not get to; so is the
  spot of an objective whose walk has no way, and a quest area without a spawn is approached by the planner's own
  walk like a spawn.
- **"Off the walkable ground" fired on the navmesh**: a bot casting in a pit of the Searing Gorge was "rescued" twice,
  the second time by hearthstone. Only the path finder's own "not using a path" (no polygon under the start) counts.
- **The top of a zeppelin tower is not on the navmesh** (the mesh begins on the landing 20 yd below): a bot that went
  ashore there could not walk on. Piers and the spots a rescue puts a bot at are moved to where the navmesh begins
  (`SnapToNavmesh`).
- Smaller ones: the rescue has a third way out (the graveyard a dead character of its side would wake up at) when no
  road node is in reach and the hearthstone is on cooldown; only a step along a route takes a node out of the graph
  (the walk to its first node says nothing about the node: "Stormwind City" and "Ratchet flightMaster" had gone that
  way, the rows are deleted); routes go around places the bot has set aside after deaths or lost fights (a link
  through one costs thirty times its length); a bot in its target zone but not in the region of the zone's hub (the
  mainland of Feralas for the Alliance) does the zone's work on its side before it takes the ferry; an errand
  without a flight is walked for at most 8000 yd of route; a bot that leads a follower walks (no mount), and a
  walk to a dock gives way to a quest event that just started.

**What the sweep leaves open**, by weight (evidence in `_work\research\sweep\sweep*.txt` while the instance lives):

(Items 1, 3, 5 and 6 and "WANTED: Murkdeep!" of item 4 are worked on: next section.)

1. *Zone choice does not know the way.* A level-21 night elf whose way to Ashenvale was refused as too dangerous
   (the route to the zone's hub passed level-30 creatures) chose Stonetalon and was flown to Nijel's Point in
   Desolace. The choice should rate zones by the route to the place the bot would work at, and a flight should not
   land in a zone far above the bot.
2. *Weak classes die where they level.* A level-50 priest in uncommon gear died five times in twelve minutes in
   Felwood (level 47 to 51 creatures), twice on the way to a vendor. The risk model of the behaviour work decides
   here; from the planner's side a zone a few levels lower for cloth healers would help.
3. *Hand-ins that fail next to the NPC*: "Report to Ironforge" at Prospector Stormpike and "Assisting Arch Druid
   Staghelm" at Fandral Staghelm, `cannot_turn_in` with the NPC 1.5 yd away, "can reward yes", "reached no". Both
   stand inside buildings on an upper floor; NewRpg does not register that it reached them.
4. *Objectives without progress*: "The Bloodsail Buccaneers", "Are We There, Yeti?", "FIFTY! YEP!",
   "WANTED: Murkdeep!" ended "no progress at this spawn" (group or named targets, items with long respawns).
5. *Surfacing ends the objective task* ("NewRpg left the quest" after every trip for air): harmless, but the task
   starts anew each time and the log is noisy.
6. *The escort "The Escape"* (a shredder that drives fast) was lost twice.
7. Level 60 behaves as decided: the warlock at 60 kept questing in Winterspring, the two 58s levelled in the Burning
   Steppes and Winterspring, nobody was sent to Outland or Northrend.

### After the sweep: where a zone is entered, walks that are not worth it, a place to clear (2026-11-12)

The sweep's open list, worked from the top (items 2 and 4 are the behaviour work's and the quest interactions'), and
what the live rounds of the same day added. T2 on the `gaps` instance unless said otherwise.

- **A zone is entered where the bot has quests to take** (item 1). The target of a travel to a zone was the zone's hub,
  the same for every level: Ashenvale's (Forest Song) lies behind level-30 creatures, so a level-21 bot's way there
  was "too dangerous", Ashenvale was set aside and the bot was flown towards Stonetalon's hub and landed at Nijel's
  Point in Desolace. The target is now the nearest giver, in that zone, of a quest the bot can take
  (`OrderService::ZoneEntry`); the hub only when it can take none. `.ga bot plan` shows it (`zone entry: Piznik at
  (963, -264) map 1, 4053 yd`). T1 plus that line: the two test bots always had a hand-in to travel for, so no
  travel to a zone as such ran.
- **A flight does not land in a zone far above the bot** unless that zone is where it wants to go: a landing in a
  zone whose level range starts more than five above the bot is left out, and so is one whose walk from the landing
  to the destination passes creatures more than eight levels above it (`FindFlight`). Seen: the level-21 hunter and
  a fresh level-21 recruit flew from Auberdine to Astranaar and on to Stonetalon Peak for their hand-ins; none landed
  in Desolace.
- **Hand-ins that failed next to the NPC** (item 3). NewRpg stays in its "visit an NPC" status when it has finished
  with one NPC and picks the next by itself; the planner saw the right status and waited, with the ender 1.5 yd away,
  until the task ran out ("cannot turn in", "reached no"). The visit is set again whenever NewRpg's NPC is not the
  task's (`BotDriver::IsVisiting`). Seen: "Report to Ironforge" handed in at Prospector Stormpike 28 s after the bot
  arrived (the sweep: `cannot_turn_in`). Fandral Staghelm was not tried again.
- **Surfacing no longer ends the objective** (item 5): after a trip for air the planner puts NewRpg back on the
  objective instead of reading its rest as "left the quest". T1.
- **Escorts** (item 6): the bot keeps the travel profile while it follows (it does not start to grind beside the
  NPC), attacks what attacks the NPC (`DefendWard`), and an NPC out of sight counts as lost after 75 s, not 45 (the
  shredder of "The Escape" drives ahead around corners). T1: not run again on the instance.
- **A place to clear** (quest event kind `clear`, hand list). The target of "WANTED: Murkdeep!" stands invisible at a
  camp fire and shows itself only when no Greymist Warrior or Hunter is alive within 80 yd; then three waves come,
  he with the last. The bot stood at the spawn and waited ("no progress at this spawn"). Now it kills what is hostile
  within 80 yd of the spawn, nearest first, stays, fights what attacks it and the creature of the objective once it
  can be seen; six minutes at the cleared place with nothing coming are a failure "no progress". Seen: a level-19
  hunter cleared the camp in five fights, then fought the three Coastrunners, the two Warriors and Murkdeep with his
  Hunter: "event done" 2 min 55 s after the task began.
- **A walk is not worth a death.** The bots wear what their quests gave them (item level 8 to 15 at level 15 to 19 on
  the live server), so two foes of their own level are a lost fight, and what kills them now is two or three
  creatures met on a walk: twice in a day a level-17 mage walked through the Mo'grosh ogre camp to the Farstrider
  Lodge, a level-16 rogue past level-18 highwaymen to a vendor. Two rules, for every walk of a task:
  - *Cost.* A link of the road map costs its length times a factor for its strongest hostile creature relative to
    the walker: 1 up to the walker's level, 2 one level above, 6 two above, 12 up to four, 20 up to six, 30 up to
    ten, 60 beyond (it was 1.5 up to three levels above). A creature counts in full within its reach of the way
    (above; it was 25 yd for every creature until live round 51), and a level less for every four yards beyond, for
    four levels. The rule "a short walk goes straight when the route is a detour" needs a straight line with nothing
    above the bot's level on it.
  - *Gate.* When the way that is left (the route of a long walk, the straight line of a short one) still passes
    creatures two or more levels above the bot (elites count three higher), the walk is not walked and the target is
    left alone for half an hour, so the planner takes another quest first (`LeaveDangerousWalk`; activity log `does
    not walk to <target> (pickup, quest ..): the way (..) passes level-N creatures (it is level M)`). For pickups,
    hand-ins, flight masters to discover, errands (with the walk from a flight's landing) and the way to an
    objective's spot, there without its last 60 yd: what lives at the spot is the risk model's business. A bot that
    stands among such creatures already walks anyway. Vendors and trainers are chosen by the way to them already
    (the service choice of the behaviour work, with a last choice when no way is safe). A travel to a zone keeps
    its limit of eight levels: the bot has to get there.
  Seen (18 bots of level 15 to 60 for eight minutes on `main` with this): 24 routes, one gate (a level-18 mage's
  hand-in at Ironband's Excavation, "level-20 creatures"), no "stuck", 7 hand-ins, 3 pickups, 7 objectives done, one
  death (at an objective). `.ga admin route` at level 17 from Thelsamar to the Farstrider Lodge: over the dam and the
  Loch, 2909 yd past creatures up to level 16 (with the old costs 2023 yd past level 20; live it was the ogre camp,
  because a rare crocolisk had made the way over the Loch "level 22" as well).
- **Objectives "close by" behind a mountain**: an objective just across the zone border counts within 1500 yd as the
  crow flies; from Stonetalon Peak that is the Zoram Strand, 8300 yd of route away. The walk to an objective's spot
  is not walked when its route is longer than 2500 yd and four times the straight line; the spot is set aside for 20
  minutes. Seen: "The Bloodsail Buccaneers", a spawn
  behind a route over a ship and the Gurubashi Arena, `objective too far around`.
- **What counts as danger.** Civilians (the flag "does not aggro") no longer count: the flight master of the other
  side in Booty Bay, level 65 elite, made every way into the town "level 68" for the Alliance (now 41). Rares do
  not count either: they are seldom there (Mugglefin at Lake Falathim, level 23 and counted three higher like an
  elite, kept a level-21 bot from the corpse it had travelled there for).
- **"Stuck" is measured along the route.** The stuck rule "not five yards closer to the target in three minutes"
  measured the straight line, and a route may lead away from its destination for minutes (around the Loch, over a
  pass). Since routes are kept up to twelve times the straight line this fired on bots that were walking: six
  "is stuck ... moving; rpg go camp" lines in one live round. While a task follows a route, what is left of the
  route is the measure.
- **A patch of ground that nothing leads from** (a boulder, a stump: there is a polygon under the bot, but the path
  finder gets nowhere from it, so every movement is a cancelled straight line "shortcut + no path"; nine in a row for
  one bot in Loch Modan, live). A bot that has not moved for 30 s, with three movements cancelled in the last two
  minutes and no way to any of the three nearest road nodes, is put back on a road (`is cut off from every road`).
  T1: not seen on the instance.

Left open here (the Wild Shore and the patrols are done in the next section): pooled quest objects ("The Bloodsail Buccaneers": four places for the
charts, one of them spawned; the paths to all four are fine, the planner tries them one after the other with a wait
at each empty one); a zone entry may be a quest giver inside a camp (Piznik in the Windshear Mine), which the
travel's own danger limit has to catch.

### Live rounds 23 and 24: the start area, vendor trips, grinding, water (2026-11-12)

**the owner's level-3 guild leader left Northshire** and fought level-6 wolves at Goldshire, with quests open in the start
area. Three things came together (integration server log; reproduced with a fresh human on the `gaps` instance):

- At a grind spot the fighting was playerbots' own grinding, which takes creatures up to four levels above the bot.

the owner's rules for this (2026-11-12): [quote left out]; [quote left out]; and such rules shall be settings the guild leader can
change. What the planner does now:

- **A place whose creatures all start above the bot is for later.** A hand-in or a pickup more than 150 yd away is
  not walked to when the weakest of the creatures spawning within 150 yd of its NPC (at least three) is more than
  `Walks.MaxLevelsAbove` above the bot; the NPC is left alone for `Walks.PostponeMinutes` (`RoadMap::WeakestAround`,
  setting `Walks.PlaceCheck`). Seen: `Startwar does not walk to Innkeeper Farley (turn-in, quest 2158 "Rest and
  Relaxation"): the creatures around it start at level 6 (it is level 3); left alone for 30 min`, and it stayed in

- **Vendor trips** (`GuildAdventure.Vendor.Trips`): `0` hub (default): selling, repairing and food and drink happen
  at a hub right after a quest was handed in there (three minutes, a vendor within 200 yd), and at once only when it
  is urgent: one free bag slot or none, gear below 20 %, a hunter nearly out of ammunition (one trip per half hour
  for that). `1` full: only when urgent. `2` any: whenever
  something is due, as before. Besides that, a hand-in or a pickup within 150 yd of the bot comes before any upkeep.
  *The repair itself* (2026-11-14, an observer's find): a trip for a repair repairs at the armorer with the bot's own
  money, piece by piece as far as it goes (`repaired its gear at .. for Nc: durability 1% -> 100%`). It used to be left
  to NewRpg, which repairs only within what mod-playerbots' budget keeps free for repairs: a level-38 mage at 1 %
  durability with 9 gold went to the armorer, came back unrepaired ("could not pay the repair", which it could), and
  its next trip waited a quarter of an hour.
- **A hunter's ammunition** (the owner, 2026-11-13: [quote left out]; `Ammunition.h`, the storage side in docs/storage.md section 9). At every vendor it visits a hunter fills its
  stock with the best ammunition the vendor sells for its weapon and level, with its own money (`Ammo::BuyAt`; nearly
  out and without money: one bundle from the guild's budget): `Hunterbm bought 2000 x Razor Arrow for its weapon (28s

  ammunition: from wherever it is below `GuildAdventure.Ammo.RestockBelow` (100) rounds (`goes to a vendor (...):

  more is missing and it has come to a hub after a hand-in or is on a vendor trip anyway (`ammunition below its
  stock`; at most every ten minutes). Neither while the guild storage holds ammunition it would take. mod-playerbots'
  own purchases at a vendor go on, held to the same stock by the vendor hook; that is how a warrior or rogue with a
  bow gets its one stack.
- **Grinding is the planner's.** Only when the zone has no quest work for the bot (as before), within
  `Grind.MaxDistance` (600 yd, was 1200), at a spot of creatures from `Grind.LevelsBelow` (3) below the bot to
  `Grind.LevelsAbove` (0) above, and never what the risk model's `CanFight` refuses. At the spot the planner picks every target (`PickGrindTarget`: the nearest creature
  within 70 yd of the spot in that level range, no elite, nobody else's, none with a stronger creature within 20 yd,
  one that stands alone before one of a pack)
  and the bot runs the travel profile, so playerbots' grind strategy is off. A spot with nothing to fight for 20 s
  is left alone for five minutes. `Grind.Enable = 0`: it waits instead. Seen: the level-3 human fought sixteen

**Water.** Round 23 had four deaths in water; three were one druid on "Deep Ocean, Vast Sea". They were not

murloc, before any surfacing), and the trip for air at 75 s pulled the bot out of those fights with one move
straight up. Fighting under water is the behaviour work's; on the planner's side:

- **Breath by the server's timer**: up for air after 42 % of `WaterBreath.Timer` (75 s at most), in a fight only

- **A swimmer's way through solid ground is cancelled.** Swimmers were exempt from the ground guard; a straight line

- **Up to the surface first**: a walk that starts under water to a place that is not under water goes straight up

**Routes and rescue, from the same rounds:**

- **A walk that finds no route and does not get going** within a minute (NewRpg has no path either: a target on a

- **Far from the navmesh** counts as off the walkable ground, like "no polygon under the start": a bot on a slope
  above a cave in Darkshore had fourteen movements cancelled ("incomplete + start far from the navmesh") and four
  targets set aside one after the other, and no rescue fired. T1.
- `.ga admin route` checks the ends of its route with the path finder, as a bot's walk does.

Left open: the tunnel of Timbermaw Hold between Felwood, Moonglade and Winterspring has no path (a bot with a vendor
in Moonglade stands at its mouth until the task runs out); a zone entry may still be a quest giver inside a camp;

### Live round 29: where to quest, grinding, camps on the way (2026-11-12)

Eight deaths in 23 minutes on the integration server, read from its activity log; what they were, and what changed.

- **A zone without quests for the bot.** A level-21 warlock had every walk in the Wetlands refused (the creatures
  around its targets start at level 24 to 28), "looked at the zones again", moved to the Hillsbrad Foothills and
  ground bears there until it had died three times. The zone list has the Foothills from level 20 for both sides, but
  the Alliance's quests there begin at level 25; the zone counted three "quests" because quests *of* the zone that are
  handed out in a city far away were counted, and a zone next door beat every zone farther away while the bot's own
  zone still "fitted" its level. Now: only quests whose giver stands in the zone count; a bot whose zone has nothing
  for it moves to a zone that has, however far (the neighbour rule is gone: the owner, [quote left out]), and more quests weigh against a longer way (`cost / (1 + quests / 4)`, twelve
  quests at most); without any zone with quests it stays where it is. The pick goes into the activity log with the
  count of every candidate: `Priestholy (level 58) picks Eastern Plaguelands as its zone: 16 quests to take or work on
  there, 10627 yd away (the others: Burning Steppes 0, Western Plaguelands 7, ...)`.
- **Grinding.** The spot was within the rules (creatures of the bot's level, `Grind.LevelsAbove` 0; a bear one level
  above joined). Three things were missing: a target with company (hostile creatures within 15 yd of it) is only
  taken when the risk model lets the bot fight that many (`Risk::CanFight(level, count)`); a creature at a place the
  bot keeps away from is no target, and a grind whose spot is set aside ends; and **one** death ends a grind and sets
  its spot and the place of the death aside (it took three: no grind spot is worth a second death).
- **Camps on the way.** Two characters died on errand travels to groups of three, five and six levels below them. The
  road map's nodes are named places, and many named places are camps: the farm and the mine were the *first node* of
  the two routes, and the walk from the bot to a route's first node (and from its last node to the destination) was
  never looked at for groups. Now those walks are (without the first 120 yd, where the walker stands, and the last 60
  yd, which whoever goes there judges), and creatures count as standing on a way within 18 yd of it (was 14).
  What a camp is, was put right at the same time: a group of three or more that is **not more than three levels
  below the walker** and that the risk model does not let this bot fight (`Risk::CanFight(level, count)`). Round 27
  had counted groups down to twelve levels below, which kept a level-58 priest from both Plaguelands for five
  level-47 creatures somewhere on 10 000 yd. A link or a walk past a camp costs 20 times its length in the route
  search, so routes go around camps where there is a way around; a task's walk whose way still passes one is not
  walked, and that now holds for travels too (errands, zone travels, the walk to a flight master): `does not walk to
  ..: N level-L creatures stand together on the safest way`.
  **What this does not catch:** the two deaths of the round. Their groups were five and six levels below the
  characters, the road map's line to the farm's node passes its three at a distance while the bot's real path led
  through them, and at the mine the three came one after another during a rest. Such fights are the fight and rest
  rules' matter; a bot that sees a camp ahead while it walks and goes around it is not built.
- **A detour for nothing** (the owner: his leader went from Westbrook Garrison to the Eastvale Logging Camp [quote left out] instead of along the road). Since round 27 any group of three on a link
  cost half the link's length more for each of them, for every walker up to twelve levels above them: three level-7
  murlocs at Crystal Lake made the way along the road dearer than the arc over the Northshire vineyards and the
  Jasperlode Mine for a level-12 character (3503 yd instead of 2405). A group now costs nothing unless it is a camp
  for that walker (above).
- **The group the bot stands in** does not count against a walk any more (the first 120 yd): a shaman among the
  nagas of Mathystra had every walk out of the ruins refused for "3 level-17 creatures on the way" and ground there.
- **Vendor trips say why**: `goes to a vendor (Homer Stonefield, 160 yd): bags full; 1 free bag slots, gear at 100%,
  ammunition 0 x 0`. The trip of the round (a hunter, 1516 yd, two seconds after a restart, with nine free bag slots

Not the planner's: the priest that died had rested for seven seconds at 10 % mana when the next fight began, and went
