### Live round 32: quest meat in the storage, a walk without a route (2026-11-12)

- **A quest's items went into the guild storage.** A mage killed Great Goretusks for twenty minutes for "Redridge
  Goulash" (twelve fights, every task ending "no progress at this spawn"). The creature was right and the snouts
  dropped; but a Great Goretusk Snout is trade goods to the game, not a quest item, and the loot filter stores
  materials: every looted snout joined the stack in the bags and the whole stack went into the storage (later
  the quest supply of package K2 took them out again, one by one). The loot filter only knew quest items by their
  class and asked mod-playerbots for the rest, which did not call these wanted. Now it asks the quest log itself: an
  item that a quest in the log asks for (open, or complete and not handed in) stays in the bags, whatever a rule or
  the default says for a character the AI plays, and for the owner's own character unless a rule of his decided
  (`LootService`, why "for its quest"). Many classic quests collect ordinary meat, hides and trinkets.
- **No route, so straight through the hill.** A hunter beside a vendor on a platform in Auberdine "found no route for
  1131 yd and walked straight": the route search only used first and last nodes with a proven walk from the start and
  to the destination, the path finder had none from where the bot stood, and without a route the whole way was one
  straight move, which the ground check stopped. When no node has a proven walk, the route now uses the nearest
  nodes anyway (start and end), and only that stretch is left to the path finder.

Not changed here: a bot whose errands are all refused and that grinds in a zone without quests moves on since round
29 (the zone choice); the spots of objectives inside camps (a banner quest in a gnoll camp with a stronger creature
among them) are the risk model's verdict on a spot, which the planner follows.

### Professions: the plan acts (2026-11-12, package K1)

the owner: [quote left out]. The plan itself (two primaries with a target, secondaries) is set in the addon's
Professions tab and stored in `ga_bot_profession_plan`; until now it was only shown. `Professions.h/.cpp` and three
hooks in the planner make a bot follow it:

- **Learning** (`GuildAdventure.Professions.LearnInPlace`, once a minute): what the trainer of a planned profession
  would teach the bot now is learned where it stands, free, like class spells: the profession itself (level 5 for
  primaries), the next rank when level and skill allow, the recipes. The list is that of the trainer of the
  profession with the most to teach (14 professions on the 3.3.5a world database); trainers with a requirement
  (specialisations) are left out. A profession that is not in the plan is never learned. With the profession the bot
  gets its tools (Mining Pick, Skinning Knife, Blacksmith Hammer, Arclight Spanner; the fishing pole comes with a
  fishing trip): without the pick
  the mining spell fails at every vein.
- **Gathering.** Skinning its kills and gathering nodes within the auto loot range existed (`AutoLoot`), for a bot
  that had the skill; now it has it. New: a mining or herb node the bot's skill opens within
  `Professions.GatherDetour` (40 yd) of a walking bot is fetched: the bot leaves its walk for up to 30 s, walks to
  the node, auto loot gathers it, and the task sets its walk again (`OrderService::GatherDetour`; activity log
  `makes a detour of N yd for <node>`). Only while a task walks (travel, the way to an NPC, an objective, a grind
  spot), never in a fight, an event or an escort. What it gathers goes to the guild storage through the loot filter.
- **Crafting at a hub** (`Professions.CraftAtHub`, `Professions.CraftBatch`): in the three minutes after a hand-in
  (the window vendor trips use) the bot crafts what still gives skill in a planned profession from its bags and the
  guild storage: among the recipes it knows that are not grey and that it has the materials for, the one whose
  skill point costs the least (the materials' vendor worth over the chance of a point), at most five casts, then
  again at the next hub ten minutes later or more. The casts are `CraftService`'s (the bot stands still, the
  reagents come out of the storage through core patch CP-7); a primary profession is not taken past its plan's
  target. Products stay in the bags until the bag sweep puts them into the storage, except what the bot uses itself
  (bandages).

Seen on the `gaps` instance (five bots given a plan in the database): at login `learned 1 thing of Mining where it
stands (profession plan; skill 1 of 75)` for each planned profession and `got its tool for the profession plan:
Mining Pick`; after hand-ins `crafts for its profession at the hub: Murktest crafts 5 x Linen Bandage` (Server.log
`crafted 5 of 5`) and `Startwar crafts 1 x Rough Sharpening Stone`. T1 only: the detour to a node (none came within
40 yd of a planned gatherer in the runs; veins and herbs are pooled spawns), rank-ups at skill 50 and above.

Not in this package: fishing (K3), the profession mode as an order (K4), trainer visits at the real price (the
open question C1), recipes that are not a trainer's (drops, vendors), a campfire for Cooking.

### Live round 33: flights for every travel, a zone pick that holds (2026-11-12)

- **Four zone picks in sixteen seconds.** A level-22 warlock in the Wetlands picked the Hillsbrad Foothills, Redridge,
  Duskwood and Stonetalon one after another, each travel ending "route too dangerous" at once (to Redridge on foot
  it is 15 000 yd through the Searing Gorge). The picks were right to move on, but only the first travel had looked
  for a flight: the clock of the flight check was the bot's, not the task's, so the three travels within the same
  minute went on foot or not at all, and Redridge and Duskwood were written off as unreachable with a flight master
  550 yd away. Every task now looks for a flight at its first step; a flight whose flight master cannot be walked
  to is ruled out for that task only.
- **The pick holds on the way.** The zones were looked at again every minute wherever the bot was; on a long way the
  distances change, and a fight or a death could leave the bot where another zone scored better. Now the clock only
  runs in the target zone; a zone that cannot be reached, a refused walk or a level-up still ask for a new pick.
- **After a refused pull** ("a pull it cannot afford", the fight rules' check) the spawn the task was for is set
  aside for ten minutes with the pack's place: the pack may stand farther from the spawn than the place's reach, and
  the same spawn was offered again at once (37 such task ends in half an hour).

Not changed: the travel that led a level-22 character through water past level-25 creatures (travels are walked
past creatures up to eight levels above the bot when there is no other way: the place is set aside by the death).

### Live round 42: a bot that held, a travel begun ten times, a quest lost at sea (2026-11-13)

Round 42 on the integration server (22 minutes, the eight old bots read one by one): 13 hand-ins for them, and
three of them lost most of the window to the planner.

- **The zone pick counts what the planner would offer.** A level-23 mage stood in Duskwood for twenty minutes with
  "Nothing left to do": every hand-in, pickup and objective it had there was refused (the way past level-25
  creatures, a pull it could not afford) or left until level 24, and still the pick stayed. `CountEligibleQuests`
  counted quests whose giver or ender `PlanQuests` drops (a place that is set aside, a place among creatures the bot
  cannot take, `IsPlaceUsable`); it applies the same two rules now.
- **An idle bot looks at the zones within a minute.** On the autopilot, the second hold in a row ("Nothing left to
  do", 30 s each) makes the zone count as empty for a quarter of an hour and asks for a new pick; the pick stays only
  when no other zone has anything either. Line: `has had nothing to do in <zone> for 60 s ...: the zone counts as
  empty for 15 min, it looks at the zones again`.
- **A quest whose tasks end for what stands in their way waits.** When an objective or interaction ends with "a pack
  on its way", "a pull it cannot afford", "left a fight", "way too dangerous" or "kept away from a creature far above
  its level" and the quest's counters have not moved since the task began, that counts against the quest; the second
  such end in a row within ten minutes leaves the quest alone for a quarter of an hour (like a quest none of whose
  spots would do) and asks the autopilot to look at the zones. Progress in between clears the count. A level-23 rogue
  had begun the same two objectives seven times in eight minutes and died three times. Line: `leaves quest N "..."
  for a quarter of an hour: 2 of its tasks in a row ended without progress for what stood in their way`.
- **A travel begun again and again without getting nearer waits.** The travel to the ender of an errand, or into the
  target zone, that is begun a fourth time within ten minutes without the bot having got 150 yd nearer is given up:
  the hand-in is not tried for half an hour (`gives up the hand-in ...: its travel was begun 4 times without getting
  nearer`), the zone waits like one the bot found no way into (`began its travel to <zone> 4 times ...: the zone
  waits for 30 min`). A level-22 priest had begun one errand's travel ten times in four minutes, six of them within
  one, each ended by a pack on its way after eight to nineteen seconds.
- **The quest log never fills up to where NewRpg empties it.** mod-playerbots' NewRpg drops quests far below the bot
  and quests of other zones, finished ones included, as soon as fewer than two slots of the log are free and it looks
  at a quest giver. A level-25 shaman took four quests in passing in Stormwind and Ironforge on its errands, and the
  finished quest it was sailing to Theramore for was dropped on the way; it sailed back (twenty minutes). Two rules
  now: an AI-played character takes no quest while two or fewer slots are free (`QuestSupport::MayTake`, the veto of
  core patch CP-9; the planner itself picks up only with three free), and the quest log care (`CareForQuestLog`) runs
  with every step of the planner wherever the bot is, not only when its zone is planned; it never abandons the quest
  of the running task.
- **A far hand-in waits for the batch.** That quest was a single level-17 one whose ender stands on Bloodmyst
  Isle, two ships and a walk across Kalimdor away, begun straight after two hand-ins in Stormwind and Ironforge. A bot
  outside its zone (on its way there, or after an errand) still does every hand-in near; one whose trip costs more than
  4000 yd (a voyage counts 6000 a leg) is begun only when three wait, when the quest log runs short or when the zone
  has no quest work left (`PlanErrand`, `distant`). And no errand across the sea at all for a quest whose level is
  grey for the bot.
- **A flight for a walk that is short as the crow flies.** From inside Ironforge the dock of Menethil Harbor is
  1169 yd away and 9282 yd by road. `FindFlight` looked at the straight line (flights only from 1500 yd) and the
  shaman walked for six minutes until Loch Modan, where the line was long enough. A destination nearer than 1500 yd
  is measured by its walk now (`WalkLength`).

Round 43 added three small things. The place check (no hand-in or pickup where every creature around is above the
bot) does not apply to the walk to a vendor or a trainer: the bot buys and leaves (the innkeeper of Menethil Harbor
was refused to a level-25 shaman for the level-28 murlocs on the shore 90 yd from the inn). The ammunition line names
the price, what the guild paid and what is left of the buyer's allowance, like the gear lines. And the quest log care
gives up a quest the bot has progress on only when nothing else is left to give up (finished quests and the quest of
the running task are never given up; an abandoned quest is not blocked and is taken again like any other when the bot
passes its giver with room in the log; the line names the quest).

Round 44 (a level-24 rogue died four times in Redridge in twenty minutes, each time back at the same camps): **a
death rests the quest at once.** A death during an objective, an interaction or an event of a quest leaves that quest
alone until the next level or for 30 minutes (it took three deaths before); the third such rest of a quest counts as
a failure (abandoned, taken again once). And **two deaths in one zone within a quarter of an hour** make that zone
count as empty for 15 minutes on the autopilot, so the zones are looked at again. Lines: `leaves quest N "..." until
level L or for 30 min: it died on it`, `died twice in <zone> within N min: the zone counts as empty for 15 min, it
looks at the zones again`.

Also from round 44: **no objective at a quest area beside or behind a place that is set aside** (the quest area
is wide and its middle is only a point: a set-aside place within 70 yd of the middle counts, and one the straight way
there leads through), and **no walk whose route leads through a set-aside place** when the route finds no way around
it (the target waits: `does not walk to <target>: the way (...) leads through a place it has set aside`). The rogue
was sent to "the quest area" of a mill four times between its deaths at the camp beside it, and its hand-in route
to Lakeshire led through that camp.

Round 45 (the nine old bots made 12 hand-ins in 22 minutes; a warlock and a priest hardly fought and spent the
window on ways that led to nothing):

- **A single hand-in only when it is close.** Outside its zone or after an errand a bot does the hand-ins whose trip
  costs at most 2500 yd (was 4000), and a single one only up to 1000 yd; with nothing left in its zone a single one
  up to 1500 yd. More wait for the batch of three or for a full quest log. The priest had walked 2,314 yd to one
  hand-in and back, eleven minutes.
- **A hand-in the visit does not make.** A warlock stood at Gakin the Darkbinder in the Slaughtered Lamb for 110 s
  ("distance 0.0, reached no") and the hand-in was given up. Two things: an NPC more than 2.5 yd above or below the
  bot (a cellar, an upper room) is walked to by the planner itself (the path finder's way to where the NPC stands;
  that walk gets up to 90 s before the task's own clock runs), and nothing is bought through a floor. And a bot that
  has stood at the ender of its finished quest for ten seconds, on its floor and in its sight, hands the quest in
  itself, as it serves itself at a vendor (`OrderService::HandInAt`, the reward playerbots rates best): `hands in
  quest N "..." at <ender> itself (the visit had not done it after N s)`.
- **A spot whose pull was refused is not the next plan's choice.** When an objective ends for what stood in its way,
  its spawn is set aside for a quarter of an hour, so the next plan takes another spot or another quest (the quest
  itself waits after the second such end, above).
- Not changed here: the trip to a vendor for drink ("out of drink", 1,230 yd) is the rest and provisions rule
  `Provisions.TripWhenOut`; the walk of 1,347 yd to a spot whose pull is then refused cannot be judged from afar (the
  pull check looks at the creatures that stand there at that moment).

Round 46 (old bots: 7 hand-ins in 24 minutes): three of them spent eleven minutes each on a ship. **A flight is
judged against the road, not the line.** From Raven Hill to Redridge it is 2961 yd as the crow flies and 8559 yd by
road; the flight was turned down because its walks (to the flight master and from the landing) were more than half
of the 2961 yd, the road was then refused for a pack on it, the next zone likewise, and the pick fell on a zone
across the sea, whose quests were not counted from afar then (round 48 below). `FindFlight` now compares the walks with the length of the
road (`WalkLength`), and takes the flight when there is no way on foot at all.

Round 47: **an interaction that stands still ends.** A warlock stood at a used-up Lumber Pile for more than six
minutes ("task interact (368 s)", moved 0 yd). When the bot of an interaction task has not moved 15 yd for four
minutes and its quest has not got anywhere in that time, the task ends, its spot is set aside for a quarter of an
hour and the end counts against the quest (`CheckStranded`): `has stood for N s at <target> without quest N getting
anywhere: the interaction ends`.

Round 48 (the old bots' best window for experience, and their worst for ships: twelve voyages, four bots on ships for
25 of 27 minutes; Wartank sailed Menethil > Theramore > Menethil > Theramore > Menethil in nine minutes). **A zone
across the sea is counted, not assumed, and a crossing needs a reason.** Three things made the ping-pong:

- *Zones across the sea were taken for "three quests" unseen* (`ChooseZone`: "across the sea the bot checks when it
  gets there"). A bot whose zone had nothing it could safely get to picked one over there, arrived, counted nothing
  it could do, and picked the zone it had come from, which was unseen again by then. Now `CountEligibleQuests(...,
  afar)` counts them from where the bot stands: the quests it could take from a giver that stands in the zone at a
  place it could use (`SpawnInZone`, the same place and set-aside checks as at home), and the hand-ins its log holds
  for the zone.
- *No order of preference between the two sides.* Now the bot's own side comes first whatever a zone across the sea
  counts (first the zones it is well into, then the ones it has just grown into); a zone across the sea is chosen
  only when none on its side has three quests, and then only with eight (`MinQuestsToCross`; five until round 51).
  When nothing has enough, the bot stays where it is and grinds near it (round 51, below); only a bot that found
  nothing at all to do there moves for fewer. A bot that has gone ashore from a ship or zeppelin does not sail again within an hour
  (`BotRuntime::lastCrossingAt`; the pick line says "it went ashore less than an hour ago and stays on this side"),
  and a zone it left because nothing in it could be got to safely waits 45 minutes (`ZoneRestMs`). The pick line of
  a crossing ends ", across the sea (no zone on its side has enough for it)".
- *No flight from the port.* A level-26 bot that went ashore in Booty Bay was sent to Duskwood on foot ("the safest
  way passes level-65 creatures"), although the flight master stood a hundred yards from the pier: `NearestService`
  leaves out services in a zone that begins more than two levels above the bot, and Stranglethorn Vale begins at 30
  (Theramore in Dustwallow Marsh likewise). The flight master within 400 yd of the bot is exempt now
  (`PortFlightYards`): it is the way on, not a trip into the zone.

Round 50: **the straight walk to an objective is looked at for a group on it.** A level-17 warrior walked 211 yd to
its Defias Pillagers through the Riverpaw camp of Westfall (four gnolls at one fire, two more a few yards on), was
attacked at 65 % health, two gnolls became four, and it died; the same camp had killed others in earlier rounds. The
group check ("N creatures stand together on the way", the risk model's answer whether this bot can take that many)
existed for routes and for walks to NPCs; a walk to an objective's spot under the routes' distance (350 yd) is
NewRpg's and had none. Now it is looked at once when the walk begins (`BotTask::crowdChecked`): the straight line from
40 yd after the bot (the group it stands beside is behind it) to 45 yd before the spot (what stands at the spot is
the pull's matter); with a group of three or more it cannot take on it the spot is left alone for the walk gate's half
hour and the planner takes another spawn or objective: `does not walk to Defias Pillager (objective, quest 13 ...):
5 level-17 creatures stand together on the straight way of 253 yd (it is level 18); left alone for 30 min`.

Round 51: **why bots of level 24 to 27 found no zone on their continent.** Their picks counted six to eleven quests
in Duskwood, Redridge or the Wetlands and none a few minutes after they got there; then they sailed to Kalimdor
(twelve minutes on a ship for six quests in one case). Read on the live log and measured on the `gaps` instance with
`.ga admin route` for every quest NPC of a zone from its town: from Menethil Harbor at level 24 the walk gate refused
14 of 23 ("the way passes level-26 creatures"), which is every NPC outside the harbour; from Darkshire 13 of 27. Each
refusal sets its target aside for half an hour, so the zone was empty by the planner's count after one pass. Neither
the grey rule nor quest chains had a part in it.
- *The danger map was twice as wide as the server's creatures reach.* A creature counted in full within 25 yd of a way
  and with a falloff out to 45 yd. The owner's server runs `Rate.Creature.Aggro = 0.5`: a standing creature of the
  walker's level attacks from 10 yd. A way of 2000 yd through a zone of ten levels always has something two levels
  up within 25 yd. Now every creature has its own reach (`RoadMap::Hostile::reach`: the core's aggro range at the
  server's rate, half of what the creature wanders, 4 yd of slack), and a group on a way counts when one of it would
  attack someone on the way. The margin (`Walks.MaxLevelsAbove`, one level) is as it was. Measured again: Wetlands at
  24: 6 of 23 refused (the level-29 end at Dun Modr and three NPCs of other zones); Duskwood at 24: 2 of 27.
- *An errand across the sea was followed by the voyage back.* A hunter in the Barrens with Ashenvale as its zone
  sailed to Menethil for two hand-ins (255 s) and straight back (266 s). After a voyage that leaves the bot's zone
  across the sea, the autopilot looks at the zones again from where it stands (`went ashore across the sea from its
  zone ...: it looks at the zones on this side`), and no errand crosses the sea within the hour after a landing
  (`BotRuntime::CrossedLately`). The clock is in memory and does not survive a restart.
- *A journey for one or two quests.* When no zone had three quests the zone with the most was taken: a level-27 bot
  rode 6700 yd for two quests after three zone changes in a quarter of an hour, and travels and voyages were a fifth
  of the old characters' time in round 50. Now such a bot stays where it is and grinds near it, as the owner had set
  ([quote left out]); only when it found nothing
  at all to do there (no quest, nothing to grind: the zone counts as empty) does it move for fewer than three.
- A crossing needs eight quests over there (five before).

What is left of the cause is not the planner's: "every spot of it near is too much for it" (about ninety lines a
round) is the risk model's verdict on camp quests for a lone character; squads are the built answer.

*The margin is two levels since the round after* (`Walks.MaxLevelsAbove`, default 2, was 1; the maintainers' ruling
of 2026-11-13, the owner can overrule it). With the narrower danger map the refusals that were left in rounds 53 and 54
were gaps of two to four levels, and 13 of 32 were exactly two (a level-26 hunter's six walks in Ashenvale past
level-28 creatures, a hand-in at Abercrombie). Two levels is the escape rule's line: a bot leaves a fight against a foe
three levels above it and fights a single one two above, so the gate now refuses what the bot would have to run
from. Routes still go around such creatures where they can (the cost factors are as they were).

*A pair counts two levels higher* (the commit after). The first test run with the margin of two: a level-25
character's errand led past a level-27 and a level-26 gnoll that stand together; both came and it died on the run.
The group gate counts from three. On the danger map a creature with another hostile one within 12 yd (the core's
assistance reaches 10) now counts two levels higher (`RoadMap::Hostile::paired`), for the gate and for the cost of
routes: a single creature up to two levels above the walker is passed, a pair above its own level is not. The gate's
log line says so ("a pair counts two levels higher"), since the level it names can be the pair's. Measured like
before, at the margin of two: Wetlands from Menethil at 24: 6 of 23 refused for danger and 2 for a group (the ways are
a tenth longer: routes go around pairs); Duskwood at 24: 2 of 27; Redridge at 22: 1 of 13. (Since 2026-11-14 a pair is
judged by the risk model instead of the bump: "Two creatures that stand together: the risk model's verdict".)

Round 52: **a character stood inside the Exodar for three quarters of an hour.** Palatwo (19) stood 59 yd beside and
141 yd below the flight master outside, with eight hand-ins waiting on Bloodmyst Isle. A short walk that has no
whole path gets a route of the road map (the rule made for the flight master on Stormwind's wall), and the rule
"the last stretch is a plain walk" threw that route away in the tick it was planned in, so the bot was sent along
the straight line the ground guard refuses, again and again. The route of such a walk is kept now. And a route
point on another level does not count as passed (`PassHeight`, 25 yd): a way out of a building passes above or
below itself. Also after a landing: the autopilot looks at the zones again only after an *errand's* voyage (the
first leg of a journey over two seas ends ashore too), and the errand a crossing was for may take its second leg
(`BotRuntime::errandCrossing`).

Also round 52: **a hand-in waits for its way to clear.** When a pack the bot cannot take, or a creature far above it,
stands on the way and there is no way around (`Escape::Result::ClearOfPack` / `Clear`), a task ends and its target is
set aside for a quarter of an hour the second time. For the hand-in of a finished quest that threw away the most
valuable walk a bot has: a level-26 mage's only hand-in was set aside after two tries 14 s apart (two raptors beside
the path to the ender), and it spent the next minutes at spawns without a target. A hand-in now waits 25 s where the
bot stands and tries again, four times before its ender is set aside, and then for five minutes: why line "Waiting
for the way to its hand-in to clear".

Round 54: **the planner does not pick a spawn that is down.** A third of the objective tasks of an hour ended "no
target at this spawn", often in runs 13 s apart. A diagnostic line (kept under `GuildAdventure.Debug`: `found no <target>
at spawn N of quest Q: <what the map knows>`) showed two kinds: places of a spawn pool that is not in use (the rare
Squiddic of Lake Everstill is an item source of "Selling Fish" and has five places: five visits in a row, "not on the
map"), and the bot's own kill ("creature dead ..., respawn in 314 s") followed by twelve seconds of standing. The
planner now asks the map (`IsSpawnDown`): a spawn whose creature is dead or whose object is taken, and stays so
longer than the bot needs to get there, is not chosen; neither is a spawn that has no object at all in a loaded
grid. `Risk::SaferSpot` gets the spawns that are up (`WithoutDown`). A normal creature's respawn time is not in the
map's list (the core saves it there for elites and dungeon creatures only): the creature's own object is asked. And
at a spawn the map says is down the task moves on after 3 s instead of 12.

Round 55: **a travel looks for a flight when it begins.** A level-28 bot's travel from Duskwood to the Wetlands went
straight to a route of 21 557 yd on foot through the Burning Steppes, was refused for what lives on it, and the zone
was set aside for three quarters of an hour; a level-34 bot in Desolace was refused its way to the Thousand Needles
the same way and took a ship of ten minutes to Stranglethorn. The look for a flight was throttled to once a minute
by a clock of the bot, not of the task: a travel that began within a minute of an earlier look never looked. Each
travel now looks when it begins (`BotTask::flightTried`). And when a way is refused the line says why no flight was
taken (`FindFlight` names its reason: "; no flight: the walk from the landing passes creatures far above it", "no
money for the flight", ...), which the log could not tell before.

Also from the binlog (the behaviour work's find): **a bot gives away only the quest items it can spare.** `QuestSupply`
worked out what a donor could spare and then put its whole stack into the storage ("Wardps puts 9 x Goretusk Liver
into the guild storage: Dotlock needs it", and 19 s later "Wardps took 2 x Goretusk Liver ... for quest 22"). Now it
moves the spare amount, and no more than the asker still lacks.

Checked and not changed: the "Dwarven Fishing Pole" in the rogue's ranged slot is item 3567, which is a gun in the
game's data (the reward of a quest); the fishing task holds its pole (item 6256) in the main hand only while it
fishes and puts the weapon back (`RestoreWeapon`), and no bot of the guild had a pole in a weapon slot. Open: targets
that can only be reached through a camp (the walk gate judges levels, not packs of the bot's own level; the
behaviour work's walk around packs comes with round 44).

Round 59: **the way to a ship is judged like a travel's, and the hearthstone is a way out.** A level-22 shaman in the
east of Ashenvale picked Duskwood, across the sea, and set out for the ship in Ratchet on foot: `takes the route ... >
Ship (The Maidens Fancy) (14053 yd, 3205 yd straight; strongest hostile creatures on it level 31)`. It died in the
Warsong lumber camp to four level-27 to 29 creatures, set out again along the Southfury (a way past the Horde's rampart,
level-77 guards) and died on the run from a level-29 lurker. The walk to a dock had no danger check at all; a travel's
had one, with a margin of eight levels from the days when the danger map counted creatures 25 yd from the way.
- The walk to a dock is judged like a travel's (`StepVoyage`, `VoyagePhase::ToDock`): past a group the bot cannot take,
  or past creatures more than `RouteMaxDanger` levels above it, it does not go: `does not walk to the dock in The
  Barrens for The Maiden's Fancy: the safest way (..., 15479 yd) passes level-29 creatures (it is level 23); no flight:
  no flight master it can walk to`. The zone across the sea waits half an hour (an errand's voyage is dropped).
- `RouteMaxDanger` is 5 (was 8), for travels and dock walks: since the danger map counts what would really attack
  (round 51), a creature six levels above the walker on its way is a fight it loses and a run it seldom survives.
- **The hearthstone** (`OrderService::HearthHome`): when a travel or a dock walk is refused for what stands on it (no
  flight was to be had either), the character uses its hearthstone if it has one, it is ready and its inn is more than
  1500 yd away, and plans again from the inn: `uses its hearthstone (no safe way to the ship from where it stood): from
  (2422, -2954) map 1 to its inn at (-6240, 331) map 0`, and from there `starts travel (target Duskwood, 4100 yd) in Dun
  Morogh` over the flight master. With the stone on cooldown the bot stays: on the autopilot it looks at the zones
  again and, with none in reach, grinds what it can take near it (seen on the test instance: a level-23 mage among
  level-20 to 22 slimes and stalkers for ten minutes, no death).
- **Grey quests are not taken.** The same shaman carried an item that starts a quest (Tzerak's Armor Plate, "Signs of
  the Legion", level 14): the quest was taken from the item and abandoned as grey 59 times in an hour. An AI-played
  character with `Quests.AbandonGrey` on no longer takes a quest that is grey for it (`QuestSupport::MayTake`, the
  CP-9 veto). The item stays in its bags.

Also round 59, from the test instance: **a hunting ground far away is a journey first, and a skin hunt goes where many
beasts stand.** A hunt for skins or for a material 2000 yd away was started as a grind task, whose walk is made for the
next spawn: a hunter stood six minutes at the Thandol Span. A ground farther than 300 yd (`HuntGroundNear`) is now
walked to as a travel task of the profession mode (routes, the walk gate, own steps), and the hunt is planned when the
bot is there. `PlanSkinHunt` no longer takes the nearest beast it can skin but, like `FindHuntGround`, the place with
the most skins to learn from within 80 yd for its way: a beast counts by the chance of a skill point its skin gives
(all of it while the skill is within 25 points of what its level asks, three quarters up to 50, a quarter beyond).

Round 61: **a place to stand still at is a quiet place; herbs are not hunted from creatures.** A level-27 priest in the
profession mode walked to a campfire on Westfall's coast to cook and was overrun there (four, then eight murlocs in
forty seconds). The place had passed the risk verdict: that verdict leaves out creatures ten levels and more below a
character, and the coast's murlocs are level 12 to 15. For a fight that is right; a bot that stands at a fire for
minutes gets them all.
- `WorldIndex::CountHostileSpawns` counts the spawns of creatures hostile to the character within a radius, whatever
  their level. `PlanFocusTrip` (a fire, a forge, an anvil) takes a place with none within 45 yd first (a town's forge,
  an inn's fire), then one with two at most, never one in a camp; on the test instance the cook that had used the
  coast's campfire (84 yd) now walked to one 756 yd away and to a "Cozy Fire". The water a bot fishes at
  (`Fishing::IsQuietWater`: the stand next to it, a school of fish, the water by an inn) may have one such spawn
  within 45 yd: `does not fish at (..): hostile creatures live at that water`.
- The profession mode hunted "Defias Drone for 20 x Briarthorn": the world database has a 21 % Briarthorn row on that
  creature (four spawns). What a gathering profession brings (herbs, ore and stone, leather), what disenchanting
  gives and gems are no hunt materials (`WorldIndex::IsHuntMaterial`): they are gathered, or wait for the storage.
  Cloth, meat and the like are hunted as before.

Round 62: **nobody fishes from the saddle; a node round does not walk to a place the map knows to be empty.**
- Every cast of a bot of level 20 and more failed: it rides to the water, and the cast answers "not while mounted"
  (`cannot cast its line at (..) (spell 7731, cast result 64, pole in hand yes)`, then `ends fish: cannot fish here`
  and the next water). `StepFishing` gets the angler off its mount, and out of an animal form, before the cast. The
  first fishing tests had used characters below level 20 and one that happened to stand.
  An enchanter that enchants its own gear for skill (`Professions::StepEnchanting`) gets off its mount the same way
  (`cannot cast Enchant Bracer - Minor Health on its Brocade Bracers (result 64)`).
- In the profession mode two miners walked to 106 places of veins in twenty minutes and found a vein at 20: the
  places of a node pool are many, and few hold a node at a time. `PlanGatherRound` leaves out a place whose node is not
  there where the map can tell (`IsSpawnDown`, the grids around the bot, 400 yd); farther away it still has to go and
  look.

Round 63: **the inn of a hub becomes a bot's home.** The first hearthstone of the live server (round 59's way out) took
a level-23 paladin from the south of Darkshore to Azuremyst Isle: a bot's home was still the inn it started at. An
AI-played character now makes the inn of a hub its home when it hands a quest in there (`BindAtHubInn`: a friendly
innkeeper within 120 yd, and its home is on another map or more than 1500 yd from that inn), as a player does on the
way up: `makes the inn of Innkeeper Trelayne in Duskwood its home: its hearthstone leads there now`. The hearthstone
of `HearthHome` and of the rescue then leads into the country the bot levels in.

Round 64: **a recipe on its cooldown is not "crafted"; a node round does not plan a vein behind creatures the walk gate
refuses.**
- A scribe in the profession mode announced `crafts 8 x Minor Inscription Research` fourteen times in twenty minutes:
  the research has a cooldown of twenty hours, the first cast of a batch failed, the batch ended, and the next look
  picked it again (it was the cheapest skill point by its materials). Each time the bot walked to a fire in between
  (another profession's recipe), started the research there and left for a herb. `CraftForSkill` leaves out a recipe

  (the crowd check's answer, `Risk::CanFight`) `FindRoute` leaves such a node out, as a start, as an end and on the
  way, and makes a link through such a camp cost twenty times its length, like a link past a group it cannot take;
  the walks off the graph, to the first node and from the last one, are asked with `Risk::LegEntersCamp`. A route
  that still leads through a camp says so (`RoadRoute::camp`, in the fields of the group on the way), and every gate
  that refuses a route for a group refuses it for the camp: `does not walk to ..: 22 level-22 creatures have their
  camp on the way`. Not the camp the walker stands in (it has to get out: within the start stretch), nor one the
  destination lies in (whoever goes there judged the place).
- The straight walk of a task without a route (a pickup, a hand-in, a vendor under the roads' distance) is asked with
  `Risk::EntersCamp` from 10 yd after the bot to 45 yd before the spot, and refused the same way.
- The nearest road node for a rescue, a rest's quiet place or a retreat is not one in the middle of a camp that holds
  for the bot's level either.
- *Roamers.* A journey (a travel to a zone, an errand's or a journey's travel, the walk of a voyage) looks every three
  seconds at the next 300 yd of its way (`OrderService::StepRoamerWait`): while a strong creature on its walk is on
  it (`Escape::RoamerOnLeg`: Stitches on the road to Darkshire) the bot waits where it stands, twenty seconds at a
  time, and goes on when the way is clear: `waits with its travel to ..: Stitches (level 35 elite) is on its way`.
  The same when the escape code has just kept it away from such a creature: the journey waits instead of ending.
  Four minutes of waiting per journey at most; then it ends as before. The stuck clocks stand still meanwhile.
  *Why:* a level-30 druid's travels out of Darkshire ended after 3 to 19 s each while Stitches walked the road ("kept
  away from a creature far above its level"), were begun again at once, two zones were written off within a minute
  ("began its travel .. 4 times .. without getting nearer") and it set out across the sea; its voyage's walk then
  ended "stuck" after 193 s of going around and keeping away.
- *What it does not do.* A walker that can take the camp (a level-36 warrior with good gear at the Shadowforge dig)
  still gets the route through it. A bot that cannot has no other link from Loch Modan into the Badlands: its way
  there is 4660 yd over the Searing Gorge past level-45 groups, which the gate refuses.

Round 80, **sea crossings back and forth; the library of Stormwind's keep.**
- *What the live log said.* A level-28 hunter crossed the sea again and again: Menethil to Theramore, by flight to
  Ashenvale and at once an errand to Stormwind (The Bravery from Auberdine) for "An Old History Book" at Milton
  Sheaf, whose hand-in ended `no way on the ground`, back to Darkshore, and seventeen minutes later the same errand

  seconds before each time it set out (23:19:46, 23:45:17, 00:47).
- *Waits survive a restart* (`ga_bot_wait`, `OrderService::LoadBotWaits / RestoreBotWaits / SaveBotWaits`): the hour
  a bot stays on its side of the sea after it went ashore (with the errand that crossing was for), the zones that
  wait for it (no way in, deaths) and the hand-ins outside its zone it gave up are written when they change (looked
  at every ten seconds) and restored when the character enters the world: `still waits with 3 things from before it
  entered the world: it went ashore 16 min ago and stays on its side of the sea, 1 zone waits, 1 hand-in given up`.
- *The ender of an errand with no way on the ground is left by the guild at once* (`NoteNpcUnreached(.., journey)`): a
  hand-in the bot travelled for and whose last steps the ground guard cancels counts as the three failures that block
  a quest NPC for the guild for a day (`ga_guild_npc_block`, which is read back after a restart): `could not get to
  Milton Sheaf .. after a journey for it, and the ground has no way there ..: they all leave it alone for 24 h`.
- *A refused way to a ship closes the sea from there* (`BotRuntime::CloseSea / SeaClosed`): for a quarter of an hour
  and within 400 yd of where the way to the pier was refused the zone pick does not look across the sea and no errand
  crosses it (three zones over there were picked and their voyages refused within ten seconds: every one led over
  the same pier).
- *After a hearth the zone that was just refused keeps waiting* (ten minutes; the other waits are dropped as before:
  from the inn the ways are other ways). A level-35 druid flew from Booty Bay to Thelsamar for the Badlands, was
  refused at the pass, hearthed back, picked the Badlands again six seconds later and flew to Thelsamar again.
- *The library.* Probed with the core's path finder (`.ga admin path`): its ground has two pieces in the keep, the hall
  with the throne room and the library's wing, and they do not connect, for a bot's filter and for a walking

  from one to the other is where the corridor to the library leaves the entrance ramp, found in a guard's patrol
  (`waypoint_data` 105280): the hall's ground ends at (-8471.8, 413.0, 111.6), the wing's begins at (-8469.3, 413.0,
  112.0), 2.5 yd on. A search for such gaps by the path finder alone was built and taken out again: nothing told the
  doorway from the wall.
- *Hand-listed crossings* (world table `ga_path_bridge`, `OrderService::LoadPathBridges / BridgeGap`): two points,
  one on each piece of ground, at most 15 yd apart. When the path of the planner's own step ends short of its target
  and a crossing within 400 yd fits (the bot's ground reaches the one point, the target is reached from the other),
  the own steps lead to the first point and straight to the second (`takes the crossing "Stormwind Keep: the corridor
  to the Royal Library" ..`, `steps across the gap in the path finder's ground, from .. to ..`; the ground guard lets
  that one step through). Three crossings per task at most. A pickup, a hand-in, a vendor or a trainer whose walk the
  ground guard cancelled three times goes over to own steps once before it is given up. One row so far; a new one
  needs two positions read at the place (a patrol's waypoints, or `.gps` in the client).

Round 82, **a bot drowned on its way up for air.**
- *What the live log said.* A level-31 warrior whose Skinning was behind hunted Loch Frenzies for their skins, 15 yd
  under the Loch. `comes up for air at (-4885, -3216, 283) .. after 71 s under water (15 yd deep)` came three times,
  88 s apart, each time at the same point, and then it drowned ("under water for 28 s, not in a fight").
- *Why.* The step up was a point movement the planner started once; the bot's own AI, hunting for its next target,
  replaced it at once. `CheckBreath` gave the way up 45 s, then took the dive for over and started its clock anew,
  while the breath the game gives ran on.
- *The fix* (`OrderService::CheckBreath`): on the way up the bot's AI is held (`BotDriver::PauseAI`) and the step up
  is set again whenever the bot has not risen since the last look; the dive's clock starts anew only at the surface;
  a bot that is still under water when its 45 s are over is brought to the surface (`did not get to the surface in
  45 s ..: it is brought up`; not in a fight) and takes its breaths there.
- The skin hunt of the gathering catch-up leaves beasts that live under water alone (`LivesUnderWater`: the creature
  only swims, or its spawn lies more than 3 yd under the surface).
- *Open.* A farm order's hunting ground and a grind spot may still lie under water (the bot then dives 70 s at a time
  and comes up between); whether such grounds should be taken at all is the farm order's and the grind's question.

Round 83, **the pier of Theramore again; a straight way where the road map goes far around.**
- *The pier.* `does not walk to the dock in Dustwallow Marsh for The Lady Mehley: the safest way (Theramore Isle
  flightMaster > Ship (The Lady Mehley), 300 yd) passes level-47 creatures`, for every bot below about 45, and a

  (`Node::transport`), the points of a link to it count as on the deck (3 yd above the sea at least), and so does

- *No zone to go to.* A bot on the autopilot with no zone it can get to goes home by hearthstone when its inn is

- *A hearth to another continent is a crossing*: the bot stays on that side for the hour, as after a voyage.
- *The straight way.* From Nijel's Point in Desolace the Kolkar village, the zone's first quest, lies 870 yd down the

  hop along the straight line (`OrderService::ChainReaches`: 180 yd at a time, each hop from where the last one
  ended); when every hop has a way and the whole is at most 1.6 times the straight line, the task walks without the

  map's (..) is 3721 yd`), and the walk gate judges the straight line as it does for a short walk.

What is the planner's in that, and fixed here:
- *Taken, abandoned, taken again.* With exactly three free slots in the quest log a quest was taken (two free), the
  log care dropped a quest it had no task for (three free), the giver beside the bot handed that one out again, and
  so on. A quest the care drops is not taken again by that character for three hours (`QuestSupport::NoteDropped /
  WasDropped`, asked by the quest veto and by the planner's pickups; kept across a restart as wait kind 4).
- *A walker at a camp's edge.* The camp rules exempt the camp the walker stands in, and "in" meant the camp's
  middle. A character at its edge (a camp on a shore, the outer tents) is at that camp too: within 35 yd of such a
  middle the way out is not refused for it (`FindRoute`'s own camp, `OrderService::StandsAtCamp` for the straight walk).
- *The straight way asks the gate first.* A straight way the path finder has (round 83) is only taken when the walk
  gate lets the straight line through: what lives on it, a group on it, a camp.
- *A bot with no zone to go to gets out.* After three minutes of `No zone for level N is reachable` what the bot
  waits with is dropped (the zones it found no way into, the hour on its side of the sea, the pier it was refused
  at), it goes home by hearthstone from anywhere but its inn, and is put back on a road when none is in its reach.
  A level-31 bot stood on a pier of Theramore for half an hour: its ways inland were refused, and the landing hour
  forbade the ship back.
- *The onward way from a landing* (`OrderService::ReachableFromLanding`): a zone across the sea is only a candidate
  when the bot can go on from the landing: the landing lies in the zone, the road map's way from it to the zone's hub
  is one a travel may take, or a flight master stands within 600 yd of the landing and another at the zone (in it, or
  within 1500 yd of its hub) with such a way on. Thousand Needles from Theramore is none of that for a level-31 bot.

Not the planner's, passed on: fights and rests of the squad (the shaman's drink), pulls at camps, the two item quests
of Dustwallow, "The Grimtotem Weapon".

Round 86, **Booty Bay and Theramore's pier again.** The window itself was a good one (no death in its first 24
minutes, two in the hour, no stuck bot; the old nine handed in 16 quests where they had six). What stood out:

- *A civilian is no hostile creature.* Eight of eight bots looked at have their inn in Booty Bay, and 15 yd from
  that inn, a floor up, stands Gringer, the Horde's flight master: level 65, a civilian, who attacks nobody. A bot

  254 yd out`, five walks north refused with no flight in their place, `no flight: no flight master it can walk to`,
  and the bot stood for half an hour. The count of hostile creatures around a bot (`LiveHostiles`, FightEscape.cpp)
  leaves civilians out now, as the look-out for strong creatures has since round 65.
- *Why no flight.* A walk of a task that is refused says why no flight took its place: `..; left alone for 30 min;
  no flight: the walk from the landing passes creatures far above it` (travels said so already).
- *An objective at "the quest area" is flown to.* Such an objective has no spawn as its spot (none of its targets
  is in the planner's reach) but the quest's own point on the map, and a journey by flight wanted a spot: from

  quest area (objective, quest 575 "Supply and Demand") by flight: .. the flight from Gyll lands 298 yd from it`.
- *No flight to a landing behind a camp.* The walk on from a landing is judged as the travel judges it once the
  bot stands there, the camps on it included (a level-38 hunter flew to the Rebel Camp for crocolisks 1246 yd on and
  was refused there: `7 level-37 creatures have their camp on the safest way`).
- *A road far around.* `finds no route for 2256 yd to (-6193, -3961) and walks straight`: from Theramore's pier to
  the Shimmering Flats the road is 30702 yd, around the mountains and through the Barrens; a route more than twelve
  times its straight line is thrown away, and the straight walk in its place led to the end of the pier and into the

  the path finder has a straight way, hop by hop (`ChainReaches`): `has no way worth walking to (..): the road (..)
  is 30509 yd for 2267 yd straight, and the path finder has no straight way`; its zone waits, an errand is dropped.
- *What swims under a pier, on the walks off the graph.* The walk from the bot to a route's first node and from

  swims counted: under the planks of Theramore's pier the Coral Sharks, level 46. From the pier's west end every

  their own height now (the line between the heights of its two ends: in the water or not), with flat distances as

Seen and left: Drywhisker Gorge in Arathi has one link in the road map, through Hammerfall (21 level-50 guardians);

Round 88, **towns of the other side are closed ground.** Two bots died to town guards within ten minutes, and both
had been put there by the rescue: `is cut off from every road at (-503, 2862, -65) .. it is put back on the ground at
Shadowprey Village innkeeper`, dead 28 s later (19 guardians of level 65); `stands off the walkable ground .. it is
put back on the ground at Hammerfall flightMaster`, dead 57 s later (21 of level 50). The road map's nodes include
the other side's inns and flight masters; those NPCs are civilians, which the danger map leaves out, and no guard
stood within reach of the node itself.

A town of the other side is found from the world's data (`RoadMap::InHostileTown`): creatures with a service or the
guard flag whose faction is hostile to this team and not to the other are its people; where three or more of them
stand within 70 yd of one another, the ground 60 yd around each is closed. (The guard flag alone would not do: the
grunts of Grom'gol, Stonard and Kargath, the Splintertree and Horde Guards do not carry it. The lone flight master
of the other side in a neutral town makes no town: Booty Bay, Gadgetzan, Ratchet, Everlook stay open.) The startup
log names the road nodes this closes for each side (287 for the Alliance, 249 for the Horde).

On closed ground the danger map answers `RoadMap::TownDanger` (250) at every height, and "a hostile creature stands
on the node" holds for every node there. So the rules that were there keep out, whatever the bot's level: the
rescue, the retreat and the quiet place take no such node; routes cost sixty times their length through one and are
refused by the walk gate, the travel and the dock walk (`.. passes a town of the other side`, `takes the route ..
(it leads through a town of the other side)`); a flight is not taken to a landing whose walk on crosses one; a vendor
behind one is no choice. A bot that stands in such a town may walk out (the gate's rule for a walker among such
creatures). The kinds of task without a walk gate of their own (a grind spot, the water to fish at, the inn of
`IDLE`, a retreat) are stopped in `WalkTo`: `does not walk to (..) (grind): the way (..) leads through a town of the
other side`, and the task ends as one without a way.

Round 89, **a bot with nothing to do looks for a way out** (the owner, 2026-11-14: [quote left out]). A level-45 warrior flew to Thorium Point for the Searing Gorge's four quests. Two were `left
until level 46: every spot of it near is too much` (its weapon is of item level 37), the third ended twice `kept away
from a creature far above its level` (a level-50 rare in the pit below), its grind spots ended the same way, the walk
out of the gorge was refused (`8 level-48 creatures have their camp on the safest way`), and `no flight: no flight
master it can walk to`, 210 yd from Thorium Point's flight master: the places it had kept away from minutes before

cooldown left. It stood nine minutes in the hold `Nothing left to do in Searing Gorge at level 45`.

- *The flight master next to the bot is its way out* (`FindFlight`): when the rules for a place to go to give none,
  the friendly flight master within 400 yd is taken if the path finder has a walk there, past nothing more than five
  levels above the bot and through no town of the other side, whatever is set aside around it. Set-aside places are
  about where to work, not about how to leave.
- *The hold looks for a way out.* Every two minutes of `Nothing left to do in ..` on the autopilot: home by hearthstone
  from anywhere but the inn (`uses its hearthstone (nothing it can do in Searing Gorge for 2 min)`); without it, what
  the bot waits with is dropped (the zones it found no way into, the pier it was refused at), the zones are looked at
  again, and it is put back on a road when none is in its reach. With nothing to do, any gap of a gathering skill is

  level-34 mage stood south of the Venture Co. camp in Stranglethorn (level 36) for more than an hour: every route

  hearthstone (its ways from here were refused 8 times in 1 min)`; `LeaveBoxedPlace`); with the stone on cooldown a
  line says when it is ready (`is boxed in at ..: .. its hearthstone is ready in N min`). Not for a squad member, on a

- *The source that has the item* (the owner, 2026-11-14, on his leader in Dustwallow Marsh: [quote left out]). The quest was "Catch a Dragon by the Tail": its Wyrmtails
  lie on the ground of the Wyrmbog (71 objects, 100 %), and the world data also lists them as loot of the Searing
  Whelps and Drywallow Daggermaws there, at 1 %. The source index kept no chance, the planner took the nearest
  source, and the leader killed 25 whelps and crocolisks in nine minutes for nothing; with more creature spawns than

  index keeps each source's chance (`WorldIndex::GetItemSourceChance`: the loot row's percent; a share of its group
  or reference where the row has none), and `GetItemSources` leaves out a source that has the item less than a
  fifth as often as the best one; the startup log counts the items this thins. With only the objects left the
  objective is an interaction that opens them.
- *Kills that bring nothing.* An item objective worked at creatures counts its fights since the last piece
  (`BotRuntime::dryKills`); after three times what one piece takes by the source's chance (ten fights at least,
  forty at most) the quest is set aside for half an hour: `sets quest .. aside for 30 min: 12 fights at Drywallow
  Daggermaw and its like without one Wyrmtail (the chance is about 25%)`. And at an object the fights around it are
  no progress any more: the watchdog's three minutes end such a task.
- *Look around, then on to the next spawn* (the owner, 2026-11-14: [quote left out], and to a first version that waited 25 s: [quote left out]). NewRpg looks for
  targets by walking to and fro around the place it was given; once that took the bot more than 35 yd from the spawn
  only the watchdog's three minutes ended the task (his leader stood 100 s at an emptied spawn of "Badlands Reagent
  Run"). Now, once the bot has been at the spawn, it looks after each fight and rest (3 s on, for the loot and the
  rest's decision) for a living creature the objective needs within 45 yd: the creature of a kill objective, every
  kind an item objective's item comes from (`WorldIndex::GetItemSourceCreatures`: all four kinds of coyote). With none
  it goes on to the next spawn at once (`sees nothing of quest .. within 45 yd: on to the next spawn`); the spawn it
  left is not chosen again for four minutes. No other wait.
- *Holiday spawns are nobody's town.* The town search counted spawns that only stand there during a holiday
  (`game_event_creature`): the fire keeper, revelers and scorchling of Hammerfall's Midsummer fire widened its closed
  ground by 90 yd to the west. They are left out.

Open: Drywhisker Gorge (the Lesser Bloodstone Deposits of "Favor for Krazek") has one link in the road map's graph,
and it runs through Hammerfall, so the planner has no route in or out for the Alliance (a bot inside leaves by
hearthstone). The path finder has a way from the hills west of the town (453 yd from (-1240, -3500) to the gorge's
node, on the ground all the way); the road map would need a link there.

### Live round 39: grinding at a camp, a walk that ended inside one, full bags (2026-11-13)

Eighteen hand-ins by the eight old bots in 21 minutes (round 38: eleven). What the round and the minutes after it
showed of the planner's:

- **Grinding prefers what is no humanoid.** A level-22 rogue with nothing left it could safely do in Redridge ground
  a level-22 Blackrock Sentry at the orcs' camp; a scout and an outrunner of the camp joined, and it died, twice
  more after a restart had forgotten the place. Grind spots are now looked at in two passes: creatures that are no
  humanoids first (beasts stand apart and call nobody), humanoids only when none of those is usable, and of them only
  ones below the bot's level.
- **Out of a camp.** A travel ended 192 yd from its target, inside the Dragonmaw camp, and the last stretch was
  refused; the bot had no other task and stood there until it was attacked. When nothing can be planned and the
  risk model would not let the bot work where it stands, it walks to the nearest road map node that is a safe place
  (`PlanRetreat`: `has nothing to do at (..) and stands among creatures it cannot take: it walks 140 yd out to ..`).
- **Room in the bags at a vendor.** mod-playerbots sells junk at a vendor and nothing else. A bot whose bags were
  full of materials and quest loot came back from two vendor visits as full as before, could not take a quest's
  reward and could not fill its phial. After a vendor visit that leaves three or fewer slots free (`MakeBagSpace`):
  the bags go through the guild's loot filter as loot does (its rules apply, and what is junk by the junk rule is
  sold: grey items and white ones nobody in the guild would wear, never materials); crafting materials go into the
  guild storage (a town trip, like a walk to the bank; also without Material Haulers, which is about storing loot
  from anywhere); then whatever else the bot does not use itself goes into the guild storage too (gear for others,
  recipes, green and better items, food and drink it does not keep) until six slots are free. The planner sells
  nothing of its own judgement; a bot whose bags are still full after that leaves the vendor trips for a while.
- **No free slot at all**: a vendor at any distance (was: within 400 yd only).
- **Stepping stones, narrowed** (round 40: 33 in 21 minutes, 25 of which only restarted an objective the bot could
  not get to): a stepping stone is taken only when it is not the task's own target that has no way (that target is
  set aside, as before), and at most four per bot in ten minutes.
- **No spot behind a place that is set aside.** A grind spawn, or the spawn chosen for an objective within a plain
  walk (350 yd), whose straight way crosses a place the bot has just set aside (a pack it would not pull, a place
  it left a fight at) is not offered while that place is set aside: after a refused pull the planner had offered
  four condor spawns in a row whose way led through the same three murlocs.
- **Ammunition for a hunter with an empty quiver** (round 41: a level-2 hunter stood for half an hour: no money for
  arrows, then a rifle out of the guild storage and arrows in its quiver). mod-playerbots buys ammunition with the
  bot's own money. Now, at a vendor visit, a hunter whose quiver holds nothing its weapon shoots puts in use what it
  carries for it, else buys one bundle of the best the vendor sells for its weapon and level, paid from the guild's
  budget like a quest's item: `bought 200 x Heavy Shot for its weapon from Haljan Oakheart`. Ammunition of the
  wrong kind counts as none for the trip, and the trip goes to a vendor that sells the right kind.
- **Vendor walks are judged** like the walk to a quest giver (a level-8 character died beside a Defias Dockmaster on
  its way to a vendor): a vendor whose way is refused is left alone for half an hour and the next plan takes another.
- **Reagents out of the guild storage leave a line**: `used 2 x Linen Cloth from the guild storage as a reagent for
  Bolt of Linen Cloth (spell 2963)`. 22 Linen Cloth had left the storage in a round without one.
