### Craft orders (2026-11-13)

the owner, 2026-11-13, on casters without wands: [quote left out].

A craft order is "make N x item" of a guild (`CraftOrders.h/.cpp`, table `ga_craft_order`). The guild leader places
it in the addon's Storage tab, view *Craft orders*: the lower list shows what the guild's characters that are in the
world can make (every recipe they know that creates an item, with who knows it), he picks one, sets a count and
presses *Order*; the upper list shows the orders with what was made and a note: who makes it on its next town trip,
or what it waits for ("waits for materials: 1 x Lesser Magic Essence (Priestholy would make it)", "nobody of the
guild who is in the world knows a recipe for it (Enchanting)").

- **Who makes it, and when.** A bot that knows a recipe for an open order starts on it on a town trip: at a vendor
  visit, in the minutes after a hand-in at a hub (before crafting for skill), and in the profession mode. It makes up
  to `Professions.CraftBatch` casts per visit; the planner leaves it alone until the casts are done.
- **Materials** come from its bags and the guild storage, as for any craft (each use from the storage is logged).
  What a vendor sells of the missing materials is bought at a vendor visit, at most 20 a visit, paid from the
  guild's budget (`GuildBudget`). Nothing is gathered for an order.
- **The tool.** A recipe that asks for a tool the bot lacks (an enchanter's Runed Copper Rod for wands) makes the bot
  craft the tool first when it knows how and has what that takes; the tool stays with it.
- **The result** leaves the bot's bags for the guild storage when the crafting ends, the order counts it, and when
  the order is full it is closed with an event `CRAFT` in the guild's feed. Casters then take a wand from the storage
  as they take any better gear (docs/storage.md §9).
- **Disenchanting** for an order's dust and essences (`Professions.DisenchantForOrders`, on since the owner's word of
  2026-11-13: [quote left out]): when an order
  lacks them, an enchanter turns up to three green or blue weapons or armour pieces of the guild storage per town
  trip into their materials: only pieces nobody of the guild in the world would wear, that its skill is enough for,
  and whose disenchanting can give what is missing (no armour for its dust when an essence lacks; the world's
  disenchant tables, read at startup). Every piece leaves a line: `<bot> disenchanted 1 x <item> from the guild
  storage for a craft order: <materials> into the guild storage`. The routine is `CraftOrders::DisenchantStored`
  (one kind of item, a count, a purpose for the log line), which the Storage tab's disenchant button of the storage
  work calls too; `.ga admin craftorder disenchant <character> <item> [count]` runs it from the console.
- **What a bot makes goes into the guild storage** (the owner, 2026-11-13: [quote left out]). Whatever a character the AI plays makes with a recipe (crafting for skill at a hub, the profession
  mode, the bot detail's Crafting sub-tab, a quest item for another member, smelting) leaves its bags for the guild
  storage when its crafting has ended (`CraftOrders::StoreCrafted`, fed by `OnPlayerCreateItem`): `<bot> put what it
  made into the guild storage: 5 x Linen Bandage`. It keeps a tool and an item an open quest of its own asks for; the
  line names those ("; it keeps 1 x Runed Copper Rod (a tool)"). A weapon, armour piece or ring it made and would
  wear is put on at once, and every copy that is still in its bags after that goes into the storage with the rest
  ("; it keeps 1 x Ring of Silver Might (it put it on)"). Not through the loot filter: nothing a bot made is sold as
  junk on the way. What the owner makes with a character he plays himself stays his. Before, a product stayed in the
  crafter's bags until a bag sweep (S8).
  *the owner, 2026-11-13: [quote left out]* Until then a whole batch was kept when the piece was "an upgrade": a jeweller made Rings of Silver
  Might in twos and threes for its skill, a bare finger makes any ring an upgrade, it can wear one of that ring, and
  twelve lay in its bags (the bag sweep left them too: the loot filter keeps what a bot would wear). Besides the rule
  above, `CraftOrders::StoreUnworn` looks once a minute at what a bot carries: weapons, armour and jewellery it made
  itself and does not wear go into the storage after it has put on what it wants of them (`put gear it made and does
  not wear into the guild storage: 11 x Ring of Silver Might`), and of a tool it made one stays. Not what a quest of
  its own asks for, what its dungeon set wants, or what is bound to it. In the storage the surplus rule takes over
  ("Surplus crafted gear is disenchanted").
- **Wands.** The bot detail's Character sub-tab has a line *Wand*: a mage, priest or warlock with nothing in its
  ranged slot shows "none" and who of the guild could make the best wand it can use ("Priestholy can make Lesser
  Magic Wand"), or that nobody can yet (`BOT^nw`, `BOT^wm`).

Bot settings: `Professions.CraftOrders` (on: a bot works on the guild's orders), `Professions.DisenchantForOrders`
(on). Commands: `.ga craftorders <character>` (the guild's orders with their notes, and the casters without a
wand); administrator, also console and SOAP: `.ga admin craftorder add <character> <item> <count>`, `.ga admin
craftorder del <character> <order id>`, `.ga admin craftorder work <bot>` (test aid: the bot looks at the orders now,
as on a town trip).

```
activity: Probepriest makes Runed Copper Rod for itself: the guild's order of 3 x Lesser Magic Wand needs it
activity: Probepriest works on the guild's craft order: 3 x Lesser Magic Wand (0 of 3 made so far)
activity: Probepriest used 1 x Lesser Magic Essence from the guild storage as a reagent for Lesser Magic Wand (spell 14293)
activity: Probepriest made 3 x Lesser Magic Wand for the guild's craft order (3 of 3): into the guild storage
activity: Probemage took from the guild storage: Lesser Magic Wand
```

To make a bot an enchanter: its Professions sub-tab, Enchanting as a main profession. It learns the profession and
the recipes its skill allows where it stands (K1); the Lesser Magic Wand needs skill 10, the Greater Magic Wand 70.

### Profession mode (2026-11-12, package K4)

the owner: [quote left out]. The order is `CRAFT` (the token the protocol had reserved; in the addon's
Orders tab it is called "Professions"; `.ga admin order <bot> CRAFT`). It takes no argument: the bot works on every
profession of its plan that is below its target (300 when the plan names none), `OrderService::RunProfessions`. It
does not quest and does not level on purpose; it keeps itself supplied like any bot (vendor, repair, rest).

What it does, in this order, whenever it has no task:

1. **Stores its goods.** Below twelve free bag slots everything it gathered (materials) and made (the products of
   recipes, unless it uses them itself) goes into the guild storage, whatever the guild's perks: the recipes take
   their materials from there (CP-7), and auto loot gathers nothing into nearly full bags.
2. **Crafts** what gives the most skill for the least material (`Professions::CraftForSkill`, up to 20 casts; every
   30 s). A recipe that is made at an anvil, a forge or a fire only counts where one stands (the core's own check).
   When nothing can be made where the bot stands, the best recipe that lacks only what the bot can get by itself is
   helped along: a **material vendors sell** is bought (the nearest vendor that has it, through the guild's budget;
   `bought N of N x Coarse Thread for a recipe of its profession from ..`), and the bot **walks to the nearest anvil,
   forge or fire** (`Professions::GetFocusSpawns`: 4279 such places; `on the way to .. to craft there`).
3. **Gathers.** Mining and Herbalism: a round over the places where nodes spawn that its skill opens and that still
   teach it something (a node is grey 100 points above what it asks), nearest first (a node far above or below counts
   as farther: caves). A place is visited once in ten minutes (nodes are pooled: not every place has its node); the
   node itself is the gather detour's (below). Skinning: a hunt for the nearest beasts its skill is enough for and
   still learns from, whatever their level is to the bot's own (`hunting .. for skins`); the planner picks the
   targets (only skinnable ones), the corpse is the detour's. The lower skill goes first.
   Farther than 2500 yd the walk is a travel with flights; places in a zone that starts above the bot, at a place it
   keeps away from, or where the risk model's spot verdict says no (`Risk::JudgeSpot`), are left out. Other
   continents are not looked at.
4. Nothing to do: it waits at an inn (`nothing to craft or gather right now`).

**The gather detour** (also for bots on the autopilot, package K1) now covers corpses: a corpse the bot killed and can
skin within `Professions.GatherDetour` yards is walked to (auto loot takes its loot on the way and skins it from
3 yd); hunters and casters, who kill from a distance, never came close enough before. No detour with fewer than four
free bag slots (auto loot does nothing then), none for a node in a camp, and none for a quest object that opens with a
herb or mining lock (a Plant Bundle, a Tear of Tilloa: 1715 such places were counted as nodes; auto loot opened them
too, and despawned them).

Open: materials that are neither gathered nor sold (cloth, the drops of creatures) are not farmed; a recipe that
needs both a bought material and a walk gets the purchase first and the walk on its next look; the
autopilot does not hand a level-60 bot without quests this mode yet; the skill a profession stops at for the bot's
level (a rank it cannot learn yet) is not told apart from "nothing to do".

### Farm orders (2026-11-13)

the owner: the guild leader picks an item and a bot farms it on and on (cloth, a rare bind-on-equip piece). For an item
with many sources the bot looks for groups of creatures in an area it covers on foot, not for single creatures in the
middle of nowhere; only creatures at least four levels below the bot; and when there are no valid targets the leader is
told. Added by him the same morning: [quote left out] (a target stock; the bot changes continent when it must). The order is `FARM <item> [<target stock>]`;
`Farming.h/.cpp` holds the knowledge, `OrderFarm.cpp` (part of `OrderService`) the behaviour.

**Sources.** `Farming::Load` reads `creature_loot_template` and `reference_loot_template` once at startup (loot mode 1,
about 117,000 rows) and takes the creatures the planner grinds from the world index (`WorldIndex::GetMobSpawns`: no
elites, no NPCs, with loot). `Farming::Yields(item)` computes, once per item, what one kill of each kind of creature
brings of it on average, as the core rolls its loot (`LootTemplate::Process`): rows without a group each by their own
chance, each group one of its rows (the rows with a chance first, the rest share what is left), a reference row the
table it names times its count, nested up to four deep. So a world drop counts too: a green of a level band sits in a
reference table that hundreds of kinds of creature roll on with a small chance. Rows that drop only for a quest do not
count. Other sources than creature loot (skinning, mining and herb nodes, fishing, chests, vendors, recipes) are not
looked at (the design log section 7 "Open" FM1): an item only they give is refused when the order is set (`FARM_INVALID`).

**Targets.** A target is a spawn of a kind of creature that drops the item, that the planner grinds, that the bot's
side may attack, and whose highest level lies at least `Farm.LevelsBelow` (4) under the bot's. At a ground the hunt
fights only such creatures (`PickGrindTarget` with the item; the level limit again on the creature in front of it).

**Hunting grounds** (`Farming::FindGrounds`). Every target on the bot's map is the middle of a possible ground: all
targets within `Farm.GroundRadius` (80) yards of it, found with a grid of that cell size. A ground needs
`Farm.MinSpawns` (4) targets; only when no place on the map has that many (an item few creatures drop) smaller groups
count. Grounds are ranked by what a round over them yields (the sum of the yields per kill; more than twelve spawns add
nothing: the first are back before the bot has killed the rest) divided by `1 + distance / 3000 yd`. The best twelve
places are judged one by one, a ground per place: not in a zone that begins above the bot's level, and usable by the
risk model's spot verdict (`Risk::JudgeSpot`, as for every place the planner sends a bot to). Only targets on the bot's
land mass count (or within 2500 yards: an island off the coast is a land mass of its own). Places the bot has set
aside (deaths, a fight it left, a pull it called off) and grounds it has emptied are left out. `Farm.MaxDistance`
(0 = no limit) bounds the search.

**Another continent.** With no target at all on the bot's land mass, `FindGrounds` ranks the grounds of every other
land mass the same way (without the risk verdict, which needs the bot there) and names the best one its side can
travel to, by the yield of its ground divided by the legs of the way (`WorldIndex::CountTravelLegs`: ships, zeppelins,
portals). The planner then takes the next leg (`NextTravelLink`, a `Voyage` task as for any travel across the sea) and
picks the ground anew when the bot has gone ashore. A bot only crosses when it must: grounds on its own land mass
that the risk model refuses do not send it away. With `Farm.MaxDistance` set it stays on its side.

**The loop** (`OrderService::RunFarm`):

1. no task: the upkeep first (`PlanUpkeep`: vendor trips for full bags, repairs, ammunition, as under any order), then
   `PlanFarm` asks for a ground;
2. a ground farther than 300 yards is travelled to (a `Travel` task: flights, a route over the road map and the
   checks of what lives on it, as for any journey; a way the planner refuses sets the ground aside for twenty minutes)
   until it is that near; then the hunt begins (a `Grind` task with the item, levels 1 to the limit, targets within
   the ground's radius of its middle);
3. after each fight the bot walks to the corpse of its kill before it takes the next target (`StepFarmLoot`: within 45
   yards, for at most twelve seconds), so that auto loot takes what is in reach;
4. the loot goes through the guild's loot filter as always; the ordered item itself goes into the guild storage with the
   note "its farm order" in the loot log (it is never junk, Material Haulers is not needed for it, and the bot does not
   keep it for itself; a rule of the guild that names the item still decides);
5. a ground with nothing left to fight (the hunt idles for twenty seconds) counts as emptied for three minutes: the
   next look takes the next best ground, or, with none, the bot waits where it is ("waiting for the creatures to come
   back") and looks again every thirty seconds;
6. a hunt ends after ten minutes at the latest and is planned anew, so a level-up, a changed setting or a better
   ground is picked up.

The why line names the item, the kind of creature most of the ground is made of, the zone and how many of the item the
bot has looted under this order (with a target stock: how many of it the guild storage holds).

**Target stock.** The order may carry a target stock (`ga_bot_farm`, `BotOrder::farmTarget`; 0 = none: the bot farms
until the leader gives another order). The stock is the item in the guild storage, every random property of it
together, plus what the bot carries; it is counted every five seconds out of combat. At the target the leader gets a
`FARM` event ("<bot> has farmed <item> up to the target stock (N of M in the guild storage) and is back on the
autopilot."), and the bot's order is `AUTO` again, as after the profession mode (FM2).

**Nothing to farm.** When `FindGrounds` has no ground, it says why, and the leader gets an event of the type `FARM`
("<bot> cannot farm <item>: <reason>."), a line in the activity log, and the why line "Farm order for <item>: nothing
to farm: <reason>". The bot walks to the nearest inn and waits (as under `IDLE`), looks again every five minutes, and
the notice is repeated only when the cause or the bot's level changes, or after an hour. The causes:

| Cause | Text |
|---|---|
| no creature drops the item | refused when the order is set: "No creature drops <item> (a farm order hunts creatures; it does not gather, fish, skin, buy or craft)" |
| only elites, dungeon creatures or creatures of its own side | refused when the order is set |
| every source is above the level limit | "every creature that drops <item> is above level N (4 below its own level M); the lowest is <creature> (level L), so from level L+4 on" |
| the sources live on another land mass and no ship, zeppelin or portal for its side leads there | "the creatures it could farm <item> from live in <land mass>, and no ship, zeppelin or portal for its side leads there" (with a way there the bot travels, see above) |
| every ground in reach is set aside or refused by the risk model | "the risk rules keep it from every place where it could farm <item> right now" |
| every source is farther than `Farm.MaxDistance` | "... are farther away than its farm orders reach" |

**Settings** (bot settings, category "Farm orders", per guild and per bot; docs/bot-settings.md): `Farm.LevelsBelow` (4),
`Farm.GroundRadius` (80 yd), `Farm.MinSpawns` (4), `Farm.MaxDistance` (0, advanced).

**Commands.** `.ga admin order <bot> FARM <item id> [<target stock>]`; `.ga admin farm <character> <item id>` (reads only): how many
kinds of creature drop the item, how many of them a bot of that side can grind, how many lie at or below the
character's level limit, the five kinds with the best yield, and the five best grounds with place, size, yield and
the risk model's verdict, or why there is none.

**Addon.** The Orders sub-tab offers *Farm item*: a search box (a name, an item id, or a shift-clicked item) and
*Search*; the answers fill the list below it, each in its quality colour and with "(from level N)" when the bot is too
low for it; below it the field *Target stock (0 = no limit)*; *Apply order* sends `ORDER_SET` with `o = FARM`, `zone` =
the item and `n` = the target stock (docs/protocol.md section 7.23). The line "Current order" shows what the guild
storage holds of the item.
