### Dungeon runs (2026-11-13, package K6, stage 1)

the owner: [quote left out]. The order `DUNGEON <dungeon>` is given to a guild bot by its owner and never
chosen by the autopilot. The bot leads its squad (Squads: its members follow it as their playerbots master in its
party; `GuildAdventure.Squads.MaxSize` up to 5). `Dungeons.cpp` holds what a run needs to know, `OrderDungeons.cpp`
runs it.

- **Which dungeons.** Of the 29 five-player dungeons of the readiness list (the dungeon finder's holiday bosses
  are left out since 2026-11-13), those with an entrance from the open world (the area trigger that leads onto their
  map), at least one spawned boss (the dungeon's encounters, in their order) and a map of their own: 13 today, the
  Deadmines, Ragefire Chasm, the Wailing Caverns and Shadowfang Keep among them. A map that
  holds several dungeons (the wings of the Scarlet Monastery, Dire Maul, Maraudon, and maps a holiday boss shares) waits.
  `.ga admin dungeon [<id>]` lists them, or one with its entrance and bosses.
- **Who may go.** Every character of the group needs a readiness of at least 50 % for the dungeon (Readiness, package
  K5); else the run ends at once and says who is not ready. The order is refused for the guild leader, for a squad
  member (it goes to the group's leader) and for the dungeon in the other side's capital.
- **To the entrance.** The group gathers at the road map's node nearest to the entrance (the entrance itself lies on
  the dungeon's own ground: the tunnels before the Deadmines' portal are full of elites) and is put inside from there,
  as a meeting stone would bring it. The way there is a travel like any other: routes, flights, and ships between
  land masses. At the entrance the leader waits until every member is there, alive and out of combat.
- **Inside.** The leader walks from boss to boss; what stands on the way is fought by the group with playerbots'
  group play. At a boss's place it attacks the boss; when no living boss is there, that one is done. A boss the
  group gets no nearer to for eight minutes (a door that an event opens, a way the path finder does not have) is
  passed over. Leaving a lost fight, the pull check and the rescue of stranded bots are off inside a dungeon; the
  rest between fights and the leader's waiting for its members are not.
- **Deaths.** A dead character is brought back by its group ten seconds after the fight. When nobody is left, the
  group starts again from the entrance after twenty seconds, and the second time the run is over.
- **The end.** After the last boss the group can get to (or a run that fails, or two hours), everybody is put back
  at the gathering place, the dungeon is reset for the next run, an event `DUNGEON` goes to the guild's feed and the
  leader's order is `AUTO` again. The last boss of the dungeon counts as a run of the tiered guild achievements
  (their own kill hook).

```
activity: Wartank starts a dungeon run: Deadmines with 5 characters (readiness: Wartank 100%, Priestholy 100%, ...)
activity: Wartank goes into Deadmines with 5 characters
activity: Wartank's group is done with Rhahk'Zor in Deadmines (1 of 6)
activity: Wartank's group is done with Gilnid in Deadmines (2 of 6)
```

Stage 1 is the server side, started with `.ga admin order <bot> DUNGEON <dungeon id>`.

**Stage 2 (2026-11-13): the order in the addon.** The Orders sub-tab of a bot offers *Dungeon*: the picker lists the
five-player dungeons in the bot's reach that a run can be ordered into, each with the bot's readiness, and the text
below says how big the squad is that it leads ("no squad: it would go alone"). *Apply order* sends `ORDER_SET` with the
dungeon's id as `zone`; the server refuses with `DUNGEON_INVALID` and the reason when the dungeon cannot be run, when
the bot follows a squad leader (the order goes to the leader) and, at once, when somebody of the group is not ready
(`CheckDungeonReady`: "not everyone is ready for it (at least 50% each: Wartank 100%, Magefrost 38%)"). The group is
the bot's squad, formed in the same sub-tab ("Squad: follow ..."); a squad may have five characters now
(`GuildAdventure.Squads.MaxSize` 5, was 3). `STATE^orders` lists `DUNGEON` and `CRAFT` (the profession mode) now: both
were accepted by `ORDER_SET` but not listed, so the addon showed them greyed out. A bot found inside a dungeon
without a run (its order was changed in the middle of one) is put back at the dungeon's gathering place
(`LeaveDungeonWithoutRun`: "is inside Deadmines without a dungeon run: back to its entrance"); before, it looked
for a way out on foot and ended every attempt "stuck". No party builder yet: the squad row is the group. The text under the picker names the group's roles by its talent templates ("1 tank, 1 healer, 3 damage", with "no tank" / "no healer" in orange); a group without one is not refused. The run's first log line names them too (`roles: ...`).

**Loot (2026-11-13).** the owner: [quote left out]. While its leader is on a dungeon run a squad's party loots by *group loot* from uncommon up
(`KeepSquadGroup`; free for all again when the run ends), and the module's auto loot starts the rolls in a dungeon or
raid as a loot window would (`StartGroupRolls` in `Storage/AutoLoot.cpp`: the core starts them in `Player::SendLoot`,
which the auto loot does not go through). mod-playerbots votes for each bot ("loot roll"): with its settings
`Playerbots.LootNeedRollLevel = 1` and `LootGreedRollLevel = 0` a bot rolls (greed) for a weapon or armour piece that
is an upgrade for it and passes on everything else, so an upgrade goes to one of the bots that would wear it. The
winner gets it at once (`activity: <bot> won 1 x <item> in its group's roll (greed)`), the loot filter sees it like
any loot (what the bot wears stays with it) and playerbots puts it on. The planner casts each bot's votes every step
(`BotDriver::VoteOnRolls`, playerbots' own action): playerbots votes from its own tick only, a resting bot's AI is
paused, and a roll would wait a minute for it. What everybody passed on is free again: the
member whose auto loot reaches the corpse takes it and the loot filter sends it on (junk sold, the rest into the guild
storage with Material Haulers, else it stays in its bags). An item a roll runs for stays in the corpse until it is
decided. After a boss the group stays for the rest of the fight and for its loot: while the leader fights, a roll
runs or a corpse of the group's within 40 yd of the leader still holds something, the leader walks to it and waits,
at most 20 s (70 s while it fights or when a character its owner plays is in the group: his roll window is open for
a minute); then `is through with the fight and the loot at <boss> after N s`, or `leaves loot behind at <boss>` with
what was left. A soulbound piece everybody passed on stays in the bags of the bot that took it: the guild storage
takes no soulbound item (the design log section 7 "Open" DL1). A
character the owner plays in the group gets the game's roll window like in any party. In the open world nothing
changes: no rolls, whoever of the party stands there takes it. The module warns at startup when
`Playerbots.LootNeedRollLevel` is 0 (bots would pass on everything).

**Roles (2026-11-13, docs/dungeon-roles.md).** The guild leader gives a bot the dungeon role tank or healer. At the
entrance, when the group is together, every member with a role changes to the talents of the role (its second talent
spec) and puts on its dungeon set (`RoleService::EnterDungeonMode`); when the run ends everybody changes back
(`LeaveDungeonMode`, or the planner's step at the member's next quiet moment). The roles in the run's first log line
and in the addon count the dungeon role first, else the role of the levelling talents; a member with a role is named
with the readiness of its dungeon set (`Wartank 100% (as tank in its dungeon set 86%)`), which does not refuse the
order. The dungeon finder's holiday bosses are no longer in the dungeon list, so Shadowfang Keep can be ordered
(13 of 29 dungeons).

**A run at the dungeon's level (2026-11-13).** The first run with a group at level (20-21 in the Deadmines) showed
what the runs with over-levelled test groups had not:

- **Patience.** "No nearer to the boss for eight minutes" passed Gilnid over while the group was clearing the mast
  room before him: a group at level fights for minutes between two bosses. The clock now only runs while the group
  could walk: not while one of its characters fights, rests or is dead, and not while the leader waits for its
  members. A gap of more than five seconds between two steps of the run counts as such time in full (the step does
  not run while the leader waits for its squad, rests or fights; the first build counted every two-minute wait as
  five seconds and passed Gilnid over once more).
- **Doors** (`GuildAdventure.Dungeons.OpenDoors`, on). A bot walks through a closed door (the server's movement
  does not know doors), but a door blocks the line of sight: whoever stands behind it is not healed and not shot at.
  Every closed door the leader comes within 14 yd of is opened by the group, also in a fight (`opens Heavy Door
  in its way`, `opens Iron Clad Door in its way`): the boss that opens it in the game (Rhahk'Zor, Sneed and Gilnid
  in the Deadmines), the cannon of the Deadmines, a key, a lever on the far side or a small event is skipped that
  way (the design log section 7, DG3).
- **The boss that ends a dungeon comes last** in the list, whatever its encounter id says (the Stockade listed
  Dextren Ward after Bazil Thredd, Razorfen Kraul Agathelos after Charlga).
- **Recovered at the entrance.** The group goes in when every character has 80 % health and, with mana, 70 % of
  it (they rest by themselves), or after three minutes.
- **Something to drink.** A paladin that went in without a drink rested 37 of the 80 minutes of two runs (39 rests,
  up to three minutes each, the leader waiting two of them). The log names who goes in with neither a drink in its
  bags nor one in the guild storage for it (`StorageSupply::HasDrink`): `goes into Deadmines with 5 characters
  (nothing to drink: Tankpala)`. No trip to a vendor is planned for it. (Until 2026-11-14 a mana user without a drink
  waited at the entrance for its next supply step; since bots take a drink out of the storage one piece at the
  moment they rest, DQ11, nothing comes into the bags to wait for, and every start stood there for three minutes.)

**Repeated runs (2026-11-13).** the owner: the low-level dungeons are to be [quote left out]. A dungeon order can ask
for several runs (`ORDER_SET^runs`, the Orders sub-tab's *Runs*, `.ga admin order <bot> DUNGEON <id> <runs>`; at most
`GuildAdventure.Dungeons.MaxRuns`, 10; table `ga_bot_dungeon_runs`). When a run ends that got somewhere (a boss
down, no second wipe), the group stands at the gathering place and the next run starts from there: the order stays,
and so do the dungeon sets and the talents of the tanks and healers. Before it goes in
again, each character has its gear repaired where it stands when its worst piece is below 90 % durability, for
what a vendor would charge and from its own money (`GuildAdventure.Dungeons.FieldRepair`; DG4), and bags with fewer
than eight free slots go the loot filter's way (`MakeBagSpace`: junk by the junk rule is sold, materials into the
guild storage). Food and drink come out of the guild storage as always. A run that fails (no boss, two wipes, no
way) ends the order with its remaining runs.

**A fresh dungeon before every run.** At the entrance, with everybody outside, the leader looks whether a character
of the group is still bound to an instance of the dungeon, resets it (`Player::ResetInstances`) and goes in when
nobody is bound any more (given up after a minute: "its old instance could not be reset"). The reset at the end of a
run does not do that: the characters are still on the instance's map while their teleports out are on the way, and
the core resets no instance with a player in it. The first double run showed it: the second run went in one second
after the first, found the old instance with every boss dead and "finished" it in five minutes.

**The hourly limit.** The core lets a character into `AccountInstancesPerHour` (5) different dungeon instances
within an hour. A group that farms a short dungeon waits at the entrance until its oldest visit is an hour ago
(`waits at the entrance of ...`, the why line says so); the wait is not counted as time of the run.

```
activity: Tankwar ends its dungeon run in Deadmines after 40 min: every boss it could get to is down (6 of 6 bosses, 0 wipes)
activity: Tankwar's order has 1 more run of Deadmines
activity: Tankwar starts a dungeon run: Deadmines with 5 characters (readiness: ...; roles: 1 tank, 1 healer, 3 damage)
activity: Tankwar reset Deadmines for its run (the group's old instance is gone)
activity: Tankwar goes into Deadmines with 5 characters
```

(Between two runs, when something was repaired or bags were emptied: `Tankwar's group between two runs: Tankwar
(repairs for ...c); Probemage (6 bag slots freed)`.)

### How a dungeon group fights (2026-11-13)

Three rules of the owner for the groups in dungeons (`OrderService::StepDungeonFight`, `TryCarefulPull` in
`OrderDungeons.cpp`; stepped once a second by the bot that leads the run, inside the dungeon; the settings are
`GuildAdventure.Dungeons.*`):

- **While the tank pulls and takes the creatures, the others hold back** ([quote left out]). The tank is the first character of the group that tanks (its dungeon
  role, else its talents). When a fight begins, every other AI-played character of the group has its AI held
  (`BotDriver::PauseAI`) until every creature of the fight attacks the tank, at most `TankLeadSeconds` (4), and for
  the whole of a careful pull. A character a creature attacks fights at once; the healer is let go when somebody is
  below `EmergencyHealth` (50 %); when the tank is below 35 % everybody helps. No tank in the group: no holding
  back.
- **The careful pull only where it is needed** ([quote left out];
  `CarefulPulls`, `CarefulPullPack` 3). Before the leader walks on, with the group able, beside it (30 yd, 60 %
  health) and out of combat: the nearest creature within 34 yd in its sight that is not in a fight, and those within
  10 yd of it (what comes with it). After a wipe of this run, after a death of the tank in this run (it counts like
  the wipe: a Gnomeregan tank died twelve times in a row in a pack of six two levels below it, and the group never
  wiped), or when that group has `CarefulPullPack` creatures or
  more and one of them is at the tank's level or above, the tank brings the creature to where the group stands
  (`Escape::BeginPull` of the behaviour work: the opener from a distance, or into its sight and back). Only a tank
  that leads the group pulls (the run window makes the first tank the leader). A creature that cannot be pulled is
  left for 20 seconds and the group walks on as before.
- **A creature that runs away is everybody's target** ([quote left out]; `FocusFleeing`).
  When a creature of the fight flees, every damage dealer turns to it: a ranged character within 36 yd in its
  sight from where it stands, a melee character by following it. It is followed only while no creature outside the
  fight stands within its aggro reach (plus 6 yd) of the runner; else a melee character lets it go, takes another
  creature of the fight (or stops), and the ranged ones finish it.
- **The healer holds back only before contact** (the owner, 2026-11-14: [quote left out]): its emergency-only rule holds while no creature of
  the fight is on anybody of the group; from the first blow it heals as always.
- **A fight in which nothing happens is ended** (`StepDungeonFight`): no creature is on anybody of the group and
  nobody casts or has a living target within 40 yd, for 45 s, while the boss the group is after is in no fight: the
  module ends the fight for everybody of the group, with a line that names who held it. (A group stood "in combat"
  so for 25 minutes before Mograine's room, its leader waiting for a member that "fights". The planner's own rule for
  this is off in dungeons, for a boss that talks.)

```
activity: the group of Tankwar holds back while its tank Tankwar takes the creatures (at most 4 s per fight; the healer heals below 50% health)
activity: Tankwar pulls Defias Overseer (level 18) carefully to its group in Deadmines: the group was wiped out in this run (3 creatures would come, the highest level 18)
activity: the group of Tankwar turns to Defias Miner that runs away (3 characters turned to it; it is followed: nothing else stands where it runs to)
activity: Tankwar ends its dungeon run in Deadmines after 36 min: ... (6 of 6 bosses, 0 wipes; the group held back for its tank in 41 fights, 2 careful pulls, 5 fleeing creatures focused)
```

The first hold of a run is logged, the rest is counted in the run's last line.

**No way on foot to a boss** (`GuildAdventure.Dungeons.HopWhenNoWay`, on). In Blackfathom Deeps the group stood
before the pools behind Lady Sarevess for eight minutes and then passed Gelihast over: players swim and jump there,
and the path finder has no way ("its step would run 354 yd through the air"). When the group gets no nearer to a boss
for 90 seconds (the same clock as below, which stands still while the group is busy), is more than 60 yd from it
(or more than 12 yd above or below it: Lord Serpentis stands on a ledge 29 yd above the way in the Wailing Caverns) and
the path finder has no path from the leader to the boss's place (`WalkReaches`), the group is put on walkable ground
before that boss, once per boss (`OrderService::FindHopSpot`): a point 25 yd (else 35 yd) from the boss, tried from
the side the group comes from round the boss in steps of 30 degrees, with a floor within 15 yd of the boss's height
and a path to the boss no longer than three times the distance; among those the one with the fewest creatures within
18 yd. Everybody of the group that is alive in the dungeon is put there (`NearTeleportTo`); the creatures between are
left standing. Where no such point is found, the boss is passed over after eight minutes as before.

```
activity: Bfdpala's group finds no way on foot to Gelihast in Blackfathom Deeps (258 yd away; a way players swim or jump): it is put 25 yd before it
```

*Sooner where the leader stands, a door before a hop, fights far below* (the owner's Blackrock Depths run, 2026-11-23: [quote left out], [quote left out]). The path finder's ground of Blackrock Depths' upper city has two levels that it does not
join: the bar, the balcony above the Black Anvil and Ambassador Flamelash's chamber above, the anvil, the Hall of
Crafting and Warder Stilgiss' vault below (`.ga admin path` from the Hall of Crafting towards Flamelash ends in the
corner at (982, -318, -72), the other way round on the balcony at z -49). The group walked into that corner and stood
there two minutes until the 90 seconds of no progress were over, and stood four minutes before Warder Stilgiss because
its members were "in a fight" with creatures on the floor below that nobody could get to; and once the hop that puts
the group before a boss's room put it from inside the Grim Guzzler beyond the closed Bar Door. Since then:
- the hop comes after 30 seconds when the leader has stood still within 4 yd all that time (the corner) and the path
  finder has no way (`HopStillMs`; the 90 seconds hold while it walks);
- a fight holds the clock only when its creature (the member's target or one attacking it) is within 40 yd and 8 yd
  of the member's height;
- before either hop puts the group somewhere, a closed door between the leader and where it goes (within 25 yd of the
  straight line, a walk to it from the leader) is walked to, opened and stepped through, and the walk goes on from
  there (`OrderService::StepThroughDoor`; given up after 90 seconds, then the hop).

```
activity: Rtanka's group finds no way on foot to Ambassador Flamelash in Blackrock Depths - Upper City (84 yd away; a way players swim or jump): it is put 25 yd before it
```

Where the two levels join (stairs the navmesh does not have) the group is still put across: from the balcony down to
Lord Incendius' floor, from the corner of the Hall of Crafting up to Flamelash.

*A patch of ground that leads nowhere* (2026-11-24, the test guild's first Shadowfang Keep run on the integration
server). The group came to stand on a wall top 7 yd above Odo the Blindwatcher, 10 yd from him, where the navmesh has a
few square yards that no path leaves (read with `tools/navpath`: from there to Odo and to the room's place "the walk
ends short of the end"). Every walk of the leader was refused for ten minutes (the room's) and eight more (the boss's),
and then Odo was passed over. Two holes let it stand: the walk check counts 12 yd as there (NPCs stand a few yards off
the navmesh), so a boss on another level that near "could be walked to" and the hop never came; and while the room is
cleared the boss's clock does not run at all. Now:
- a boss or a room's creature within 12 yd and more than 4 yd up or down counts as reachable only when the core's path
  ends at it (`NoWayOnFoot`, `PathEndsAt`): the hops before a boss, onto a boss's floor and to a room's creature ask
  that;
- the leader that has stood still 30 seconds out of a fight, more than 8 yd from the place its group clears a room from
  and with no way on foot there, is put at that place with its group, once per boss (`roomPlaceHopFor`):

```
activity: Stonehorn's group stands where no way on foot leads to the place it clears the room of Odo the Blindwatcher from in Shadowfang Keep (45 yd away, 10 yd up or down): it is put there
```

*How it got up there: the hop put it on a roof* (2026-11-24, the owner: [quote left out]). The "wall top" is the roof over the prison and Odo's room: read with
`tools/navpath`, a navmesh of about 50 by 50 yd at z 108 (x -270 to -230, y 2107 to 2157), 8 yd above Odo's floor and
joined to nothing. The group's first step in the dungeon is the hop onto the boss's floor ("stands 23 yd below Odo ...:
it is put on its floor, 30 yd from it"), and `FindHopSpot` took the first ground under 8 yd above the boss, which
there is the roof, and let it through because the path from it ended right above Odo, within the 12 yd the walk check
counts as there. On the `j5` instance a run put its group up there the same way (its leader later stood at
(-263, 2124, 109) above Rethilgore). The Shadowfang Whitescalp that held the live group in a fight for 14 minutes
(14:23 to 14:37, "cannot reach its target", at full health) went for the healer, which most likely stood on the roof
(its place in its status lines, (-248, 2143), lies within the roof's outline; those lines have no height), and the
creature's chase in the core finds no way up there, so it stood beside the others and healed (the core lets a creature in a dungeon that
cannot reach its target regenerate). Now `FindHopSpot` looks at the ground at the boss's height first and takes a
spot only when the core's path from it ends at the boss (within 8 yd across and 4 yd up or down; a spot on a ledge the
navmesh does not reach is taken only when no other passes). A fight a creature holds that cannot reach its target
names both places and the creature's path in its line now (`UnreachableDetail`), so the next case shows where its way
ends. The prisoners' cells that the group opens on its way (Cell Doors, lock 85, which no player opens) are not
changed here.

**Walks of a dungeon group on the whole navmesh** (2026-11-24, the owner: [quote left out]). Counted in the live activity log since 2026-11-12 with `tools/analysis/dungeon_moves.py`
(every line a run writes when it puts its group or a member somewhere): 120 relocations, 92 of them hops before a boss
("finds no way on foot to ... it is put 25 yd before it"), 12 hops onto a boss's floor, 12 members caught up with
their leader by teleport; Blackrock Depths' Upper City 60 in five runs, the Sunken Temple 24, the Wailing Caverns 10,
Maraudon 10, Shadowfang Keep 4. The cause, read with `tools/navpath` (the whole navmesh of a map, the core's filter for
bots) from each dungeon's entrance to each of its bosses: every boss of the Upper City, the Sunken Temple, Maraudon's
Pristine Waters and Shadowfang Keep has a way on foot, 300 to 2400 yd long (Odo the Blindwatcher 620 yd for 51 yd as
the crow flies). The core's path finder stops after 148 polygons and sees only the tiles of loaded grids, and the
module's walk check (`WalkReaches`) wants every leg 15 yd nearer to the end; on such a way both said "no way", and the
group was put there. Now `DungeonNav` (`DungeonNav.h/.cpp`) loads the whole navmesh of a dungeon or raid map from the
mmaps folder once and finds walks of any length on it (Detour, 8192 polygons, the bots' filter). Inside a dungeon
(`OrderService::ViaDungeonPath`, used by `WalkTo` and by the run's own walks, `DungeonGoTo`) a walk goes to a point 35 yd
along that way, so the core's path finder walks it a stretch at a time; "no way on foot" (`NoWayOnFoot`, the room's
and the floor's hops, a member's catch-up in `OrderSquads.cpp`) means that this finds no way; the "no nearer to the
boss" clock measures the way that is left, not the line (Odo's way leads away from him through the stables first). A
line `walks the navmesh's way to (x, y, z) in <dungeon>: N yd (M yd straight)` names a walk that winds. On the `j5`
instance a group of level 22 in Shadowfang Keep walked from the courtyard to Odo through the keep ("530 yd (29 yd
straight)"), killed Rethilgore, Razorclaw and Silverlaine on the way and then Odo: no relocation, where every run of the
same group that day had had a hop onto Odo's floor, a hop to his room's place and three members put beside their leader.
**Drops: a jump down a ledge** (2026-11-24, the same order of the owner's). The navmesh of a dungeon falls into parts no walk
joins: the plateau of Lord Serpentis and Verdan the Everliving in the Wailing Caverns is reached only by a jump of 6 yd
from a passage above it, and left by a jump of 28 yd into the pool below. `DungeonNav` finds such drops when it loads a
map: from every border edge of a part's polygons a fall of 2 to 12 yd onto a polygon of another part no more than 6 yd
away, or, where there is none, a fall of up to 30 yd onto ground or 50 yd into water within 15 yd (a player jumps from
higher up where nothing else leads down, into water without harm), at most 24 per pair of parts 8 yd apart (the Wailing
Caverns: 173 parts, about 800 drops). A drop counts when its fall is clear of walls (`DropClear`, looked at once: a line
out over the edge at its height to a landing 2.5, 5, 8 or 12 yd out from the cliff, then straight down to it) and a
fall of more than 30 yd lands in water (the map's liquid: the navmesh marks no polygon as water in the caves). A way may
lead over drops (Dijkstra over the parts); at the edge the leader, and a member that walks the way to its tank, jumps
(`OrderService::DropDown`: a straight move without a path; the ground guard lets such a fall of up to 30 yd onto ground
and 55 yd into water through inside a dungeon). Log line `activity:
<bot> jumps down N yd from (x, y, z) to (x, y, z) in <dungeon>: no walk leads there, a drop does`; `.ga admin navway
<character> <x> <y> <z> [<from x> <from y> <from z>]` gives the way on the whole navmesh with its drops, or why there is
none (each drop off the start's part with what stood in its way: `out` the line over the edge, `down` the fall, `dry` no
water under a deep one).

**The stretches and the near-boss phases follow the way** (2026-11-24, the Wailing Caverns on `j5`). The group's walk in
stretches of 35 yd (package P3, `StepDungeonWay`) took each stretch from the core's path finder, which ends below a
plateau after 148 polygons: the tank turned back to the foot of Verdan's plateau every few seconds, 60 yd from him and
1950 yd by the way, and gave him up after eight minutes. The stretch is the point 35 yd along the navmesh's way now, and
a boss whose way is much longer than the straight line (more than 1.5 times it and 40 yd) is not "near": no room to
clear, no gate, no pull until the way left is short. On `j5` the tank walked the 1950 yd through the caves, jumped the
6 yd onto the plateau and its group after it, and Lord Serpentis fell without a teleport onto his ledge.

What the whole navmesh still has no way to: off the Wailing Caverns' plateau none of its 36 drops is clear (the rock
of the cave under the ledges, or 40 yd onto dry ground below Serpentis's ledge), so the group is put down before Lord
Pythas after Verdan and Serpentis (once per run). For it the hop stays.

**Swims** (2026-11-25, Blackfathom Deeps on `j5`). Lady Sarevess and Old Serra'kis lie in deep water off the walkable
ground: the navmesh's parts there are islands in pools. `DungeonNav` also joins an edge of a part to a part at about the
same height (5 yd up or down) 4 to 60 yd across, outward from the edge, when the line between them is water (`Drop::swim`:
`DropClear` samples the water every 3 yd a little, two and four yards below the lower shore, one dry sample in five
allowed, and looks for a line of sight through plants and small rocks a little above the shores or 1.5 or 3 yd under
the lower one: across the pools every line over the shores was stopped by the dungeon's model, lines under the surface
were not, and without them none of the swims to Lady Sarevess's island counted).
The leader and a member that walks the way to its tank swim it (`DropDown(.., swim)`, a straight move; the ground guard
lets a swim inside a dungeon through), log line `swims N yd from (..) to (..) in <dungeon>: no walk leads there, the
water does`. A swimmer floats between two parts, the pool's floor and the shore it swims to: in the water the way's
start is the part with the shortest way (its distance from the swimmer counted), looked for 25 yd up and down (the
group, back on the surface for air 20 yd over the pool's floor, had been put near Lady Sarevess for having no way). On
foot the start is the part under the feet, not one a few yards above (after a jump of 6 yd down beside Lorgus Jett's
ledge every way began with that jump again, and the group stood below it for eight minutes). A drop or swim under way
is not planned anew until its landing (`BotRuntime::dropUntil`: a member caught half way across had its way planned from
the water, began at the edge behind it, turned back and swam the same 9 yd every two seconds for a minute), and a cast is
broken off for it (a warlock that began Create Soulstone at the shore again and again did not move a yard). A character
in a fight with a creature 8 yd or more below or above it that the path finder has no way to walks the navmesh's way to it
when there is one within 120 yd, down a drop or across water (`HopDownToFight`; the healer above a pool had been put
beside a myrmidon 17 yd below it in the water); the hop stays for a creature no way leads to.
A swimmer is also one floating at the surface with its feet less than half a yard under it (the water checked at its
feet and half a yard below them): the leader that had swum to the shore before Ghamoo-ra floated 2.5 yd above that
shore's part and 0.5 yd above a ledge's part, was taken for a walker on the ledge, every way began with the swim from
the ledge again, and it stood for eight minutes and gave Ghamoo-ra up (`does not get to Ghamoo-ra (43 yd away)`).
The point some yards along the way (`DungeonNav::PointAlong`) lies on the navmesh: where it falls between two corners of
the straight path it is moved along the navmesh's surface from the corner before it (`moveAlongSurface`). The line
between two corners does not follow the ground: on the way down from Lethtendris's platform in Dire Maul East the
point hung 14 yd over the floor below the ramp, the core's path to it ended on that floor, the ground guard refused the
walk as one through solid ground, and the tank tried it every 25 s for five minutes.
**A next point nothing brings the bot to** (2026-11-25, Blackfathom Deeps on `j5`). The leader stood eight minutes each,
without a line, at Lady Sarevess, Old Serra'kis and once more at Sarevess, 6 to 7 yd from the next point of its way (a
drop's top at the pool's edge): NewRpg's walk from where it floated had no path, and `WalkTo`'s rule for a walk that does
not get going looks only at points more than 8 yd away. A next point within 12 yd and 8 yd up or down that the bot has
not come a yard nearer to in 6 s is walked to straight (the AI held 3 s, a cast broken off), log line `does not get to the
next point of its way at (..) in <dungeon>, N yd away, in N s: it goes there straight`; the same for a destination of a
walk this near (the run's stretches give the edge of a drop 4.7 yd off as theirs: `does not get to (..) in <dungeon>, N yd
away, in N s: it goes there straight`), not in a rest. A leader 6 yd or less from the edge of a drop or swim of its way
that gets no nearer to it in 5 s takes the drop from where it stands (`does not get to the edge at (..) in <dungeon>, N yd
away: it jumps / swims from where it stands`; the walk to the edge had taken it up onto the part a yard above, whose way
began with the swim back). A first drop or swim the character has as good as done (its landing nearer than its top and
within 3.5 yd) is left out of the next way (a swim of 5 yd had ended 2 yd short of its landing, and every way began with
it again); the run's stretch is not planned anew while a drop or swim is under way (it was planned from half way down a
jump, `StepDungeonWay`). Over water, the polygon right under a character goes before the nearest one beside it.
**After a drop or swim into a pool** the character floats at the surface, yards above the pool's floor, the way's part: for
half a minute the way is planned from the landing (`NavFrom`), and the next point is swum to straight (`SwimAlong`, log line
`swims along its way in <dungeon>, N yd above the way's ground under the water: on to (..)` every 30 s at most); the path
finder started on the ledge beside the pool and had no way. A drop whose character comes down 2.5 yd or more above its
landing, not over water, stopped on something the navmesh does not show: it no longer counts until the server restarts
(`DungeonNav::BlockDrop`, log line `came down at (..) in <dungeon>, N yd above the landing at (..): the N drops of the navmesh
there no longer count`).
**A drop or swim is held to its end** (2026-11-25, `OrderService::KeepDropMoving`). The leader of Blackfathom Deeps swam
from the ledge towards Ghamoo-ra and stood on the ledge again 18 s later, for 13 minutes: the drop's hold kept the planner
from planning anew, but the bot's AI was held for 2 s of a swim of 11 s and walked it back. Now the AI is held and the
straight move to the landing set again for as long as the drop or swim runs (`is off its way down or through the water in
<dungeon> at (..) (moving elsewhere, movement N): on again to (..)`).
**A room's place both ways on the navmesh; the tank comes back for a member with no way up** (2026-11-25). In Twilight
Lord Kelris's room of Blackfathom Deeps the group's place was moved up to a Twilight Shadowmage on the raised floor 5 yd
above the walkway; the tank got up there in a fight, a warlock stayed on the walkway with no way up, and the group
waited for it for over five minutes (the member's catch-up looked only from 60 yd, or 20 yd with 8 yd of height). A
room's new place must have a way on the navmesh from the leader and back (`DungeonNav::FindWay` both ways); a member
20 yd or more away with 3 yd of height is looked at, and when it has no way to its leader but its leader has one to it,
the leader walks back to it (`goes back to <member> in <dungeon>: <member> has no way up to it`, then `is back with`)
and the room is fought from there; only after a minute and a half of that is the member put beside its leader. A drop whose landing lies under another part of the navmesh below its edge is not taken (the fall
would end on that part). On `j5` the leader got out of the pocket before Ghamoo-ra (an hour of standing and going to and fro on the builds
before) and went on through the instance to Twilight Lord Kelris, past the places of Lady Sarevess and Old Serra'kis
where it had stood eight minutes each (those bosses lay dead from the morning's run).

**The open world's navmesh for a long walk to another level** (2026-11-25, the owner: [quote left out]). The Document Chests
of "Grimtotem Spying" (5064) stand on the mesas of Thousand Needles, 120 yd from the canyon floor below them as the crow
flies and 1470 yd by the ramps that lead up; the core's path finder stops after 148 polygons and sees only loaded grids,
so the planner set the chest aside as "on another level" (`SetAsideOtherLevel`) and the leader rode back to Freewind Post
for its other quest. `DungeonNav` now also answers for the four open-world maps (`IsOpenWorld`: Eastern Kingdoms,
Kalimdor, Outland, Northrend): it indexes the map's tiles once (`the navmesh of map N for long walks in the open world: N
tiles, loaded where a way is asked for`) and loads the tiles of a box 800 yd around both ends of a way when one is asked
for (at most 200, then a fresh mesh), without drops or swims. Before a target on another level is set aside the walk asks
it once (`BotTask::openTried`); a way of up to 2500 yd is walked like a dungeon's (`BotTask::openWay`: `ViaDungeonPath`,
35 yd at a time), log line `walks to (..) with the path finder from where it stands: the navmesh has a way of N yd there
(M yd straight), and it walks that way`. The stuck rule measures such a walk by the yards left along its way
(`BotTask::navLeft`), not by the straight line, which does not shrink while the bot rides round a mesa.
Off the mesas the same (round 219: Thunderhoof and Mojowind, up on the Grimtotem mesas by that way, were "cut off from every
road" on their next tasks and rescued down to the canyon): a walk whose route's start is a guess, and a character the
path finder cannot bring to any road node (`CutOffWayOut`), ask the navmesh for a way of up to 4000 yd to the task's spot
first and walk it (`finds no walk from where it stands to the road (..) towards ..: the navmesh has a way of N yd there`;
`is cut off from every road on its way to ..: the navmesh has a way ..`), before the way it came and the rescue. An
exploration's spot is the ground inside its area trigger nearest to the trigger's middle when the middle has no navmesh
(`DungeonNav::NearestOnMesh`; the middle of "Test of Faith"'s trigger hangs beside a pillar, 118 yd above the canyon floor).
"Test of Faith" itself stays open: no ground lies inside its trigger, which a player reaches by a jump off the pillar
beside it. Since 2026-11-26 it is on the hand list of quests AI-played characters leave alone (`ga_quest_block_template`):
30 tasks of the test guild's bots on it in two days ended "jumped", "no way to its level", "spot not reached" and nine
times "rescued", and none of them finished it.


**No level limits for a dungeon group** (the owner, 2026-11-14: [quote left out]). The guild leader sends
whom he wants: the squad rule "at most three levels apart" does not hold for the group of a dungeon run (neither
when it is formed nor while it runs; `SquadService::AllowAnyLevel`, and no `LevelGap` state under a leader whose order
is `DUNGEON`), and readiness is shown, not asked for (`GuildAdventure.Dungeons.MinReadiness`, 0; it was a fixed 50 %).
What stays is the game's own door: a character below the level the core asks for to enter the dungeon's map is
refused with that level.

**The tank goes in front** (`OrderService::PutTankInFront`). The run window makes the first tank of a group its
leader. A dungeon order given to a squad whose leader does not tank while a member does (the Orders sub-tab,
`.ga admin order <bot> DUNGEON`) gets the same when its run starts: the squad becomes a group of the run window that
its first tank leads (`StartDungeonGroup`), so the tank walks ahead and pulls; when the order is over the squad is
what it was before, and its leader is on the autopilot (what a dungeon order ends with). When that is not possible
(a member is not in the world or not ready), the squad's leader leads as before and the log says why.

```
activity: the tank Tankpala goes in front: it leads the dungeon run of Probemage's squad (the squad is what it was before when the run is over; Probemage is on the autopilot then)
```

**Bosses that an event brings** (world table `ga_dungeon_event_template`; `OrderService::StepDungeonEvent`). Mutanus
the Devourer (Wailing Caverns) and Grubbis (Gnomeregan) are not spawned: an NPC brings them when a player picks its
gossip option. Such a boss is a stop of its own in the dungeon's order (`DungeonBoss::talkEntry`; `before_boss` says
before which boss, 0 = after the last): the group walks to the NPC's place like to a boss; when the group is
together and able, the leader walks right up to the NPC and picks the option (the client's gossip packets; an NPC
that does not offer it is asked five times, six seconds apart, then the stop is given up). **Before the talk the
group walks the way the NPC will walk** (its SmartAI waypoints, every third point and the last; a point it does not
get to in 40 steps is one players jump or swim to, and the group is put there): the NPC walks ahead of the group,
and what stands on its way kills it (the Disciple of Naralex died five minutes into its walk in the run before
this rule). From the talk on the group
stays with the NPC, walks with it when it walks off (`follow`: the Disciple of Naralex walks to Naralex's chamber),
fights what attacks it, and when the boss is there the leader goes up to it and attacks. The stop is done when the
boss was seen and is not alive any more (the rest of the fight and the loot first); it is given up when the boss has
not come after `timeout_s`, or when the NPC has been gone for 45 seconds. A boss that an event brings does not count
for "the dungeon is finished": a run that has the dungeon's own bosses down opens the guild's next dungeon also when
an event did not start.

| Dungeon | NPC, option | Boss | Where in the order |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wailing Caverns | Disciple of Naralex, "Let the event begin!" (offered once the four fanglords are dead); it walks off | Mutanus the Devourer | after the last boss |
| Gnomeregan | Blastmaster Emi Shortfuse, "I am ready to begin."; she walks from tunnel to tunnel | Grubbis | before Viscous Fallout |

```
activity: Tankwar starts the event of Mutanus the Devourer in Wailing Caverns: it talks to Disciple of Naralex (the group stays with it on its way)
activity: Tankwar's group is done with Mutanus the Devourer in Wailing Caverns (8 of 8)
```

**A boss that is a friend.** Baelog and his brothers in Uldaman are the Alliance's friends. A boss the group sees
that is friendly to its side and cannot be attacked is left out at once (a neutral one is not: Witch Doctor Zum'rah
in Zul'Farrak turns on whoever comes near; the first build of the rule left him out) (the first Uldaman run stood before them
until the eight minutes of "no nearer to the boss" were over).

**A boss that sleeps until something is used** (`DungeonBoss::useObjects`; a row of `ga_dungeon_event_template`
without an NPC and with `go_entries`). Archaedas in Uldaman is spawned, but stoned until the Altar of Archaedas is
used; the Altar of the Keepers before it opens the way. While such a boss "sleeps" (stunned, not a valid target, not
attackable, or out of sight), the leader does not attack it: it walks to the listed objects one after the other,
uses each (the client's use of a game object; twelve seconds for a ritual to work), skips one it cannot get to in
60 seconds, and fights the boss once it is awake. After four rounds without a waking boss the group goes on. An object
beyond 100 yd is walked to by its spawn on the map (the spawn nearest to the boss; 90 seconds for the way): the Altar
of Archaedas stands in the vault behind the Altar of the Keepers, too far to be seen from it, and the owner's group used
the first altar four times, gave Archaedas up and left with 4 of 6 bosses (no unlock: the end boss was not down); the
six statues of the Sunken Temple stand round the pit, and only the first was used. They work in their order only, so
an object it does not get to is tried again (not the next one), and the way's clock stands still while the group
fights, rests or waits (the owner's second Uldaman run walked back to the first altar once). The boss is given up only
after the last use has had its twelve seconds: the sixth statue woke Atal'alarion one second after its use, and the
group had given him up in that second. T2 on the `roles` instance: Atal'alarion woke after the statues and fell
("done with Atal'alarion in Sunken Temple (1 of 5)").

```
activity: Sfkwar uses Altar of The Keepers in Uldaman: Archaedas sleeps or stands behind a door until it is used
activity: Sfkwar uses Altar of Archaedas in Uldaman: Archaedas sleeps or stands behind a door until it is used
activity: Sfkwar's group is done with Archaedas in Uldaman (6 of 6)
```

**A boss that is not at its place.** A boss that walks or flies a round (the dragons of the Sunken Temple) is found
by its spawn wherever it is on the map (`DungeonBoss::spawnId`, the map's creatures by spawn id): while it lives it
is not "done", and the group walks to where it is now. (The first Temple run counted Dreamscythe and Weaver as done
without having seen them: nothing of their kind was within 150 yd of their place.) A boss that fell in this instance
away from its place (pulled to the group) or before a restart of the server is done at once: the map holds a respawn
time for its spawn, and the group does not walk to its place to see it is gone. (The owner's group killed Highlord Omokk
in Lower Blackrock Spire 90 yd from his place five seconds before its run began anew after a restart; the tank set
out for his place every 17 s for twelve minutes, and its walk there had no way: the path finder's way from the group's
spot down the ramp ended "shortcut + no path" while the dungeon's navmesh had one, 2026-11-25.) **When the core's path
finder has no way where the dungeon's navmesh has one** (the same ramp: the core's query of that instance found no
polygon for the walk's start or end, while a fresh instance's path finder walked the ramp in 24 points and
`DungeonNav` had its 91 yd): after a walk the ground guard refused within 30 s, `ViaDungeonPath` walks the straight
leg to the next point of the way along the navmesh's surface itself (`DungeonNav::SurfaceLine`: a point every 6 yd
on the surface, a spline over them, no path finder), when that line lies on the navmesh to within 3 yd of the point;
activity line `walks the navmesh's surface to (..) in <dungeon>, N yd: the path finder had no way there`. Why the
live instance's query had no polygon there is not known.
*(Also when it gets no nearer, 2026-11-25.)* One refused walk and then mod-playerbots' long walk: where the core's path
finder has no way, NewRpg's `MoveFarTo` samples points in a cone towards the goal and then walks to a random point near
by, again and again. The owner's group in Scholomance ([quote left out], 23:53 to
00:02): its tank walked 1611 yd in five minutes with 19 turns back and came 35 yd on, then 1770 yd with 34 (the
activity counters of the status line), on its walk to its place in Jandice Barov's room, until the room's ten minutes
ran out. Now the surface walk follows too when the bot gets no nearer to its next point by 3 yd in 8 s, refused or
not, as often as it takes (`BotTask::navBestDist`, `navBestAt`; activity line `... N yd: it got no nearer in 8 s`).

**A dead character stays with its body.** mod-playerbots releases a dead bot's spirit to the graveyard outside; the
way back in is a change of map, and while it lasts the group takes its leader for gone, plays its own orders inside
the dungeon, dies and walks to an inn. A dead character of a run has its AI held while it lies inside the dungeon
(`StepDungeonDead`), so its group revives it where it fell. (An Uldaman group fell apart that way after its tank's
sixth death.)

**A member under attack** (the owner, 2026-11-14, from his own Uldaman run: [quote left out]; `OrderService::StepDungeonRescue`). What his server's log
showed: the mage and the healer fought three Stonevault Oracles 55 yd behind the tank, the mage died, and the tank stood
"waiting for its squad: Magefrost is dead" for two minutes while the healer fought on alone for three minutes; a
leader helped only a member within 40 yd, only when it was not fighting itself, and a dead member came before one that
fights. Now, every second of a fight: the creatures that attack a member who is not the tank are the group's first
targets, the healer's first, then those on the member with the least health. The tank goes to them at once, up to
100 yd and also out of its sight (its own movement walks there; the creatures on the tank follow it), and leaves a
creature on itself for them; a tank already on such a creature changes only for one on the healer. The damage dealers
within 60 yd turn to them too (a ranged one from where it sees it; out of its sight it walks there when it has no fight
of its own), unless they are on such a creature already (and the healer is not attacked by another); they keep
holding back for the tank as long as the hold of a pull lasts. In a dungeon run the leader's wait counts a member that
fights within 100 yd before everything else, a dead member included. One log line per member and fight, and a count
in the run's last line:

```
activity: Palatwo's group goes to help Shammpower (its healer) (62% health) against Stonevault Oracle (level 37, 48 yd from Palatwo): the tank Palatwo goes to it (out of its sight: it walks there), 2 damage dealers turned to it
```

**Not brought back into its killers** (the observer of the owner's server, 2026-11-14: in Uldaman two characters were
brought back every 11 to 15 s at Grimlok and died again within seconds, twelve deaths in 87 s, until the owner stopped the
run; they stood in other instances than their group, which did not fight, so "ten seconds after the fight" came at
once). A dead character in another instance of the map than its leader is not revived there (it is taken to its
group, above). A death within 30 s of its last revival makes the next one wait longer (10, 30, 50 ... s, at most
110 s); creatures alive at its body (within 25 yd, those walking home included) bring it up beside the character that
stands, and only when nothing hostile is near that one either: `brought back by its group in Uldaman (beside Palatwo:
creatures stand at its body)`.

**The dead always come back** (the dungeon rework's baseline runs of 2026-11-14: a Deadmines group's mage and rogue
stood beside three corpses and nobody was brought back; a Cathedral and a Zul'Farrak group wiped out at their first
pull and their tank lay dead for over an hour). "The group fights" is a fight that is one: something is on a living
member or it has a living target within 40 yd (the game's "in combat" also holds for a creature that keeps a
combat reference and does nothing). After three minutes dead a character comes back beside the one that stands,
whatever stands about it: `Gnomwar is brought back by its group in Lower Blackrock Spire (beside Gnompala: dead for
260 s)`. And a character that lies dead in the dungeon belongs to the run whatever the run's phase, so a group wiped
out before the run counted as inside is a wipe too (back to the entrance, all alive). Nobody comes back while
hostile creatures within 40 yd of a living member or 30 yd of the body are still in a fight (not evading), for 90 s
after the death (the owner's Molten Core raid, 2026-11-27: its two healers stood apart with nothing on them while the Flame
Imps were still in their fight, the dead came back among them, died again, and no wipe was ever counted). When all are
dead the wipe comes 10 s later (the owner: [quote left out], was 20 s): all of them alive at the entrance.
While the party's leader or a member near it lies dead and nobody near it fights, a member rests by itself (the group's
rest is its leader's step): the shaman that had brought the tank back stood at 7 % mana with no drink in its bags for a
minute and a half and only ate, since mod-playerbots' drink finds nothing there and the one piece out of the guild
storage comes with a rest.

**A member with no way to the group** (Maraudon's inner part: the healer and the hunter fought alone for seven and
four minutes, 100 to 150 yd from the group and two levels below it, and died; the group waited for them). In a dungeon
run a member is far behind from 60 yd on when the path finder has no way on foot from it to its leader (looked at
every 10 s), and it catches up (to its leader's side) also out of a fight it has fought alone for a minute. The line:
`caught up with its squad leader ... (it was 112 yd behind, with no way on foot to it, out of a fight it fought alone)`.

**One instance for the whole group** (the owner, 2026-11-14, in Uldaman as the tank: [quote left out]). His group stood in three instances of Uldaman: the tank, the
druid and his own character in instance 5, the dead mage alone in 3, the healer fighting alone in 6, at almost the
same coordinates. The core sends a character into the instance it is bound to, else into its party leader's (once that
leader is bound to one), else into a new one; the start sent all five in in the same second, and the members whose way
in came before the leader's got instances of their own. And the squad's catch-up made it worse: a teleport on the same
map stays in its instance, so it put the two "beside" their leader in their own instances. A character in a party
goes into the instance of its party's leader only (else into a new one, whatever it is bound to), and the core lets
nobody in who is not in the party of those inside (the healer of a test group stood outside Razorfen Downs: its
leader's party was full with a bot of an earlier group, who also led it). Now the leader goes in first; the run's
leader leads the party, the group's characters are put into it (a character of an old party that is no part of this
group makes room); each member is bound to the leader's instance (`OrderService::BindToLeaderInstance`) and taken in
beside it once the leader is inside (`StepDungeonEnter`, every two seconds of the leader's ticks, also while it
fights); a member that
stands in another instance of the map is taken out to the entrance (a dead one brought back first) and in to its group;
the catch-up of a squad does the same for a member in another instance; a dead member in another instance is no wipe
of the group, and a member there is not counted as beside its leader. After a restart of the server, which puts the
dead of an instance at a graveyard outside and starts the run's state anew, the group's dead are brought back to it.
When the group ends, the guild leader's own character leaves its party also when it had an order of its own (Retadin,
watched on the autopilot, stayed in a party of three with a squad's two bots after his Uldaman run). And the members
take what the run uses out of the storage once they are inside: they leave the leader's squad for a few seconds
while its teleport runs (it is "not in the world"), and the list dropped every member not found then, so only the
leaders used anything (the owner: [quote left out]). At the entrance a member
with nothing to drink (bags, storage) is not waited for to get its mana back, unless it is the healer.

```
activity: Shammpower stands in another instance of Uldaman than its group (instance 6, Palatwo's is 5): it is taken out to the entrance and in to its group
```

**The room before the boss** (the owner, 2026-11-14, after a wipe in the Scarlet Monastery's cathedral: [quote left out]). The creatures within 30 yd of a boss
that is not in a fight yet (hostile, attackable, in no fight, no critter or civilian, no boss of the dungeon) are
fought before the boss. For Scarlet Commander Mograine the room is 80 yd: his engage sends every monk, abbot,
champion, centurion, wizard and chaplain within 80 yd at the group (the core's Scarlet Monastery script), and a group
that had cleared 30 yd had 15 creatures on it, on the owner's server and on the roles instance. The room is fought from a
place out of the boss's reach (the owner: [quote left out]): at least 45 yd from it
(its aggro range plus 15 yd, if more), where the leader stands when the group comes within that distance plus the
room plus 20 yd of the boss, else walkable ground on the side the group comes from (`FindHopSpot` with rings of that
size); the group turns to the room before it comes near the boss. It goes to that place first (within 12 yd); from
there the leader pulls the creature nearest to the place to it (`Escape::BeginPull`: it opens from a distance and the
group fights where it waits), one beside the group is fought where it is, one that cannot be pulled is walked to when
it stands out of the boss's reach or within 20 yd of the place, and left for a minute when it does not. At most ten
minutes per boss, twenty for a room as big as Mograine's. Why so far: a creature in a fight calls those of its side
within 10 yd every few seconds and one that flees runs to a helper within 30 yd; the group that fought the cathedral
from beside Mograine (within 40 yd of him) had him and 21 creatures on it, the one that came within 40 yd of him after
Fairbanks had a monk flee to him, and the one that took Whitemane for a creature of his room walked to her. On the roles
instance (level 55, Bfdpala tank, Sfkpriest healer, warlock, hunter, rogue) the Cathedral then went through: 27 of the
33 creatures of Mograine's room were pulled to the place in 22 minutes, Mograine came with 7 creatures (before: 25 and
30), 3 of 3 bosses, no wipe, no death, 39 minutes. Lines: `Bfdpala's group clears the room of Scarlet Commander Mograine
in Scarlet Monastery - Cathedral first: 33 creatures stand within 80 yd of it (the nearest: Scarlet Monk level 34); it
fights them at (1163, 1342), 58 yd from it`, `... is through with the room of ... after 1310 s (6 creatures left: the
time is up, or the boss is in a fight)`, `... cannot pull ... out of the room of ...: it stands 36 yd from it; left for
a minute`. Open: the six left were wizards, champions and monks 36-45 yd from Mograine that `BeginPull` found no pull
for (the cathedral is crowded: every way passes another creature's sight) and that stand inside the 45 yd.

**The cathedral's order** (the owner: [quote left out]). Scarlet
Commander Mograine has no encounter of his own in the core's data, so the Cathedral's list was Fairbanks and
Whitemane, and the door rule opened the High Inquisitor's Door on the way: the group went in to Whitemane while
Mograine lived. Now the wing's hand list names Fairbanks, Mograine and Whitemane, a hand-listed boss without an
encounter is put before the boss that ends the dungeon, and the door rule never opens the High Inquisitor's Door
(Mograine's death opens it).

**A boss that a gong or an object brings** (a row of `ga_dungeon_event_template` with no NPC to talk to and with
`go_entries` for a boss that is not in the dungeon's list: `DungeonBoss::summonObject`, `OrderService::StepObjectEvent`).
Tuten'kash in Razorfen Downs (the owner: [quote left out]) comes after three waves that the gong (game object 148917) brings, one per
use; the gong cannot be used while a wave lives. Such a boss is a stop of its own before `before_boss`: the group walks
to the object, waits there until it is together and able, the leader uses it, the group stays within 10 yd and fights
what comes, the leader uses it again whenever it can be used (every 8 s at most, at most six times), and the stop is
done when the boss was seen and is dead (its loot first), or given up after `timeout_s`. A boss that comes this way
does not count for "the dungeon is finished".

**The statues of the Sunken Temple** (a row with `go_entries` for a boss that is in the list: the six Atal'ai statues
148830 to 148835 for Atal'alarion). The statues are used in that order (the Altar of Hakkar shows it in the game);
Atal'alarion stands in another phase until the sixth is used, so to the group it "sleeps" and the rule of a boss that
sleeps (above) walks the group to the statues one after the other.

**Jammal'an's force field** (a boss inventory of the classic dungeons: six
balcony defenders, `DATA_DEFENDER_KILLED`; Jammal'an the Prophet is immune to players until all six are dead). The
six (Zolo 5712, Gasher 5713, Loro 5714, Hukku 5715, Zul'Lor 5716, Mijan 5717) are hand-listed bosses of the temple
that come before Jammal'an: `ga_dungeon_wing_template.before_boss` names the boss a listed boss without an encounter
comes before (0: before the last, as for Mograine). Each has its room (30 yd) like any boss.

**The Shade of Eranikus after a restart** (the owner's runs of 2026-11-22: "does not get to Shade of Eranikus (0 yd away)" in
four runs). The instance script frees the Shade (unit flag not selectable) at Jammal'an's death only, and sets the flag
again whenever the Shade is created: after a restart of the server, or when his grid was not loaded at that death, he
stays unselectable for good. The run frees him when the map holds a respawn time for Jammal'an (he is dead). And a
group that stands at the Shade while his room (every dragonkin within 250 yd, the nearest 102 yd from him) has nobody
within 45 yd walks towards the room's nearest creature, not on towards the Shade (it stood "on the way to the room"
beside him for eight minutes).

**Wings** (`Dungeons::Load`). A map that holds several dungeons of the dungeon finder (the Scarlet Monastery's
Graveyard, Library, Armory and Cathedral; Maraudon; Dire Maul; Blackrock Depths and Spire; Stratholme) has an entrance
per wing. Every area trigger from the open world onto the map is an entrance; a dungeon's wing is named by the boss
that ends it for the dungeon finder: its entrance is the one whose inside lies nearest to that boss, and its bosses
are those that lie nearest to that entrance. Each wing is a dungeon of its own for orders, the run window and the
guild's unlock order; the instance itself is one (a run resets it before it goes in, as always). A wing whose end
boss is not spawned can be run only with a hand list that names its entrance (Stratholme's Main Gate: Balnazzar comes
out of Grand Crusader Dathrohan); every boss of its list counts for "finished". Where the rule is wrong, the world table
`ga_dungeon_wing_template` lists a wing's bosses and the area trigger of its entrance by hand (Maraudon: the purple
wing's Lord Vyletongue lies nearer to the orange entrance). Checked against the dungeon finder on 2026-11-14 (the owner:
[quote left out]; the end bosses are
`instance_encounters.lastEncounterDungeon`, the rest by where they stand): Maraudon's Purple Crystals are Lord
Vyletongue alone (Celebras the Cursed had been listed there, before him, and the group went past him into the inner
part), Pristine Waters Celebras, Landslide, Tinkerer Gizlock, Rotgrip and Princess Theradras; Dire Maul East Zevrim
Thornhoof, Hydrospawn, Lethtendris and Alzzin (the rule had kept Alzzin alone: the other three lie nearer to the wing's
southern entrance), Dire Maul West Illyanna Ravenoak, Magister Kalendris, Tendris Warpwood and Prince Tortheldrin (not
Immol'thar, behind the force field of the five pylons); Stratholme's Main Gate the living side (The Unforgiven,
Hearthsinger Forresten, Timmy the Cruel, Cannon Master Willey, Malor the Zealous, Archivist Galford, Grand Crusader
Dathrohan), its Service Entrance the undead side (Magistrate Barthilas, Baroness Anastari, Nerub'enkan, Maleki the
Pallid, Baron Rivendare; Ramstein comes from the slaughterhouse's event; the rule had given it The Unforgiven and
Hearthsinger Forresten). The Scarlet Monastery's four wings and Dire Maul North were right. A dungeon that is no wing can have such a
list too, to leave a boss out: Uldaman is listed without Ironaya, who stands behind a sealed door that an event
with a staff opens and who killed the tank through it, run after run. Since 2026-11-14 also by hand: Blackrock
Depths' Prison (Lord Roccor, Houndmaster Grebmar, High Interrogator Gerstahn) and Upper City (Pyromancer Loregrain to

(Atal'alarion, Jammal'an, Morphaz, Hazzas, Eranikus; not Dreamscythe and Weaver, which fly their rounds and are not
walked to): the nearest-entrance rule gave the wings of Blackrock mountain each other's bosses.
