### The acceptance numbers of a run (2026-11-14)

Package P7 of the plan of the dungeon rework: what each later package is judged by, counted
by the run itself instead of from the log afterwards (`OrderService::StepDungeonMetrics`, four times a second for the
bot that leads the run, inside, from `OrderService::Update`; `BotRuntime::DungeonRun::Metrics`; once a second missed
the short fights of a group far above its creatures, and a boss of three). The line that ends a run gets them:

```
Dmtank ends its dungeon run in Deadmines after 41 min: every boss it could get to is down (6 of 6 bosses, 0 wipes; ...;
metrics: 58 fights, a member in a fight before the tank in 2 (3%); 5 s or more after the tank: melee 9 of 55 (16%),
healer 3 of 54 (6%), others 6 of 100 (6%); bosses pulled with the whole group ready at the tank: 2 of 6; waits for a
member over 60 yd behind: 4; went on without a resting member: 1; walked 2840 yd)
```

- **A fight** of the group runs from the first character of it in combat until nobody of it has been in combat for
  3 s; it counts once it is over (a run stopped in a fight leaves that fight out). The character its owner plays by
  hand counts as a member.
- **A member before the tank:** the tank (the run's leader: the first tank of the group leads it) came into the fight
  after another member, or not at all. Acceptance target of the Doc: under 10 % (32 % in the owner's runs of 2026-11-14).
- **5 s or more after the tank**, by role: the healer (its dungeon role), melee (`BotDriver::FightsInMelee`), the
  others. Members that did not come into a fight are not counted (only who came, and when). Target: under 10 %
  (rogue 49 %, healer 30 % in the owner's runs).
- **15 yd or more from the tank 5 s into a fight:** where the members stand five seconds after a fight began. The
  members hold back while the tank pulls (DP3, up to 4 s), so they come into a fight late by design; this counts
  whether they are with the tank (the Doc's [quote left out]).
- **Bosses pulled ready:** when a boss of the run's plan is in combat within 80 yd of the leader, once per boss and
  entry, the group is judged: everybody alive and within 15 yd of the tank, health 90 % or more, a healer's mana 80 %
  or more, a damage dealer's 60 % or more (the owner's thresholds for bosses, E2); for the character its owner plays by
  hand only its place counts (E6). A line per boss names what was missing:
  `Dmtank's group pulls Rhahk'Zor in Deadmines: not ready: Dmheal mana 54%, Dmhunt 38 yd away`. Target: every boss.
- **Waits for a member over 60 yd behind:** the squad's "catches up" waits of the leader during the run.
- **Went on without a resting member:** the leader waited for a resting member until `Squads.MaxWaitSeconds` ran out
  and went on (target: none, P6b).
- **Bosses that fell before they were judged:** a boss the group was done with whose pull the run never saw (already
  dead when the group came, or dead within a quarter of a second).
- **Walked:** the leader's way inside (steps of 40 yd or more in a second, teleports and hops, are left out).
  The Doc's target is at most 1.3 times the shortest way from boss to boss; that way comes with P4 (the boss order
  by the length of the way), until then the yards stand alone.

ga-probe scenario `dungeon-metrics` (extended): a run with Probemage and Probepriest, stopped after a fight, its end
line read for the numbers.

### The gate before a boss and a big pull (2026-11-14)

Package P1 of the plan (the Doc [quote left out]; the owner's E2 and E6): no boss and no
big pull before the whole group stands at its tank with its health and mana up (`OrderService::DungeonGate` in
`OrderDungeons.cpp`, called by the run's leader before it walks up to a boss and before a careful pull).

- **What is asked:** every living member within 12 yd of the tank, nobody in a fight, health 90 % or more, a healer's
  mana 80 % or more, a damage dealer's (and a tank's, if it uses mana) 60 % or more. For the character its owner plays
  by hand only its place counts (E6): the group waits until it stands at the tank, and he is told so once in chat; his
  health and mana are his own business. A damage dealer that has nothing to drink anywhere (bags, guild storage, a mage
  of its group) does not hold the group for its mana; it is named once per run.
- **Where:** before a boss, after its room is cleared, at the place the room was fought from (out of the boss's reach),
  or, with an empty room, where the group is when the room would have begun (about 95 yd from the boss); before a careful
  pull (the big pull of today's rules: a pack of `CarefulPullPack` at the tank's level or above, or any pull after a
  wipe or the tank's death in the run) where the tank stands. A fight after the gate opened (a patrol) closes it again
  before the boss.
- **How the members get there:** a member below a threshold is asked to rest up to it (the rest raises its own start
  and end values to the gate's while the gate asks: `BotRuntime::gateHealth / gateMana / gateUntil`, read by
  `StepRest`); it eats and drinks for it. A member farther than 12 yd that does not come is walked to the tank after
  3 s (a point 3 yd behind the tank, its AI held for the walk) and put beside it after a minute (a ledge, a wall the path finder sends it around; a log line names it). There is no
  "120 s, then on" at a gate: it waits until the group is ready.
- **Lines:** `Dmtank's group gathers at its tank before Rhahk'Zor in Deadmines: Dmheal mana 54%, Dmhunt is 38 yd from the
  tank` (when what it waits for changes, at most every 20 s), `Dmtank's group is ready for Rhahk'Zor in Deadmines after 31
  s at its tank`, and the end line's metrics count the gates and their time (`gathered at the tank before a boss or a big
  pull N times (M s)`). The why line reads `In Deadmines: gathering before Rhahk'Zor (...)`.
- The thresholds and the 12 yd are constants for now; they become settings of the run window with package PW.

### The bosses in the order of the way (2026-11-14)

Package P4 of the plan: the bosses of a run come in the order of the way, not of the dungeon finder's encounter ids
(Zul'Farrak's first target had been Hydromancer Velratha 609 yd away, then Antu'sul 534 yd back the other way).
`OrderService::BossOrder` (`OrderDungeons.cpp`) computes it once per dungeon, the first time a group of it stands
inside (the core's path finder needs the instance's map). The ways between the entrance and the bosses are walks on the
whole navmesh with its drops and swims (`DungeonNav::FindWay`; without one the path finder's, with none three times the
straight line), and the order is the shortest from the entrance (Held-Karp over those ways, up to 14 bosses; the way on
to the boss that ends the dungeon counted; more bosses: the nearest each time). A boss the way to the next passes is taken
on the way (it is nearer, and the way through it at most a tenth and 20 yd longer). With the path finder's 148 polygons
Blackfathom Deeps went Gelihast, Lorgus Jett, Twilight Lord Kelris, Old Serra'kis and then back past the entrance to
Ghamoo-ra and Lady Sarevess; the nearest each time went Lorgus before Gelihast, whose cave lies on the way up to him; the
shortest order went to Lady Sarevess past Ghamoo-ra's pool. Now: Ghamoo-ra, Lady Sarevess, Gelihast, Lorgus Jett, Old
Serra'kis, Twilight Lord Kelris, Aku'mai, the order players take (2026-11-25). What has
to stay where it is stays: a stop that must come right before a boss (a hand-listed boss with its `before_boss`, an
event stop: `DungeonBoss::before`) goes with that boss, and the boss that ends the dungeon and event stops that come
after every boss (Mutanus) stay last. The run keeps its order in `DungeonRun::order` (`OrderService::RunBoss`,
`RunBossCount`); a boss once chosen stays the target until it is down or passed over, and one passed over ("does not get
to ...") is tried once more before the boss that ends the dungeon. Doors are opened by the door rule (DG3), so the way
comes to no door the group cannot open but the one Mograine's death opens, which lies before the last boss anyway.

Within a boss's room the creature the group chose stays its next until it is dead or left (`DungeonRun::roomTarget`);
before, the nearest to the room's place was taken anew every second.

The order is one line in the activity log: `the bosses of Zul'Farrak in the order of the way: Antu'sul (...), ... The
list's order was: ...`.

### The conductor: the group walks behind its tank (2026-11-14)

Package P2 of the plan: the group stays together and walks the tank's way instead of a line to it.

- **The way:** four times a second (`OrderService::StepDungeonConductor`, from `OrderService::Update`) the bot that
  leads a run inside records where it walks, a point every 1.5 yd (`DungeonRun::trail`, the newest first; a teleport or
  hop starts it anew).
- **The places:** while the tank walks out of any fight, every AI-played member that does not rest walks that way
  behind it to its place: melee 3 yd, ranged 6 yd, the healer 8 yd behind the tank along the way, two or more of a kind
  side by side (1.6 yd apart, where the ground and the line of sight allow). Its AI is held for those moments (it walks;
  mod-playerbots' follow aims at a point beside the leader and cuts corners through the next pack). A member farther
  than 30 yd runs to the tank first. When the tank stands (a gate, a rest, a wait), the members are left to their own
  AI: buffs, drinks, pets. Not while the tank pulls carefully: the group waits where it is.
- **The spread limit:** the tank stands while a member of its group is farther than 15 yd from it (was 60 yd), and goes
  on when all are back (`OrderService::StepDungeonSpread`, in its once-a-second step); a member that has not come for a
  minute is put beside the tank (a ledge, a wall the path finder sends it around; a log line names it). Not for a member
  that is dead, in a fight, in another instance or played by hand (other rules see to those), and not while an event's
  NPC walks.
- **No "120 s, then on" in a dungeon run:** the leader's wait for a member (it rests, fights, is dead, catches up) lasts
  until the member is with it; ten minutes are the last word.
- **Lines:** `Dmtank stands for its group in Deadmines: Dmheal is 22 yd behind`, `... did not come to its tank Dmtank in
  Deadmines for 60 s (41 yd away): it is put beside it`; the end line's metrics count both (`the tank stood for its group
  N times, M members put beside it`).

### Fight rules: one target, taunts, to the tank (2026-11-14)

Package P5 of the plan, in the fights of a dungeon group (`OrderService::StepDungeonSkull`, `StepDungeonRescue`):

- **One target for all:** the run marks the group's target with the skull (raid target icon 7). mod-playerbots' damage
  dealers and tank take the creature with their icon first (their "rti" value is the skull), so our target choice and
  theirs no longer pull against each other. The skull goes on a creature that attacks the healer (the owner's DP6: the
  group's first concern), else on the tank's own target when it is a creature of the fight; it is taken off when the
  fight is over. The damage dealers are turned by hand only to the healer's attackers; otherwise they follow the skull.
- **Strays:** a creature on another member is the tank's to take back: with two or more such creatures within 8 yd of
  the tank it uses its area threat (Thunder Clap, Consecration, Swipe, Death and Decay, Challenging Shout or Roar; one
  every 6 s), else it taunts the most pressing one in reach (Taunt, Hand of Reckoning, Growl, Dark Command; one every
  1.5 s). It walks there for its healer, for a creature within 15 yd, and (since 2026-11-25) for a creature that
  stays off: one that has been on a member for 3 s and is still more than 15 yd from the tank (a caster shoots from
  where it stands; a member more than 40 yd away does not run to the tank), up to 100 yd, 30 yd while it holds a boss.
  Dire Maul East, 2026-11-25: a Satyr patrol caught the owner's hunter, mage and paladin 60 yd behind the tank, its
  Felsworn cast from there, and the tank stood "in a fight against 0 foes" for 25 s while the mage died with three on it.
- **Aggro means: to the tank.** A healer or a ranged member with a creature on it runs to a point 2.5 yd in front of
  the tank (its AI held for the few seconds of the run), where the tank takes the creature; a melee member only when its
  creature is not the skull. Once per member every 4 s.
- **Lines and numbers:** the help lines name `the tank X taunts it` and `Y runs to the tank`; the end line counts
  `N taunts, M area threats, K runs to the tank`.

### The healer of a dungeon group (2026-11-14)

Package P6a of the plan (the owner's E5: [quote left out]), four times a second for
the group's healer (`OrderService::StepDungeonHealer`, from `OrderService::Update`):

- **No damage spells in a dungeon:** mod-playerbots' strategy "healer dps" is taken from the healer for the run, looked
  at every step (a level-up inside a run resets the strategies by the talents and gave it back once: a priest cast Smite,
  Holy Fire and Shadow Word: Pain for the rest of a Scarlet Monastery run, 2026-11-25; "save mana" likewise while it heals
  through), with a line `had "healer dps" back in <dungeon> (its strategies were reset): it is taken off again`. While
  nobody of the group is below 85 % health it shoots its wand at the group's target (the skull, else the tank's
  target); a healer without a wand (druid, paladin, shaman) does no damage.
- **Healing through** while the fight is heavy: the tank below 70 % and 15 % gone within 3 s, four or more creatures on
  the tank, a boss fight, or anybody below 40 %. Then mod-playerbots' "save mana" is off, and the module casts the
  strongest heal the healer knows (Greater Heal, Heal, Flash Heal, Lesser Heal; Holy Light, Flash of Light; Healing
  Touch, Regrowth; Healing Wave, Lesser Healing Wave) on the tank while it falls, else on the lowest member, whenever the
  healer is not casting. "Save mana" comes back when the fight is over. One line per fight: `Dmheal heals through in the
  fight (a boss fight): ...`; the end line counts the fights.

### The group rests together; the healer keeps the tank in sight (2026-11-14)

Package P6b of the plan (the owner's E2 for the rest):

- **Together, not each for itself:** in a dungeon run a member does not start a rest on its own thresholds any more
  (`StepRest`); the group goes on until a member falls below its trigger (health 50 %, a healer's mana 40 %, a damage
  dealer's 20 %; a damage dealer with nothing to drink anywhere does not count for its mana), and then all of it rests up
  together to 95 % health and mana (`OrderService::StepDungeonGroupRest`, in the run's step; what each rests to is asked
  through the gate's fields). The tank stands meanwhile; three minutes are the last word. Lines: `Dmtank's group rests
  together in Deadmines: Dmmage mana 18%`, `... is rested in Deadmines after 24 s`. A healer with nothing to drink is
  waited for too (2026-11-24: its low mana began the rest, and the rest ended in the same second because only members
  with a drink counted; Ragefire Chasm's group did that three times in a second after Jergosh).
- **Up when the group fights:** a member that rests stands up as soon as another member of its group within 40 yd is
  attacked.
- **The healer keeps the tank in sight:** in a fight, a healer that does not see its tank or stands farther than 36 yd
  from it walks to a place 10 yd from the tank on its own side (or 4 yd behind the tank), once every 3 s
  (`StepDungeonHealer`).
- The end line counts the group's rests and the healer's walks.

### The way in stretches; walk in or pull to a camp (2026-11-14)

Package P3 of the plan (the owner's E3 and E4), in the run's step while the group walks to its next boss
(`OrderService::StepDungeonWay`; the old look 34 yd around the tank, `TryCarefulPull`, is gone):

- **Stretches:** the tank walks to a point at most 35 yd along the path finder's way to the boss and looks again
  there, once a second.
- **What stands on the stretch:** every hostile creature out of a fight whose reach touches the stretch: the core's
  aggro range for the group's lowest member (the character its owner plays included) plus 8 yd, at least 15 yd (E4:
  [quote left out]). The
  nearest one to the tank is engaged before anybody walks past it.
- **Walk in or camp** (E3): its pack (out of a fight within 10 yd of it) is a big pull from 4 creatures, from 6 when the
  group's lowest member is five or more levels above the highest of them, and whenever a caster is among them; after a
  wipe or the tank's death in the run every pull is (the owner's DP1, DP5). A small pack: the owner's release for normal pulls
  first (health 70 %, a healer's mana 50 %, a damage dealer's 30 %, everybody within 15 yd: the gate's normal form),
  then the tank attacks it and the group comes up behind it. A big one: the gate (P1), then the tank pulls the creature
  nearest to it to a camp 25 yd back on the way it came (the conductor's trail), with its ranged opener or by walking
  into its sight (`Escape::BeginPull`); with no pull possible from there it walks in.
- **Lines:** `Zftank walks into Sandfury Blood Drinker (level 45) on its way in Zul'Farrak: 2 creatures with it, the
  reach of its lowest member Zfheal is 15 yd`, `Zftank pulls ... carefully to its group in Zul'Farrak: 5 creatures (the
  camp 25 yd back on its way; ...)`; the end line counts both.
- Not built yet: patrols crossing a stretch (the Doc: wait up to 8 s or pull), the run window's settings for the margin
  and the pull size (package PW), the Farm mode (every room cleared).

### The run's settings (2026-11-17)

Package PW of the plan: the numbers of E2 to E4 are bot settings of the category *Dungeon runs* (the Settings tab,
guild-wide; the value of the bot that leads the run counts): `Dungeons.EngageMargin` (8 yd beyond the lowest
member's aggro range), `Dungeons.BigPullAt` (4 creatures, two more five levels down), `Dungeons.GateHealth`,
`.GateHealerMana`, `.GateDamageMana` (90 / 80 / 60 % before a boss or a big pull). Not built: the choice Progress /
Farm (every room cleared), and the settings per run in the run window (the window's preparation step has the fight
rules of DP4; these are the guild's).

### The buff plan (2026-11-14)

Package P8 of the plan (the owner's E7, §7 DB7 and DB8; `OrderService::StepDungeonBuffPlan`, every 5 s inside a run):

- **Paladins:** mod-playerbots' own blessing plan already gives each kind of blessing to one paladin of the group by
  what it brings: the strongest Blessing of Might and Wisdom by the highest rank and the Improved talents, Kings and
  Sanctuary by the roles, a greater blessing per class. It counts a paladin its owner plays by hand as one of its
  providers (the placeholder AI), so the bots leave his share to him: he is told once per blessing and run (`Your
  group leaves Blessing of Kings to you: its paladins do not cast your share of the blessings.`).
- **Warriors** do not shout over a stronger Blessing of Might (mod-playerbots' trigger compares the two, Commanding
  Presence counted).
- **Shamans:** two or more played by the AI set the totems of their talents inside, the second the other totem of
  each element where it knows it (stoneskin for strength of earth, flametongue for magma or searing, healing stream
  for mana spring, wrath of air for windfury; `BotDriver::ComplementTotems`); in the open world each sets one Searing
  Totem as before.
- **The log** names who gives what once per run (`the buffs of ...'s group in ...: ...`).
- Levelling squads: mod-playerbots' plan works in every party, so the blessings of a squad follow the same rules; the
  totems there stay the one Searing Totem.

Three fixes found in the acceptance runs and on the live server the same evening:

  walks the navmesh's way to a creature out of its sight itself until it is within 8 yd and sees it (`GoForWalkIn`,

### The guild leader in a dungeon run (2026-11-14)

the owner: [quote left out]. The guild leader's own character can be a member of a dungeon group: the run window's group step
lists it first ("(you)"), `DUNGEON_START` takes its guid among the group's characters. It never leads the group:
the first tank among the bots does, else the first bot, and a group needs at least one bot. The run stays the
group's own, automatic run; the leader's character is one of its five, and at every moment either the owner plays
it by hand or the AI plays it (watch mode, *Watch / Take over* on the leader panel and the control bar; also while
the owner plays a bot of his, and in the offline window).

*No wait for a character the AI plays* (2026-11-24). The group's wait for the character played by hand ends when no
character is played by hand any more: a restart in the Wailing Caverns brought the test guild's leader back played by
hand for two seconds, then the owner's client watched it; the wait begun in those seconds was never ended, the "no
nearer to the boss" clock stood still and the group stood eight minutes below Verdan's ledge without its hop.

**No walk of its own while it follows** (2026-11-22). A squad member's NewRpg walk (to its zone's camp, a grind spot, an
NPC) is ended while it follows its leader: mod-playerbots' follow is its weakest action and any such walk wins over it.
the owner's leader, watched in a Sunken Temple run, kept the walk to its zone's camp it had begun before the run for 33
minutes, stood 25 to 54 yd behind its tank and held the group at every gate for up to ten minutes.

**How the character is in the group.** It becomes a squad member of the bot that leads (`SquadService::Set` lets
the guild leader in only for a dungeon group). A leader without an order (it holds its position) gets the order
`IDLE` for the run, so that the planner plays it whenever its owner does not (`ga_dungeon_group_member.in_group` =
2 remembers that); when the group is over it holds again, and a watch mode that ran on that lent order ends. A
leader with an order of its own (`AUTO` ...) keeps it and goes on with it afterwards.

**Played by the AI** (watch mode, or the owner plays another character, or he is offline): it is a member like any
bot: it follows the tank, is taken along by every teleport of the run, holds back for the tank, is brought back by
the group and repaired between runs. It has no dungeon role (docs/dungeon-roles.md DR7), so nothing changes its
talents or gear.

**Played by hand.** The run does not steer it, does not use the guild storage's consumables on it and does not
count it as one of the characters it moves (`OrderService::DungeonGroup` holds only characters the AI plays; the
hand-played one is `DungeonGuest`). What the run does for it:

- *The party.* It joins the bots' party (group loot: its owner rolls himself; the group stays up to 70 s at a
  boss's loot while he is inside). It leaves its own party for that; bots on `FOLLOW` do not come into the dungeon
  group's party.
- *The group stays with it* (`StepDungeonGuest`): while the character is inside and more than 45 yd behind the
  tank, sits (eats or drinks), fights or is dead, the tank waits, for as long as a squad waits for a member
  (`GuildAdventure.Squads.MaxWaitSeconds`, 120 s); then the group goes on and waits again once the character is
  with it. What the character fights, the tank attacks. The stuck clock of the run stands still meanwhile.
- *A death.* Once the group's fight is over the character gets the request a resurrection spell sends (every 30 s
  while its spirit has not been released); accepted, it stands beside the tank. While the character lives, the
  group is not wiped out: the bots come back beside it.
- *Teleports* (`GuildAdventure.Dungeons.TakeOwnerAlong`, on): the character is taken along like the bots: into the
  dungeon at the start (the start waits for it as for a bot that is dead, in a fight or on a flight), ahead with
  the group where the run puts the group on (no way on foot, beside an event's NPC; only when it stands within
  60 yd of the tank, alive and out of a fight), to the entrance after a wipe when it died with the group, out
  and in again between two runs, out at the end. Each with a line in the owner's chat. With
  the setting off the run never moves it: he walks in himself, stays inside at the end, and an order of several
  runs ends at its reset when he is still inside ("its old instance could not be reset").
- *The end of a run* (also *Stop*, and between two runs): the character leaves a moment after its group; when it is
  in a fight, as soon as the fight is over (the server looks every second and a half, for two minutes), and a
  character that lies dead inside, or dies in that fight, is brought back and taken out (`LeaveAfterGroup`). The
  first build left a character that was in a fight inside, alone: in round 88 of the integration server the probe's
  leader was fighting a Defias Overseer when its run was stopped, died there once the bots were gone and stood as a
  spirit at Sentinel Hill's graveyard, which stopped the next round's probe ("You can't chat when you're dead!").
- *The owner logs out, or the server restarts, during a run.* A leader that has an order (its own, or the `IDLE`
  the run lent it) is played on by the AI inside the offline window (`Leader.OfflinePlay`), so it stays a member
  of the group and leaves with the bots at the end. After a restart inside the window the module logs it in again
  with the bots and the group takes its order up anew from the start (in by teleport, or from where its bots
  stand). A leader that is offline when the run ends (no window, `Leader.OfflinePlay` off) keeps its place in the
  database; the core puts a character that logs in on a dungeon map without its instance at that dungeon's
  entrance outside.
- *Names in the party frame.* The client asks for the name of a party member it does not know the moment the party
  is formed, and the run teleports the character in that same moment; the core drops what a client sends while its
  character is between two maps, so the bot that leads stood as "Unknown" in its party frame for the rest of the
  session. The names of the group are sent to its client unasked, before the teleport and once more inside
  (`SendGroupNames`).

**The placeholder AI.** mod-playerbots makes a party member that has no playerbots AI the master of every bot in
that party whose master is a bot or nobody (`PlayerbotAI::UpdateAIGroupMaster` / `FindNewMaster`): with the owner's
character in the party the group would follow him and leave its tank. So a character its owner plays by hand
inside a dungeon group carries a playerbots AI that never runs (`GuildBotHolder::StartPlaceholder`,
docs/take-control.md §5.14): for mod-playerbots it is a bot among bots, for the module it is no AI-played
character (`BotDriver::GetAI` returns none for it, so the loot filter, the quest rules, the ammunition rules and
everything else treat it as the owner's own character). The same holds for a bot of a dungeon group that the owner
takes over during a run.

Log lines: `the guild leader sends a group into ...: <tank> (leads), ..., <leader> (the guild leader's own
character)`, `<leader> is played by hand inside a group of bots: it carries a placeholder AI ...` (Server.log),
`<tank>'s group has waited 120 s for <leader> (is 80 yd behind) in ...: it goes on`, `<leader> is out of the group
of bots: its placeholder AI is gone` (Server.log). Choices taken without the owner: the design log §7 GL1-GL6.

### The dungeon run window (2026-11-13)

**How much the group fights on its way: three modes (2026-11-19).** the owner, on the Farm sweep built the same day (the
whole instance after the last boss): [quote left out]; instead three modes for a run. The run window's last step has *How it fights*:

- **Bosses** (the default): only what would attack the group on its way, the reach of its lowest member (the core's
  aggro range) and 3 yd, at least 10 yd; one pack at a time (a small pack walked into, a big one pulled carefully to the
  group, as P3 has it).
- **Clear: every room on the way**: as well everything in the tank's sight on the way's level within 35 yd of the way
  ([quote left out]); one pack at a time.
- **Clear in big pulls**: as *Clear*, but the tank gathers: the cluster is what stands within *Big pull: within* (15 to
  40 yd, default 25) of the first creature, in its sight and on its level, the nearest to it first, up to *up to* (4 to
  12 creatures, default 6). After the gate before a big pull (the whole group at the tank, its thresholds) the tank's AI
  is held; it runs from creature to creature of the cluster (8 s at most for one, 30 s for all) until that many are on
  it, its health is below half, or the cluster is gathered, and back to where its group waits (15 s at most); the others
  wait there, the healer heals it. After a wipe or the tank's death in the run, one pack at a time (DP1, DP5).

`DungeonFightRules::mode`, `gatherYards`, `gatherCount` (the sixth to eighth field of `ga_dungeon_group_options.fight`),
GADV `DUNGEON_START^md/gr/gc` and `DPREP_BEGIN` the same, `OrderService::StepDungeonWay` (the band, the cluster) and
`StepDungeonGather` (the tank's walk); test aid `.ga admin dungeonrun <id> <runs> <bots> [bosses | rooms | bigpulls]`.
Log lines: `<tank> gathers a big pull in ...: N creatures within 25 yd of ..., until 6 are on it`, `<tank> brings its
big pull back to its group in ...: <why> (N creatures on it)`, `<tank> is back with its group in ... after N s: N
creatures on it at most`; the end line counts the big pulls and the most creatures in one. The Farm sweep of the same
morning is gone (it had cleared 50 creatures of the Deadmines in 21 minutes).

**After an event's boss.** The group stays beside the event's NPC for 20 s before it goes to the boss's corpse for its
loot: Blastmaster Emi Shortfuse blows up the cave Grubbis came out of 12 s after him, and the whole group of the level-34
acceptance run died at his corpse there.

**The dungeons from level 55 at their level (2026-11-19/20, the `dclear` instance).** the owner asked whether every classic
dungeon runs; the ones from 55 on had not been run at their level. Four test groups (levels 56, 58, 60, 60; tank, healer,
mage, rogue, hunter) ran them, and each failing spot was fixed and run again:

- *What holds a boss back is cleared first* (`DungeonBoss::clearFirst`, from the SmartAI conditions "no living creature
  X within N yd" of the boss's own events and of the objects it is woken by): Timmy the Cruel comes when the Scarlets of
  his square are dead, Immol'thar's force field drops when the guardians of the five crystal generators are dead
  (`ga_dungeon_event_template` and `ga_dungeon_wing_template` list Immol'thar before Prince Tortheldrin). The group
  pulls the nearest of them as on the way, leaves one it gets no 5 yd nearer to in a minute, at most 20 minutes, and
  waits up to 30 s for the boss afterwards.
- *Put only where nothing sees it, rest out of sight*: a hop to clear a boss's room goes to a place no idle creature
  sees (rings out to 30 yd farther), and a group rest begins at the first place back along the tank's way that no idle
  creature sees, at most 80 yd (Lower Blackrock Spire's group was put into the ogres' hall; Stratholme's rested beside
  the ghouls of a street).
- *An elite counts three levels higher* when the tank decides how to pull a pack (the owner's E3 rule as it is: a pack is
  pulled to the camp from 4 creatures at the group's level, from 6 when the group is 5 levels above).
- *Traps*: a member that loses health out of a fight twice at one place within a minute (not by a fall or under water,
  not a warlock's Life Tap or a warrior's Bloodrage, not by a lower maximum health), or dies there out of a fight, marks
  a trap there for three minutes; when the group rests near it, it goes back out of it along the tank's way and rests
  there, and it brings nobody back within 25 yd of it (a body there comes back beside one that stands, and not while
  that one stands in it too). A trap beside the way is no reason to turn round: until 2026-11-25 the group went back out
  of it whenever its tank came within 25 yd, with nobody to rest (Dire Maul East, the owner's guild: after Choking Spores hit
  the hunter the group turned round five times in 70 s, "rested after 0 s" each time, beside a Satyr patrol's round,
  which then caught the hunter 60 yd behind the tank).
  The Ironhand Guardians of Blackrock Depths' Iron Hall breathe fire on a timer while Magmus fights and, in this core,
  on after he is dead, without putting anybody in a fight: the group rested and brought its dead back in the hall and
  was wiped out there twice.
- *A boss on another level*: a group that stands 8 yd or more above or below its boss with no way on foot to it is put
  on the boss's floor out of its reach before the pull, once per boss (the way to Immol'thar ended on the top of his
  force field, 18 yd above him; the tank pulled from there and the others dropped down to him one by one and died); and
  inside a dungeon any bot that fights something 8 yd above or below it with no way to it for 8 s is put beside it.
  Not for a boss that cannot be fought yet (Rend Blackhand waits on a balcony over the stadium). A spot the group is put
  at must lie on the navmesh (its path to the boss does not start far from it): Blackrock Depths' group was put 50 yd
  before Lord Incendius on a spot off the navmesh and stood there for two hours; and the hop to clear a boss's room has
  its own once per boss, so the hop before the boss still comes after it.
- *Traps by damage over time*: a DoT counts for a trap unless its caster fights (ruling every DoT out let the group rest
  in the Iron Hall after Magmus and die to the guardians' flames).
- *An event an area trigger starts* (`ga_dungeon_event_template.area_trigger`): a client reports an area trigger when its
  player walks in; a bot has none, so the leader walks into it and reports it the client's way
  (`WorldSession::HandleAreaTriggerOpcode`), once, after the whole group is ready as before a boss. The walk counts only
  while the group walks. Until the boss can be fought the group holds the place where the event began and opens no gate
  (Upper Blackrock Spire: it opened the stadium's wave door, fought in the pen behind it with every wave and was wiped
  out twice; held, the waves, Gyth and Rend fell in eight minutes). The Blackrock Altar wakes Pyroguard Emberseer the way
  objects wake other bosses.
- *What a boss brings belongs to its room*: neutral creatures its script turns on the group (`BossScriptJoiners`: its
  SmartAI "on aggro: set data" on creatures of an entry within a range; Scholomance's Vectus and Marduk Blackpool turn
  the 32 students of the Viewing Room on it, the owner: [quote left out]), and what a
  C++ script calls for help (Emperor Dagran Thaurissan calls his whole throne room, 100 yd). A boss that is no enemy
  until it is attacked has no reach to keep away from (30 yd for splash). A room's place keeps away from the dungeon's
  other bosses (the place in Vectus's room lay 12 yd from Marduk) and 16 yd from the room's other creatures, counting
  the ones left for a minute (a creature in a fight calls those within 10 yd of it every 3 s,
  `CreatureFamilyAssistanceRadius / Period`); when none is found within 45 yd of the boss, one out of its sight only
  (the Emperor's throne room lies all within 45 yd of him). A far place is walked to along the way with its look ahead.
  When the room's time is up and six or more creatures the boss's script would bring are still there, the boss is passed
  over instead of pulled into a sure wipe.
- *Away from creatures that are in no fight yet*: the camp of a careful pull goes farther back along the tank's way (at
  most 60 yd) while a creature that is not pulled would come at it, a rest counts a walking creature's walk, and after
  a fight the group goes back to the first place none of them comes near, once per fight; a patrol is pulled only once
  nobody stands within 12 yd of it (a minute at most, then the careful pull judges its pack). On stairs a creature's
  height is judged against the way where it comes nearest, not against the tank's (Scholomance's hall at the foot of the
  entrance stairs lay 30 yd below the tank until it stood among its creatures).

**Dire Maul West passed (2026-11-21).** The crystal generators that hold Immol'thar's force field stand on two levels:
three on the terraces, two below in the courtyard of his floor, which the terraces join only by drops the path finder
has no way down. Before, the tank stood with the walk to an Arcane Aberration below set and left one creature after the
other, or the group stood on top of the force field 18 yd above his floor with every step down refused. Built: a tank
that gets no 5 yd nearer to a creature that holds a boss back for 20 s walks the core's path itself; a creature it has
no way on foot to puts the group near it, once per creature (as before a boss, DG6); inside a dungeon the ground guard
lets a drop of up to 25 yd pass (its levels are joined that way, the run leads on from below); a member on another
level 20 yd from its leader catches up; and a tank that holds a boss walks to help only within 30 yd (it had left
Tendris Warpwood and his treants for an Ironbark Protector 93 yd away on the healer, and the group was wiped out).
The Ed group (level 60) from the entrance, 12:04 to 12:48, no restart: "is done with Tendris Warpwood (1 of 5)",
Magister Kalendris, Illyanna Ravenoak, "clears what holds Immol'thar back ... first: 34 creatures (Arcane Aberration,
Mana Remnant)", "has cleared what held Immol'thar back", Immol'thar in a fight of 16 s (Vigilance Charm and Demon Howl
Wristguards from his loot), Prince Tortheldrin, "ends its dungeon run in Dire Maul - West after 43 min: every boss it
could get to is down (5 of 5 bosses, 0 wipes ...)"; one death (the mage, to an Ironbark Protector, brought back).

**Scholomance passed (2026-11-21).** In eight runs before the group stopped in three places: (1) the hall at the
foot of the entrance stairs (43 creatures, most of them walking about their spawns and linked by the 10 yd calls for

Necrofiends and Risen Lackeys on the way to the Viewing Room's far side. What made the difference: the way counts a
creature's walk about its spawn (`engageOf`: its wander distance on top of its reach); a creature on a round of
waypoints and one in a formation behind its leader count as watching a place (`IdleSees`); the group rests away from
patrol rounds, up to 220 yd back along its trail where the fewest creatures watch (`restWalkLimit`); and in the room of
a boss a neutral creature that joins, 20 yd or more from every boss, is fought where it stands (the owner: [quote left out]), the students one at a time or in their small groups. The run of
the Ec group (level 60, rooms mode), 08:20 to 11:18 with four restarts of the test server in between (the stress test
and three installs; the run went on inside each time, the bosses killed before a restart stayed dead): "is done with
Vectus ... Marduk Blackpool ... Ras Frostwhisper ... The Ravenian ... Lord Alexei Barov ... Lady Illucia Barov ...
Instructor Malicia ... Doctor Theolen Krastinov ... Lorekeeper Polkelt ... Rattlegore ... Jandice Barov ... Darkmaster
Gandling (12 of 12)", "ends its dungeon run in Scholomance ...: every boss it could get to is down (12 of 12 bosses, 0

**The Dire Maul tribute run (2026-11-21, `OrderTribute.cpp`).** the owner: [quote left out] (with a guide to it): the guards and the other named ogres of Dire Maul North live, only
King Gordok dies, and the more of the six (Guard Mol'dar, Stomper Kreeg, Guard Fengus, Guard Slip'kik, Captain
Kromcrush, Cho'Rush the Observer) live, the better the Gordok Tribute. AzerothCore scripts all of it in the world
database (SmartAI): the Broken Trap is the giver of quest 1193, whose reward summons the fixed trap and has Slip'kik
freeze when his round reaches it; Knot Thimblejack's quest 5518 gives the Gordok Ogre Suit; Kromcrush's gossip option
(menu 5738) makes him storm off; King Gordok's death turns Cho'Rush friendly and summons Mizzle the Crafty, whose gossip
crowns (King of the Gordok, 22799; the ogres are friendly then) and summons the tribute (menu 5740), and the instance
script gives the tribute a loot mode by how many of the six died (`instance_dire_maul.cpp`). The guards' gossip gives
their buffs to the new king. So the group does the steps a player group does:

- The run window offers the mode *Tribute run: the guards live* for Dire Maul North only (`DUNGEON_START^md=3`,
  `.ga admin dungeonrun 38 1 <bots> tribute`). It starts only with the materials in the guild storage: 1 Frost Oil and 1
  Thorium Widget for the trap, 4 Bolts of Runecloth, 8 Rugged Leather and 2 Rune Thread for the suit (the owner's choice
  of the default: else it does not start, and what is missing goes on the shopping list when vendors sell it or becomes
  a craft order). The materials go into the leader's bags at the start, and the run's consumables leave the Frost Oil
  alone (the first test run put it on a weapon).
- The bosses of the run are King Gordok alone; the six are never pulled, are no blockers, patrols or packs of the way,
  no rescue goes for them, and no member keeps one as its target (another foe of the fight, else none; pets too).
  One that comes at the group before the throne room is fought after all, and the tribute is smaller by one.
- The steps, each checked against the world first (a door open, a key in the bags, Slip'kik frozen), so a wipe or a
  restart picks up where they are: the Gordok Courtyard Key out of Fengus's Chest while Fengus is 30 yd or more from it
  (waited for from 45 yd, his round passes the chest three times); the courtyard door with it; the Broken Trap repaired
  while Slip'kik is 22 yd or more from it; the Ogre Tannin out of its basket (a Gordok Bushwhacker comes); the suit at
  Knot; then the group waits by Knot for Slip'kik to walk into the trap (at most six minutes); the inner door; the
  leader puts on the suit 70 yd from Kromcrush, walks straight to him while the group stands, and talks to him; King
  Gordok by the boss loop. A guard on his round near the stretch the leader walks next (Fengus, Slip'kik) is waited
  for off his round (three minutes at most), and a leader that has not got on for half a minute out of a fight walks
  the core's path to the step's point itself for 25 s.
- The suit (quest 5518) is given once per character: the leader makes it when it never had the quest, else another
  bot of the group that never had it (not the owner's own character); that member opens the basket itself (the
  tannin binds when it is picked up), takes the runecloth, leather and thread of the guild storage, hands the quest in
  at Knot and gives the suit to the leader (it binds to nobody, as in a trade). A suit somebody carries from before is
  used as it is. With nobody left who could make one, Kromcrush is fought.
- The inner door (the owner's list): a rogue of the group with Lockpicking 300, else an engineer (Engineering 200) with a
  Large Seaforium Charge of the guild storage, else a blacksmith (Blacksmithing 200) with a Truesilver Skeleton Key of
  it (the charge and the key are used up), else Guard Mol'dar is killed first for the Gordok Inner Door Key.
- A step that cannot be done costs one ogre: it is put into the run's bosses before King Gordok (no trap: Slip'kik; no
  tannin or suit: Kromcrush). The normal run's door rule leaves the two Gordok doors to the tribute run.
- After King Gordok: every member is crowned by Mizzle (once his walk ends and he offers his gossip, at most three
  minutes), the leader asks for the tribute and opens it (the group's loot rolls as for a chest), and every member gets
  the buff of a guard that lives within 60 yd of the throne (two hours). The walks across the halls to Fengus and
  Mol'dar are left out: in the sixth test run both came at the group although every member wore the crown, and two
  members died. Then the run ends.

Tests on `dclear` (the Ef group, level 60; its rogue given Lockpicking 300 for the test, so Mol'dar lives), nine runs

the owner: [quote left out]

It is built in stages. **Stage A (this section): the choice of the dungeon, the group, the number of runs, the start
with the teleport, the way out and the reset between runs, the stop.** Stage B: the dungeons unlock one after the
other. Stage C: the preparation (talents for the run, consumables out of the guild storage, how the group fights).

**The addon** (the main window's *Dungeons* tab, `UI/Extras.lua`; no modal window, the rest of the UI stays usable).
Four steps on the left, the runs that are going on the right:

1. *Dungeon*: the five-player dungeons, by level, each with its level range and how many of the guild's bots are
   ready for it; a dungeon a run cannot be ordered into yet is grey.
2. *Group*: the guild's bots with class, level, role (their dungeon role, else the role of their talents), their
   readiness for the dungeon and, for a tank or healer, the readiness in its dungeon set. A click puts a bot into
   the group or takes it out (up to the dungeon's size). Bots that are benched, offline, played by the owner or on
   a run already cannot be picked. The line below says who tanks and who heals, and who is not ready.
3. *Preparation* (stage C, below): what each bot goes as, what the group may use out of the guild storage, how it
   fights. Nothing there has to be changed.
4. *Start*: how often (1, 2, 3, 5, 10 runs, or until it is stopped), and *Start*.

The list on the right shows every run of the guild: the dungeon, who leads and how many follow, where the group is
(getting ready; inside with the bosses down and the next one), which run of how many, wipes, minutes; *Last run*
makes the run that is going the order's last, *Stop* ends it at once.

**The server** (`OrderService::StartDungeonGroup`, `StopDungeonRun`, `DisbandDungeonGroup`, `GetDungeonRunStatus`,
all in `OrderDungeons.cpp`; GADV `DUNGEON_START`, `DUNGEON_STOP`, block `DRUNS`, docs/protocol.md section 7.24).

- **The group.** The chosen bots become the squad of one of them for the run: the first tank (dungeon role, else
  talents), else the first bot; that bot gets the order `DUNGEON` with its runs, and everything a dungeon order
  does applies (roles, loot rolls, the readiness rule of 50 %). What they were before is written down
  (`ga_dungeon_group`: the leader's order and zone; `ga_dungeon_group_member`: the squad leader each bot followed,
  also for followers of a chosen bot that stay outside and play their own order meanwhile) and comes back when the
  order is over, also after a restart of the server, and also when the owner gives the leading bot another order.
- **In.** `GuildAdventure.Dungeons.Teleport` (on; it holds for every dungeon order, also `.ga admin order ...
  DUNGEON`): nobody walks to the entrance. The leader waits until every character of the group is alive, out of
  combat, not on a flight and not inside the dungeon any more (six minutes at most, then the start is given up and
  the log says who was not free), then come the steps that were at the entrance before (tanks and healers change
  talents and set where they stand, the dungeon is reset when
  somebody is still bound to an old instance, the hourly limit), and everybody is teleported to the dungeon's
  entrance inside.
- **Out.** `GuildAdventure.Dungeons.LingerSeconds` (30) after the last boss the run ends: every character is
  teleported to its hearthstone place (`m_homebind...`), also after a run that failed. With more runs the next one
  starts there: repairs and bag space as before, the reset (nobody is inside any more), the hourly limit, in again.
- **How often.** 1 to `GuildAdventure.Dungeons.MaxRuns`, or until it is stopped (`runs` 0 in the protocol and in
  `.ga admin order <bot> DUNGEON <id> 0`; 255 in `ga_bot_dungeon_runs` and in `BOT^druns`). A run that fails ends
  the order, as before.

```
activity: the guild leader sends a group into Deadmines: Tankwar (leads), Probepriest, Probemage; run after run until it is stopped
activity: Tankwar goes into Deadmines with 3 characters
activity: Tankwar's group is through with Deadmines: it leaves in 30 s
activity: Tankwar's order goes on with another run of Deadmines (1 done; until it is stopped)
activity: the dungeon group of Tankwar is over: its bots are what they were before (1 squad link back); Tankwar has the order AUTO again
```

Test aids without a client: `.ga admin dungeonrun <dungeon id> <runs> <bot> [<bot> ...]` (the guild leader's own
character may be named among the bots), `.ga admin dungeonstop
<bot that leads> [now]`.

**Stage B: the dungeons in their order** (`GuildAdventure.Dungeons.UnlockInOrder`, on; the owner: [quote left out]). The order (`OrderService::DungeonOrder`) is the
list of the five-player dungeons of the guild's side that a run can be ordered into, by lowest level, then target
level, then id; dungeons that cannot be run yet (the wings on shared maps) are not in it, so they do not block the
ones behind them, and come into the order where their level puts them once they can be run. The first dungeon is
open. A run that brings the end boss down (the boss the dungeon finder names as the last; where it names none, every
boss of the list) counts as finished for the guild (`ga_guild_dungeon`: runs, first and last time) and opens the
next dungeon, for good; a run that passes the end boss over, or fails, does not. The run window and the Orders
sub-tab refuse a dungeon that is not open yet and name the one to finish first; the test aids of `.ga admin` are
not bound. For the Alliance at level cap 60 today: Deadmines, Wailing Caverns, Shadowfang Keep, Blackfathom Deeps,
Stormwind Stockade, Razorfen Kraul, Gnomeregan, Razorfen Downs, Uldaman, Zul'Farrak, Sunken Temple, Scholomance
(`.ga admin dungeondone <character>` lists it for a guild with what is finished and open; with a dungeon and a
number it sets what the guild has finished, a test aid).

```
activity: the guild of Tankwar has finished Deadmines for the first time: Wailing Caverns is open now
```

The addon's dungeon list follows the order (`DUNGEON^ord`), shows how often each was finished (`fin`) and what is
locked and why (`lock`, `need`); the server sends the dungeons again when the guild finishes one.

**Stage C: the preparation** (the owner: [quote left out]; [quote left out]; and on the fight rules: [quote left out]). The window's third step has three parts:

- **Talents for the run.** One line per bot of the group with a choice: *As it levels* (no dungeon role: it keeps
  its levelling talents and gear), or *Tank* / *Healer* with one of the role's talent templates, for the roles its
  class can fill. The choice is the bot's dungeon role (`ROLE_SET`, docs/dungeon-roles.md): it is set at once, the
  talents and the dungeon set change at the start of the run and change back after it, and the role stays with the
  bot for later runs (and for what it collects while it levels).
- **From the guild storage.** The kinds of items in the guild storage that a run can use (`DungeonSupplies::List`):
  elixirs and flasks, scrolls that leave a buff of five minutes or more, stones and oils for a weapon (a temporary
  enchantment), scopes. **Every kind is ticked** and the leader takes out what he does not want used (the owner,
  2026-11-14: [quote left out]; until then nothing
  was ticked by itself). What he took out stays out for the next runs of his session. **Once at the start of a run
  and once after a wipe**, at its first quiet moment inside (alive, out of a fight), each character of the group
  uses **what fits it best** out of the storage (`DungeonSupplies::Use` with the character's role; nothing is used
  again when it runs out during the run): of the elixirs one battle and one guardian elixir (a flask is both), of
  the scrolls one, each rated like gear (`BotDriver::BuffScore`: the stats the buff gives, times the stat weights
  the character's gear is rated with: a tank's or a healer's by its dungeon role, a damage dealer's
  mod-playerbots' weights of its talents); what rates nothing for the character, or does nothing for how it fights,
  is left alone, a kind whose effect it has already is not used, and neither is a piece that would not stack with
  something on the character or with a piece chosen before it (the core's spell groups: no scroll of spirit under a
  priest's Divine Spirit, no scroll of stamina under Power Word: Fortitude, and on this core no second scroll at
  all, group "Scrolls"; the next best piece is taken instead), nor a weaker rank of a buff that is on the character
  (a Scroll of Stamina II would take a Scroll of Stamina III's place). (The first build rated buffs with
  mod-playerbots' item rating; that reads no spell of the potion family, so no elixir was ever chosen. A scroll used
  before the group's priest has cast its buff may be replaced by that buff.) Then, the strongest first: a stone on the main or off hand weapon of a melee character, a poison for a rogue, an oil for a caster, when
  the weapon has no temporary enchantment; a scope on a hunter's bow, gun or crossbow that has no enchantment (a
  scope stays on the weapon). A piece that did nothing (a stronger effect was on the bot) goes back into the storage
  and is not tried again for ten minutes. Every piece is a line of the activity log with what is left. The choice
  holds for that order (`ga_dungeon_group_options.items`), through every run of it and through a restart.
- **How the group fights.** The four rules of "How a dungeon group fights" for this order: how long the others wait
  for the tank (off, 2 to 8 s), below which health the healer heals while they wait (30 to 70 %), careful pulls (off,
  or from 2 to 5 creatures), and whether creatures that run away are focused. Untouched they are the server's
  (`GuildAdventure.Dungeons.TankLeadSeconds / EmergencyHealth / CarefulPulls / CarefulPullPack / FocusFleeing`);
  changed they hold for that order (`ga_dungeon_group_options.fight`, `OrderService::GetFightRules`).

```
activity: the guild leader sends a group into Deadmines: Tankwar (leads), Probepriest, Probemage; 2 runs; it may use 3 kinds of items of the guild storage; fight rules: wait for the tank 6 s, emergency heals below 50%, careful pulls off, fleeing creatures focused
activity: Tankwar used 1 x Coarse Sharpening Stone out of the guild storage for its dungeon run (on its Heavy Mace) (19 left there)
activity: Probemage used 1 x Elixir of Wisdom out of the guild storage for its dungeon run (4 left there)
```

GADV: `GET^what=dungeonprep` (block `DPREP`: the server's fight rules and one `DITEM` per kind), `DUNGEON_START`
with `items` and `tl / em / cp / cpon / ff` (docs/protocol.md section 7.24). Test aid without a client: `.ga admin
dungeonitems <character> [<item> [clear]]` (what the storage holds for a run; with an item the character uses that kind now,
as a run's group does).

Open: a group without a tank or a healer is not refused, dungeons on shared maps (the wings of the Scarlet
Monastery), a vendor trip between runs instead of the repairs on the spot, elite and group quests in the open
world.

### Raid runs (2026-11-21)

The classic raids are dungeon runs of a bigger group (the maintainers' brief: playable and automatically runnable by a
guild raid of up to 40 bots, on the leader's order only; the design log section 6 "Next steps" 18). Everything of a dungeon
run holds for them (the run window, roles and dungeon sets, consumables, the three modes, event stops, wipes, the guild
leader as a member); this section is what is different.

**Which raids.** The readiness list's raids of the level cap 60: Molten Core (LFG id 48), Blackwing Lair (50), Zul'Gurub
(42), the Ruins of Ahn'Qiraj (160), the Temple of Ahn'Qiraj (161). Onyxia and Naxxramas are level-80 raids in 3.3.5a.
`Dungeons::Load` makes a plan of each (`DungeonPlan::raid`, `size` 20 or 40): its entrance in the open world (Molten
Core's window in Blackrock Mountain, area trigger 3528), or, for Blackwing Lair, whose only trigger lies in Upper
Blackrock Spire, that trigger's inside with Upper Blackrock Spire's own entrance as the place outside (the run takes the
raid in by teleport). Its bosses are the spawned encounters, in the order of the way, like a dungeon's.

**Bosses the instance brings.** `ga_dungeon_event_template` has a place now (`x`, `y`, `z`) and `gossip_steps`:
- a row with no NPC, no object and a place is a boss the raid waits for there (`DungeonBoss::summoned`): Molten Core's
  Majordomo Executus, whom the instance summons when the seven rune bosses are dead. The group walks to his place after
  the bosses he comes before and waits up to the row's timeout (180 s) for him; when he does not come (he fell this week,
  or a rune boss lives) it goes on. After his defeat he is the raid's friend and the run leaves him;
- a talk NPC without a spawn takes the row's place: Majordomo in the lair of Ragnaros, where the leader picks option 0
  three times (menus 4093, 4109, 4108) and Majordomo summons Ragnaros, who emerges after the intro (the row's timeout 420 s).
  An event stop whose boss is the raid's end encounter (`instance_encounters.lastEncounterDungeon`) is `last`: its kill
  finishes the raid (a dungeon's event bosses do not, DE2).

**The raid group.** A squad holds five and a party five; the core lets nobody onto a raid map who is not in a raid group
(`MapMgr::PlayerCannotEnter`). So:
- the dungeon group of a raid run is one squad of up to 40 (the squads' size rule does not hold while the run window forms
  a dungeon group, `SquadService::AllowAnyLevel`);
- the leader's party becomes a raid group as soon as it is full (`KeepSquadGroup`) and at every step of the run
  (`OrderService::KeepRaidGroup`): the first tank by its dungeon role (the leader when it tanks) carries the main tank
  flag, the other tanks the assistant flag, which is what mod-playerbots' main and assist tanks are made of
  (`PlayerbotAI::GetMainTankGuid`, `IsAssistTank`);
- before the leader goes in, the raid group forms: the leader waits until it leads a raid group and the whole group is
  in it (two minutes at most for those still on their way into it; a raid group that does not form in three minutes ends
  the run).

**Raid rules in the run.** No reset at the entrance: a raid's lockout holds for the week, the raid goes into its saved
instance, and what fell there stays dead and is counted when the raid comes to its place. Five wipes end a raid run
(two a dungeon run), and a raid run may take five hours. One run per order (`ga_bot_dungeon_runs` gets 1 whatever the
window asked for). The formation has rows: five places a row, each next row 2.5 yd farther back; the spread halt waits
for members 25 yd away (15 in a dungeon).

**Boss mechanics.** mod-playerbots has boss strategies for Molten Core (Living Bomb out of the raid, Baron Geddon's
Inferno, Shazzrah, the lava, Golemagg and his Core Ragers, the core hounds' marks, resistance auras and totems),
Blackwing Lair, Zul'Gurub and the Ruins, and puts them on by itself on the raid's map
(`PlayerbotAI::ApplyInstanceStrategies`, also after every strategy reset of the module, `Playerbots.ApplyInstanceStrategies
= 1`). What the module adds:
- *creatures that burst at their death* (`OrderService::StepRaidBursts`, a hand list): while one is below its health line,
  every member but its own tank steps out of its reach for 1.5 s (Garr's Firesworn: Eruption at their death, 15 yd, below
  30 %; the first Molten Core raid lost 30 characters in four seconds to eight of them);
- *creatures whose fire pulses round them all through a fight* (`OrderService::StepDungeonPulsers`, a hand list in
  `PulserOf`; Molten Core's Flame Imps: Fire Nova, 10 yd, every 4 to 7 s, about 500 a nova): only a tank stands among
  them. A melee damage dealer with nothing on it holds back while they fight (its attack on one stops, its walk into
  their reach stops at the edge), who stands in a pulse without one of them on it steps to the nearest place out of the
  reach of all of them, nobody runs "to the tank" while the tank stands among them, and a melee member does not turn to
  one that is on the healer (the owner, 2026-11-27: [quote left out];
  his raid of 40 walked into twenty imps and died in 15 s). The line: `the group in Molten Core keeps out of the pulse
  of Flame Imp (only its tank stands among them; melee damage dealers hold back while they fight)`;
- *a boss that wiped the raid twice is left for that run* and the raid goes on to the next (`DungeonRun::bossWipes`), as a
  guild raid does with a boss beyond it: the five wipes are for the whole raid, not five tries at its first wall;
- *repairs* at the start of a raid run and after each wipe, where the raid stands (the dungeon run's field repair);
- *Hakkar's Blood Siphon* (`OrderService::StepRaidHakkar`): every 90 s from 90 s into the fight it heals Hakkar from each
  character in 100 yd that has no Poisonous Blood and hurts him from each that has it. The poison (90 s) comes from the
  cloud a Son of Hakkar leaves where it dies (8 yd, 10 s); the core casts the cloud's spell (24320) but does not apply its
  effect, so the module's spell script `spell_ga_poisonous_blood` gives the poison (a `spell_script_names` row in
  `ga_dungeon_events.sql`). In the 60 s before a siphon the raid's assist tanks and ranged kill a Son within 60 yd of
  Hakkar and everybody without the poison but Hakkar's own tank steps into its cloud (one line per siphon each);
- *in a raid the ranged open on a room creature* the group walks into (`rangedOpen`): where no way on foot leads to it
  (Hakkar's platform) it comes to them;
- *a boss an object brings* (Arlokk: the Gong of Bethekk, a `ga_dungeon_event_template` row before Hakkar): a group
  that gets no 3 yd nearer to the object in a minute is put beside it, but only where the navmesh has no way on foot
  there (since 2026-11-27: the owner's raid walked on to the gong and was put beside it 31 yd short of it, the minute having
  run from where it first came within 30 yd; the navmesh has a flat walk of 80 yd from the east), and a boss that was
  seen and is not found alive any more counts as done only with its corpse there (Arlokk vanishes in her fight);
- *out of a trap* (`StepRaidBursts`' trap list: Kurinnaxx's Sand Trap, 9 yd): everybody steps to 13 yd from it;
- *a tank swap by debuff stacks* (`OrderService::StepRaidTankSwap`, a hand list: Kurinnaxx's Mortal Wound at 5 stacks):
  an assist tank of the raid (its assistant flag) with at most one stack within 25 yd taunts the boss, and the raid's
  main tank flag goes to it;
- *Ossirian's crystals* (`OrderService::StepRaidOssirian`): while his Strength is on or his weakness ends within 10 s his
  tank walks him to the crystal nearest to where its raid stands, and a member uses a crystal within 28 yd of him
  (`GameObjectAI::GossipHello(player, true)`: the crystal's trigger casts a weakness within 30 yd); while his Strength
  is on and no crystal is near him the raid holds where it stands and nobody goes to help. His first crystal stands
  126 yd from his terrace: the raid waits there (*a boss pulled to a place*, a hand list in `PullPlaceOf`, also the
  place a group with no way on foot is put at), its tank walks up alone on foot, taunts him from 29 yd (Shield Wall or
  the like with it) and runs back. What stands within 70 yd of that place is fought first, and a pull that meets a fight
  on its way stops and is made again from the place (an Anubisath Guardian 57 yd from the crystal). Healers heal through
  the hold. Eight tries failed (2026-11-22: his Strength killed the tank on those 100 yd, his War Stomp at 30 s twelve
  of the raid, the healers' threat on a tank that deals no damage on the way back took him off it); the ninth killed him
  2 min after the pull with 31 deaths: a threat list written once a second showed his victim going from the tank to a
  hunter's pet, rogues, the second tank, warlocks and priests, a member's crystal use 15 s in that took his Strength
  off, and the raid's damage on him from then on;
- *Razorgore's eggs* (`OrderService::StepRaidRazorgore`): while eggs are left (the instance's egg event) the run does not
  pull him (damage that kills him in that phase kills the raid); Grethok and his guards at the Orb of Domination are
  fought first, then a mage, rogue, warrior or priest without a dungeon role uses the orb (`GameObject::Use`: he is
  possessed for 90 s, Mind Exhaustion 60 s after, the next member takes over) and the module walks him from egg to egg
  and casts Destroy Egg (a bot has no client to steer him); with the 30th egg his second phase begins and the run
  fights him as any boss;
- *a boss that is its own NPC* (Vaelastrasz the Corrupt: a `ga_dungeon_event_template` row with two gossip menus, 21333
  and 21334): it is not taken for there already while it is friendly; after the talk he turns hostile;
- *the list's order* for Blackwing Lair and the Temple of Ahn'Qiraj (`BossOrder`): their levels lie over each other, and
  the way's order sent the raid to Firemaw first, through the suppression room before Broodlord Lashlayer;
- *the way players come to a boss* (`ApproachPlaceOf`, a hand list): a group with no way on foot to Broodlord Lashlayer
  is put in the suppression room 45 yd west of him on his floor, and his room is fought from there. The hop round him
  from Vaelastrasz's room (the side the group came from) had put the raid of 40 behind his portcullis beside Firemaw,
  who came with his room and wiped it;
- *a formation that comes whole*: the pack the tank walks into or pulls counts every member of the blocker's formation
  whose members assist each other (`creature_formations` with an assist flag), however far apart they stand; Blackwing
  Lair's formations of 14 (a Death Talon Overseer with technicians, warlocks and spellbinders) were "an Overseer with 2
  creatures" before and wiped the raid; counted whole they are big pulls to the camp;
- *Chromaggus's lever* (a `ga_dungeon_event_template` row with the lever 179148 as the object to use): he is immune to
  everything behind his door until it is used; the object is used as a client uses it, `GameObject::Use` and then the
  report of the use (`GameObjectAI::GossipHello(player, true)`, on which the lever alone acts), and a group that gets no
  nearer to an object on another floor in a minute is put beside it;
- *Nefarian's talk* (a row: Lord Victor Nefarius, three menus 21330, 21331, 21332, option 0 each): 42 drakonids from the
  two spawners, then Nefarian flies in and lands at the end of his path; Victor Nefarius dies with him, so a body of the
  event's boss after the talk counts as its kill.
- *whirlwinds* (`StepRaidBursts`, a hand list: Battleguard Sartura and her Royal Guards): a whirlwind hits everybody
  within 10 yd once a second and runs after a random member, whoever holds the creature; everybody within 12 yd of one
  that whirls steps out of it, its tank too, a healer and who fights from afar keep 18 yd from such a creature while it
  lives, nobody runs to the tank with one on it, and her guards get the skull before her (`KilledFirst`); her room has a
  hand approach place (`ApproachPlaceOf`). The raid of 40 stacked at its tank lost half its members in ten seconds
  before; with the rules Sartura fell with 3 deaths (2026-11-22);
- *Viscidus's globs*: shattered, he comes back with 5 % of his health for each glob that reaches him, so the globs get
  the skull first, the one nearest to him (they attack nobody and were no creatures of the fight);
- *spreading out* (`StepRaidBursts`, a hand list: Princess Huhuran): her Noxious Poison lands on a random member and
  hits everybody within 15 yd of it (750 nature damage every 2 s and a silence), her Poison Bolt the 15 nearest; a
  healer and who fights from afar keep 23 to 34 yd from her and 10 yd from each other while she lives (the nearest such
  place in her sight, on her floor, with a path), so a poison hits few of them, the healers are not silenced together,
  and the bolts fall on the melee. The raid of 40 that stood within 20 yd of her was wiped out 80 s after the pull;
  spread out, she fell 72 s after it with 18 deaths, nearly all melee in her berserk below 30 % (2026-11-23);
  High Priest Venoxis (Zul'Gurub) in his troll form casts Holy Wrath at the one he hits, and it jumps to the nearest
  other within 10 yd and both their sizes, up to 50 times, half as much again at each jump: the owner's raid of 20 stood
  together at its tank and lost seven at once to the sixth to thirteenth jump (3085 to 55304 damage, 2026-11-26).
  While he is above 50 % (his snake form casts it no more) everybody but the one he hits keeps 22 to 34 yd from him
  and 16 yd from the others, the melee too: their AI is held out there and they do not attack (one that something
  else attacks fights it); below 50 % they come in;
- *Gurubashi Bat Riders* (Zul'Gurub, the trash round Jeklik): below 30 % one casts Unstable Concoction (3 s, 4375
  fire within 10 yd); a row of the burst list with the spell: from 38 % down to 30 % everybody but its tank keeps 13 yd
  from it, while it casts its tank too, and below 30 % without the cast it has cast it. The owner's raid of 20 fought ten
  creatures (two bat patrols, a witch doctor, the riders) at its tank and lost 15 members in one second (2026-11-27);
- *High Priestess Jeklik* (Zul'Gurub) is pulled down, not walked up to: the navmesh has no way onto her platform (a
  part of 53 polygons 12 yd above the floor round it, no chain of steps under 9 yd; `tools/navpath` ISLAND), and
  players do not climb it either: pulled, she flies her intro path (`boss_jeklik`, PATH_JEKLIK_INTRO) to (-12274,
  -1408) on the floor and fights there. She is a row of the pull place list with a place to pull from: the raid
  walks to her landing (the boss walk, its clock and the hop ask the way to the place, not to her), clears what
  stands within 70 yd of it that it can walk to (not the bats on her platform), and her tank walks to a point under
  her flight 26 yd from her and taunts her. The owner's raid was put up to her by a teleport, "a way players swim or
  jump" (2026-11-27);
- *Bloodlord Mandokir* (Zul'Gurub): the Vilebranch Speaker's death starts him (he rides down 6 s later and puts the
  whole instance in his fight), so the speaker is a hand-listed boss before him (`ga_dungeon_wing_template`) and the
  raid gathers and gets ready before it; a member he watches with Threatening Gaze stops attacking and casting until
  the gaze is gone (`OrderService::StepFast`: any threat on him meanwhile ends in his charge and Guillotine, and every
  kill raises his Level Up); his Whirlwind is a row of the whirl list (everybody within 12 yd steps out). The owner's raid
  of 20 killed the speaker as a creature on its way, scattered and low on mana, lost three members to Guillotine and
  four to the Whirlwind, and was wiped (2026-11-26);
- *the Twin Emperors' marks* (`StepDungeonSkull`): Vek'nilash takes no magic damage, Vek'lor no physical damage, and
  what one takes the other takes too (Twin Empathy, by the share of its health); the skull marks Vek'nilash, the cross
  Vek'lor, and each member's own "rti" value of mod-playerbots (`BotDriver::SetRti`) is the cross when it deals magic
  damage (a mage, warlock or priest, a druid or shaman that fights from afar), else the skull; back to the skull after
  the fight. Everybody keeps out of Vek'lor's Arcane Burst (10 yd, a whirlwind row with aura 0: always while he
  fights). The bugs of their room (Qiraji Scarabs and Scorpions, neutral until Vek'lor makes one explode, 2813 fire
  damage within 15 yd, or Vek'nilash mutates one) belong to his room within 100 yd (`BossScriptJoiners`), and the
  room is cleared from the floor between the thrones (`ApproachPlaceOf`). **Not enough to kill them:** in four tries
  the raid of 40 was wiped out with the twins at 82 to 100 % (2026-11-23): they fight within 60 yd of each other, so
  each heals the other 30000 every 3.6 s, and after every swap (30 to 40 s) each attacks the member nearest to where it
  appears. What they want is a fight on two sides (see the open list below);
- *an Anubisath Defender's Plague and Explode* (`StepRaidBursts`): a member that carries the Plague (1008 nature
  damage every 3 s to all within 5 yd of it) goes where nobody stands within 8 yd of it, and everybody but its tank
  keeps 20 yd from a Defender below 11 % (it explodes for 4688 fire damage within 20 yd); one Defender with the Plague
  killed 27 of the raid on the way from Huhuran to the twins.

**Raid buffs.** mod-playerbots casts a raid-wide buff only with its reagent in the caster's bags, else the single buff on
each of the 40 characters (its priests went to 0 % mana buffing during the first raid's rests). `KeepRaidGroup` takes the
reagents out of the guild storage, up to 20 for a caster that carries fewer than 5: Sacred or Holy Candles (Prayer of
Fortitude and Spirit), Wild Thornroot or Wild Berries (Gift of the Wild), Arcane Powder (Arcane Brilliance), Symbols of
Kings (the greater blessings); a line per take. A guild that raids keeps them on its shopping list.

**Drink in a raid.** Each rest of a dungeon or raid holds the whole group, so a kind out of the guild storage at least 20
levels better than what a bot carries comes first there (`StorageSupply::TakeOne`): raid healers of level 60 drank level-1
water for minutes before.

**Tests** (2026-11-21, dev instance `raid`, a test guild of 40 recruits boosted to level 60 with rare gear,
`.ga admin boost <bot> 60 rare`, four tanks and nine healers by dungeon role; SOAP, no client). Rooms mode (mode 2) is the
mode for a raid: in bosses mode the 40 walked into packs on the way and Baron Geddon came with them.

| Raid | Group | Result | What stopped it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Molten Core | 40 | 10 of 10 in 53 min, 0 wipes (rooms; the instance had Gehennas and Garr dead from a bosses-mode try); then **a fresh instance (the 40 unbound): 10 of 10 in 140 min, 0 wipes**, 115 deaths all brought back, 7 of 10 bosses pulled with the whole raid ready, Ragnaros 4 min after the talk | — |
| Zul'Gurub | 20 | 6 of 7 in 122 min, 2 wipes; on 2026-11-22 with the Hakkar rules, four more tries at Hakkar in rare gear (14 to 45 %), then **Hakkar down in epic gear** (3.5 min, 1 death) | Arlokk's gong is struck, but her arena below the gong's pyramid has no way on foot from it and she is never fought |
| Ruins of Ahn'Qiraj | 20 | rare gear: 3 of 6 (Rajaxx, Buru, Moam) in 71 min, 5 wipes; on 2026-11-22 in epic gear (`.ga admin boost <bot> 60 epic`) with the trap and swap rules: Kurinnaxx with 0 deaths, then Rajaxx, Buru, Ayamiss, Moam, and in the evening **Ossirian** (the ninth try: the pull from his crystal, a weakness 15 s in, he fell 2 min after the pull with 31 deaths and no wipe): **6 of 6** in one saved instance | Ossirian costs the raid most of its members: his victim changes between tanks, warlocks and priests by threat (the healers' threat on a tank that deals no damage on the way back), and his Strength is on until the first crystal is used; at rare gear Kurinnaxx wiped the raid in his Sand Traps |
| Blackwing Lair | 20, then 40 | **all 8 encounters** in one saved instance over the day (epic gear): Razorgore (30 eggs under the orb in 3.5 min, 0 wipes) and Vaelastrasz (by his talk) with 20; with 40 and the approach place the suppression room in 3 min without a death and Firemaw (6 deaths, no wipe); Broodlord in a try before (put beside Firemaw); Flamegor and Ebonroc (1 death) after the formations were counted whole; Chromaggus by his lever (3 deaths); Nefarian after Victor Nefarius's talk and the drakonids (17 deaths, no wipe; the instance's encounters all done) | the formations of 14 on the way to Ebonroc wiped the raid twice before they were counted whole; the run counted Nefarian as an event given up (fixed after it: his body counts) |
| Temple of Ahn'Qiraj | 20, then 40 | 2026-11-21, 20 in rare gear: in, 0 bosses (the Obsidian Eradicators at the entrance killed 13 of 20); 2026-11-22, **40 in epic gear: the Eradicators in 10-13 s each without a death, The Prophet Skeram down without a wipe** (12 deaths, all brought back); 2026-11-22/23 in one saved instance: the Bug Trio, **Sartura** (3 deaths, with the whirlwind rules), **Fankriss** (0 deaths, the tank swap), **Huhuran** (18 deaths, spread out; the raid was wiped out at the first try); the Twin Emperors four times, wiped with them at 82-100 %; 2026-11-23/24, each from a fresh instance with `.ga admin dungeonskip`: **Ouro down** (3.5 min after he came, 12 deaths), the Twin Emperors on two sides 16 tries (the last with every member at its place and a clean pull: both to 57 %, wiped after 2 min), Viscidus 3 tries (frozen once after 53 s, wiped at 87-92 %), C'Thun 1 try (the Eye's phase, wiped after 3 min); 2026-11-24/25: C'Thun's Eye phase passed, his body at best to 14 %; **the Twin Emperors down** (Vek'lor's five Defender guards first, then the floor's bugs; 18 min) | Viscidus: his volley's poison kills the healers before the raid freezes and shatters him (5 of 40 can cleanse poison, 5 mages freeze him in about 50 s); C'Thun's body: the Giant Claws and the Giant Eye's beams after one or two windows without his carapace (a kill wants three) |

**Ouro** (`ApproachPlaceOf`, the frontal table and the Dirt Mound whirl row of `StepRaidBursts`; passed 2026-11-23). His mound
brings him up when a player is within 40 yd of it in its sight (npc_ouro_spawner); the raid's way ends at a hand place 33 yd
east of it, so he comes up beside the raid, not under it (the leader that walked onto the mound had his Ground Rupture
and Sweep under it, three tanks dead in five seconds). Who is not a tank keeps out of the 135-degree cone in front of him
(his Sand Blast: 3400 nature damage every 20 s to all in it; melee 0.8 of his reach behind him, the others 12 yd beyond
it, on the side their guid gives them), and everybody keeps 11 yd from a Dirt Mound (its Quake: 675 nature damage within
8 yd while it runs after a random member). A summoned boss that came and fell while the leader fought counts as fallen by
its body (the raid had waited ten minutes for him at the mound after killing him). **Passed:** 40 bots in epic gear, he
fell 3.5 minutes after he came up, 12 deaths, no wipe (most to Dirt Mounds after his submerges). The tries before: put on
his mound (the test aid's own teleport) he came under the raid; with broken gear the raid wiped at 21 % (a test raid left
with its durability at 0 % from many wipes: the test scripts now repair its gear before each try).

**Viscidus** (`StepRaidViscidus`; built, not passed). The owner's guide of 2026-11-23, without a nature resistance set (§7 RA9 in
the design log): druids, paladins and shamans that heal take the volley's poison off the member with the most of it within 38 yd
(Cleanse, Purify, Abolish or Cure Poison, Cure Toxins); everybody drinks a nature protection potion out of its bags or the
guild storage at the pull and again when it is gone and two minutes are over; the mages cast the first rank of Frostbolt
(a 1.5 s cast: the frost hit counts, not its damage); everybody keeps 9 yd from a Toxic Slime (his Toxin cloud, a whirl
row); frozen, everybody but the healers hits him in melee (his script counts 150 hits in the 15 s from the freeze, though
