his Freeze aura breaks on the first hit: the raid went back to frost after one second before); among the globs the first
tank waits at the middle of the room, where he comes back, and the healers hold for 3 s when he does; the globs get the
skull first (`StepDungeonSkull`). The raid gathers 42 yd north of him before the pull (`ApproachPlaceOf`). **Not enough:**
in three tries (2026-11-23/24) he was frozen once 53 s after the pull, and his volley had killed the healers by then (1313
nature damage and 413 every 2 s, stacking, every 10-15 s on all within 100 yd; of the test raid's 40 five can cleanse
poison, and five mages need about 50 s for his 200 frost hits); the raid wiped at 87-92 %. What would help: more frost
hits (frost wands for every caster, a shaman's Frost Shock, a frost mage's frost spells beyond the first Frostbolt) and
more who can cleanse, or nature resistance.

**C'Thun's pull after the owner's guide** (2026-11-24, `StepCthunPull`; not passed). The Eye takes whoever comes within 90 yd
in its sight and stands higher than 100 (boss_cthun), and its first three beams go at the one it engaged. So the raid
waits on the ramp up into its chamber, 68 yd from it but below the chamber's floor (`ApproachPlaceOf`, the hook on the
run's boss, which is C'Thun's body), until everybody is there; then a hunter drinks a nature protection potion, puts on
Aspect of the Wild and goes alone to its place on the rings, and the raid runs to its places when the Eye fights. In the
stomach a tank leaves at once (it is needed for the Giant Claw Tentacles), a healer heals the others there first, the
damage dealers stay up to ten stacks of the acid. **Five tries:** the hunter's pull never came: the first waiting place
(behind the dragons on the ledge) lay beyond the chamber and the way there led through the Eye's sight; on the ramp the
leader walked up from where the test put it before the hold began. The Eye's phase wiped the raid each time. **Since
then** the hold comes before the room and the gate of the boss (they walked the leader up), the raid gathers on the ramp
before the places are dealt, and from the pull on the squads' waits and follow, the rescue run and the spread fetch stay
out (the leader had waited for the hunter and pulled it back, again and again). The raid runs to its places on the rings
when the hunter steps onto the chamber's floor: a raid that set off only when the Eye fought ran up the ramp in a column,
and the beams at 12, 15 and 18 s went through all of it (39 dead at once). **Three tries:** in the last the raid stood on
its rings, dodged the first Dark Glare and took the Eye to 59 % in almost four minutes; nine died at once 42 s in, to a
beam that jumped through members closer to one another than 12.5 yd. **Six more tries:** the raid is put at its places on
the rings the moment the Eye takes the hunter (as the twins' halves are put at theirs): nobody can stand at a place before
the pull, and a raid that walked there was still in a crowd when the first beams came. The Eye Beam jumps 10 yd (the
core's default for a magic chain, up to 60 members), so the places are 11 to 15 yd apart: eight melee at 17 yd, 13 at 31
yd, 20 at 42 yd (the bots cast from 28.5 yd of the Eye's edge, whose reach is 15 yd), half a step out of line with the ring
inside, and in the Eye's phase everybody is kept within 1 yd of its place (two that had left theirs by 2 yd were in the
beam's reach, and 17 spread members died at once); melee on the outer rings hold and fight only a tentacle beside them; the
skull is on the Eye (on the nearest Claw Tentacle the raid fought tentacles). Last try: no beam through the raid, four
Dark Glares, the Eye at 17 % after almost six minutes, the deaths in the glares. Open: the raid's damage on the Eye, the
glare's dodge.

**C'Thun** (`StepRaidCthun`; built, one try, not passed). The Eye's beam jumps 12.5 yd from member to member, so the raid
stands on three rings round the Eye, 14 yd apart: the melee at 17 yd (7 places), the others at 30 yd (13) and 43 yd (19);
the skull marks a Claw Tentacle (the nearest), the cross an Eye Tentacle (the weakest), else the skull is on the Eye, and
who deals magic damage takes the cross (rti); the Dark Glare (43750 shadow damage within 100 yd along a line that turns
half a circle in 35 s from 4 s after the Eye turns red): who stands on its line steps aside, and once the way it turns is
known, who stands ahead of it runs past the end of its half circle; in the body phase the skull is on a Giant Claw, the
cross on a Giant Eye, C'Thun himself when his carapace is gone; in his stomach a member attacks the flesh tentacles and
walks to the exit (and sends the client's area trigger 4033 there) with 8 stacks of Digestive Acid, below 45 % health or
when no flesh tentacle is left; the melee keep out of the body's middle. **One try** (2026-11-24, a fresh instance): the
rings, the marks and the glare's two rules came in their order and the raid fought the tentacles; it was wiped out three
minutes after the pull with 40 deaths, still in the Eye's phase (15 of them at once four seconds after the rings were
given, not in a fight: likely the first glare, the Eye having engaged the first member the test teleported into its
sight). The stomach and the body phase were not reached.

**C'Thun's Eye phase, as the core plays it** (2026-11-24, ten more tries with the last hit in each death line; the Eye's
phase passed). The Eye Beam (26134) is a magic chain of up to 60 jumps: the core jumps to the nearest other player within
10 yd and both their sizes (13 yd between two players) and multiplies its damage by 1.5 at each jump (2625, 3900, 5900,
8900 ... 874000 on the twelfth). The places are therefore the widest 40 places in the Eye's reach: 7 melee at 17 yd, 14 at
31 yd and 20 at 44.5 yd, half a step out of line, 13.5 yd apart or more, kept within 0.7 yd. The Dark Glare (26029) is a
"cone line" (spell_custom_attr 4, `HasInLine`): it hits whoever stands in front of the Eye within 16.5 yd of the line it
looks along (the Eye's reach of 15 yd and the member's 1.5), at any distance, once a second as it turns 1/35 of a half
circle; within 16.5 yd of the Eye that is all of its front half. Its spell_cone row of 5 degrees is not used for it.
So at the glare's start whoever stands in the band at its first angle steps out of it, three of its steps beyond its
edge on the nearer side; once the way it turns is known, whoever stands where the band will sweep runs ahead of it,
always the way it turns (the shorter way round led back through the band), around its ring (the melee out to 25 yd, where
the band leaves room), to a place of its own beyond the end of the half circle: the runners of a ring spread over what is
free there, the nearest the end first. Nobody runs across the ring (the band hits whoever stands within the Eye's body),
nobody stays at a Claw Tentacle in the band. The step runs four times a second (`StepRaidCthunFast`). Each Eye Tentacle
(3000 health, a Mind Flay of 750 a second every 10 to 15 s) carries an icon of its own (seven icons, the skull stays on the
Eye) and whoever does damage takes the marked one nearest to it in its reach (28 yd from afar, 8 yd in melee). The Eye
is immune to interrupts. **Tries:** the deaths of one try by their last hit: 14 of 14 glare deaths 2 to 6 yd from the
Eye's middle (runners across the ring), 29 of 40 in a minute to chained beams on rings 13 yd apart, 28 to the band with
a 5-degree line assumed, 10 at once to runners that took the shorter way back through the band; then two glare deaths
in four glares, and in the last try the Eye dead three minutes after the pull with two deaths. C'Thun's stomach: the
navmesh does not cover it and the collision data takes its floor for solid ground, so the ground guard refused every step
there (to the flesh tentacles and to the exit); it lets a member below the chamber's floor move freely
(`GroundGuard::FreeFor`), and the exit is walked as a straight line. **Not passed:** the body phase (38 alive at its start,
wiped after four minutes: Eye Tentacles, the Giant Eye Tentacles' chained beams, the Giant Claw Tentacles, the acid).

**The Twin Emperors after the owner's guide** (2026-11-24; not passed). At each end of the room a warrior tank for Vek'nilash
and a warlock that tanks Vek'lor: the first two warlocks of the raid tank him, one per half; a third warrior tank fights at
Vek'nilash's half as his next tank. At the pull the warlock of Vek'lor's half casts Searing Pain on him in the moment of
the warrior's taunt on his brother (turned to him first): his brother's engage made him attack that warrior with no threat
on it, and the first damage on him makes the warlock his victim, so he stays at his throne. In the fight each warlock at
Vek'lor's half stands 26 yd from him and casts Searing Pain (Life Tap below a quarter of its mana, Demon Armor and Shadow
Ward on their cooldowns, a shadow protection potion before the pull and every two minutes out of its bags or the guild
storage); the warrior of that half waits 11 yd from him, out of his Arcane Burst and the nearest to him, for his brother
after the next swap (each twin comes where the other stood and takes the nearest player after 2 s); the melee of
Vek'nilash's half step back from him from 26 s after the last swap until the next; mages, warlocks and hunters take the
mutated bugs first; whoever stands within 10 yd of a bug about to explode steps away; the healers heal the four tanks
(mod-playerbots' focus heal targets); every priest keeps Shadow Protection on the raid and one paladin healer of each half
its Shadow Resistance Aura. Everybody stands on the door side of the twin at its half, on the line from his throne
through the half's place (a healer that stood beyond Vek'lor was 50 yd from the warlock it was to heal). The generic
group rules stay out of the twins' fight: no member is put beside the tank across the room, nobody runs to help a member
of the other half, and Vek'lor's whirl row is gone. **Six tries (2026-11-24):** the split holds (5 s into the fight
Vek'nilash on his warrior, Vek'lor on his warlock at the other throne, swaps seen every 30 s), but Vek'nilash kills his
warrior in 5 to 22 s (with bugs on it) and Vek'lor's Shadow Bolt (3600 shadow damage every 2.5 s) his warlock in about
15 s; no try lasted two minutes. **With shadow resistance gear** (two tries, 210 to 245 from cloth on the two warlocks
besides the buffs and the potion) the warlock with Vek'lor still died about 15 s after it took him, the warrior tanks
after 14 to 19 s, the raid within 50 s: the gear does not change the outcome. Since then the dead of a run are not brought
back while the run's boss is in a fight (the twins stand two seconds without a victim at each teleport, and the dead came
back into the fight at half their health). The test raid's tanks and paladin healers wore damage gear (the test boost
chooses by the levelling talents); in T3 plate with a shield the warrior tanks live 25 to 37 s at Vek'nilash (14 to 19 s
before) and one try took the twins to 18 %. Then the room's bugs kill them, up to 18 on a tank: a bug attacks whoever in
a fight stands within 10 yd of it. Shooting the bugs around the places before the pull pulled the twins; in the fight the
ranged take a bug that attacks a member after the mutated ones. Open: the bugs on the tanks, the Defender patrol.

**The Twin Emperors on two sides** (`StepTwinsPull`, `StepRaidTwins`; the first version, 2026-11-23). Vek'lor keeps 45 yd from his
victim and stands still when nearer; Vek'nilash follows his tank; both are immune to taunt, and after each swap a twin's
victim is the member nearest to where it appears. The raid's way ends at a hand place 35 yd from Vek'nilash's throne
(`ApproachPlaceOf`, also the target of the leader's travel now, for every boss with such a place). There the raid is split:
tanks, healers, melee and hunters, casters each in turn to Vek'nilash's half and to Vek'lor's, every member to a place 35
yd from its half's throne (the tank on it, the others in rows behind it; who is not there after 20 s is put there); the
casters of Vek'lor's half open on him, and his brother, coming after one of them, passes the tank of his own half, which
takes him. In the fight each member acts only when the twin at its half suits it (the tank, melee and hunters at
Vek'nilash, the casters at Vek'lor, healers always, within 28 yd of the twin at their half); the others wait out of reach
(a tank 13 yd from Vek'lor, so that it is the nearest when Vek'nilash appears there). Marks on a twin are taken off
before the pull and after a wipe (a skull left on Vek'nilash pulled both twins the moment the raid came back), and a bug
about to explode is stepped away from. **What went wrong in thirteen tries (2026-11-23):** the twins came while the
halves were still taking their places (a member walking to 20 yd of a throne, an Anubisath Defender's patrol through the
room, its Plague and its summoned Swarmguards, bugs a fight beside them turned on the raid), and when the pull came on
time Vek'lor still walked over to the other half (his first victim was the tank of his brother, or Vek'nilash crossed
the floor after the caster before the tank had him); every fight ended with both twins in the middle and at 82 to 100 %.
**Sixteen tries (2026-11-23/24) brought the setup to work:** the room's Anubisath Defender within 130 yd of the leader
is fought first; nothing is placed while anybody fights or is below 70 % health (a healer below 60 % mana); the places lie
towards the room's door (33 yd from Vek'nilash's throne, 30 yd from Vek'lor's, where his half's spells reach him), the
casters of Vek'lor's half in a row across their place; every member's AI holds still on the way and at its place, its
follow movement cleared (mod-playerbots' follow walked the half at Vek'lor's throne back to the leader, and the tank's own
pull strategy walked the leader 15 yd from Vek'nilash and pulled both twins), and the members of the squad hold instead of
following while the halves stand (`OrderService::UpdateBot`); a member whose straight way to its place passes within 35 yd
of a throne is put there at once (the leader came back from the Defender past Vek'nilash), the others after 4 s; everybody
gets off its mount; the tank opens with a taunt from its place, the casters open on Vek'lor at once; for the first 3 s each
twin belongs to its own half, after their first teleport (3.6 s into the fight) each half fights the twin that stands at
its throne; a fight that began while the halves took their places is taken over and logged with whom the twins came for.
**The last try** (every member at its place, the pull on time): both twins to 57 %, the raid wiped after two minutes:
Vek'lor stood at the other half one second after the taunt (his casters' spells were out of range from then on), and the
twins healed each other in the middle again. What is left: why Vek'lor leaves his throne at once (a probe client to watch
it), and a raid that damages them faster.

**The Twin Emperors passed: Vek'lor's guards first** (`StepTwinGuards`, 2026-11-25). What wiped the raid in every try
was not the twins: the five Anubisath Defenders of the twins' door and of the hall north of it walk in Vek'lor's
formation (`creature_formations` with group flag 1, members assist their leader; `linked_respawn` to him as well), so
the pull of the twins brought all five, the last from 365 yd, with their Meteor, Shadow Storm, Thunderclap and Plague.
So before the raid goes down into the throne room (the call stands in the run's boss walk, before the walk to the
twins' approach place), its leader goes to the nearest guard on the path finder's way (its task and AI held: the run's
own walk led towards Vek'nilash's throne) and pulls it from 40 yd; only a guard that no other walks within 45 yd of
(two pass each other at the north end of the hall, and a pull there brought three and wiped the raid); while none is
alone the raid holds where it stands. A guard explodes at its death (`Explode` 25699): who stands at it dies. Then the
floor's bugs: every Qiraji Scarab and Scorpion within 45 yd of a half's place and at least 32 yd from both thrones is
killed by the damage dealers (melee only those 45 yd from both; nobody's way passes within 35 yd of a throne, or nearer
to one than the member stands), the raid holds (no follow, no rescue run, no squad wait), the tanks stand; the bugs
nearer to a throne stay (six mages sent to a half's place to pull them with one spell each pulled both twins). They
come back after five minutes; the clearing ends after two. With the guards dead the twins fell 18 minutes after their
pull (the dead brought back during the fight), "Rtanka's group is done with Emperor Vek'nilash in Ahn'Qiraj Temple (7 of
9)". The twins came while the raid cleared the bugs, so the halves' setup did not run in that try: what pulls them then
is not known yet. The twins' fight writes their health every 30 s.

**C'Thun's body phase** (`StepRaidCthun`, 2026-11-24/25, about 25 tries; not passed). The whole raid turns with the
Dark Glare: when its way is known each member's place is taken out of the band to its nearer edge, and every member
stands as far on as the line has turned, in steps of 0.45 rad and one step ahead of it (a turn without steps held the
AI paused through every glare and 32 died to Mind Flay); at its end every place keeps the turn. In the body's phase the
cross marks the weakest Giant Eye Tentacle, the skull the Giant Claw Tentacle (else a Claw, else C'Thun while he is
weakened), the square the weaker flesh tentacle for the swallowed, and the Eye Tentacles get icons by how many damage
dealers can reach each (a caster 30 yd, melee 8 yd), so that nobody hits C'Thun in his carapace; the moon goes to the
Giant Claw only while he is weakened. Each Giant Claw gets the nearest free tank, and the member a claw is on stays in
its melee range (a claw whose victim is out of its reach with nobody within 5 yd sinks and comes up healed under another
member). The melee leave the claws and C'Thun from 33 s into each 60-s cycle of his body until the Giant Eye has come, and
casters take the Giant Eye only within 30 yd of its edge (from 90 yd they walked in a line into its chained beam). The
squad's catch-up stays out of the chamber (it took swallowed members out of the stomach with the acid on them). The
stomach's exit: its script throws a player up and 3 s later puts it above C'Thun and takes the acid off, but only with an
Exit Trigger (15800) within 10 yd, and the world has no spawn of one, so the run does it 3 s after the member sent the
exit's area trigger; a healer alone in there fights the flesh tentacle itself, a warlock leaves it below 35 % (its Life
Taps). Best try: C'Thun 100 -> 36 % in one window without his carapace and 35 -> 14 % in the next; most tries have one or
two windows, then the Giant Claws kill the tanks and the Giant Eye's beams the rest. A window takes 36-45 % of him at the
raid's damage (about 320 a second per bot): a kill wants three. The test raid's instance has the trash of the tunnels
under the chamber taken out of its world database (a test aid; exit jumps and corpse runs pulled it). Two more tries on
the evening of 2026-11-25 put the ranged damage dealers around each Giant Eye Tentacle the moment it came up (13.5 yd
apart, 20 to 26 yd from it): only three to five of eleven found such a place among the others' places, the eye died in
23 to 50 s instead of 50 to 100, and the raid still fell within three minutes of the first window (99 -> 46 % and
99 -> 69 %): between two windows the Eye Tentacles' Mind Flays (14 deaths in one try, all four priests), the Giant Eye's
beams (11) and the Giant Claws, once the tanks are dead, take more than the healers can give back. Not kept (no better
result). What C'Thun wants is more damage in the windows and between them (the bots' rotations), not more placing.

**Open for the raids:** Ossirian with fewer deaths (the threat of the tank on the way back from his terrace), whole runs
of Blackwing Lair and the Ruins from the entrance in a fresh instance, a whole run of the Temple of Ahn'Qiraj,
Gahz'ranka, the Edge of Madness boss, Arlokk's arena (the way from her gong), the Twin Emperors' pull from their places,
Viscidus (more frost and more cleansers), C'Thun's body phase. A raid wants epic gear for AQ20 (Kurinnaxx) and Hakkar.

**The run window** lists the raids after the dungeons (no unlock order: a raid is open; `IsDungeonUnlocked` is true for a
plan outside the order); the group step takes up to the raid's size, names the tanks and healers by their number, and asks
for several tanks and a healer for every four or five others.

### Gear made for the guild, readiness (2026-11-12, package K5)

Gear out of the guild storage is the behaviour work's `StorageSupply`: an AI-played character takes the weapon or
armour piece mod-playerbots rates best for it per place on the body (docs/storage.md §9). Package K5 adds what puts
such gear there on purpose, and a number that says how far a character is.

**Gear made for the guild** (`Professions::CraftGearFor`, `OrderService::CraftGearForGuild`, bot setting
`Professions.CraftGear`, **off by default**: the guild leader switches it on for the guild or for single crafters).
What it draws: the reagents of the one recipe it casts, from the crafter's bags first and then from the guild
storage (as every recipe does, core patch CP-7), for one piece per look; nothing else leaves the storage. In the
three minutes after a hand-in at a hub, when nothing gives skill, and in the
profession mode, a bot looks through the recipes of its planned professions that make a weapon or a piece of armour
and that it can make now: the materials in its bags and the guild storage, the anvil or forge where it stands. The
piece with the highest item level that one of the guild's AI-played characters in the world would put on, by
mod-playerbots' rating, is made once; the crafter itself comes first, and a piece that binds when it is made is only
made for the crafter. Not while such a piece already lies in the storage or in the wearer's bags. One look every
five minutes per crafter. When the cast is done the crafter puts the piece on, or puts it into the guild storage,
where its wearer takes it at its next look (within a minute):

```
activity: Probehunter crafts gear for the guild: Gray Woolen Robe (item level 21) for Probemage
activity: Probehunter made Gray Woolen Robe for Probemage: it lies in the guild storage for it
activity: Probemage took from the guild storage: 12 Melon Juice, Gray Woolen Robe
```

The storage hands a piece to whoever looks first and rates it an upgrade, which need not be the character it was
made for.

**Second version (2026-11-14; the owner: [quote left out]).** The option was on for his guild and made
25 pieces in 14 hours, item level 10 to 35, for characters that wear 28 to 37 on average. Read on the live server:
(1) a piece was only made when every material lay ready in the storage, and the storage held 624 Copper Ore, 508 Tin
Ore, 286 Wool Cloth, 515 Silk Cloth and 363 leather but no Copper Bar, one Bronze Bar, no bolt of wool and no
thread: of 16 crafters only the engineer had a single gear recipe it could cast (35 of a leatherworker's 60 recipes
lacked nothing but Fine Thread, a vendor's ware); (2) most skills are too low to make anything a level-35 character
gains from (the best green recipe: smiths at 99 / 100 item level 20, tailors at 140 item level 28, one
leatherworker at 214 item level 42); (3) the recipe's tool was not looked at: an engineer began Bright-Eye Goggles
eleven times in a night and every cast failed for its missing spanner; (4) the piece with the highest item level
was made for whoever would wear it, not for the character that needed it most; (5) no smith crafts at a hub: no
quest giver stands at an anvil. What is built for it:

- **Whose piece.** Of all the pieces the crafter can get to (below), the one whose wearer gains most: the item
  levels above what that character has in the piece's place (a bare place: all of them). At the same gain a piece
  that can be made now comes first, then the higher item level. The log line names the gain.
- **What a piece lacks comes first**, as far as the crafter can get it by itself (`WayToCast` in Professions.cpp,
  two steps deep): a material it has a recipe for is made out of the storage (`makes a material first for gear for
  the guild: .. crafts 6 x Bronze Bar`: bars out of ore, bolts out of cloth, cured hides, a jeweller's wire and
  settings; any profession it has, a smith smelts with its Mining); a material a vendor sells is bought at a vendor
  within 300 yd of the hub, from the guild's budget like the materials of crafting for skill (`buys 4 x Fine Thread
  from .. for gear for the guild`); a piece or material made at an anvil or forge takes the bot to one within 200 yd
  of the hub (`walks to Anvil for gear for the guild`). A material nobody sells and the crafter cannot make, or a
  tool it does not carry, takes the piece out of the choice. The steps follow one another a few seconds apart, six
  per hand-in at most (three purchases, two walks); the piece itself still once in five minutes per crafter.
- **A cast that fails** (nothing more of the piece afterwards than before) is noted; the second time the piece is
  not chosen again until the server restarts.
- **Before what only gives skill.** The look for gear comes first now, at a hub and in the profession mode (still one
  piece in five minutes per crafter). It used to come after every recipe that gives skill, and something always
  gives skill.
- **The anvil or forge next to a hub, also for skill.** Crafting for skill at a hub walks to one within 200 yd as
  well, twice per hand-in at most, and the hub's three minutes begin anew when the bot stands at it.

What this does not change: a crafter makes what its skill allows. With skills around 100 at level 35 to 47 most
crafters cannot make an upgrade; their skill rises with crafting for skill at the hubs (now also the smiths') and
in the profession mode.

**Dungeon sets count too** (the owner, 2026-11-13: [quote left out]). When
nobody would level in anything the crafter can make, the piece with the highest item level that improves the
dungeon set of a tank or healer among those characters is made (`RoleService::IsRoleUpgrade`: rated for the role,
against what the set has for that place; docs/dungeon-roles.md). Levelling pieces come first, as everywhere with the
roles. A piece for the crafter's own set goes from its bags into its role store at its next look; a piece for
another character goes into the guild storage, and that character's supply step takes it into its role store
(`RoleService::TakeFromStorage`, within a minute; a character that would level in it takes it first).

```
activity: Probehunter crafts gear for the guild: Silvered Bronze Breastplate (item level 26) for Tankpala: for its dungeon set as tank
activity: Probehunter used 10 x Bronze Bar from the guild storage as a reagent for Silvered Bronze Breastplate (spell 2673)
activity: Probehunter made Silvered Bronze Breastplate for Tankpala's dungeon set: it lies in the guild storage for it
activity: Tankpala took from the guild storage: for its dungeon set (into its role store): Silvered Bronze Breastplate
```

**Readiness** (`Readiness.h`, `.ga readiness <character>`). One number per character and dungeon, 0 to 100, the
entry condition of the dungeon orders (package K6):

- The **dungeons** are the client's own list (`LFGDungeons.dbc`: lowest, highest and target level; a map can have
  several entries, the wings of the Scarlet Monastery), those of the content the level cap allows: 32 dungeons and 5
  raids at level 60. The Stockade is only listed for the Alliance, Ragefire Chasm only for the Horde.
- The **gear level** of a character is the average item level of what its fights depend on: chest, legs, feet,
  hands, waist, wrists; the back from level 10, the shoulders from 20, the head from 30 (as such pieces exist); the
  main hand (twice for those who strike with it), the bow or gun of a hunter twice, the wand of a caster. A bare
  place counts 0. Jewellery and trinkets are left out.
- A dungeon **asks for** a gear level of its target level minus 2 (a character that levelled in what quests gave it
  wears about its level); the classic raids ask for 58 (Molten Core), 60 (Zul'Gurub, Ruins of Ahn'Qiraj), 64
  (Blackwing Lair) and 68 (Temple of Ahn'Qiraj).
- **Readiness** = level part x gear part: the level part is 0 below the dungeon's lowest level, 60 at it and 100
  from its target level on; the gear part is the character's gear level over what the dungeon asks for, at most 100.

```
Probehunter (level 30): gear level 21 (the average item level of its armour and weapons).
  dungeon Razorfen Kraul (id 16, level 22-32, 5 players, asks for gear level 24): 87% (gear level 21 of 24)
  dungeon Scarlet Monastery - Library (id 165, level 30-40, 5 players, asks for gear level 32): 39% (level 30 of 34, gear level 21 of 32)
```

The addon shows it in the bot detail's Character sub-tab: the gear level (red when eight item levels below the
character's level, yellow at three) and a bar per dungeon in the bot's reach (two levels ahead of a dungeon's lowest
level to five past its highest). On the wire: `BOT^gl`, `BOT^rdy`, block `DUNGEONS` (docs/protocol.md §7.20).

Open: roles (a group needs a tank and a healer: package K6 reads them from the talent template); the numbers the
raids ask for are estimates; a character that is not in the world has no gear level.

### Fishing (2026-11-12, package K3)

A bot with Fishing in its profession plan learns it where it stands (package K1); its pole comes with its first
fishing trip. `Fishing.cpp`:

- **The task** (`TaskKind::Fish`, `OrderService::StepFishing`): walk to a place at the water, find a spot to stand on
  (`Fishing::FindShore`: dry ground the path finder reaches, with water 11 to 19 yd ahead, where the bobber lands,
  and not more than 8 yd below the feet), put the pole into the main hand (the weapon it replaces goes back into the
  hand when the task is over, or at once when the bot is attacked), face the water, cast. When the bobber splashes
  the bot uses it (the core rolls the catch and the skill point), takes what is in it and releases the loot. A place
  where the cast does not start four times, or where no spot is found, is left alone for twenty minutes.
- **For the skill** (profession mode, `PlanFishing`): the water next to the bot when there is some within 45 yd (a
  dock, a canal, a pond by the inn), else the nearest school of fish within 2500 yd in a zone whose fishing skill the
  bot has (1822 schools of fish mark water; the spot verdict and the walk gate apply). 25 casts per trip. In the
  profession mode the lowest of the bot's gathering skills goes first, Fishing among them.
- **For a quest**: an item objective with no loot source that is fished (249 items are, by `fishing_loot_template`
  and one level of its references: "The Family and the Fishing Pole" wants six Darkshore Groupers) gets a fishing
  task in a zone or area where the item is fished: where the bot stands, else the nearest school of fish there,
  else the zone's hub. Only with the spell, a pole, and a chance of at least 25 % that a bite is a fish and not junk
  (the core's rule: the square of skill over the zone's skill plus 95; with skill 8 in Darkshore it is 1 %). Such a
  quest is left alone by a character that cannot fish (`QuestSupport::IsLeftAlone`), like the quests on the hand
  list, from which 1141 is gone. The "no progress" blocks bots collected on such quests before they could fish are
  dropped once by the module's SQL (`ga_quest_block_fishing.sql`: two of them had made 1141 a "learned" quest that
  every bot left alone); a bot that can fish and fails again is counted afresh.
- A fishing pole stays with the bot: the loot filter kept profession tools by their tool category, and a pole is a
  white weapon to the game (it was sold as junk within a minute; `LootService::Process`). mod-playerbots still sells
  it at a vendor (a weapon the bot does not fight with), so the pole is not handed out with the profession any more
  (a bot got a new one after every vendor visit) but when a fishing trip begins and the bot has none: `got a fishing
  pole for its trip`.

Open: the catch for Cooking is not asked for (fish go into the guild storage as materials and are cooked by what
`CraftForSkill` picks); no fishing in the schools themselves on purpose (a bobber that lands in one takes its catch,
the core's rule); a quest whose fish needs more skill than the bot has waits without raising the skill by itself
(the profession mode does that).

### Professions that stayed at skill 1 (2026-11-13)

the owner gave every bot professions (2026-11-13) and four of them stood at skill 1 on the live server: Alchemy,
Enchanting, Inscription, Fishing. What was missing, and what a bot does now at a hub after a hand-in (and in the
profession mode, with larger batches):

- **A vendor's material is bought.** Alchemy had 198 Peacebloom and 256 Silverleaf in the guild storage and no Empty
  Vial: crafting for skill at a hub only used what was there. Now the best recipe that only lacks something vendors
  sell (vials, thread, parchment, a copper rod) sends the bot to a vendor within 300 yd that sells it
  (`PlanMaterialPurchase`, the guild's budget; at most three purchases per hand-in), and it crafts when it is back:
  `bought 5 of 5 x Empty Vial for a recipe of its profession from <vendor>`.
- **An enchanter enchants its own gear** (`Professions::EnchantForSkill`, `StepEnchanting`). Enchanting has few
  recipes that make an item; its skill comes from enchantments. The bot puts the enchantment that still gives skill
  for the least material on a piece it wears that carries no enchantment, or one of its own recipes', up to
  `Professions.CraftBatch` times; the planner leaves it alone meanwhile: `enchants its own gear for its profession at
  the hub: 5 x Enchant Bracer - Minor Health on its Brocade Bracers`, then `put Enchant Bracer - Minor Health on its
  own Brocade Bracers 5 times for its profession: Enchanting 3 -> 8`. The rod a recipe asks for has to be in its
  bags; the first one is a recipe like any other (a copper rod from a vendor, dust and an essence).
- **Dust and essences for it** come out of the guild storage's green and blue pieces nobody of the guild would wear
  (the owner's word on disenchanting, E7; the setting `Professions.DisenchantForOrders`, now "Disenchant storage items
  for materials"): three pieces at most per look, only pieces that can give what is missing: `disenchanted 1 x
  Coldridge Hammer from the guild storage for its Enchanting: 1 x Lesser Magic Essence into the guild storage`.
- **A scribe mills** (`Professions::MillStored`): the pigment its best recipe lacks comes out of the storage's herbs,
  five at a time as the Milling spell takes them, those its skill allows, four stacks per look at a hub (eight in
  the profession mode), rolled on the game's milling table; the pigments go into the storage: `milled 5 x Silverleaf
  from the guild storage for its Inscription: 3 x Alabaster Pigment into the guild storage`. The Virtuoso Inking
  Set is handed out with the profession like a mining pick, and a jeweler's kit likewise.
- **A bot's two professions take turns** (`BotRuntime::lastCraftSkill`): the cheapest skill point always belonged to
  the same profession (a tailor's bolts), and the other one never got a batch.
- A recipe whose tool is not in the bags is not chosen any more (it was started and failed on the cast).

**Each profession has its own look** (the commit after live round 52). On the live server the three professions
above still stood at 1 for every character that had them, through 98 hand-ins, although the hub step ran (bandages,
bolts and grinding stones were made). Two faults of the first build:
- All professions shared one look. What a blocked recipe lacks was fetched only when *no* profession could make
  anything, and only for the one cheapest blocked recipe of all. A tailor with linen in the guild storage never got
  the rod of its Enchanting; a scribe or an alchemist that also cooks had a Cooking recipe without a fire as its
  cheapest blocked recipe, which hid the pigments and the vials. (The test bots of that build had Enchanting and
  Inscription only.)
- The look ran once in ten minutes and a hand-in did not reset it: one batch of one profession per hand-in at most.

Now `OrderService::WorkOnProfessions` goes through the professions of the plan in the order of their turns (the one
after the last batch's first; `CraftForSkill` with `onlySkill`). The profession whose turn it is makes a batch, or
gets what its own best blocked recipe lacks: pigments milled, dust and essences disenchanted, a vendor's material
bought; only when it can do neither does the next one get the turn in the same look. A hand-in resets the look, and
up to three batches follow each other at the hub (`BotRuntime::hubBatches`, about a minute). The profession mode
uses the same code with its larger batches, any vendor and its walks to a fire or an anvil.
- A recipe may lack two things the bot makes itself (`CraftNeed::makeItem2`): the enchanter's first rod takes dust
  *and* an essence, and with the second counted as "nothing the bot can get" no enchanter ever made its rod.
- A druid leaves its animal form (a shaman its ghost wolf) when a batch starts: nothing is crafted in a form, and
  its batches ended with their first cast.
- The water for the casts at a hub may be 120 yd away (it was 45: a town's canal, its pier).
- *Which piece is disenchanted* (the commit after the first live round with the above): the piece most likely to give
  what is missing, by the chances of the game's disenchant tables (`CraftOrders::DisenchantChance`; a chance of 0 in
  a table is the share the others of its group leave), none below 15 %, and a material counts as served once the
  storage has more of it than when the look began. On the live server an enchanter had taken nine green pieces in
  twenty seconds for the dust and the essence of one rod: any piece whose table holds the material was taken in the
  storage's order, most of them for an essence they give one time in five.

Fishing only starts where the water's level fits the skill: at Fishing 1 the 20 to 30 zones (Redridge, Duskwood, the
Wetlands: base 55) give the core's catch chance of (1/55)², so a character that levels there needs a hand-in in a
city or a starter zone for its first points, or the profession mode.

**Fishing in AUTO** (the commit after): a bot with Fishing in its plan casts eight times at water within 45 yd (120 yd since round 52) of
where it stands in the three minutes after a hand-in, at most every twenty minutes (`PlanFishing` with `nearCasts`):
`fishes at the water by the hub for its profession: 8 casts (Fishing 1 of 75)`. No trip to water for it; that is the
profession mode's.

Also in this commit, from live round 49: **the planner takes over a walk NewRpg does not start.** A warlock sat on
its mount at Whelgar's Excavation for five minutes ("movement 0; rpg do quest") through two objectives, each ended
"objective spot not reached" after two minutes, until the rescue. When a bot on its way to an objective's spot has
stayed within 15 yd for 25 s (not fighting, not casting), the planner walks it to the spot itself (`WalkTo`) and
hands the quest back to NewRpg in sight of it; once per task: `has not set off for N s, D yd from the spot of
quest Q: the planner walks it there itself`.

### Profession mode: back to the autopilot, a journey to water, recipes from the storage (2026-11-13)

the owner put eight bots into the profession mode and asked how it works; three rules came out of it.

- **Nothing left: the autopilot again** (the owner: [quote left out]). A bot whose profession mode finds nothing to craft and nothing to gather for two minutes (the looks of
  the single ways come round in that time) gets the order AUTO: `has nothing left to craft or gather for its
  professions (Tailoring 75, First Aid 150): its order is the autopilot again`, with an event for the owner. It does
  not go back to its professions by itself.
- **A journey to water its Fishing reaches.** With no water its skill reaches next to it and no school of fish within
  a walk, a bot travels (flights) to the nearest school of fish on its land mass in a zone whose water its skill
  reaches, however far (`Fishing::WaterForSkill`), and fishes there; with no such school, to water within 70 yd of an
  inn or a flight master in such a zone. A character with Fishing 1 in the Wetlands goes to Loch Modan or Dun Morogh.
  Lava and slime are no water (the first build's journey went to the Great Forge of Ironforge).
- **Recipes out of the guild storage** (the owner: [quote left out]; [quote left out]). Once a minute per guild (`Professions::LearnStoredRecipes`): a
  recipe item in the storage is taken out and learned by an AI-played guild character in the world that can learn it
  now (it has the profession, the skill, the level, whatever else the item asks, and does not know it): the one with
  the highest skill in that profession, on a tie the one that knows more of its recipes. One copy per character; a
  second copy goes to the next one that can learn it; a recipe nobody can learn yet stays. `took 1 x Pattern: Red
  Linen Robe from the guild storage (a recipe it can learn) and learned it: Red Linen Robe (Tailoring 135)`.
  Only characters in the world at that moment take part; the character you play yourself does not.
- **Materials that creatures drop are hunted** (cloth, meat, claws; the answer to the owner's [quote left out]). When the best recipe of a profession lacks a material that neither the bags nor
  the guild storage hold, that no vendor sells and that the bot cannot make, and creatures drop it, the profession
  mode hunts for it (`OrderService::PlanMaterialHunt`): `hunts Sea Crawler for 20 x Crawler Meat that a recipe of its
  profession lacks (694 yd; 9 of them and their like within 80 yd of each other)`. The hunt is a grind task at a
  hunting ground and ends when the bags and the storage hold that many more (`material gathered`) or nothing is left
  to fight there; then the recipe is looked at again. A look every two minutes; a journey first when the ground is
  far. `WorldIndex` knows the sources: the trade goods that profession recipes take are indexed like quest items
  (creature loot from a 10 % chance, one level of reference loot; 2615 to 2803 items with sources).
  **The hunting ground** is `OrderService::FindHuntGround(player, rt, item, maxLevel = 0, minGroup = 1)`, written so
  that other orders can use it (the FARM order): of the creatures that drop the item and that the character may
  fight (not elite, attackable, on its land mass, not in a zone above it, not at a place it keeps away from;
  `maxLevel` 0 = up to its own level and what the risk rules let it fight above it, else only kinds up to that
  level), the nearest 80 spawns are looked at as the middle of a ground, the others within `GroundYards` (80) of
  each are counted, and the middle with the most for its way wins (300 yd of way count like one creature less, more
  than twelve count as twelve), when the risk rules let the character work there (`Risk::JudgeSpot`). `minGroup`
  leaves out grounds with fewer spawns. It returns the spot, the levels of the kinds there, the count and the
  distance; `OrderService::GetRuntime(guid)` hands callers outside the planner the character's planner state.

**A profession far behind first; materials it makes itself** (2026-11-14; the owner: [quote left out]). His
smith Wartank stood at Blacksmithing 123 and Mining 202 and walked from vein to vein: every recipe of its smithing
wanted bars, the guild storage held 600 copper and 500 tin ore and no copper bar, and the look at a blocked recipe knew
of vendors, pigments, disenchanting and hunting, not of a material the bot makes itself, so it held the recipes
impossible and gathered for its Mining.
- **The lagging profession alone** (`LaggingProfession`, bot setting `Professions.FocusBehind`, default 50, per guild
  and per bot; 0 = off). Of the professions of the plan the bot has learned and not taken to their targets, the
  lowest is worked on alone while it is more than that many points below the highest (`works on its Blacksmithing
  (60) alone in the profession mode: it is more than 50 points behind its Mining (118)`); within that again it has
  caught up and the professions take turns (`has caught up on its ..`). A crafting profession is worked on by
  crafting only (nothing is gathered for the others meanwhile); a gathering profession by gathering for it (a miner
  smelts while that gives it skill). Craft orders and gear for the guild still come first. When it can do nothing for
  the profession as things are (no recipe that gives skill and nothing its best recipe lacks that it can make, buy or
  fetch; nothing in reach to gather), its other professions have their turns for two minutes (`can do nothing for its
  .. now (..): its other professions for 2 min`). Not on a catch-up of the autopilot.
- **A material it makes itself comes first** (`Professions::CraftForSkill`, `CraftNeed::matSpell`): a reagent of the
  best blocked recipe that the bot makes with a recipe it knows (any profession: a smith smelts with its Mining; one
  step deeper too: bronze out of copper and tin bars out of ore) is made first, whatever that recipe's colour for its
  own skill, as many as the other materials let the recipe be made in a batch (`makes a material first for its
  Blacksmithing (profession mode): Startwar crafts 80 x Copper Bar. (Copper Bar for its recipes)`); its forge first
  when it is made elsewhere. At a hub after a hand-in the same, where the forge stands. Every ore taken leaves its line.
- **No half-made pieces.** In the profession mode the next look comes 3 s after a batch (it was 30 s): a smith that
  had smelted the bars for a piece of gear for the guild set off for a vein before the piece and came back five
  minutes later to smelt again (Wartank, eight copper bars every five minutes).

**Across the water to a target** (2026-11-14, the observer on the live server: a druid with "The Bloodsail
Buccaneers" stood nine minutes on Booty Bay's cliffs and then had the Bloodsail Charts set aside; the charts and
orders lie on the Bloodsail hulks off the Wild Shore, and the road map's way there leads over the node of a ship's
dock and ends at the water). A walk to a task's target that has no way on the ground (the ground guard refuses a step
to the target itself, or the planner's own steps find no path three times) now looks once per task for a swim
(`OrderService::StepSwim`): the landing is the nearest water within 60 yd of the target from which the path finder
leads to it; the way in is where the bot swims already, water within 40 yd it can see, or water up to 250 yd off that
a walk on the ground reaches, towards the landing (`walks first to the shore at ...`); the way through the water is a
search over cells of 6 yd that are at least 2 yd deep, within 300 yd of both ends, pulled into straight stretches; the
bot swims point by point with NewRpg resting, and gives the swim up after 40 s without getting 2 yd nearer. The
ground guard's reaction to cancelled movements stays out of a swim. Lines: `swims to (..) for its target at (..): no
way on the ground leads there; N yd through the water over N points, from (..)`, `has swum to (..)`, `gets no nearer
to (..) on its swim`, `finds no water to swim from ..`, `finds no way through the water ..`. No lava, no slime, no
dungeon, nothing nearer than 30 yd or farther than 1500 yd.

**Round 174: a rock top beside Terrordale** (2026-11-23). Retadodino (60) was grinding in the Eastern Plaguelands. It
fought a Cannibal Ghoul that wanders at the foot of a rock beside Terrordale (its spawn at (3247, -3049, 158)) and ended
on the rock's top, 7 to 15 yd above the ground around it. The navmesh covers the top, but no polygon joins it to the
slope below: every path from there is "incomplete" and ends at the top's edge. The bot's walks were refused, a restart
came 45 s later, and it entered the world on the top. Its trail was 12 yd long after the login, short of the 50 yd a
walk back needs, so the way out of a place cut off from every road went straight to the rescue (`CutOffWayOut`). A walk
back along the path finder's path would have ended at the top's edge anyway. The trail is kept out of fights, so a fight
that carries a bot somewhere leaves no way back in it.

Two changes:
- **A step down off the ledge** (`OrderService::StepOffLedge`, the first thing `CutOffWayOut` tries). Around the bot, 6
  to 26 yd off in 16 directions, a point whose floor lies up to 5 yd below the bot and from which the path finder walks
  to one of the three nearest road nodes on the navmesh; the straight line there is probed for the ground (no rock, no
  drop of more than 6 yd: the ground guard's own drop rule). The bot walks that line, a step down any walker takes; the
  path finder's path would stop at the edge. Once per quarter of an hour; when it does not get down, the rescue as
  before. Lines: `steps down off the ledge it stands on at (..): N yd to (..), N yd lower, from where the path finder
  walks to a road; ...`, `ends its step down off the ledge after N s: down`. The top's south-west edge is 3 to 4 yd
  above the ground beyond it.
- **No climb without a way back down** (the ground guard, `GroundGuard::MayMove`, also for a fight's chase since core
  patch CP-13). A movement that ends 2.5 yd or more above the bot on ground from which the path finder leads no way back
  down to where the bot stands is refused, as a drop of 6 yd with no way back up has been. Not in dungeons, not for a
  plain navmesh path. Line: `does not walk from (..) to (..) (its chase in a fight): it would climb N yd onto ground
  from which no way leads back down`.

**Round 179: a slope beside a Rich Thorium Vein; the Naxxramas attunement** (2026-11-23). Pewpew (60, hunter) made a
gather detour to a Rich Thorium Vein in the Eastern Plaguelands for quest 9121 "The Dread Citadel - Naxxramas". The walk
there was a whole navmesh path to the vein at height 32. A Living Decay attacked it there, and the fight's chase took it
17 yd up the slope beside the vein, off the navmesh, to (2004, -4370, 49). Its step down to the floor below was refused
("the way drops 13 yd ... no way leads back up from there"), and three seconds later the rescue put it on a road. Three
causes and three changes:
- **The drop rule held it up there.** The ground guard refuses a drop of 6 yd or more when no way leads back up to
  where the bot stands; off the navmesh no path leads to where it stands at all, so every way down was refused, and
  the way down was its way out. The two "no way back" rules (a drop, and the climb of round 174) are asked only where
  the bot stands on walkable ground now.
- **The chase crept up the slope.** Steps under 3 yd pass the guard unprobed; a rising step onto ground without
  navmesh was refused only from walkable ground, so after the first step off the navmesh the next ones passed. A
  rising step (half a yard or more) that ends on ground without navmesh is refused wherever it starts.
- **The rescue came first.** Both places that rescue a bot standing off the navmesh (three cancelled movements, and
  30 s of walking without getting on) try the step down off a ledge of round 174 first (`StepOffLedge`), which now looks
  for a floor up to 30 yd lower (a slope; the probe of the straight line still refuses a drop of more than 6 yd through
  the air).
- **The quest.** 9121, 9122, 9123 and 9378 are the attunement to Naxxramas, a level-80 raid in this client: they are on
  the list of quests the bots leave alone, quest items from the guild are not fetched for a quest left alone
  (`QuestSupply`), and what such a quest asks for is not kept in the bags against the guild storage (`QuestLogAsksFor`,
  `MakeBagSpace`, the loot filter's "for its quest" rule and mod-playerbots' quest usage in `BotDriver::WantsItem`, for
  characters the AI plays): Arcane Crystals taken or gathered for it go into the guild storage.

**Round 183: a short stun on the run, a lake's floor, a lift's upper stop, a hive** (2026-11-23).
- **Held fast by a short stun.** Sheesh (60, warrior) ran from two Shadowmages at 56 % health. A Dark Adept's Snap Kick
  (a stun of two seconds) held it, and the run ended "held fast, fights on". Eight seconds later it ran again, was held
  again after one second and died. A stun, root, fear or confusion that ends within six seconds (every one of them on
  the bot) is now waited out, and the run goes on when it ends (`Escape::ShortHold`); the AI is not held meanwhile, so
  a rooted bot fights where it stands. The line says `(waited out Snap Kick)`. A longer hold ends the run as before.
- **Into the ground under a lake.** Shadow (60, priest) fought Blighted Surges in Lake Mereldar and was rescued 3.4 yd
  under the shore ("no floor under it (surface at 65)"). A swim may end a little under the lake's sloping floor, where
  the core counts no water; from there the bot is a walker, and a walker's steps under 3 yd were not looked at. The
  ground guard now refuses a walker's movement that ends inside the ground (under the terrain, no floor under it)
  deeper than it starts, and a swim that ends more than 1 yd under the floor (2 yd before). A plain navmesh path is
  not looked at (its mesh may lie a little under the terrain on a slope). Line: `does not walk from (..) to (..): the
  way ends N yd under the ground (..)`.
- **A lift's upper stop.** Bloodyo (60, profession mode) went for a Truesilver Deposit on the floor of Thousand Needles
  from Dustwallow Marsh. Its route ended at the upper stop of the Great Lift's elevator, 129 yd above the deposit: the
  route's ends were the nodes nearest by the map alone, and the stops of a lift stand one above the other. The walk
  from there led along the Barrens' rim to a place the path finder joins to no road, and the bot walked back the way it
  came, set out on the same route again and was rescued. A node is no end of a route when it lies more than 10 yd
  further above or below than it lies away (`SteepNodeYards`), the 8-yd trusted walk to a node counts only on its own
  height, and the upper stops of lifts (nodes one above the other that a ride with an object joins, 44 on the map) are
  no ends of routes and no places to put a bot (`Node::liftTop`).
- **A sea cave under Faldir's Cove.** Unholymoly (60) mined an Iron Deposit 65 yd down in a sea cave of Arathi; its
  next node lay 25 yd off, and it was "cut off from every road". A gather round's walk (and a fishing trip's) in the
  water counts as being at a target in the water, like an objective's (`IsAtWaterTarget`): the swim leads on.
- **Inside Hive'Zora.** Buffadin (60) ground inside Hive'Zora; a target 208 yd off in the hive got a route whose start
  was a guess, and from under the surface that is a walk back the way it came (round 146): twice in two hours, the
  second time 91 s among the hive's packs. A whole path of the path finder to the target is walked first.

**Round 184: the lake's shore again, a run from one wasp, Thorium Bars for a quest nobody works on** (2026-11-23).
- **Lake Mereldar.** Stormstrikey (60, shaman) was rescued 4 yd under the shore at the spot of round 183, beside a
  Blighted Surge that spawns 3 yd under the lake's sloping floor. The core counts a point in water down to 2 yd under
  the terrain, so a swim's way that ended under the floor "was in water" and passed. The swimmer's and the walker's
  rule now ask the terrain first: under it by more than 1 yd is no water. A bot that is found 1 to 8 yd inside the
  ground with no floor under it (the two off-navmesh checks, the under-the-ground check) is put on the terrain right
  above it first (`OrderService::LiftOutOfGround`, once in two minutes), not on a road 200 yd away; deeper down, the
  rescue as before. Line: `stands N yd inside the ground at (..): it is put on the ground right above it (..)`.
- **A run from one wasp.** Mageyo (60, mage) kept away from three Hive'Zora Wasps on its way; the one that came was in
  combat with it before it was "on" it, so the keep-away became a run at once, 36 s from one wasp through the hive (no
  open way: every direction led past other creatures), down to 22 % health, and a fight against five. A keep-away in
  combat with nothing on it yet goes on for 2 s until the attacker is known (then the usual rule: an ordinary foe at
  its health is fought), and a run that began as a keep-away looks again every 2 s: when the usual rule says it can take
  what is on it, it fights (`the foes on it are ones it can take, fights on`).
- **Churn.** Retadk (60, profession mode) took Thorium Bars out of the guild storage for "That's Asking A Lot" three
  times in 80 s, its Engineering made Thorium Widgets out of them (the bags' reagents go first), and it smelted one more
  bar for the quest. Quest items from the guild are not fetched on an order that works on no quest (the profession
  mode, a farm order, a dungeon run).

**Round 191: Hive'Zora's wasps and a hunter's Feign Death** (2026-11-24). Pewpew (60, hunter) led a warlock as its
squad's leader towards a Hive'Zora Wasp 129 yd away. The wasps stand in clusters of four or five within 5 yd (106 of
them around the hive, `.ga admin spot` calls such a cluster a camp the bot alone cannot take). The warlock rested (55 s,
no food or drink), the hunter waited where its walk had stopped, and a cluster came at it alone. It cast Disengage and
Feign Death on its run, ran on and died after 31 s at 83 % health when it began.
- **Feign Death is lain in.** The run's leg began before the spells went out, and a Disengage went out after the Feign
  Death: both stood the hunter up again. Now nothing is cast after a Feign Death on a run, the hunter stops where it
  is, and it lies still while hostile creatures are within 25 yd (on their way home included), up to 20 s; still in the
  fight 1.5 s after it (resisted) it gets up and runs.
- **The squad's leader waits beside its member.** A leader that waits for a member that rests or catches up, with
  hostile creatures within 30 yd of where it stopped, walks to that member (`StepSquadWait`, `waits for its squad beside
  ..`).

**Round 192: a civilian elite in the fight** (2026-11-24). Magefrost (60, frost mage) pulled a creature on its way to
quest 8323 in Silithus; four seconds later a Sand Skitterer and Twilight Marauder Morna were on it, it left the fight 18
seconds after that at 73 % health ("used Blink, Frost Nova": its Frost Nova had been spent in the fight and went out
again only on the run) and died on the run 15 seconds later. Morna is an elite of level 60 with 3.45 times the health
and 4.6 times the damage (worth level 70 by the look-outs' measure) on a 342-point round through Silithus, and she is
flagged a civilian (`flags_extra` 2): the core lets her start no fight and help nobody (`Creature::CanStartAttack`,
`CanAssistTo`), so she came in only because something of the bot hit her; with no "[... was near]" in its line, the
look-out for strong creatures had let her be the whole time, because it leaves civilians out ("a civilian never
attacks", the rule of Gringer in Booty Bay). The same mage had her in a fight at 02:08 already ("3 foes at once
(Twilight Marauder Morna level 60)"), left by the count at full health with its Blink ready and got away. Three changes:
- **A civilian in a fight with the bot counts.** The look-out leaves out a civilian only while it is not in a fight
  with the bot (`IsInCombatWith`); one that is gets the rule of every strong creature: in a fight the bot leaves at
  once, its getaway spells still ready.
- **A mage's area spells not beside a strong creature that is out of the fight.** Frost Nova and Cone of Cold (12 yd
  around the mage, the cone only in front of it) and Blizzard and Flamestrike (10 yd around their target) are not cast
  where they would hit a creature far above the mage (an elite by its health and damage) that is hostile, attackable
  and not in a fight with it, a civilian included (`Escape::StrongBystanderWithin`, mod-playerbots' four actions
  replaced in the mage's context as its "blink back" was). Line: `does not cast Frost Nova: Twilight Marauder Morna
  (level 60 elite) stands N yd from where it would land and is not in the fight; the spell would draw it in`, once
  per half minute.
- **No step back to beside one.** A step back in a fight (mod-playerbots' "flee", the "blink back", the run to range)
  is not taken to within 12 yd of such a civilian (`Escape::StepWakes`; ordinary hostile creatures already counted by
  their reach).

**Round 194: a Nerubian Overseer during a keep-away; a corpse beside it** (2026-11-24). Stormstrikey (60, shaman)
ground in the Eastern Plaguelands. At 05:49:46 it kept away from four Cannibal Ghouls on its way; two seconds later a
Nerubian Overseer was on it, a rare elite of level 60 with six times the health and four times the damage (worth level
72 by the look-outs' measure) on a round of 150 points whose way passes 4 yd from the place. Its Enveloping Web held the
shaman for 9 s ("left ... at 100% health (used Stoneclaw Totem, Earthbind Totem): held fast, fights on"; a hold of up to
6 s is waited out), and it died. It died at 33 % durability, under the 40 % from which a ghost takes the spirit healer,
so the corpse rule (the spirit healer when the corpse lies among creatures or beside a strong one) did not hold: the
ghost ran back, rose 8 yd from the Overseer and was dead again fifteen seconds later. Two changes:
- **The look-out runs during a keep-away too.** While the bot keeps away from a pack, goes around one or out of the
  reach of a creature that keeps to its place, the look-out for strong creatures did not run, and the keep-away's legs
  led wherever the pack was not. It looks every second, 50 yd far (a rider 63), and a strong creature that comes near
  is the one kept away from from then on (`keeps away from Nerubian Overseer (level 60 rare elite), N yd away, which
  came near while it kept away from creatures on its way`).
- **The spirit healer beside what killed it, whatever the gear.** A corpse under water, among two or more hostile
  creatures or beside one far above the bot sends the ghost to the spirit healer at any durability: its quarter of the
  durability costs less than rising there, and the urgent vendor trip repairs worn gear. (The 40 % still holds for the
  second death at one place.)

**Round 196: grinding at the edge of the Twilight camp** (2026-11-24). Pewpew (60, hunter) ground Stonelash Scorpids
in Silithus right after its quest pair with Owldudu had parted beside the Twilight camp. Ten seconds after a won fight
three of the camp's Overlords and Masters were on it ("it was attacked"), six in the end; it left at 54 % health "the way
it came (used Feign Death, Disengage)", was held fast, stayed, left again at 41 % "the way it came" and died inside the
camp at (-6473, 212). The camp: ten spawns of level 57 to 61 within 41 yards of (-6453, 216), "a camp for walkers up to
level 60: it cannot take it" by `.ga admin spot` on the live server; its creatures wander 25 yards, and the scorpids
wander into its edge. None of the Twilights is strong enough for the look-out for strong creatures (ordinary creatures
of the bot's level), and the look for packs looks only along a moving bot's way. Three changes:
- **No grind target in the middle of a camp it cannot take, nor across one.** The grind's target choice
  (`PickGrindTarget`) looked at the creatures 15 yards around a target, not at the camp around it: a scorpid that had
  wandered to the camp's edge was a target like any other, and at the level cap the grind takes creatures of its own
  level, the Twilights themselves among them. A target in such a camp, or one whose straight way from the bot leads
  into one, is passed over (the check made only for the target that would be the best so far).
- **The way it came not into a camp.** An escape's first leg goes back along the bot's trail when nothing stands on it
  now; the legs in the seven directions kept out of camps it cannot take, the trail did not. The trail of a bot that
  rode along the camp's edge led back into it. A trail point in such a camp (deeper into it, for a bot that stands in
  one), or a way to it that leads into one, is passed over (`the way it came was closed (into a camp)`).
- **Nothing after a Feign Death, on any tick.** The rule of round 191 stopped the casts of the tick that cast Feign
  Death; the run calls for its help spells every tick of its first seconds, and the next tick's Disengage stood the
  hunter up. Nothing is cast while the Feign Death lasts (one that was resisted the run removes, and Disengage follows).

**After round 196: nothing it can safely get to, twice** (2026-11-24). Thunderhoof, a level-13 druid of the test guild,
went south from the Crossroads on its quests in the Barrens and stood 45 minutes among creatures of level 16 to 19
(Hecklefang Snarlers, Sunscale Scytheclaws, the rare Stormsnout): every way north was refused ("passes level-17
creatures", "3 level-16 creatures stand together on the way"), it left five fights and kept away from a creature every
few seconds. Four times it "has nothing in The Barrens it can safely get to: it looks at the zones again", and each time
the look kept it in the Barrens (no other zone on its side has as much), where the grind led into the same creatures.
Its inn was the Crossroads (it had bound there at 07:00), 1300 yards north; the hearthstone was never used: the
boxed-in rule counts refused ways, and its ways ended in packs and fights it left. Now the second "nothing it can
safely get to" within half an hour sends the bot home by hearthstone when its inn is 250 yards or more away (`it found
nothing in The Barrens it can safely get to from here twice within half an hour`). Nochnwar's death at the Twilight
camp of Silithus the same morning (its own pulls of Twilight Overlords at the camp's edge, a walk around three of them,
then caught 50 s later) is the case of round 196: a grind target in the middle of such a camp is passed over since.

**The walk to a quieter place through a camp** (2026-11-24). Hordeboss, a level-18 warrior of the test guild, fought
in the Bristleback camp of the Barrens for "Consumed by Hatred", ended a fight at 23 % health and sat down to eat; a
moment later it "walked 58 yd away when something came near (9 hostile creatures near, 0 there)" straight through the
camp, was attacked on the way and died seven seconds into its run. The walk to a quieter place (`FindRestSpot`, through
`CanWalkTo`) refuses a path into the reach of a creature (its aggro range and 8 yards, at least 14), but left out every
creature the bot already stood within that reach of: in the middle of a camp that was all of them, though none had
seen it. Such a creature now counts too: the path may not lead nearer to it than the bot stands and into its aggro range
plus 3 yards (one already in a fight with the bot does not count). The same holds for the other callers of that check
(the lure out of a caster's sight).

**Round 272: the strait to Fray Island, a knockback off a plateau, a mine under Stonard** (2026-11-27). Three bots of
the round stood where the rescue or a loop took them, each for a cause of its own:

- *The strait to Fray Island.* Graveborn (44) handed a quest in on Fray Island and swam back along the road map's link
  "The Barrens Fray Island > The Merchant Coast", one of the short swims the sea scan keeps (about 250 yd at sea
  level). Halfway across it was put back on the ground as one that "swims in the open sea, where fatigue kills": that
  rule rescued after 8 s in the core's dark water, and the strait's middle is dark water. The fatigue bar runs a minute
  before its damage begins (`Player::HandleDrowning`, a second a second in dark water, ten back a second out of it).
  `OrderService::TrackBreath` now counts it the same way (`BotRuntime::fatigueUsedMs`), and `CheckStranded` rescues at
  40 of the 60 s, before any damage (the 40 s the test guild thread chose for the same case, a281d30); a swim of the
  strait uses less. The link's way across is no wrong choice: Fray Island is an island, and of the strait's water the
  core's map data (the liquid flags of `maps/0013439.map`) calls a stretch of about 95 yd on the link's path dark
  water, about 20 s of a swim; east of it the water is not dark, but the walked path is mod-playerbots'.
- *Knocked off the plateau above the Infectis Scar.* Unholymoly (60, death knight) walked a whole path to the rim of
  the plateau at (2000, -4388, 72) and pulled a Stitched Horror with Death Grip; the Horror's Mighty Blow (14099, a
  knockback) threw it over the rim onto the slope 31 yd below, off the navmesh, where its walk back up was refused and
  `StepOffLedge` found no step it accepted: the straight line down to the scar's floor ran through the air above the
  slope's bend (Pewpew stood on the same slope in round 179). `StepOffLedge` now also takes a way down the slope along
  its ground (`SlopeWalk`: a point every 1.5 yd at the floor below the one before, a rise of at most 1 yd and a drop of
  at most 4 yd a point, no water, nothing in the way, ending at the candidate's height on the navmesh), walked point by
  point like a walk back (`StepTrailOut`), its line "..., down the slope along its ground". (Leel's step down at
  (2052, -4358) in the same round was the straight kind and needed no rescue.) And so that the blow does not throw a
  bot over an edge in the first place (three such rescues in four days): `WorldIndex::KnocksBack` knows the creatures
  whose SmartAI script casts a spell with a knock back effect (443 kinds, the Stitched Horror among them);
  `Escape::DropBehind` finds a drop of 6 yd or more 3 to 12 yd behind a character, in the direction from the creature
  through it (water is none). The rule of a melee bot that has not got under way to its target (`CheckPull`) does not
  pull such a creature to a place with a drop behind the bot, it walks up to it ("it walks up to it (it knocks back, and
  the ground drops behind the bot)"); and in a melee fight with one `Escape::StepKnockbackSide` (four times a second)
  steps round the creature to a side with no drop behind it, the other side first, then a quarter and a half round
  either way, on the floor at the creature's height and by a whole path ("steps round ... to its other side"). The
  Horror's first Mighty Blow comes 5 to 8 s into the fight.
- *A mine under Stonard.* Zulkash (53, test guild) travelled from the Blasted Lands to Stonard's flight master for a
  zeppelin and looped from 04:42 on in the Nethergarde mine 25 yd below the town: the travel node graph has a node in
  the mine ("Blasted Lands Garrison Armory", a miner's spawn) and walking links from it to Stonard's flight master,
  innkeeper and spirit healer whose walked paths run in the town and drop the last 25 yd straight through its ground;
  every route to Stonard from the south ended with that step ("its step would run 17 yd through solid ground"). The
  navmesh's walk between the two is 1026 yd (through the mine's entrance). `tools/gen_road_links.py` looks for such jumps
  from 10 yd on now (was 40: a rise or fall of 10 yd or more in less than two thirds of it on the ground, with no
  navmesh walk between the two points of at most four times their distance, 200 yd at least): 276 links are left out
  (were 111), 40 walks take their places (were 33), the bridges between parts are as before. New in the old world: the
  mine under Stonard, the Azurelode Mine (a 601 yd walk in its place), the Drowned Reef off Southshore and the Wetlands,
  and Witch Hill in Dustwallow Marsh (a node 11 yd above the end of every path to it).

**Round 266: a grind target on the rock beside Light's Hope** (2026-11-26). Five bots of level 60 (Retadodino, Cleaveyo,

**Round 249: a camp of a kind that costs the bot more** (2026-11-26). Priestyo (60, priest) ground in the Eastern
