Priestyo 33 % against its average of 24 % (`ga_bot_foe_cost`). A camp now carries its two commonest kinds
(`CampAt::kinds`), and the camp verdict (`CannotTake`, behind `EntersCamp` and `InCampItCannotTake`) judges a camp
whose kind costs the walker 1.2 times its average or more by that cost (`Risk::CanFight` with an entry), also above
the walker level; a kind it found cheap does not make it bolder. The road map's camps (no character) are unchanged.
`.ga admin spot` names it: `its creatures are far below it, but what it learned of their kind says it cannot take them`.

**Round 242: a portal of the other side; the way to a portal without a gate** (2026-11-26). Bloodyo (60, an Alliance
death knight) started an errand from Feralas for quest 5089 (its ender in the Burning Steppes) and took a voyage on "the
Portal to Blasted Lands to Blasted Lands": the one in Thunder Bluff. Its route ("Feralas The Forgotten Coast > ... >
Thunder Bluff flightMaster (14507 yd ...; it leads through a town of the other side)") went through the Barrens, up the
Mesa Elevator into Thunder Bluff; it died to the Bluffwatchers, took the same way from its spirit healer at Red Rocks,
died again, hearthed to Cenarion Hold and took it once more. Two causes. *The link:* the teleporters players click
(since the Orb of Translocation, 2026-11-24) were travel links for both sides ('C'); the Portals to Blasted Lands of the Horde's
capitals carry the Horde's faction (1735), those of the Alliance's 1732. A teleporter's side now comes from its game
object's faction (`IndexTransports`: friendly to one side only, that side; hostile to both, no link), and no ship,
portal or teleporter serves a side whose town of the other side one of its ends lies in (`ServesTeam`, for
`CountTravelLegs` and `NextTravelLink`: a portal of faction 0 stands in Orgrimmar, another leads into Stormwind). *The
gate:* WalkTo's town gate leaves a voyage to the voyage's own gate, and that gate (creatures far above the bot, a group
it cannot take) stood in the dock branch only; the way to a portal or teleporter had none. Both branches share it now
(`gateWalk` in `StepVoyage`), and it refuses a way to a dock, portal or teleporter in a town of the other side, and one
whose route leads through such a town unless the bot stands in one (it may walk out): `.. does not walk to .. for ..:
the way (..) leads through a town of the other side`, with the dock gate's consequences (the errand dropped, or the zone
written off and the hearthstone).

**Round 238: a Shadowmage with a Dark Adept; a getaway that cannot go out** (2026-11-26). Warriorio (60, warrior)
ground in the Eastern Plaguelands and pulled a "pair of Shadowmages" six times in forty minutes ("its own pull (2
expected)"): it won four of them going down 13, 39, 15 and 45 %, ran once at 51 % with a Major Healing Potion and got
away, and the sixth time left at 80 % health seven seconds into the fight "by how the fight went", used Hamstring,
waited out a Snap Kick and died on the run after 35 s with its target at 86 %. Read in the world database: the pairs
there are a Shadowmage and a Dark Adept standing 6 to 7 yd apart (two of the four Shadowmage spawns near the place),
not two Shadowmages. Two causes. *The pull check:* a fight against two or three creatures of different kinds taught
nothing (round 163 taught pairs of one kind only), so its note of the Shadowmage stayed where a fight it had to leave
against two Shadowmages had put it (0.4 against one of its level, 7 fights, last written the evening before) and the
Dark Adept was judged by its average: the pair came to about 64 %, below the limit of 80 %. `Escape::OnFightEnd` now
learns from such a fight too (`BotRuntime::Fight::kinds`, entry and level of each creature that came, passed when every
one was on the bot at once): the fight's cost (the lowest health, mana at half weight; all it had for a death or a fight
it had to leave) against what `FightNeed`'s own sum reckoned with each kind's cost, the same factor for every kind of
it, each kind's note learned toward that as in a single fight (a death or a forced leave never lowers it); its average
is not touched, and a fight with an elite among them teaches nothing. A line for a death or a forced leave: `.. died to
2 at once (Shadowmage, Dark Adept): from now on it counts them together as about N% of what it has (it had reckoned
M%)`. A death or a forced leave counts as two fights of each kind (`CountSevere`), so the note counts at once: a kind's
note counts from its second fight (`EntryCost`, `Risk::KindRatio`), and the test guild's first line read "Thunderhoof
died to 3 at once (Private Hendel, Theramore Sentry): .. about 54% (it had reckoned 54%)". The same held for a pair of
one kind since round 163: all the bot had shared out by 2.5 is below the 0.8 at which one fight counts at once. The notes feed `Risk::KindRatio`, so the other warriors judge the Dark Adept higher too. *The leave:* the run was
reckoned at 40 % of its cost for a getaway that was ready by its cooldown: Intimidating Shout, 25 rage the warrior had
not seven seconds in, and a fear 8 yd around it that would not have reached the Shadowmage bolting from range. Without
that share the run (its learned run factor is 3.6) was one it would not live through, and it would have fought on, as
it had won the same pair at 52 % a minute before. A getaway counts (`GetawayHelps`) only when the bot can pay for it
(`CanPay`: rage, energy, mana) and, for a spell that holds or scares the foes in an area around the bot (Frost Nova,
Psychic Scream, Howl of Terror, Intimidating Shout), when every foe stands within its radius (`ReachesAll`); every help
counts as ready only when it can be paid for (`HasReadyHelp`). Of the warriors' runs "by how the fight went" at 70 to
90 % health in the live log about a hundred got away and two died: the runs themselves stay as they are.

**Round 231: what a creature's death brings** (2026-11-25). Catdudu (60, feral druid) ground the Tortured Druids and
Sentinels in the south of Silithus and died at (-7145, 394) to a Hive'Ashi Drone: "fight 42 s: 2 foes at once (Hive'Ashi
Drone level 58), health 100% -> 0% ..., its target at 72% health, it was attacked", left at 31 % and died on the run. No
drone stands there: the Tortured Druids' and Sentinels' script casts "Summon Hive'Ashi Drones" (21327, one drone of level
57-58) at their death. Its fights against them cost it 3 to 10 %, a drone's 16 %; in the fatal one it was attacked, killed
two of them and had their two drones on it. Nothing of the module knew a creature's death brings another: `WorldIndex::
MinionOf` leaves deaths out (they mostly come after a quest's end or an event step). `WorldIndex::DeathSummonOf`: what a
creature's script summons at its death (`SMART_EVENT_DEATH`, a summon or a spell with a summon effect, with the count of
that effect), when it is hostile to players and attackable. It counts as one more foe of the fight wherever a fight is
judged: `FightNeed` (the check before a pull and the decision to leave a fight: each foe still alive brings its summon, at
the summon's level and its kind's learned cost, not held by a pet), the spot verdict (`FightAt`: the target's and each sure
joiner's, as company, so such a target is no single one; not among the foes that join at once) and the lines (`.. at the
death of ..` in the pull line, `the target brings .. at its death (counts in full)` in `.ga admin spot`). And the bystander
rule of round 147 had left the Dredge Crushers of the same place alone ("it is a civilian or serves the other side": the
world database gives that monster a quest giver's flag) while they attacked the bot, and a grind spot with them "counted
as empty" after a minute of picked targets: a service counts only on a creature whose faction is not hostile to every
player (Georgia, the Horde's flight master of Light's Hope, stays a bystander for the Alliance).

Ashmire (test guild, 26) "gives that up" at (-4638, -1792, -32) and (-4629, -1816, 53): no fight, the other caller

The older catch-up of a member 250 yd or more behind or on another map (SQ3) travels now too ("Squads", "Catching
up"). *Only near its leader* (2026-11-26): the walk along the roads starts only within `Squads.CatchUpYards` (250) of the
leader; one farther off travels after it by the catch-up, with flights. Sunwhisper flew from Thunder Bluff to Freewind
Post, Ashmire "had no way on foot to it (4865 yd away, 87 yd below it)" and walked 7898 yd of road for 13 minutes while

rest's pause every bot whose task had begun within its last step was "stuck" the second its rest ended (live, 19 in the
quarter of an hour after the pause was installed, about one a day before). `PauseStuck` moves a clock at most to now,
and `UpdateStuck` starts a clock again that stands ahead of now.

**Round 221: the rock beside Light's Hope once more** (2026-11-25). Shamanheal (60, enhancement shaman) was on a grind
for Rotting Sludge in the Eastern Plaguelands when Living Decay attacked it at the foot of the rock beside Light's Hope,

minutes every chase step towards the bat was refused, and every two seconds "fights something it cannot get to ... it

once. Then, after the module had ended a fight in which nothing happened, a run got it onto the rock's slope (6 yd up,
off the navmesh) and an 8 yd straight line on onto the top (`.ga admin path` on the integration server: from the foot a
path, from the slope and to the top "not using a path"); the rescue took it down. Three causes, three changes:
- *Up from a place without navmesh:* the ground guard refused a straight line onto ground without navmesh only from a
  start on the navmesh (`EndsOffTheNavmesh`), or for a step under 3 yd. Now any straight line that rises onto ground
  the navmesh does not cover is refused, wherever it starts (`GroundGuard::MayMove`, `climbsOffMesh`).
- *Giving up held for no time:* in a fight with every step refused and no way out, the creature is left alone as a foe
  that does not die (15 minutes, its spawn too), the fight is ended and the bot walks away from it
  (`OrderService::LeaveUnreachableFoe`, one line "cannot get to ... leaves that creature alone"). *Round 275:* it
  took 40 s and 20 "gives that up" before it held (Enhancer at the same rock, (2243, -5141, 53)): it looked for the
  creature in the bot's victim and in its attackers alone, and found neither most of the time. A melee bot that
  cannot get to its target has no victim (mod-playerbots' melee attack waits for the reach), and the bat that cannot
  reach the bot either regenerates in its place (the core's "cannot reach" state, its target at 100 % in the fight
  line) and attacks nobody; at each look the rule found nothing, only dropped the target and said nothing. It asks
  the AI's intended target and the creatures that have the bot on their threat list too now, and when it still
  finds none (or the bot is running) it says so once in half a minute ("cannot get to what it fights and lets go of
  its target: ...").
- *No pull of what cannot be reached:* a melee fighter does not pull a creature 4 yd or more above or below it when the
  path finder has no way to it (a straight line or nothing, or a path that ends more than 3 yd under or 5 yd beside
  it); the creature is left alone for 15 minutes (`Escape::CheckPull`, one path search per target). Not for a creature
  that flies (it comes down to whoever pulls it) or a bot that swims; a ranged fighter may still shoot it.

**Spawns under the ground** (2026-11-26). Wardps (60, warrior) worked "The Twilight Mystery" in Silithus for half an
hour around one Dust Stormer: every 30 s "does not cast Charge at Dust Stormer (-6740, 719, 5): the path finder has no
walkable ground there", twice "does not pull Dust Stormer: it stands 8 yd below it and no way on the ground leads to
it", once "cannot get to Dust Stormer ... on a level the path finder has no way to", a task "stuck" after 270 s with
its walk not getting on, 153 turns back in half an hour. That Dust Stormer's spawn (guid 46100) lies at height 4.9, 22
yd under the sand (the terrain there 24-28, the navmesh 27): no player can get to it either. mod-playerbots picks it
from above all the same (its grind target asks for 5 yd of height and the line of sight, and the core's line of sight
does not look at the terrain), so the AI turned to it again at every look, and the pull check's answer for a creature
it leaves alone was `BotDriver::DropTarget`, which stops every movement: four times a second while the walk to the
next spawn went on. Two changes:
- *The spawns put on the ground:* `tools/gen_spawn_ground.py` finds the creature spawns of maps 0 and 1 that lie 6 yd
  or more under the terrain of the server's .map files (60 yd at most), with no navmesh within 4 yd up or down, no
  walkable ground below them, no hole in the terrain and no water above them, and writes
  `data/sql/db-world/base/ga_spawn_ground.sql` (generated: an UPDATE of `position_z` per spawn onto the navmesh's
  polygon at the terrain's height there; Stitches and the Enthralled Atal'ai of the Temple's courtyard are left as
  they are). 23 of 59713 spawns, among them the Dust Stormer, the Putrid Gargoyle of the Eastern Plaguelands that a
  grind of round 156 kept picking 18 yd under its hill, a Skeletal Flayer, Demetria's spawn and a Cobalt Wyrmkin
  of Winterspring. A creature in the world moves with its next respawn or the next start.
- *Left alone without a standstill:* the pull check lets go of a creature it leaves alone with `BotDriver::LetGo`
  (the target and a chase, not the walk).

**Through a portal to its zone's side: the crossing hour** (2026-11-26). Graveborn (15, undead) wrote Silverpine off
in Undercity ("2 level-17 creatures stand together on the safest way"), picked Ghostlands for its 21 quests, took the
Orb of Translocation to Silvermoon and walked seven minutes to Ghostlands; the moment it arrived an errand of three
hand-ins outside its zone ("Return to Quinn" in Silverpine, 9000 yd) took it back through the Orb, and after a restart
the same again. A ship or zeppelin that takes a bot across sets its hour on that side (`lastCrossingAt`: no zone and no
errand across the sea for an hour, round 48); a portal or a teleporter players click set nothing, so the errand rule
saw three hand-ins and went. Now the arrival through a portal is such a crossing too when it was for a hand-in
(`errandCrossing`, its second leg allowed) or when the bot arrived on the side of its target zone; the first portal of
a longer way to its zone (Darnassus to Rut'theran for Darkshore) sets nothing.

**Round 237: a tank that cannot act; a ship's node far from the walk** (2026-11-26). Duduheal (60, druid healer) died
in Lower Blackrock Spire at Shadow Hunter Vosh'gajin: the group (Bloodyo the death knight tank, Nochnwar, Warlockdot,
Enhancer) pulled him ready, with the two Smolderthorn Shadow Priests that stood beside him, and 8 s into his fight his
SmartAI cast Hex on his victim (spell 16097: a polymorph, magic, 10 s; nobody of the group dispels magic). The boss and
both priests turned to the healer, whose heals had the most threat after the tank, and it died in 11 s beside the frog;
the rescue rule (DP6) knew only the tank as the one who takes a creature off a member. Now when the tank is dead or
crowd-controlled (confused, stunned, fleeing), another member of the group with a taunt it can cast where it stands
(Mocking Blow, which a warrior has in Battle Stance too, Dark Command, Hand of Reckoning, Taunt, Growl) takes what attacks
the healer off it, the boss first, else the boss from whichever member it went for (`StepDungeonRescue`, a line "takes
... off ...: its tank ... cannot act").
And a route of the road map no longer ends or begins at a ship's or zeppelin's node unless the walk's own end or start is
within 45 yd of it (`RoadMap::FindRoute`): a level-38 druid's walk to Jungle Stalkers 423 yd beyond Grom'gol took the
route "... > Gromgol Base Camp > Zeppelin (The Iron Eagle)", whose node stands 50 yd up beside the tower where the
zeppelin stops; the walk from it was judged through the air, the step up to it was refused at the tower's foot, and
the task ended "objective spot not reached".
*Off a zeppelin at Orgrimmar's tower.* A bot that went ashore there stood in the air and was rescued (Liriel at 02:25,
Caelithra at 02:00, eleven bots in two days, each "stands off the walkable ground" at (1318, -4658, 74)): no friendly
service stands within 250 yd of that tower, so the hop off the deck went to the zeppelin's own stop, 8 yd above the
platform, and the path finder's search for the navmesh's ground did not reach the platform from there. The hop now takes
the nearest ground of the navmesh within 25 yd of that point (`DungeonNav::NearestOnMesh`), the old search after it.
*The objective's item in a corpse it left.* A caster or a hunter kills its target 20 to 35 yd away, auto loot takes a
corpse only within `GuildAdventure.AutoLoot.Range` (10 yd), and the look at the spawn (round 91's "on to the next spawn")
moved the bot on 3 s after the fight: the item of the objective stayed in the corpse. Durgash (22, warlock) set "Consumed
by Hatred" aside twice for "10 fights at Bristleback Hunter and its like without one Bristleback Quilboar Tusk", a drop of
80 %; Vozjin (hunter) and Mahiri (shaman) the same at drops of 80 %. Now a corpse of its own kill (or its group's) within
45 yd that holds the objective's item for it is walked to before anything else of the objective, 12 s at most each
(`StepObjectiveLoot`), and the objective's NewRpg status is set again after it (the check that NewRpg left the quest
waits meanwhile: the walk is a status of its own, and the first build ended the task "NewRpg left the quest" a second
after each fight).

**Round 239: a pull that brought the hall** (2026-11-26). The owner's Bloodyo (death knight tank) died in Lower Blackrock
Spire with eleven Firebrand creatures on it: it pulled a Firebrand Grunt carefully "to its group: 6 creatures" (those
within 10 yd of it), and 14 came over 35 s, the last whose homes lay 22 to 27 yd from the Grunt. Two causes. *The count:*
every creature in a fight calls those within `CreatureFamilyAssistanceRadius` (10 yd) of it that would assist it, at
once and again every `CreatureFamilyAssistancePeriod` (3 s) from wherever it is (`Creature::CallAssistance`,
`CanPeriodicallyCallForAssistance`), so a hall whose creatures stand within that reach of one another comes one after
the other; the Firebrand hall's spawns make chains of 8, 11 and 5 within 12 yd. The conductor's pack now follows the
chain (`StepDungeonWay`: every creature within the call's reach and 2 yd of a member that would assist it, 40 at most;
the line says "N of them by calls for help"), and the camp lies where no member of the chain is within that reach and
12 yd (at most 60 yd back). *Where the group stood:* the gate gathered the group where the tank stood, and the camp lay 25
yd behind it; the pulled creature turned to the healer, who stood between the camp and the hall ("called off (something
else attacked it)" after 8.7 s), and the fight was 15 yd from the hall. Now the camp is chosen first and kept for that
creature (two minutes), the tank walks back to it and the group follows, and the gate gathers it there before the pull.
*A run from foes as fast as the bot.* Grimtusk (29, hunter) left two Needles Cougars at 66 % health ("used Disengage, Wing
Clip") and died on the run 15 s later: cats run 14 % faster than a player, and the run's estimate counted the foe at its
heels for 8 s and the other for 2.5. A foe whose run speed is the bot's or more (and that is not rooted or stunned) now
counts at its back for 15 s each (`RunNeed`), so the bot stays and fights such foes unless the run still costs less.

**The night of 2026-11-26: a target that did not die, a post of the other side** (test guild). *A nearly dead target
that does not die.* Grukthar (18, rogue) pulled two Bristleback Hunters in the Barrens; one fled at 11 % for help, the
Gouge that stopped it came 14 yd from a Bristleback Water Seeker, two Seekers joined (Frost Nova, Poison), and the rogue
died 28 s later with "its target at 20% health". The escape keeps a bot in a fight while its target is at 20 % or less
(the kill takes a foe out within seconds); a hunter that shoots from out of reach of a rogue held by a Frost Nova does
not die. That rule now holds only while the target keeps losing health: 6 s without a new low and the bot no longer
finishes it first ("no longer finishes .. first: it has stayed at N% health for 6 s"), and the fight's own estimate
decides. While the Frost Nova holds it the bot cannot run anyway (`CanRun`). *A post of the other side.* Thunderhoof
(40, druid) walked from the Dreadmurk Shore to its hand-in at Brackenwall Village; the road map's way led past Sentry
Point, where seventeen Theramore Sentries (level 35-36) stand a few yards apart around Private Hendel. It was attacked
there by three, left the fight at 31 % and died on the run. Two things let the way through: a group counted for a
walker only from three creatures not more than three levels under it (the sentries are four and five under a level-40),
and the group was what stood within 18 yd of one point of the way (three), while the sentries call one another through
the whole post (`Creature::CallAssistance`, again every few seconds from wherever the one in the fight is). Now
(`RoadMap::CrowdAt`) creatures hostile to one side only (the other side's soldiers and guards) count as a chain: every
one within 12 yd of a counted one that is a friend of it, up to 40; and a group counts for a walker from three creatures
not more than three levels under it or from four not more than eight under it (`RoadMap::GroupCounts`, used by the
route search and every walk gate): four or more creatures five to eight levels below a bot cost it 43-46 % of its
health in the live fights, with nine deaths in 105. Camps of creatures hostile to everyone keep their count. On `j5`
the way from the Dreadmurk Shore to Brackenwall's flight master for a level-40 Horde walker went over Swamplight Manor
and Sentry Point ("biggest group 3 (up to level 36)") and goes past the spirit healer now (the post counts as a group of
9, which it cannot take). Also from that night: the levelling thread's rule that a death to a group of several kinds
teaches each kind its share left the count at 54 % after Thunderhoof's death ("from now on it counts them together as
about 54% ... (it had reckoned 54%)"): a kind's note counts only from its second fight, so a first death teaches it
nothing (reported to the maintainers, not changed here).
*No stand at the quest area while the one target is dead.* Stonehorn (40) stood 263 s at "the quest area" of "Tiger
Mastery" (its Paw drops from Sin'Dall alone, one spawn, a respawn of 300 s) and Sunwhisper 240 s at the area of "Khan
Dez'hepah": the creature's spawn was down ("sees nothing ... within 45 yd: on to the next spawn" set it aside), no spawn
was left to choose, and the planner fell back to the quest's POI, where nothing happened until the rule for a quest area
that gets nowhere ended the task. A kill or item objective whose target has spawns in the zone (on the bot's map, within
the reach of quest NPCs) does not fall back to its quest area any more: it waits for those spawns, and other work comes
first.
*The tank's taunt for what attacks the healer.* the owner's Duduheal (60, druid healer) died in the Firebrand hall of Lower
Blackrock Spire at 04:32, eleven seconds after two Firebrand Grunts came onto it beside a Firebrand Invoker that cast
at it; the death knight tank had four on itself and the Invoker as its target, and the rescue's line read "3 damage
dealers turned to it" without the tank. The taunt of the rescue (P5) went only to the first creature on another member
and only when it was not the tank's target already, so the Invoker, which the tank "attacked" from 23 yd while it cast
at the healer, was never taunted, and the Grunts behind it neither. The taunt now goes to the first creature on another
member that the tank's taunt reaches (range and sight), the healer's first, whether or not it is the tank's target.

**Round 241: a walk-in round a corner, a fight it loses without hurting anyone** (2026-11-26). *A walk-in whose way
goes round.* the owner's Bloodyo (60, death knight, the tank of a Lower Blackrock Spire run) walked into a Smolderthorn
Berserker at 05:01:50 ("2 creatures with it"), 35 yd away and out of its sight; the navmesh's way there led round a
corner past Bloodaxe Evokers, which came with the Berserkers: "6 foes at once (Bloodaxe Evoker level 59)", dead 18 s
later "during travel" (the walk-in's own walk). The conductor chose the Berserker as the creature in its sight on the
way, but its way was more than twice the straight line. `GoForWalkIn` now leaves out a creature more than 15 yd away
whose way on the navmesh is longer than 1.5 times the straight line plus 10 yd (at least 40 yd): "does not walk into
..: its way there is N yd for M yd straight; the group meets it on its way", and it is no walk-in for 30 s (the
group's stretch walks the way and meets it there, with what stands on it in sight). With it: a walk-in at a creature
that is in a fight already came again each second (six lines in ten seconds for one Scarshield Legionnaire on `j5`,
"18446744073709551615 creatures with it" when its pack was empty): one line and one count per creature in 20 s.
On the same run the tank stood a minute and a half "walking into" a Smolderthorn Witch Doctor 86 yd away and a floor
below, every second, its walk getting no nearer: the creature a camp pull had been chosen for is kept for two minutes
while the group goes back to the camp, without a look at where it is now, and the walk-in's hold lets go of one beyond
60 yd. A kept creature now counts only while it is still among what stands around the tank; else it is forgotten.
*A fight it loses without hurting anyone any more.* Brakthar (21, warrior of the test guild) fought a Stormsnout to 42 %
at "Egg Hunt" and then hurt nothing for 60 s, a healing potion included, until the rule for a foe that does not die
ended the fight at 39 % health; a minute later it fought a Thunderhead (21) for 80 s, a second potion, and died, "its
target at 100% health". The rule for a foe that is not hurt at all (fifteen seconds) did not hold, since a foe had been
hurt, and the 60 s of no progress came too late. Now (`TrackFight`) a bot outside a group that has hurt none of its
foes for 20 s and lost 20 % of its health since the last foe it hurt (potions counted against it) has its fight ended
as for a foe that does not die (the creature and its spawn left alone 15 min, the task ended, a walk away), and the
line names its target, its distance and reach, whether it swings and faces it, and what holds its AI, so the next case
shows why it did no damage (the live log has no reason: the lizards fought normally in other fights).
*A pull of one that brought three.* Thunderhoof (41, druid) pulled a Firemane Scout in Dustwallow Marsh ("its own pull
(1 expected)"), two Firemane Ash Tails came and it died with its target at 1 %. Not changed: the Scout and the Ash
Tails stand 30 to 40 yd apart with no call for help or flee script in their rows, and the live log has no `pull joiner`
line (debug is off there); the cause is not known.

**Round 242: a chain that drew in a neutral pack** (2026-11-26, test guild). Liriel (32, paladin) fought a Highland
Strider in Arathi, "its own pull (1 expected)"; two seconds later Fozruk (42) and three seconds later Sleeby (40), Znort
and Feeboz (39) were on it, and it died with Lay on Hands spent. The four are a formation (Fozruk the leader, his
companions assisting him) on a round of 235 waypoints across the Highlands, and they are neutral (faction template 15,
the "Creature" faction with no enemy group): they attack nobody by themselves, so the pull check rightly did not count
them. What drew them in was Liriel's own Seal of Command (it knows spell 20375 and had it on): in 3.3.5 each melee swing
with it chains to up to two more creatures within 5 yd of the target, and a chain, like every spell that hits enemies,
hits neutral creatures too; the formation walked past the Strider (Sleeby's last home 2 yd from where the Strider stood)
and Fozruk's companions came with him. Now (`Escape::StepSealOfCommand`, four times a second for characters the AI
plays) a paladin in a fight takes its Seal of Command off while a creature in no fight stands within 5 yd of it or 6 yd of
its target ("takes its Seal of Command off: Fozruk (level 42, neutral, 4 yd away) is in no fight and its swings would
chain to it"), and mod-playerbots' "seal of command" is not put on meanwhile (its list then takes the next seal,
Righteousness); Consecration is not cast while such a creature stands within 9 yd. `Escape::StrongBystanderWithin`
(the mage's area spells, a step back) counts neutral creatures as well. Not covered: the area attacks of the other
classes (a warrior's Cleave or Thunder Clap, a druid's Swipe, ...) beside a neutral pack.
(Only for a creature beside a target the paladin swings at, within 10 yd of it: on `j5` the seal came off for a Sand
Skitterer 148 yd away that stood beside a victim as far off.)

**Round 242, the rest of it: a walk-in refused again and again; a rest in the sea with no place for it** (2026-11-26).
*A walk-in refused again and again.* the owner's Palatwo (the tank of a Blackrock Depths Upper City run) "could not pull" a
Doomforge Craftsman to a camp and "did not walk into" it every 2 to 4 s, "its way there is 1065 yd for 38 yd straight"
(53 lines in a round). The careful pull had chosen the camp for the Craftsman before its pull failed, and the blocker
choice keeps a camp's creature for two minutes past every other rule, so the creature that GoForWalkIn had just left out
came back each tick: the camp chose it, the pull failed, the walk-in refused it. Now a failed pull gives its camp up, the
kept camp holds only a creature the pull and the walk-in have not left out, and a creature GoForWalkIn leaves out for
its way is no blocker for two minutes (`DungeonRun::wayRefused`), its line once in ten minutes.
*A rest in the sea with no place for it.* Mahiri (21, shaman of the test guild) worked the naga of "Naga at the Zoram
Strand" 12 yd under the sea of Ashenvale; at 74 % health and 25 % mana it "needed a rest ... and found no dry ground
within 150 yd: it does not rest in the water and goes on", fought a Sea Witch down to 2 % mana with a potion, pulled the
next at 4 % ("1 expected"), a Razortail came from 38 yd and it died with its target at 1 %, "under water for 99 s" (the
death line's note; it did not drown). Two causes: the rest's search for dry ground looked at its rings at the bot's own
height, 12 yd under the beach, where the path finder finds no ground (it looks 5 yd up and down), and from under the
surface the path finder has no whole path at all; and with no place found the bot went on and pulled. Now
(`Escape::FindRestSpot`) a bot in the water looks at the ground under each spot of its rings, and a bot under the surface
asks the path from the surface above it and swims that way, up and along the surface ("went N yd ashore first (up and
along the surface)", `MoveSplinePath`); and while a rest is due and there is no place for it the check before a pull
holds every pull ("does not pull ..: it needs a rest (health N%, mana N%) and has no place to take one here; it waits for
its health and mana where it stands"), so it starts no fight until its health and mana are back above the leader's
thresholds. A creature that attacks it is fought as before.
*A camp that walks towards the way.* Hordeboss (45, the test guild's leader, in watch mode) worked the Wastewander
camps of Tanaris and set out for a Southsea pirate 498 yd away; 13 s later three were on it (a Wastewander Shadow Mage,
voidwalkers) at the mages' camp, and it died. Staged on `j5` with the debug lines: it "went around 4 creatures on its way
.. and the 2 that stand with them", rode on from the walk's end along the edge of the camp's circle, and three seconds
later a mage was on it 17 yd from its spot: the mages walk 15 yd about their spots, and the circle and the look on the
way counted each creature where it stood at that moment. Now (`NearestOnWay`, `WalkAbout`) a creature that walks about at
random counts as near as its walk about its home can bring it (up to 15 yd; a summoned minion with its summoner's walk):
for the look on the way, the circle of a walk around a camp and the leg to its point.
*A fight that ends beside a pack.* Stonehorn (43, warrior, the test guild) went around a Bloodsail camp of the Southern
Savage Coast on its way to a hand-in, was attacked by a warlock and its succubus, and chased the warlock when it ran for
help towards three swashbucklers and a warlock that stand together; it killed it and stood 7 yd from them when its fight
ended. Five seconds later the four were on it ("it would not live through the run") and it died. Now a fight that ends
within the reach of creatures the bot cannot take together (not in a fight, within their aggro range plus 10 yd, with
what stands within the core's call for help of them; the pack look's own measure) sends the bot back the way it came
before anything else (`Escape::BackOutAfterFight`, "backs out of the place after its fight, beside N creatures it cannot
take together"); the task it was on ends as for a pack on its way. Not in a dungeon.

*A pack on its round coming at a bot that stands.* Skelwyn (30, rogue, the test guild) ground in Thousand Needles and
stood six seconds after a won fight when Achellios the Banished (a level-31 rare on a waypoint round) and his three Galak
Packhounds (his formation) came along their round onto it: six foes in all, and it died. The look for a pack on the way
looks only along a moving bot's way. Now a bot that stands (out of a fight) also looks at creatures that walk a round, or
with a formation leader that does, whose next leg leads into their reach of it and nearer to it than they are now: with
their formation and what answers their call for help, a pack it cannot take together (the pack look's measure) sends it
away as from a pack on its way that walks (`Escape::FindPackComing`, "keeps away from N creatures that come at it on their
round that it cannot take together"); the task waits for them to pass.

*A shaman's Fire Nova beside neutral creatures.* Rhazko (23, enhancement shaman, the test guild) pulled one creature in the
Barrens ("1 expected") while the herd of four kodos of the Field of Giants walked past it; two seconds later all four were on
it and it died. Kodos are neutral (faction 7, which has no reputation: the core lets a player hit them) and attack nobody by
themselves, so the pull check rightly left them out; but they walk as one formation (`creature_formations`, group AI 515: the
others engage what one fights), and mod-playerbots' enhancement shaman casts Fire Nova whenever its foe is in melee: the
flames burst from its fire totem (10 yd, spell 8349) and hit neutral creatures as any area spell does. Now Fire Nova is not
cast while a creature in no fight stands within 12 yd of the shaman's fire totem (the radius and the creature's size;
`GuildFireNovaAction` in `BotDriver::GuardConsumables`, `Escape::BystanderWithin`, the same search as the mage's area spells
without their strength limit; "does not cast Fire Nova: Barrens Kodo (level 20, neutral) stands 8 yd from its Searing Totem
III and is in no fight").

*A patrol's formation on a rest's road.* Thrakgar (30, the test guild) won a fight in Thousand Needles at 52 % health, took
a bandage and rested 23 yd away ("1 hostile creatures near, 0 there"); seven seconds later a Pesterhide Snarler and
Steelsnap were on it, and it died. Steelsnap (level 30) walks a round of 94 points with two Snarlers that have no path of
their own (`creature_formations`, group AI 514: they follow him), and the risk model's packs on a round (`PatrolPacks`)
knew only patrols with paths of their own (the Crimson Courier and his bodyguards). Now a patrol's formation members walk
with it in that count (`sFormationMgr->CreatureGroupMembers`; a rare member is left out), so a formation on its round
that the bot cannot take together is "too strong for it" for spots (the spot verdict) and for a rest's quiet place
(`Risk::OnStrongRoad`: 40 yd off its road). The look for a pack coming at a bot that stands (above) also covers a rest.

*No forge in a town of the other side.* Liriel (35, Horde, the owner's guild) caught up on its Mining in Duskwood and walked
1500 yd to the forge of Goldshire to smelt ("it leads through a town of the other side"); every travel out of the town
was then refused for the town it stood in, and it went home by hearthstone. A travel to an anvil or forge
(`PlanFocusTrip`) had no way gate of its own and the town rule of `WalkTo` counted every travel as one with a gate. Now
`PlanFocusTrip` leaves out a place in a town of the other side (`RoadMap::InHostileTown`), and the walk to an anvil or
forge and the walk to a waiting squad member are held to the town rule of `WalkTo` like the walks without a gate.

*A straight way past a town of the other side.* Durgash (28, Horde, the owner's guild) stood among creatures at Raynewood
Retreat in Ashenvale with nothing to do and was sent 351 yd out to the spirit healer of Nightsong Woods; the path finder
walks straight there, but the road map's way (1491 yd over The Shady Nook) led past five Ashenvale Sentinels 75 yd beside
the healer, the town rule refused the walk, and two such ends sent it home by hearthstone. Now, when the road map's way
leads through a town of the other side and the straight line does not, the path finder's way hop by hop (`ChainReaches`,
at most 1.6 times the straight line plus 100 yd) is walked instead ("takes the straight way to (x, y) (travel): the road
map's way (...) leads through a town of the other side; the path finder has one of N yd past it").

*An objective far around by road, near on the navmesh.* Gorruk (33, the owner's guild) at Ghost Walker Post in Desolace had
the Hatefury satyrs of "Befouled by Satyr" 1260 yd off and 7000 yd by the roads; the path finder's straight way hop by hop
(148 polygons a hop, the grids loaded around the bot) had none, so the spawns were left as too far around three times in a
row, the quest set aside, the zone written off twice and the bot sent home by hearthstone. `tools/navpath` on the whole
navmesh walks there in 1375 yd. Now the rule for an objective far around asks the open world's navmesh (`DungeonNav`)
after the path finder, once per task: a way of at most 1.6 times the straight line plus 100 yd (4000 yd at most) whose
own legs the walk gate lets through (what lives on them, a group, a camp, a place set aside, as for a straight way) is
walked along the navmesh ("takes the navmesh's way to ... for quest ...: N yd (M yd straight), the road map's (...) is L
yd"; else "does not take the navmesh's way ...: it passes ..."). For a level-31 test character at the same place the way
is 1346 yd, refused for what lives on it, as the straight line was.

*A grind spot behind a camp.* Priestyo (60, priest, the owner's guild) kept away from Zaeldarr the Outcast's pack of
Mossflayers in the Eastern Plaguelands, was given a Putrid Gargoyle 319 yd off as its next grind spot, walked into the
Mossflayer camp and died there with three on it and no way out. A grind spot whose straight way leads through the
middle of a camp the bot cannot take is now left out (`PlanGrind`, `Risk::EntersCamp`, the last 40 yd the spot's own
matter; not for a bot that stands at a camp). Open: that camp is of level 53 to 55, so for a level-60 bot it is "too far
below it to count" by level (camps hold up to three levels above their creatures), although a Mossflayer costs Priestyo
33 % of its strength alone; a camp judged by the kinds' costs a bot has learned would catch it.

*The hearthstone for nothing safe, in one zone.* Thrakgar (30, the test guild) found nothing in Thousand Needles it could
safely get to, travelled to Ashenvale, found nothing there 13 minutes later, and the rule "the second time within half an
hour" sent it home by hearthstone, to Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. The two times now count only in the same zone.

**Round 245: a stair that a straight surface line clips; a pulled creature's formation** (2026-11-26).

*The surface walk along the navmesh's corners.* Palatwo (60, paladin of the owner's guild) led the group of his Blackrock
Depths Upper City run (a run until it is stopped, begun anew after every restart of the round) and stood an hour, from
08:57 to 11:05 in bursts, at the top of the East Garrison's stair at (597, -64, -52) on its way to the Emperor: "starts
travel", the step to its next point of the navmesh's way (640, -128, -46), 77 yd on, refused as "shortcut + no path"
(the core's path finder had no polygon there, as in Lower Blackrock Spire on 2026-11-25), "travels and stands ... gives
that up", "ends travel after 17 s: stuck", every 17 s, until the boss clock passed the Emperor over. The surface walk that
answers such a refusal (`ViaDungeonPath`) walked the straight line to the next point over the navmesh's surface, and from
there that line clips the side of the stair 4 yd out (the navmesh's way bends round it: `tools/navpath` gives 79 yd over
corners at (598.9, -67.7) and (600.5, -71.5)), so `moveAlongSurface` stopped there and the walk was not taken; from 6 yd
beside it, at 02:09, the same line had gone through. When the straight line stops short, the surface is now walked leg by
leg along the corners of the navmesh's own way to the point (`DungeonNav::FindWay`, `SurfaceLine` per leg).

*A pulled creature's formation.* Grimtusk (37, hunter of the test guild) died in Arathi to Fozruk (a neutral level-42
ogre) and Sleeby, Znort and Feeboz, the three companions of his formation on their round through the Highlands: its own
pull of one of them, "1 expected", brought all four in the same second ("pull joiner ... after 0 s"). The core makes the
members of a formation engage with the one that engages when its row in `creature_formations` says so (`CreatureGroup::
MemberEngagingTarget`: the leader's row needs "members assist the leader", a member's row "the leader assists its
members"; Fozruk's companions have 515, so a pull of any of them brings all four, neutral or not). The pull check counted
creatures that answer a call for help and creatures whose aggro reaches the way, neither of which neutral formation
members are; it now counts every member such a row brings, of the target and of every sure joiner. On the j5 instance
Hordeboss (46) turned to Sleeby on that round: "attacked, foe 1 ... 4 after 0 s" (Fozruk, Sleeby, Znort, Feeboz), as live.
With it, a hunter's Multi-Shot, Volley and Explosive Trap are not cast while a creature in no fight stands in their reach
(the rule of Fire Nova and Seal of Command, rounds 242 and 243).

*A quest item inside a clam.* Thunderhoof (46, druid of the test guild) stood 338 s at "the quest area" of the Zesty Clam
Meat of "Clamlette Surprise" in Tanaris until NewRpg gave up. The meat comes only from opening a Big-mouth Clam, whose use
spell (58165) hands out `spell_loot_template` loot, and the clam drops from 94 kinds of creature (up to 53 %); the item
source index knew containers by `item_loot_template` only, so the meat had no source. Items whose use spell has loot of
its own now count as containers of what that loot holds (`WorldIndex::IndexItemSources`), for the source index only:
LootService opens such a clam when it is looted (CT1), so they are not quest containers. On the j5 instance: 2738 quest
items with sources (2737 before).

**Round 246: a long walk the path finder has no path for** (2026-11-26). Liriel (36, paladin of the test guild) took the
straight way to the Syndicate Highwaymen of "Foul Magics" in Arathi (the road map's way led round by Hammerfall and
Witherbark Village): 877 yd from (-986, -2987, 61) to (-894, -2115, 46). Its own steps found "no path ... path type 0xa,
2 points" three times, the walk ended "no way", and that end counted against the spot for the whole guild: the third
such end within a day, so the guild left the camp alone for 24 h; the same a minute later for a second camp 640 yd off,
then the quest waited a quarter of an hour. The navmesh has both ways, 893 and 932 yd along almost straight lines
(`tools/navpath`); the core's path finder sees 148 polygons of the loaded grids, and `.ga admin path` on the j5 instance
gives "shortcut + no path" for the same walk where `.ga admin navway` gives 893 yd over 12 corners. Before a walk's own
steps are given up as "no way", the whole navmesh is asked once per task in the open world (`WalkTo`, the own steps'
fail rule): with a way of up to 4000 yd the bot walks it as an open way (`task.openWay`, `ViaDungeonPath`), with a line
`finds no path with the path finder ... the navmesh has a way of N yd there`. With it: the danger map leaves out spawns
that stand there only during a holiday (`game_event_creature`: the Flame Eaters of the Midsummer fires, level 42-60),
as `WorldIndex` does for everything else (`RoadMap::IndexHostiles`); the look-out still sees what stands there while
the holiday runs. (Liriel's refused flight walk at Apocryphan's Rest was the Siege Golems, rank 2 of level 40, counted
nine levels higher as elites: as built.)

*A navmesh walk that ended at its first refused step.* The walk along the whole navmesh's way to a target on another
level (the round of the Grimtotem mesas) was set aside at its first refused step: the refusal reaction asked
`SetAsideOtherLevel` again, which had tried the navmesh once already and went on to the road node and then to "set
aside", 6 to 19 s after "the navmesh has a way of 255 yd there, and it walks that way" (Graveborn and Morthos at Apothecary
Zinge in the Undercity's Apothecarium, 27 yd below the ring they stood on, 2026-11-26 01:21 and 03:42; the third such end
of the day made the guild leave Zinge alone for 24 h). While the bot walks the navmesh's way, four refused steps are let
pass, and the walk's next leg goes along the navmesh's surface (`ViaDungeonPath`'s refusal rule, which did not see the
refusal because the reaction had taken it: `BotTask::navRefusedAt`). On the j5 instance Hordeboss handed "Zinge's
Delivery" in from the Undercity's ring by the road map's route (Undervator, Khanok, Putress) and its own steps, without a
refused step, so the new rule did not come into it there.

**Round 247: a dive to the sea floor; a flight at the master; the journey gap of a flight not taken** (2026-11-26).
*Dives.* Ainuha (16) of the test guild swam 211 yd towards a Drysnap Crawler of "Clam Bait" off Shadowprey Village and
was 34 yd under the sea floor 26 s later (rescued); Frostvein's next swim there ended 11 yd under it. The swim's last
stretch went from the surface to the target's depth in one slanting line, which runs through the rock where the floor
rises between them. A landing more than 3 yd under the surface now gets a point over it at the surface first, and the
swim goes straight down from there (`StepSwim`); its legs are measured in three dimensions (a leg straight down has no
2D length). On the j5 instance the shaman's AI put Water Walking on Mojowind a second into such a swim, and on the water
no character dives: while the next point lies under the surface the AI rests and the aura is taken off. A fight on the
way holds the leg's clock (Mojowind gave a swim up five seconds after a fight of 24 s, "gets no nearer"). An objective's
spot within sight is NewRpg's to walk to, and the swim looks only in the planner's walks: when a refused step arms the
swim, the planner takes the objective's walk over until within 8 yd (a crawler 15 yd down behind a rock, 41 yd away,
was set aside at the next refusal without a look). The objective's look around ("sees nothing of quest .. within 45 yd:
on to the next spawn") reaches as far up or down as the spot lies, up to 60 yd more (a bot over a crawler 47 yd down saw
nothing within 45 yd). With the dive point and the aura rule Mojowind (32) dove to the crawlers on the floor of
Shadowprey's bay on the j5 instance and fought them there, no rescue. *A flight at the master.* A flight asked for after the way on foot was refused is judged at the
master as it was then (`TryFlight(.., afterRefusal)`: the walks to the master and from the landing do not count against
it); Ashmire walked 14 yd to Gringer in Booty Bay for Grom'gol, was turned down there for "the walks are most of the way"
and walked into the country its way had been refused for. *The journey gap.* A journey that ended before its flight
(`BotTask::flew` stays false) does not hold the next one back: its five-minute gap made seven tasks of Ashmire in
Stranglethorn Vale end "no flight: it has just flown for another task" within 16 s, and the zone was written off for
six hours.

*Up from a detour under water.* A long walk that begins under water goes up to the surface first; that look was
latched for the whole task when the task began ashore. Sheesh (60) mined an Iron Deposit 58 yd down in Faldir's Cove on
a detour of its vendor walk, and every step on ran through the rock of the cove, refused for a minute and a half until
the vendor was given up. The look now runs whenever the bot is under water (`WalkTo`), and only a destination down there
too latches it. *Across the sea when nothing is left on its side.* A bot that found nothing to do where it stands goes
for the zone on its side with the most quests, however few; with none left there it now crosses for a zone worth a move
(three quests, not the eight of an ordinary crossing; the hour after a landing and the zones it found empty from where
it stood still hold). Morwenna (30, Horde) counted 0 in every zone of the Eastern Kingdoms but Stranglethorn Vale's 1,
whose way was refused, went home by hearthstone and ground on with Thousand Needles at 5 across the sea.

*A forge within reach by its walk.* A place to craft looked for within a reach (a hub's 200 yd, the 1500 yd of smelting
on a Mining catch-up) is taken only when its walk (`WalkLength`: the road map's route, else the path finder's) is at most
one and a half times that reach. Skelwyn (33), catching its Mining up in Desolace, set out for the forge of Shadowprey
Village 1410 yd away as the crow flies, a route of 5077 yd round the centaurs' land, walked eight minutes and gave it up
for a pack on its way.

**Round 248: "nothing it can safely get to", and what a level above costs** (2026-11-26). The hearthstone of a bot
that found nothing in its zone it could safely get to twice within half an hour gave 42 of the live server's 70
hearthstones that day, nearly all of the test guild's Horde bots of level 25 to 36 in Desolace, Thousand Needles,
Ashenvale and Stonetalon, the two checks one to fifteen minutes apart and the stone mostly to Freewind Post or Shadowprey
Village, in or beside the zone (the owner: the hearthstone for the utmost emergency only, L32). The second check now counts
only when it comes at least five minutes after the first and within 300 yd of where the first was made: a bot that moved
on is not boxed in, and two checks a minute apart say the same thing; a check too soon from the same place leaves the
first standing. *Why so often.* The refused walks of those bots that day: 376 for a group on the way (pairs one to three
levels above the bot 146 of them, trios at its level 33), 147 for a camp (all but 13 at the bot's level or below), 138
far around, 110 for a level, 89 for a town of the other side, 67 for a place set aside. The groups are judged with the
bot's own fight costs, every level above the bot multiplying a foe's cost by `CostPerLevelAbove`, 1.3, which nothing
had measured. Over 15,000 single fights the bots below level 60 won from 2026-11-20 to 26, each bot against its own
fights at its level (health and half the mana), one level above cost 1.20, two 1.44, three 1.61 to 1.70: 1.2 a level
(three below 0.70, two 0.78, one 0.89; `CostPerLevelBelow` stays 0.92). Pairs two levels above cost 2.28 single fights at
the bot's level on average and 3.81 in their worst tenth, and none of 119 was lost; the model with 1.3 made them 4.2,
with 1.2 3.6. `CostPerLevelAbove` is 1.2 now; what an elite's or a rare's health and damage are worth in levels
(`ThreatLevelOf`, `EliteMultiplier`) keeps the old 1.3 (`StrengthPerLevel`). Trios at the bot's level are left as they
are: 20 of 57 such fights were left or lost. Camps too: they are trios and more at the bot's level.

**Round 252 (round 257 of the server): a look that did not reach the spawn, a hearthstone that waits, the navmesh's way judged** (2026-11-26).
Kodahorn (33, a cat druid) walked to Khan Dez'hepah (35) of "Khan Dez'hepah" in Desolace, got off its mount 55 yd before
him and saw "nothing of quest 1365 within 45 yd": the look at an objective's creatures begins once the bot is within
60 yd of the spawn (`SightDistance`) and reached 45 yd from the bot. The task ended, the next one (Hatefury Betrayers,
534 yd east) led straight through Khan's place, and 6 s later the bot fought Khan, his Kolkar Destroyer (22 yd west of
him) and a Kolkar Battle Lord and died. On the j5 instance a level-33 druid turned to Khan from 48 yd was refused the
pull ("1 more would join (Kolkar Destroyer 32); the fight would cost it about 145%"), as the quest's task would have been.
The look now reaches the spawn and 15 yd beyond it (80 yd at most) and as far up or down as before.
*A hearthstone that waits.* Sunwhisper (42, priest) found nothing in Tanaris it can safely get to from Wavestrider Beach
twice, 15 min apart, used its hearthstone to Gadgetzan, 1300 yd off in the same zone, and a second later picked Feralas,
a flight from Gadgetzan it could have walked to. The second such look no longer uses the stone at once: it waits three
minutes, and the stone is used only when the bot then still stands within 300 yd of the place, between two tasks and
out of a fight (`BotRuntime::nothingSafeHearthAt`, at the top of `RunAdventure`).
*The navmesh's way judged.* Stonehorn (49) stood on a cliff above the Southsea pirates' cove in Tanaris; its routes to
Gadgetzan's flight master began with a guessed first step, so it asked the whole navmesh and took its way, four times in
a minute, and each time the look for packs ended it at once: "its way led into the middle of their camp" (32 creatures).
Then "the place holds it" and the hearthstone. The navmesh's way is the shortest and knows no creatures. Every place that
takes it now judges its legs first as the straight way of an objective is judged (`OrderService::NavWayIsSafe`: danger,
a group it cannot take, the middle of a camp it cannot take, a place set aside), and a way that does not do is not taken
(`... the navmesh's way (N yd) does not do: ...`). At a camp's edge only the first 60 yd are let pass (the way out); before,
a bot at a camp's edge had its whole navmesh way let pass.
*A target four levels up.* Rhazko (31, shaman) pulled a Sparkleshell Snapper of level 35 among the tortoises of "Hardened
Shells" in Thousand Needles: the estimate said "1 expected" and a cost it could afford, a Crystalhide and a Reaver came, and
it died. The spot verdict leaves a target four or more levels above the bot alone (`Risk.MaxFoeLevelAbove`), but the AI
turns to whatever stands among the quest's targets, and the check before a pull judged only the cost. A target whose
strength (its level, an elite's by its health and damage) is four or more levels above the bot is not pulled now, whatever
the estimate says, and no rest is waited for it (`does not pull ...: it is 4 or more levels above it`).
*A copy of what it wears, put on every minute.* Mojowind (50, shaman) carried five Franciscas (main hand only) beside the
one it wore; the module's look for an upgrade beside an older copy of its kind (`StorageSupply::WearBagDuplicates`)
put one of them on in place of the one it wore every minute, 573 times in a day, Zulkash 144 times, and once in place of
an Axe of Rin'ji (53) it had just taken out of the guild storage: mod-playerbots' upgrade check compares a piece with the
weakest place of its kind (the off hand), and the place it goes to may hold a copy of it or a better piece.
`PutOnThisOne` puts nothing in place of what scores as much or more there, and a one-hand weapon of a bot that holds
two goes in place of the one that scores less.
*An island.* Kodahorn (34) was given the hand-in of "Claim Rackmore's Treasure!" at Rackmore's Chest on Ranazjar Isle,
680-850 yd off Desolace's coast; its travel ended "stuck" at once, twice, and the errand was given up for half an hour,
again and again: the swim to a target (round 101) is armed only by a step the ground check refused, and a walk that
never starts refuses none. A walk with no route and no whole way of the path finder looks for the swim first, once per
task (`OrderService::WalkTo`).
*The guild leader's consumables.* the owner watched his leader through a Dire Maul West run: its four bots used their
elixirs and scrolls inside, Retadin nothing. The leader's character was played by hand at the start (or not yet in the
world), so it was not among the members that got their round; once the AI plays it, it is. A member that is in the
group and had no round of the run's consumables yet gets it then (`DungeonRun::suppliesGiven`).
*A caster that turns to the healer while the tank pulls it back.* Wartank taunted a Petrified Treant to a camp 65 yd
back ("casters among them"); the Treant stood and cast at the priest, and the group stood 16 s "too far away" before the
tank went to it (the owner: [quote left out]). A
careful pull whose creature, on the way back or while the tank waits, turns to somebody else ends at once and the tank
goes to it (`Escape::StepPull`: `the creature turned to <name>, the bot goes to it`).
*A run from casters and nets (round 259).* Mojowind (50, shaman) had a hand-in at the Bloodsail Correspondence in the
middle of the pirates' camp on the Wild Shore, an errand across the sea from Tanaris: the errand judged the ender's
place only when it lies on the bot's own map. At the camp's edge three Bloodsail of level 40 were on it; it left the
fight at 87 % health and died on the run 36 s later: two Bloodsail Mages cast Fireball at its back every four to six
seconds, a Raider's Net held it. The run's estimate counted a foe that cannot keep up for its first seconds only. A kind
whose script casts a damage spell of 20 yd's reach or more every eight seconds or less, or a spell that roots, counts
for the whole run like a foe as fast as the bot (`WorldIndex::HoldsARunner`, in `RunNeed`), so the bot stays and fights
where the run would not save it; and an errand's ender is judged on any map (`OrderService::FindErrand`).
*The watched leader in a dungeon group (round 260).* the owner: [quote left out]. The conductor's rules for the members (the slots on the tank's trail, the walk to the tank, the catch-up, out of
traps, the rescue runs, the spread, the stomach and the twins' sides) asked `GuildBotHolder::IsAIDriven`, which is true
only for a guild bot on its home session: the leader's character in watch mode is played by the AI on its owner's client
session, so the conductor left it out and only mod-playerbots' follow moved it. They ask `IsAIPlayed` now (a guild bot or
a watched character), and so do the look for ground effects and the Starfall rule.
*Alone after a restart, and the way back to the group (round 260).* the owner: [quote left out]. Read on the live log: the run began anew at 18:13:46 with its four bots, which stood among creatures
and were taken to the entrance; the owner's login put Retadin into the world two seconds later where it had stood with them,
243 yd from the entrance, and the AI played it (watch on login). Then the tank, waiting for it, walked 243 yd straight
back to it (the rule of round 191 that walks a waiting leader beside its member when hostile creatures stand near), and
the member walked the navmesh's way to the tank: both through Petrified Guardians and Treants nobody had fought. Now:
- a member that comes into the world within a minute and a half of its login after its run had begun, more than 60 yd
  from its leader inside the same instance, is put beside the leader once, as the members are when a run begins with
  its group apart (`came into the world inside ... after its group's run had begun`);
- a member of a dungeon group 40 yd or more from its leader whose navmesh way back passes a hostile creature in no fight (within
  its aggro range and 4 yd, 6 yd up or down; one the leader stands that near to does not count) does not walk it: it
  holds where it is (its movement stopped and its AI held, `RunSquadMember`) and its leader comes back for it along the way, the tank first, as for a member with no way up
  (`waits where it is ...: its way to ... passes ..., which is in no fight; its group comes back for it`, the leader's
  `goes back to ...: ... would pass ... on its way`); the way is looked at again every 10 s, and after two and a half
  minutes the member walks as before;
- the waiting leader's walk to its member is for the open world only (in a dungeon creatures stand near wherever a
  group waits, and the run has its own rules for a member behind).
*Two foes at once, by class (option A).* The estimate counted two foes of the bot's level as 2.5 single fights for
every class (`Escape::OthersShare`: while the cheaper foe is killed, the other counts half a foe). Measured on the
integration server's fights since 2026-11-24 (won fights against two foes within three levels below the bot, against
the same bot's single fights), the median was 1.8 single fights for a rogue, priest or mage, 2.0-2.2 for a warrior,
paladin or shaman, 2.3-2.4 for a hunter, warlock or druid and 2.6 for a death knight: the flat share made the cheap
classes refuse pairs they take (Morwenna and others turned from one refused Kolkar pair of Desolace to the next every
few seconds) and the expensive ones pull pairs that cost more. The owner chose option A: each class learns from these
fights what two foes really cost it. Now every fight against exactly two ordinary foes teaches the character what the
second foe cost on top of two single fights, as a share of the cheaper one by what the character knew of each kind
before the fight (a fight lost, or left by how it went, counts as costing all it had); its value is the mean of its
first five such fights, then a running average, kept in `ga_bot_pair_share`. The share every estimate uses (the check
before a pull, the spot verdict, `Risk::CanFight`, the look for a group on the way, the kind notes' own sums) is the
mean of its class over the characters with three such fights or more, between 0 and 1.5 (`Escape::OthersShareOf`,
`Risk::PairShare`); 0.5 while no character of the class has three. The startup line `two foes at once, the share of
a second foe by class: ...` names what each class has learned.
*No hearthstone while it grinds (round 260).* Thunderhoof, a level-52 druid of the test guild, ground the dinosaurs of
Un'Goro at about 65000 experience an hour (its quests there lay behind places it had set aside) and took its
hearthstone to Feralas: it had found nothing it could safely get to twice, and the rule of round 196 (with its wait of
three minutes between two tasks) let the stone go 74 s after its last fight. A bot that grinds where it stands has
work: the delayed hearthstone now waits while the bot has fought in the last three minutes
(`BotRuntime::lastFightEndAt`, set when a fight ends), and after 15 minutes of such fights the pending stone is dropped.
The stone of a bot boxed in (eight refused ways at one place, round 99) waits the same way: Saelanya, a level-33 priest,
ground the satyrs of Sargeron in Desolace at 30000 experience an hour for six minutes while its ways out were refused,
and took its hearthstone a minute after its last fight (round 263).
*Walks that stand still; a camp below a cliff (round 260).* In an hour of the integration server (2026-11-26) 41
objectives waited 26 s on average before the planner took the walk over from NewRpg ("has not set off"), and 145 walks
of the planner stood 10 s before its own steps took them ("does not get on with its walk"), most of them seconds after a
fight or a loot: about 42 minutes of standing an hour over some 70 bots. The first now waits 12 s (was 25). The cause
of the second is not found yet: no moving flag was left set in any of the stalls looked at (a first guess), NewRpg's
state was "go camp" with the idle movement, and in four of ten the AI was held for six to nine seconds more at the
moment of the stall. So the stall line names NewRpg's state, the movement and the AI's state, and the AI's state names
a pause of the module of 3 s or more by its place in the code (`BotDriver::PauseAI` keeps its caller's place:
"held for N ms more (the module's pause of M ms from File.cpp:line)", else "mod-playerbots' own"); the next round's
lines are to show who holds it. And Gorruk, a level-42 warrior of the test guild, walked along the beach of the Wild
Shore through the middle of the Bloodsail camp for the Naga Explorers of "Akiris by the Bundle", which stand on a cliff
100 yd above it 200 yd away, and died there with five on it: the camp look (`FindCampAhead`) passes over a camp near
the spot of the bot's task, and did so for a spot on another level. It does so now only for a spot within 20 yd of the
bot's height, and the pack look takes the creatures beside such a spot in three dimensions.

*Why the walks stood: a creature let go of and picked again (round 263).* The stall lines of the next round (419d988
live, 25 minutes, 67 stalls) said "rpg go camp, movement 0" in 64 and the AI held in only 12, never by a pause of the
module: NewRpg had the walk and the AI was free, and the bot did not move. In 25 of them the bot had let go of a
creature beside its way a few seconds before ("leaves ... alone on its way: nothing its work wants"; that line is
written once per creature in ten minutes, so more of the others were the same). mod-playerbots' grind target is the
nearest creature within its aggro range and ten yards while NewRpg walks, and its "attack anything" took it again at
every look of the AI; the module's check before a pull let it go four times a second, and each pick stopped the walk
and put the AI into its combat engine for a moment. Now the module puts its own "attack anything" into each bot's AI
context (`GuildAttackAnythingAction`, as the drink and food actions): it is not used for a creature the bot let go of
in the last 30 s (`BotDriver::LetGo` notes it, `BotDriver::IsLetGo`), so mod-playerbots leaves it alone and NewRpg
walks on. A grind and a quest's creatures are not let go of, so nothing they fight changes.

*Loot beside the way held for twice in vain.* Graveborn and Ainuha (35, 37) got off their mounts again and again for a
Food Crate of Nesingwary's camp in Stranglethorn that mod-playerbots did not loot: the hold of 30 s, then mod-playerbots'
own short retry delay, then the next look brought it back; Graveborn's travel ended "stuck" 86 yd from where it began.
An object it held for and did not loot (the object still there to loot when the hold ended) is left alone for a quarter
of an hour the next time it comes up within ten minutes, and at once after a hold that ran its 30 s
(`BotRuntime::lootIgnored`); the line "leaves <object> beside its way ... alone for 15 min: it held for it before and did
not loot it".

*A helper the core counts and the module did not (Sheesh).* Sheesh, a level-60 warrior grinding in the Eastern
Plaguelands, pulled a pair of Shadowmages ("2 expected"); 18 s in a third Shadowmage came from 31 yd and a Crypt Slayer
from 36 yd, and it died. A Shadowmage runs for help below 15 % health (its script), and the core looks from the runner
itself and counts both creatures' sizes (`IsWithinDistInMap`: 30 yd and about 3 more); the check before a pull looked
2D within 30 yd of the fight's middle without sizes. It looks now from the nearer of the fight's middle and the runner's
own place (a caster runs from where it stood casting), with both sizes; the same sizes count in the escape's look at a
runner's helper (`AddFetched`), in stopping a runner (`StepStopRunner`) and in the spot verdict (3 yd more).

*A dungeon group bigger than a party (Upper Blackrock Spire).* Blackrock Spire's map takes 15 characters (the run
window offers that many for Lower and Upper Blackrock Spire), and a party holds five. The owner's group of 15 for Upper
Blackrock Spire went in with the five of its leader's party; the other ten stayed outside: the core takes a character
into the instance of its party's leader, and the run could not put them into a full party. Its party is a raid group
now whenever the group has more than five characters, as for a raid (`KeepRaidGroup`, the wait for the raid group
before the leader goes in, `StepDungeonEnter`, and a squad member's join through `LeadsRaidRun`). And before the run's
teleport the squad's catch-up sent eight of the fifteen after their leader by ship from Silithus and Dustwallow while
the leader waited for those that caught up, two and a half minutes: a leader on its way to a dungeon run with the
run's teleport (`Dungeons.Teleport`) waits for nobody behind it and its members do not travel after it; the run takes
them in from wherever they are.

*A runner followed into other creatures (Again).* Again (60, warrior) pulled a Shadowmage and a Dark Adept in the Eastern
Plaguelands; the Shadowmage runs at 15 % health (its script's "flee for assist", in fear when no helper is within the
core's 30 yd), the warrior followed it 41 yd across the field, a Diseased Flayer 8 yd from its way joined, and the
warrior died to the three. A melee character in the open world does not follow a foe of its fight that runs away (in
fear, or for help) where the runner stands within the aggro range (plus 6 yd) of a creature in no fight, nor more than
18 yd from where the run began: it turns to another foe on it, or waits where it stands until the runner comes back
(`Escape::StepChaseRunner`, four times a second, the open world's version of the dungeon groups' rule). A line per
runner it lets go: `lets <creature> run and does not follow it: <who> stands where it runs to; it waits where it stands`.

*A helper that walks about, and its voidwalker (Gorruk).* Gorruk (45, warrior, the test guild) pulled a Wastewander
Shadow Mage in Tanaris as "2 expected" (the mage and its voidwalker); the mage ran for help at 15 % to another Shadow
Mage 36 yd from the fight that walks 5 yd, and that one came with its voidwalker. The pull check counts the helper of a
runner with its walk (up to 10 yd), and the helper's minions come with it (the minion of a creature answers no call for
help, it follows its owner); the spot verdict counts the helper's walk too.

*An open-world squad shares out no foes (Gorruk and Bramhorn).* The two warriors (45 and 44) of a squad pulled
Wastewander camps as affordable for two: three foes stayed on the member and killed it, then the leader pulled "5
expected" and died with the member at full health beside it. Foes stay on who pulled them or on who hit them first, and
nobody of an open-world squad takes them off another: in the pull check (`Escape::PullBudget`) the squad's partners count
half (`PullPartnerShare`), also for "one more guild character would make it affordable". The pull check is off in a
dungeon run (the tank holds the creatures there).

*The class's ratio for a kind: the middle one (Mojowind).* A kind a bot has fought fewer than twice is judged by what the
guild's characters of its class learned of it, as a share of each one's average (round 172). That was the mean, and one
character whose average sits at the floor (0.15) or who died to the kind once drew it up for every other: a level-53
shaman judged two level-49 Felpaw Scavengers in Felwood at its class's mean of 1.95 (one shaman's note stood at 3.8
times its floored average, the others at 0.9 and 1.3), kept away from them on its way four times in a minute and went
home by hearthstone, 13 km from Winterspring. It is the middle one now (`Risk::KindRatio`), and the bot's own single
fight with the kind counts beside it, half each (Mojowind's one Felpaw fight had cost it three quarters of its average).

*Pyroguard Emberseer's hall (Upper Blackrock Spire).* the owner's group of 15 rested 125 s in the Dragonspire Hall in front of
Emberseer's room, set off for the Blackrock Altar along a way of 208 yd, and 7 s later was put beside it: "no nearer to
object 175706 in a minute". Two causes. The minute of the walk to an object that wakes a boss is a wall clock (a group
that fights all the time never moved it), and it ran on through the group's rest; the clocks of that walk now stand
still while the group rests together (`groupRestBegan`). And the two doors to Emberseer stayed shut: the instance's
script opens them only when the Blackhand Dreadweavers, Summoners and Veterans within 15 yd of the hall's seven runes are
dead, and it counts them only after a player walked into area trigger 2046 at the hall's west entrance, which a client
reports and a bot has none to report. When a member the AI plays stands in a trigger of a short hand list the module
sends the report for it, once per run (`StepWayTriggers`, the line `walks into area trigger N in <dungeon>: reported as a
client does`); and the hall's rune guards hold Emberseer back like the conditions other bosses have (`clearFirst`, a hand
entry in `Dungeons::Load`): the group clears the hall first, the doors open by the instance's own rule, and it walks up
to the altar as players do. Not every scripted trigger of a dungeon is reported: the Ring of Law's starts the arena's
waves, Scarlet Monastery's sends Mograine to the player, Upper Blackrock Spire's stadium is the event of Rend's row.

*A battle resurrection is accepted.* the owner: [quote left out]. mod-playerbots' druids cast Rebirth on a
dead member of their group in a fight, and a dead bot accepts a resurrection in its AI's update (its dead strategy's
"resurrect request" trigger); but the AI of a dead character of a dungeon run is held so that its spirit stays with its
body, so the requests went by. A dead character the AI plays accepts a resurrection somebody offers it at once, as a
player clicks Accept (`OrderService` dead step, before the dungeon run's own revival), with the line `accepts the
resurrection <who> offers it in a fight`; its run's revival clock starts anew.

*No hearthstone for a ship on the same continent.* The test guild's leader (60) found nothing it could do in the Eastern
Plaguelands, picked Silithus across the sea, was refused the walk from Plaguewood to the zeppelin past seven level-54
creatures and used its hearthstone to Light's Hope, 2500 yd away in the same zone (the rule of round 145: from the inn the
flight master is near). By the owner's rule the stone is for the utmost emergency or the quick way to another continent or
back to a capital (L32): after a refused walk to a ship it is used only when the inn is on another continent or in a
capital, or out of a zone that keeps killing the bot, as after a refused way to a zone; otherwise the zone waits, the sea
is closed for a while and the autopilot picks another zone or grinds where it is.

*A way through Zul'Gurub's drops in a second.* Zul'Gurub's navmesh has 4997 parts and 53833 drops between them. While
the owner's raid had no way on foot to High Priestess Jeklik (her place is a part no drop reaches), every step of its leader
asked for that way, and each search looked at every drop for every drop it reached: about 600 ms of the world thread, every
second for two minutes (`the planner took 1052 ms in one world tick ... Wartank (travel) 1052.0 ms`, nine such ticks in
ten seconds). The drops are indexed by the part they leave (`MapNav::dropsFrom`), and a pair of parts no drops joined is
not searched again for a minute (`MapNav::failedPairs`; a drop is only ever taken out, never put back). The same search on
the j5 instance: about 220 ms the first time, nothing within the minute after.

*Thunder Bluff's Hunter Rise: a road point under the ramp, a pickup on foot.* Ashmire (44) went for the pickup of
"Deadmire" at Melor Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff from Dustwallow Marsh, 4451 yd away, and walked it (a route of 7646 yd,
twelve minutes) where its next travel flew back in 91 s: only travels and voyages looked for a flight. At the ramp up to
Hunter Rise the route's next point, (-1384, -48, 157), lay 3.3 yd under the ramp's surface (mod-playerbots recorded its
link so); the core's path to it ended short, the ground guard refused the climb ("it would climb 14 yd onto ground from
which no way leads back down": the walk back from a point under the ground finds no way), the bot left its route and
stood 14 minutes at the ramp's foot until the pickup was given up. Two changes: a point of a route goes onto the ground
of the map's navmesh nearest to it, 2 yd sideways and 5 yd up or down, when it lies more than a yard off it
(`NavmeshGroundNear`, PathProbe; the nearest ground, so a road under a bridge stays the road); and a pickup, hand-in,
vendor, trainer, objective, interaction, quest event or exploration whose spot is 2500 yd or more away looks once for a
flight when it begins (`StartJourney` with `longWay`; FindFlight weighs the walks to the flight master and from the
landing against the way on foot, and the five minutes between two journeys hold). The line reads `goes to ... by flight:
the way on foot from here is long`. On j5 the path from the ramp's foot to the point 3 yd higher, on the ramp's surface,
is a normal one (`own step 1 from (-1356, -14, 143) to (-1383, -48, 160), 47 yd along a path of type 0x1`).

**Idle time, the night of 2026-11-27** (the owner: [quote left out]). The status lines of the live round of
00:00 to 01:20 gave 59 s of every five minutes standing still, 33 s of it with a walk to do. What was found and changed:
*A new walk waited for the AI's last move.* mod-playerbots' NewRpg walks with MoveTo, which sets the AI's next look to
the time the move takes, up to `Playerbots.MaxWaitForMove` (5 s); a place the planner gave right after a move (a new
task's GoTo, DoQuest or Visit) was looked at only after that wait (Nayeli stood 31 to 54 s of five minutes between the
spawns of "Dream Dust in the Swamp"). BotDriver wakes the AI (`SetNextCheckDelay(0)`, `WakeForNewWay`) when the place
or the NPC changes and the AI's wait is no longer than a move's (5.5 s), not in a fight, a cast, death or a hold of the
module (`PauseAI`).
*Gather walks that a pack ended.* They did not count among the refused gather ways (three refusals pause gathering for
ten minutes), so a bot went for the next node behind the same camp at once (Durgash at the Southern Savage Coast); they
count now, and the count goes back to 0 only when a node is reached.
*The objective nudge.* A creature an objective needs, in sight, that the AI does not attack is given to it after 10 s
(was 30: the warlock of the test guild stood beside its Searing Hatchlings).
On j5 the same 43 bots stood 27 s with a walk to do of every five minutes with the first two changes and 23 s with all
three (and 80 and 75 s in all); the nudge turned 12 bots to a creature in 17 minutes.
*Where the rest of the standing is.* The status line now ends its activity counters with `stood most while: hold 40 s,
