turn-in 12 s` (the tasks the bot stood still with, the longest first; "waiting on purpose" for the planner's waits).
*Skinned corpses an item wanted.* Thrakgar (43, Skinning 306) worked "The Essence of Enmity" (Brogg's Totem on a slain
Firemane dragonkin) 41 minutes in four hours: 96 kills and 19 uses. Auto loot skinned each corpse, and the core removes a
skinned corpse at its next update (`Creature::AllLootRemovedFromCorpse`), so the totem had nothing to go on. An
interaction that wants a corpse keeps the corpses of its creatures from being skinned for 90 s from its last step
(`QuestInteraction::KeepCorpses` / `KeepsCorpse`, asked by auto loot on the map threads and by the gather detour). (A
staged test on j5, Ashmire with Skinning 300 and the quest, did not come to the quest in ten minutes: the live log shows
it.)
*A spawn in the rock beside a cave.* Durnok (9) stood five minutes in the Burning Blade Coven: two Razormane Scout spawns
of its objective lie in the rock beside the cave, NewRpg walked to a spot that near itself and tried again every 31 s,
each step refused (14 and 22 yd through solid ground), and the rule that sets a target aside wants three refusals within
45 s; the objective's own "no progress at this spawn" came after three minutes, then the second spawn, then the rescue.
A refused step onto the task's own spot within sight, with no way at all and no whole path there, sets the spot aside at
the first refusal (`cannot get to its spot ...`).
*A hop onto a lift as it left.* Bullhide (12) hopped onto the upper stop of Thunder Bluff's Mesa Elevator as the platform
went down and stood in the air over the shaft until a rescue. A bot over the shaft with the platform gone hops back onto
the landing (`stands over the shaft of the lift ...`).
*A capped bot's slow looks.* Magefrost's steps at the level cap took 50 to 97 ms every quarter of an hour (the looks for
the guild's ammunition, consumables, materials and enchantments run in one step); a look of 20 ms or more now writes
`looked for ... at the level cap for N ms`, so the next round names which.

**Idle time, the second look (2026-11-27, 02:09 on).** With the commit above the live status lines gave 26 s of every
five minutes standing with a walk to do (31 to 32 s before), 60 s in all, and the breakdown named where the rest is:
the grind, 19,446 s in 345 windows, the level-60 grinders of the Eastern Plaguelands 70 to 80 s each. *An empty grind
spot.* A spot with nothing left to fight was left after 20 s (`GrindIdleMs`), three or four times in five minutes (Baumi:
a fight, 20 s, "nothing to fight at the spot"). It is left after 8 s now when nothing is left to loot within 30 yd
(`BotDriver::HasLootTarget`; 20 s at most), a hunt for skins and a farm order keep the 20 s. On j5 the same guilds stood
38 s of every five minutes while grinding (64 before), 50 s in all (72), the same number of fights (1,189 in 17 minutes;
1,183 before: the spots' creatures are the limit) and 453 grind spots against 368. *What holds the AI.* The AI state line
names the action that held the AI longer than a move's wait (`mod-playerbots' action "..." of N ms, M ms ago`), or says
`set outside an action` with what the bot was doing (casting, sitting, teleported, on a flight or transport, mounted,
moving): on j5 the long holds (12 to 18 s) were set outside any action, every time with the bot mounted; six such walks
in 20 minutes for 45 bots, what sets them is open. *Slow navmesh ways.* A way on the whole navmesh that takes 50 ms or
more (or waits for another thread's) writes a line with its ends and its caller (`DungeonNav::FindWay`): the leader of
the owner's Zul'Gurub raid had planner steps of a second every ten seconds for twenty minutes with no route search counted.

**Idle time, the third look; openers that did not go out (2026-11-27, 03:20 on).** *Openers.* Of the careful pulls of
two days 75 ended "could not open on ..." and became a walk into the creature's sight or up to it. 50 of them were the
core's "line of sight" (38 Exorcisms of a paladin tank in Blackrock Depths): the place was chosen with the creature's
own `IsWithinLOS(x, y, z + 2)`, which adds the creature's height to the point as well, so a place behind a pillar or a
rock passed. The place is chosen as the core measures a player's cast now (from the caster's eyes to the creature's hit
sphere, `SightFrom`), and an opener the core refuses for the line of sight chooses its place anew from where the
creature stands, also to either side, twice at most (`has no line of sight to ... from where it stands: it pulls from
... instead`). 15 were a shaman's Lightning Bolt with the result OK four times in four seconds and never a hit (Ainuha,
46, then walked to its Sprite Darter for quest 3125, two Grimtotems came with it, and it died on the run). A bot sends
no movement opcodes, a flag of a direction can stay after its last spline ended, and the core cancels a spell with a
cast time at its first update when the caster "moves" (`Spell::update`); before an opener such flags go when no spline
is under way (`still had the movement flags 0x.. of a move that has ended: cleared before its opener on ...`), and a
creature that walks about can leave the bolt's range while it is cast from 28 yd, so an opener with a cast time is cast
from 7 yd further inside its range (never from inside the creature's sight); it waits up to 3 s for a creature that
walks to stand, and a cast whose creature walks out of its reach meanwhile is broken off and cast again (`breaks off
its opener on ...`, a debug line). During a warrior's Bladestorm the core refuses every other spell with "spell in
progress" (`PLAYER_ALLOW_ONLY_ABILITY`): the opener waits for it to end, 10 s after the pull began at most (a warrior
threw seven times into its last four seconds and walked into the bat's sight). Each walk of the creature is waited out
(3 s at most, for 20 s after the pull began), and a spell with a cast time that the core calls out of range steps 7 yd
inside its range (3 yd for an instant): a paladin cast its Exorcism ten times at a scorpid that wandered off. Under
`GuildAdventure.Debug` an opener that ended without a fight writes what the bot and the creature were doing (a thrown
weapon's projectile still in flight gives such a line too). *Processing.* At the level cap two to four miners switched
to the profession mode for the same Thorium Ore above the line and walked to a forge each; the guild's processing has
one maker at a time now (half an hour), and a walk to an anvil or forge only for a surplus of 100 casts (a warrior
walked 218 s to the forge of Aerie Peak for the 30 ore above the line). *Consumables.* An Elixir of Healing Power (item
level 61, a recipe of the Burning Crusade whose vial only Outland's vendors sell) sent a druid into the profession mode;
no consumable above the guild's highest level is made, and one whose material no vendor in reach sells or whose place
the bot does not get to is left out for an hour (`cannot make ... for the guild here`). *The profession mode at the
cap.* A bot at the level cap whose professions have nothing to do hands back to the autopilot after 30 s (was two
minutes, ten after a look among hostile creatures) and waits where it stands meanwhile (the druid had walked 236 s to an
inn in the Hinterlands). The cap's looks for the guild's jobs (ammunition, consumables, processing, enchantments) wait
their interval after the profession mode has handed back (a warrior was sent back into it 2 s later for the same Dense
Weightstone), and ammunition and consumables send a bot into it only below three quarters of their stock (19 of 20
sent the warrior on a walk of 726 yd past camps to a quiet place for one weightstone; the profession mode then makes
the stock up). A consumable the cap's look sent a bot in for and the profession mode did not raise in the storage is left
out for an hour (`made no ... in the profession mode it was sent into for it`), and a craft for the guild that does
not start says why (`could not start ... for the guild: ...`): a mage was sent in for Wizard Oil every quarter of an
hour: its look asked for 5 casts, the mode for 20, and the materials were there for fewer; the look for the guild's
consumables now tries fewer casts. Nothing that binds when it is made is a consumable for the guild (a warlock made
bound, unique Firestones six times for a storage that stayed at 0). *A place that holds the bot.* When its travel was begun four times without getting off the spot, a bot
with two or more hostile creatures within 40 yd goes back the way it came at once instead of waiting a minute there
(`... and it does not wait among it`): a warrior of 58 waited beside the Mossflayers of the Undercroft, began the same
travel again and died with five on it. *The open sea.* A bot in water where the fatigue bar runs is rescued after
40 s (was 8; the core's fatigue kills after 60 s): the swim to Fray Island off the Barrens, which the road map lets
stand, takes about half a minute, and three bots were taken out of it. *Nothing to do for two minutes.* The hold's way out
uses the hearthstone only for an inn 1000 yd away or more (was 100: a warrior used its stone for an inn 770 yd away in
its own zone and picked Tanaris a second later). *An interaction's spot without a way.* A step to an interaction's
spot that the ground check refuses sets the spot aside as for an objective (interactions were missing from that rule:
a bot walked its own steps towards an object 54 yd away behind 37 yd of rock for 518 s, "gives that up" nine times).
*The objective's creature.* A creature of the objective in sight that the AI does not take is
given to it 5 s after the last progress (was 10: a warlock of 12 stood 10 to 19 s before every Wind Witch, 217 s of five
minutes). *A navmesh way across a continent.* A mage cut off in Silithus asked the open world's navmesh for its way to
an ender in Winterspring, and loading the tiles around both ends cost the world tick 667 ms; no way of more than
4000 yd straight is asked of it. *What a creature summons in a fight.* Ashmire (48, warlock) pulled one Centipaar Swarmer
in Tanaris ("1 expected"); the Swarmer casts Silithid Swarm (spell 6589) every one to three seconds of a fight, four
were on the bot after 11 s, it left at 76 % health and died on the run with its target untouched. The index of minions
(`WorldIndex::MinionOf`) leaves out creatures of no type, which the swarms are, and the check before a pull counted
only the minions that are alive. What a creature's script summons in a fight (in combat, at a health, on aggro; hostile
to players, whatever its type; twice for a timer of five seconds or less) is one more foe now in the check before a
pull (`... that Centipaar Swarmer summons in the fight`) and in the spot verdict (`the target summons ... in the
fight`), as what a creature's death brings is (`WorldIndex::CombatSummonOf`). Once the summoner fights, its summons
stand in the fight and count as foes of their own. *A voyage's walk into a camp.* A voyage's walk to its dock was let walk on
when a pack stood on its way (only a ship's wait should be): a level-54 priest's walk from Felwood through Timbermaw
Hold to the flight master of Everlook kept away from the furbolgs' camp every seven seconds for 393 s, until the stuck
rule ended it, and the next voyage took the same route. On land and 250 yd or more from a dock it ends at a pack as
other tasks do, the second time the route's first node is no start of its routes for half an hour, and an errand's
voyage stopped twice drops the errand for a while. *No zone for three minutes.* The waits a bot holds were dropped and
its hearthstone used in the same step: a level-54 warrior in Silithus had five zones waiting, and from its inn in
Feralas it picked Felwood with five quests, a flight Cenarion Hold had as well. When something was dropped the zones
are looked at again first, and the way out (the hearthstone, the rescue) comes half a minute later if there is still
no zone. *A squad member on the Cauldron's rim.* Its leader rode the lift down; in the second its ride ended at a middle
stop the member set out for the spot in the shaft, and two minutes later for the leader on the floor, 8 yd away on the
map and 50 yd below: a walk under 20 yd was never probed and never routed, and the straight steps down were refused
every 30 s, twice two minutes. A short walk to a destination more than 8 yd above or below is probed like a longer
one (the road map then leads over the lift: `Searing Gorge > Scaffold Cars > (lift) Scaffold Cars`), and the walk
back does not begin while the leader stands where no walkable ground is. *A call for help.* Gorruk (55, warrior)
pulled one Deadwood furbolg in Felwood ("1 expected"); 15 s in a Den Watcher called for help at half its health
(its script's SMART_ACTION_CALL_FOR_HELP, every creature of its side within 20 yd), a Den Watcher, an Avenger and
Chieftain Bloodmaw came, and it died against four. Running for help was counted, calling for help was not. What a
creature's script calls in a fight (in combat, at a health, on aggro; `WorldIndex::CallForHelpYards`, 65 kinds, 10 to
50 yd) counts for sure in the check before a pull (`... (Deadwood Den Watcher calls for help)`) and in the spot
verdict (`the target calls every creature of its side within 20 yd for help in the fight`).

**Round 251 (round 257 of the server): a shaman's mana, a voyage without a flight, a mesa, a stunning creature, sold-out vendors** (2026-11-26).
*A shaman's mana.* Thrakgar (34, enhancement) spent 60-70 % of its mana on one creature of its level and all of it on a
Lashtail Raptor (36) in 44 s, then died with the raptor at 5 %. mod-playerbots' enhancement strategy casts Fire Nova
whenever a foe is in melee (its aoe strategy's trigger "enemy within melee", 22 % of the base mana a cast) and Call of
the Elements at the start of every melee fight, which sets every totem of the bar (Strength of Earth, Healing Stream,
Searing: 20 % of the base mana). On the j5 instance a level-32 shaman cast Fire Nova 338 times and Call of the Elements
128 times in about 1200 fights, 1108 of them against one creature. Now Fire Nova needs two foes in a fight within 10 yd
of the fire totem (as Consecration, DQ19), and Call of the Elements is not cast in the open world, where the shaman sets
one Searing Totem (`BotDriver::KeepTotems`); in a dungeon or a battleground its talents' totems stay
(`GuildFireNovaAction`, `GuildCallOfTheElementsAction` in `BotDriver::GuardConsumables`). Under `GuildAdventure.Debug`
a refusal is a line once per half minute (`does not cast Fire Nova: 1 foe(s) in a fight within 10 yd of its fire totem
(from 2)`, `does not cast Call of the Elements: in the open world it sets one Searing Totem`).
*A voyage that looked for no flight.* Caelithra (33) was refused a travel to Arathi, whose flight check set the bot's
minute; six seconds later it picked Desolace across the sea, and its walk to the zeppelin in Tirisfal looked for no
flight from Tarren Mill: refused for a group on the way, then the hearthstone. A voyage's walk to the dock looks for a
flight at its first step whatever the minute says (`BotTask::flightTried`, as a travel since round 55); from Hammerfall,
after the stone, it flew to Undercity at once.
*Off a mesa by the navmesh.* Saelanya (29) went for an Incendia Agave of "Sacred Fire" on the canyon floor of Thousand
Needles, 140 yd below the mesas: its route led onto a mesa, the straight step down was refused, it walked back the way it
came and, the second time, was rescued. The navmesh has the way down (1322 yd round the mesa, `.ga admin navway` on the
live server), but each of the four places that ask it did so once per task, and the first try, from where the task began,
used it up. It is asked again from a place 40 yd or more from the last try, three times a task at most
(`BotTask::OpenTryDue`), and a failed try names the navmesh's reason in the line it belongs to (`the navmesh has none
either: ...`).
*A creature that stuns.* Thunderhoof (50, a cat) pulled a Frayfeather Stagwing for "Hippogryph Muisek" with one
Hippogryph expected and one more possible; three came, it judged them at its average (48 %) and died in 42 s. The
Stagwing's Swoop (spell 5708) stuns all within 5 yd every 3-5 s by its SmartAI script. A kind whose script casts a spell
with a stun aura on a fight timer of 12 s or less (`WorldIndex::StunsOften`, 85 kinds) counts half again until the bot
has fought it itself (`EntryCost`, the class's notes when they say more).
*A warrior among ogres, no change.* Gorruk (38, arms) walked to its hand-in at Hammerfall by a route over the node
"Boulderfist Hall", was attacked by three Boulderfist ogres of level 36 and died with a potion drunk. The route judged
the three as a group it can take, and the log says so: of 225 fights of the guild's warriors against three creatures of
their level since 2026-11-24, 211 were won, at a median cost of 1.8 times their single fights (the estimate counts 4.5),
4 lost. By class the same count gives mages 5.6 and warlocks 8.9 times (they leave such fights often), rogues 2.4,
paladins 3.1; a cost by class is a change for later.
*Engineers that walked from vendor to vendor.* Retadk and three more engineers of level 60 (skill 312-315) walked across
the Wetlands, Arathi, Hillsbrad and the Hinterlands, one vendor after the other, to buy 25 Coarse Blasting Powder each,
and bought nothing: the powder is sold two to four at a time and comes back after three hours, and 879 purchases of the guild
bought nothing in two days. What they bought it for was to turn the storage's surplus Linen Cloth into Coarse Dynamite.
The processing of the guild's materials makes no explosive or device (`Professions::ProcessForGuild`), and no trip is
planned to a vendor whose limited stock is smaller than what is wanted, nor to one a guild character found sold out
until its restock time (`OrderService::PlanMaterialPurchase`, `_soldOut`).
*A forge for one bar.* Whenever a miner's ore brought the guild storage one above the line of
`Professions.ProcessAbove`, level-60 miners walked to a forge to smelt one Thorium Bar ("1 of its scarcest material above
1000"), up to nine at once and 200 such walks in a day. A material is processed only when at least 20 casts of it are to
spare.
*A zone counted again from afar.* Zulkash (43) found nothing in Feralas, went to Tanaris, found nothing there either and
picked Feralas again 19 minutes later with 4 quests. The mark "nothing it can do where it stands" (round 159) held for a
zone across the sea only; it holds for every zone the bot does not stand in.

**Round 250: a stalk into a camp, a zone's entry behind strong creatures, a keep-away that ended a task, groups the zone count did not see** (2026-11-26).
Frostvein (35, a mage) worked "Foul Magics" in Arathi; a Syndicate Highwayman in stealth 32 yd from it was walked onto by
the stalking rule (a straight walk), into the Syndicate's camp; it won that fight, three Mercenaries beside it came on it
on its way out and it died. The rule takes the nearest hidden creature that stands where the bot may fight (the spot
verdict at its place, `IsPlaceUsable`) with no camp on the straight way (`Risk::EntersCamp`), and names one it leaves
once per task (`does not walk onto ... in stealth`). Morwenna (32, a priest) and Kodahorn (32) picked Thousand Needles for
9 and 5 quests and set off for its nearest giver, Pao'ka Swiftmountain on Highperch, whose way passes level-39 creatures;
the zone's count had left that giver out (round 167), the travel did not: the way and the flight were refused ("no flight:
the landing lies in a zone far above it", the reason of the nearest landing, Camp Mojache or another), the zone was
written off, and Morwenna went home to Arathi by hearthstone after 15 minutes of travel. `ZoneEntry` takes the nearest
giver the count counts (a place the bot may use, its work and its way from the zone's hub within the walk margin) and
the nearest of all only when there is none. Under `GuildAdventure.Debug` a line per landing a flight leaves out names the
landing and its reason (`would not land at ...`). And Sunwhisper (42) kept away from Brimgore, a rare elite on his round
in the Wyrmbog, twice for 82 and 102 s, and its objective ended "objective spot not reached" after 210 s: a keep-away and
a run pause the task's stuck clocks, as fights and rests do (`PauseStuck`). And the zone pick counted Desolace with six
to eight quests for bots of level 32 and 33 whose work lay behind pairs and camps of level-33 and -34 creatures on every
way from Ghost Walker Post: they went there and had their tasks refused one after the other (25 "a group on the way"
for one bot in half an hour, round 256). The count judged the way from the zone's hub by the strongest creature on it
only; it now judges the groups on it as the walk gate does (`JudgeHubWay`: the safest way and the way around every
group, the group or camp no way avoids; `HubWayPasses` asks the bot's own `Risk::CanFight`), for a quest's work
(`QuestWorkReachable`), a giver or ender (`PlaceWayReachable`), the zone's entry and the pickups of `PlanQuests`.

**Round 249: the call for help of a creature beside a stalking druid's target** (2026-11-26). Thunderhoof (49, a cat
druid of the test guild) pulled a Southsea Dock Worker in Tanaris with Faerie Fire (Feral) from 28 yd, "3 fewer would
join than at its place (Andre Firebeard 45, Southsea Dock Worker 44, Southsea Dock Worker 45, Southsea Freebooter 45);
1 may still come"; two Dock Workers whose homes lay 5 yd from it were on it two seconds later, then six, and it died on
the run. A creature within the core's assistance radius (10 yd) of the one that engages answers its call at once
(`Creature::CallAssistance` from `Unit::Attack`, the assistants after 1.5 s), wherever the bot stands, so the two had to
count at both places. They did not because the core's `Creature::CanAssistTo`, which the pull check asked, ends with
`CanSeeOrDetect(enemy)`: mod-playerbots' cat druid prowls within 30 yd of its target before a fight (its prowl
trigger), a rogue sneaks, and asked while they crept no creature beside the target saw them; at the target's place the
Dock Workers counted only by their aggro range on the bot's way. The call goes out when the creature engages, by which
time the bot has attacked and is out of stealth. `Escape::WouldAssist` is the core's check without that look (react
state, alive, not evading, no civilian, attackable, not engaged, no owner, no flag that ignores calls, the same faction
answering calls, hostile to the bot) and stands in for it in the pull check, the helpers a fleeing foe fetches, what a
pack on the way brings and the dungeon's pack count. *And the AI's hold in a stuck line.* Every stuck line of the day
said "ai held (an action's time or a pause)": playerbots waits `Playerbots.ReactDelay` plus up to 200 ms after every
update of its AI and a cast holds it for the global cooldown, so `IsActionDurationActive` is nearly always true between
two looks. The line names the hold with its milliseconds now, and only above 2 s ("held for 13677 ms more"). The case
that showed it, Ashmire (35) on "Panther Mastery" with 31 turns back in five minutes, was NewRpg's quest walk that killed
a panther every 36 s 100 to 160 yd from the spawn the planner had picked (the task ends after three minutes "objective
spot not reached" and begins again: no change). *An instant flight is waited for.* Hordeboss booked a flight from
Bloodvenom Post to Orgrimmar for an errand; NewRpg drops its flight status in the moment it asks for the flight, and
in the next second the travel step, seeing no flight, planned the way on foot from the master, gave the errand up as
"too far on foot" and sent NewRpg off along the road; the core's teleport came a moment later, and the walk that went
on from the master of Orgrimmar took it 77 yd into the rock under the city, where it fell for seven minutes until a
rescue. With instant flight paths the planner never saw a bot at the master after its booking either (the teleport came
first), so 914 of the 6354 flights of the live log were taken for a jump the planner did not cause and the task was
planned anew. The booking now counts as standing at the master, the travel step waits up to 8 s for the teleport
("taking the flight"), the booking is not forgotten in those seconds, and a landing sends NewRpg to rest, so nothing of
the old place walks on. *No Water Walking.* mod-playerbots' shaman casts it whenever it swims, a character that walks on
the water cannot dive, and the module's swims and dives took the aura off again: 44 Fish Oils of the guild storage that
day for three shamans on "Clam Bait", whose crawlers live 55 to 70 yd down off Desolace. The action (on itself and on
its party) is the module's now and never useful. *No retreat into a fort.* Velmira (24) had nothing to do beside
Northwatch Hold and "walks 180 yd out to The Barrens Northwatch Hold": the node of the fort, among 13 Theramore marines
of level 16 and 17, which one link out of it left free (the rule for a node among groups asks for every link), and
every travel from there ended on a pack until the place held it and it used its hearthstone. A retreat's node is no
place in the middle of a group the bot cannot take (`RoadMap::GroupAtPoint`, the count of the way).

**Round 215: a death in Dire Maul "during no task"** (2026-11-25). Magefrost (60, mage) was no bot standing about in
Dire Maul: it was a member of the group of a Dire Maul East run of the owner's guild (Wartank leading, Retadin, Priestholy,
Hunterbm), and a squad member has no task of its own, it follows its leader. After Lethtendris the group waited for a
Wildspawn Felsworn on its round to cross the way ahead, then went back out of a "trap" four times in 70 s (Choking
Spores had hurt Hunterbm out of a fight: back 65, 65, 3 and 10 yd along the tank's way), and the satyrs of that round
came onto Hunterbm, 60 yd behind the tank; Magefrost and Retadin turned to them, the tank's fight had no foe on it in
its 25 s, and Magefrost died with three on it (Retadin lived with a potion). The death line now names the leader
("during no task of its own (it follows its squad leader Wartank on a dungeon run)"). The group's way back and forth
out of a hazard next to a patrol's round, and a tank that does not take creatures off its members 60 yd behind it, are
the dungeon conductor's (`OrderDungeons.cpp`, the trap rule after `NoteHazards`, the help rule of DP6).

**Round 207: a ship's passenger off its ship** (2026-11-24). Probehunter, a probe bot of level 60, was 93 s into its
voyage on The Lady Mehley at Menethil when the ga-probe's `orders` scenario gave it the order FOLLOW, and it stood in
Northshire beside its leader five seconds later. From then on every walk the ground check let through was "normal + not
using a path, 2 points" on plain ground (Northshire, Menethil, Baradin Bay), it was found "off the walkable ground" and
put at a graveyard every 36 s, 45 times. A ship adds a bot it takes on board to its passengers with the core's "no path
finding" state (`MotionTransport::AddPassenger` with all), and only a removal with all takes the state away again: the
module's going ashore does that (`BotDriver::LeaveTransport`), a teleport off the deck does not (`Player::TeleportTo`), so
every path of the core was a straight line from then on. Now an AI-played character that is on no transport and has that
state gets it cleared, four times a second, with a line in the activity log. Not the grids before the path finder
(ccdeaec) or the swimmer's probe (1f883fd): a login clears the state, which is why a restart ends such a loop.

**Round 204: a swim under a lake's floor** (2026-11-24). Pewpew, a level-60 hunter, fought Blighted Surges under water in
Lake Mereldar (one of them spawns 3 yd under its floor), began a rest 15 yd on and was lifted out 3.7 yd inside the
ground 30 s later, as two characters had been there in rounds 183 and 184; no movement of it had been refused. The
ground check judges a swimmer's movement only by its end and by how far it runs through solid ground (3 yd may), and the
probe counted a swimmer's samples under the lake's floor as no solid ground at all: the core counts water down to 2 yd
under the floor (those samples were skipped as water), a sample less than 4 yd under the terrain found the terrain above
it as a "hump" to stand on, and less than 6 yd under the surface counted as air. So a straight swim could run up to six
yards under a sloping lake floor and pass, and a swimmer whose movement stopped on such a line (a fight, a rest) stood
inside the ground. Now a swimmer's sample more than 2 yd under the terrain with no floor of a building or cave below it is
inside the ground for the probe (the ground guard's own measure of `UnderTheGround`), so a swim with more than 3 yd of
such a line is refused. Walkers keep their rules (their lines down a ledge clip the slope). The lift's line names the
last walk the ground check let through.

**A foe it cannot get at** (2026-11-24, the test guild). Hordeboss, a level-20 warrior, was attacked in a lake of the
Stonetalon Mountains by a Venture Co. Deforester (a caster: Fireball every two seconds, its SmartAI) from the bank, stood
47 s in the water without a hit ("its target at 100% health"), left at 31 % by the fight's numbers and died on the run;
then it "learned" that the Deforester costs it 130 %. A single foe of its level is fought out until the bot is low (the
rule for one ordinary foe), and the rule for a foe that does not die waits 60 s of no progress, which a fight that hurts
the bot never reaches in time. Now a fight in which no foe has been hurt at all after 15 s while the bot lost 15 % of its
health or more ends like a fight with a foe that does not die (`TrackFight`): the module ends it, the bot walks away and
leaves that creature alone for 15 minutes (its spawn too), a line names the creature and its distance; also beside its
group's fight. And a fight in which its foes lost nothing teaches no cost (`Escape::OnFightEnd`), a death in it neither.

**A pair it had to leave, and a runner for help** (2026-11-24, the test guild). Sunwhisper, a level-17 priest in the
Ghostlands, pulled two Dreadbone Sentinels ("its own pull (2 expected)"; one cost it about 12 % of what it has), left
the fight at 27 % health with the first at 54 % ("by how the fight went", Psychic Scream), rested 16 s, and a minute
later pulled the next two on its way to another quest by the same estimate and died to them on the run. A fight the bot
left taught nothing, and a death on such a run neither, so the pair was judged as before. Now a fight it left by how
the fight went against the foes it had pulled (not for a strong creature that came near, not a keep-away) counts as
costing all it had, as a death counts (`Escape::OnFightEnd`): for a pair of one kind the kind's cost per creature rises to
at least that share of the pair (2 x 2.5 = everything), so the next pair is too much and two Sentinels on the way are
walked around; a single kind it had to leave the same; its average and its pace stay. A death on such a run counts as
the death it is. The Sentinels were for "Spinal Dust", which it had set aside until level 25 a second before: a quest
the bot has set aside (until a level or for a while) no longer makes its creatures the bot's work on the way
(`QuestWants`), so it fights them only where they stand in its way or attack it.

Thunderhoof, a level-17 druid in bear form in the Barrens (Cat Form comes at 20), pulled a Bristleback Water Seeker
carefully ("1 fewer would join"; a Bristleback Hunter counted "if one runs for help"). Both kinds poison and run for
help at low health (their SmartAI); the Seeker ran 27 yd to the Hunter, the Hunter came 24 s into the fight, a second
Hunter 45 s later, and the druid died on its run with the first Hunter at 66 %. Now a foe of the bot's fight that runs
for help (the core's assistance movement) toward a creature of its faction in no fight within 30 yd of it is stopped
once per runner with what the bot's class has and can cast now (`Escape::StepStopRunner`, four times a second): a
bear's Bash, a cat's Maim, Entangling Roots or Moonfire in caster form; a warrior's Hamstring, Piercing Howl or Heroic
Throw; a rogue's Kidney Shot or Gouge; Hammer of Justice; Frost Shock or Earth Shock; Fire Blast, Ice Lance or
Frostbolt; Concussive Shot, Wing Clip or Arcane Shot; Mind Flay; Curse of Exhaustion; Chains of Ice or Death Grip. The
core decides form, stance, range and cost; a line in the activity log names runner, helper and spell. (The mana at
"0 %" in a fight line of a death is the death's, not a sign of spells cast.)

**Round 200: rescued onto Acherus** (2026-11-24). Mageyo, a level-60 mage of the owner, entered the world after a
restart in the Eastern Plaguelands at (2764, -5530), where it had ground for an hour, and 32 s later was "cut off from
every road" and "put back on the ground" at the node "Acherus: The Ebon Hold" (2528, -5549, 377): Acherus floats about
200 yards above the ground there, and its seven nodes (Death's Breach and its halls) link only to one another and by
flight to Light's Hope. From the deck every grind task ended "grind spot not reached" (no whole way, or a way through the
air), 120 in a row and no fight, and the next login put it there again. The chain had three causes:

- *Grids that did not exist.* After a restart only the grids around the characters in the world are created, and the
  navmesh of a grid that was not created answers no for every way into it. The bot stood 74 yd from one grid's edge and
  160 yd from another's: the route's first node, Browman Mill, 413 yd away in the grid that did not exist, got the path
  finder's straight line (incomplete, two points, 297 yd through the hill), which the ground check refused; the walk
  checks of the cut-off test said no to every node beyond the edge (a "no" is remembered for three minutes), and the
  nearest node it found on the navmesh was the one in the grid that did exist: Acherus above it. Now the grids along
  the straight line between the ends of a way are created before the path finder is asked (`EnsureNavmesh` in
  PathProbe: their terrain, collision and navmesh, no creatures; the core keeps created grids until the map unloads):
  for the walk checks, the probes, the planner's walks (`WalkTo`, own steps) and the ground check (for the movement after
  the one it judges).
- *Acherus as a node to put a bot at.* A few nodes whose walking links lead only among themselves and that all stand at
  least 40 yd above the terrain under them (the terrain of the map's grid, not what is built on it) are an island: no
  place for a rescue, a retreat or a rest, and no end of a route. Small groups on the ground keep their nodes (Camp
  Narache on its mesa, Rut'theran by the sea, Freewind Post at its lift); the startup line names every island found.
- *No count of the loop.* A task whose target no way led to ("grind spot not reached", "objective spot not reached",
  "spot not reached", "no way to its level") now counts like a refused way at the place the bot stands: eight within
  300 yd and 15 minutes and it walks back the way it came, else it uses its hearthstone (its inn is at Light's Hope,
  290 yd from the deck). Its next login on the deck is cut off from every road again, now with Light's Hope's nodes,
  and the rescue or the hearthstone takes it down.

**Two Shadowmages "at 45 %"** (2026-11-22, after round 172). In the gaps test of round 172 a level-60 warrior's pack look
judged two Shadowmages of the Eastern Plaguelands on its way at "about 45%" of its strength. It took them, and they killed
it. The guild had fought such pairs 562 times in three days (2026-11-20 to 22). For a warrior a pair costs 50 to 60 % of
its health down to the lowest point of the fight (Cleaveyo 53 %, Nochnwar 63 %), and in half of those fights the warrior
drank a Major Healing Potion. Casters and hunters lose 15 to 28 %. A single Shadowmage costs any of them 7 %. There were
two causes:

- **A kind's cost was learned from the health at the end of the fight.** A potion or a heal in the fight brings the end
  back up: 100 % -> 71 % with the lowest point at 27 % taught 29 %. So Cleaveyo had learned 16 % per Shadowmage, about
  40 % a pair. `OrderService::EndFight` now passes the lowest health of the fight to `Escape::OnFightEnd`. Over the
  guild's fights of those days, ordinary fights against one foe cost 6.7 % down to the lowest point against 5.5 % to the
  end, so a bot's own average rises by about a fifth as it learns.
- **A kind a bot had not learned was judged by the bot's own average.** That is what the 45 % was, while four warriors
  of the guild had learned what a Shadowmage costs a warrior. `Risk::KindRatio` keeps, per class and kind, what each
  character learned (a note of two fights or more, or one that took nearly everything) as a share of its own average.
  A bot without a note of that kind takes the mean of the others of its class against its own average, upwards only
  (what the others found cheap does not make it bolder before its own first fights; `EntryCost` in FightEscape.cpp).
  On the live notes of that night the warriors' ratio for the Shadowmage is 1.4. A warrior that never fought one
  judges a pair at about 65 % of its strength (was 45 %). A warrior at 79 % of its strength, as the one in the test
  was, does not take that: its limit is 80 % of that, 63 %.
- **And elites in the pack look** (found in the test run of this fix): `FightNeed` and the run's estimate counted an
  elite by its level times 2.5. A level-60 mage's pack look judged a Scarlet Praetorian (56, three times the health,
  3.75 times the damage) and a Scarlet Archmage of Tyr's Hand at "about 64%: it takes them", and it died to them. An
  elite now counts for what its health and damage are worth when that is more (`EliteMultiplier`, the look-outs'
  `ThreatLevelOf`: the Praetorian is level 66). The next pair of Scarlet elites on its way was "a pack it cannot take",
  and a single Praetorian cost it 52 % of its health when it was attacked by one.

**Round 210: a flight round Thunder Bluff, the marines of Northwatch Hold, a passenger of a lift** (2026-11-24, the
test guild Hordeboss Adventurers on the live server; the maintainers: rescues and hearthstones are workarounds, find the
causes). (1) Hordeboss (25, on its way to Stonetalon) went round six times in fifty minutes: from Mulgore it walked to
Camp Taurajo's flight master, flew to Thunder Bluff, rode the lift down and walked the road to Malaka'jin, and on that
road the next look for a flight sent it back to Camp Taurajo. `FindFlight` measured the walk from the landing as the

and the Barrens. The walk from a landing is now the route's length when there is a route (`fromLanding`, also in
`FlightPlan::fromLanding`), and the share of a flight's walks is judged with it. On the `j5` instance the same bot put at
its Mulgore spot walked to Camp Taurajo and flew to Stonetalon Peak (two hops) and landed in Stonetalon Mountains.
(2) Thunderhoof and Stonehorn (23) worked "The Guns of Northwatch" inside Northwatch Hold, where marines of level 15-17
walk rounds in groups; every walk out ("a pack on its way ... [they walk: no way around them]") ended the task, the
zone was written off and both went home by hearthstone. A pack that walks a round now waits like one strong creature on
the way (`BotRuntime::packWalked`, `PauseForRoamer`: 20 s at a time, a minute per task), and its place is not set aside
(it does not stay there). (3) Hordeboss stood ten minutes at (-1197, 109, 95), 120 yd from the Mesa Elevator and 48 yd
under the mesa's top, "on a transport", until the lift's wait gave up and it was rescued from under the ground: it was
a passenger of the lift's platform without standing on it (mod-playerbots adds a bot to a transport its position is
over, once a second, and takes it off again only in the same look, which does not run while the module holds the AI),
so each ride of the platform carried it up and down through the rock. A passenger of a static transport more than 12
yd from it that is not riding with the module's lift step is taken off where it stands and put on the ground there
(`is a passenger of the lift .. yd away from it .. it is taken off the lift`). Not reproduced on `j5`: two rides there
(`steps onto the lift`, `rode the lift ... in 13 s`) went as they should.

**Round 211: an item that brings waves** (2026-11-24). Sunwhisper (23) and Ashmire (22) died in Ashenvale "during no
task" within 100 s of each other to Foulweald furbolgs of level 23 to 25. They had used Karang's Banner of "King of the
Foulweald" (quest 6621): its spell puts down a banner whose trap sends event 6721, and the event's script summons 17

summon a creature themselves and saw nothing. Now it follows an event a spell sends (`SPELL_EFFECT_SEND_EVENT`, the
`event_scripts` rows that summon) and an object it puts down whose trap casts a spell, each creature with the second it
comes at, and judges the costliest 40 s of them together (a bot does not finish one wave before the next); the reason
line names them: `using Karang's Banner summons 4 x Foulweald Ursa (level 24), ... in waves over 180 s, too much for it at
level 23`.

**Round 212: a rest that ended in the water** (2026-11-24). Sunwhisper (24) died in a lake of Ashenvale to Eck'alom, a rare
of 27 (not elite, three levels above it: within the owner's rule, no keep-away), in a fight of 42 s it lost with the rare at

the place still in the water ("ended by: still in the water"), and the priest went on to its next target at 44 % mana.
A rest that stops within 4 yd of its dry place in the water now walks on to it once (to 2 yd beyond it) before it gives

**Round 213: a wandering neighbour with a minion** (2026-11-24). Thunderhoof (26) pulled a Son of Cenarius in
Stonetalon for quest 1058, "2 expected" (the Son and the Treant Ally it summons at a reset); a second Son that wanders
15 yd, its home 21 yd from the target, came with its own treant, four, and the druid died on the run, its squad's shaman
after it against three treants. The check before a pull counted that Son a quarter ("may walk in", its walk capped at
10 yd) and its treant at the same quarter. A creature that walks about and has a minion of its own

**Round 172: a strong elite on a long round** (2026-11-22). Shamanheal (60) was grinding in the Eastern Plaguelands when
a single Nerubian Overseer (60) attacked it. It could not run ("held fast"; the way back was closed by four creatures),
went from 100 % to 0 % in 15 s, and only then learned that the fight costs it about 120 %. The Overseer had killed it 70 yd from there
on 2026-11-18. It is a rare elite with six times the health and four times the damage of an ordinary
creature, and it walks a waypoint round of 1135 yd (150 points). Shamanheal died 3 yd from that road.

`.ga admin spot` at that place said "Nerubian Overseer 60 elite on patrol, its way 3 yd from here (a round of 1135 yd;
counts 9%) ... it would work there". Two rules let it through:
- An elite counted as its level plus three (63) and as 2.5 times an ordinary foe (37 % for the shaman). The look-outs
  had weighed it by its health and damage for a long time (`ThreatLevelOf`: level 72), and they kept away from it a
  second before the fight.
- A patrol on a round over 400 yd was never "too strong for it alone", only discounted for being away most of the time.

Now an elite near a spot counts as at least what its health and damage are worth (`Escape::ThreatLevelOfKind`, the
look-outs' measure; `EffectiveLevel` in RiskModel.cpp). A creature too strong for the bot alone counts in full on any
round, as packs have since round 161. And a rest's quiet place is not within 40 yd of such a creature's road
(`Risk::OnStrongRoad` in `Escape::FindRestSpot`). The same `.ga admin spot` now says "(a round of 1135 yd; too strong for it
alone, counts 100%); the fight would cost about 300% ...: the spot waits: a creature far above the bot stands there".
Scarlet Warders (54, three times the health, 3.5 times the damage) count as 62 by their health and damage and stay
workable for a level-60 bot.

*Round 187 (2026-11-24):* the road rule looked at each patrol alone, and the Crimson Courier (elite, 60) and its four
bodyguards (elites, 57-58) walk paths of their own side by side, none of them too strong alone. A level-60 shaman
grinding beside their road walked 58 yd to a quieter place ("14 hostile creatures near, 7 there"), 33 yd from the road,
and died to the five of them 39 s into its rest. The rule now also counts a pack the bot cannot take together, as the
spot verdict has since round 161 (`PatrolPacks`).

*Round 189 (2026-11-24):* the next death there came on a walk around a pack. A level-60 shaman grinding Hate Shriekers
86 yd from the road went around Vile Tutors to a point 24 yd from it; the Courier came by five seconds later, the shaman
left the fight at full health and died on the run. The walk around (`StartDetour`) took no road into account, and the
look-out for strong roamers did not run while it walked (the detour returned before the look). Now a point to walk
around to, or the middle of the way there, within 35 yd of such a road (`Risk::OnStrongRoad`, packs included) is no
choice, and a strong roamer that comes within its reach plus 20 yd during a walk around ends it ("breaks off its way
around ..."), so the next step keeps away from it.

**Round 170: Starfall pulled what stood around** (2026-11-22). Owldudu (60, a balance druid) died for the third time that
day while grinding at Hive'Zora in Silithus: "left a fight against 3 foes (Hive'Zora Reaver level 60) at 86% health: held
fast, fights on ... the way it came was closed (no path)", and dead 16 s later. Each of its deaths there (and one to the
Cyclone Warriors) began with "its own pull (1 expected)" and ended with three to five creatures on it, all at once, from 27
to 56 yd away. A call for help does not reach that far (the core's assistance radius is 10 yd, and the hive's Reavers,
Wasps, Waywatchers, Hive Sisters and Tunnelers have no formation and no call-for-help script), and the spot verdict
counted the one to three creatures that stand at those spawns. So the spot choice was not the cause. The cause was
**Starfall**: its stars fall once a second for ten seconds on up to two random enemies within 30 yd that the druid can
see, also on creatures in no fight (core script `spell_dru_starfall_dummy`). mod-playerbots casts Starfall only when no
unengaged enemy is within 40 yd (`CastStarfallAction::isUseful`), but it looks only at the moment of the cast, and the
druid moves while the stars fall: "ran to range", and the rest's walk to a quieter place. On the dev instance a star
pulse hit a Stonelash Scorpid 27 yd away six seconds after a Starfall cast, and a second Waywatcher 28 yd away after the
rest had walked the druid 22 yd. `Escape::StepStarfall` (FightEscape.cpp, called four times a second from
`OrderService::StepFast` for AI-played characters) ends a druid's Starfall when its fight is over (`ends its Starfall:
its fight is over`, a debug line) or when its stars would reach a hostile creature that is alive, in no fight, in sight
and attackable within the star spell's radius (`ends its Starfall: its stars would reach Hive'Zora Tunneler (level 58, 7
yd away), which is in no fight`). The cast's mana and its cooldown are lost then; the stars that fall in a fight of its
own still do their damage.

**Round 169: inside a lake bed** (2026-11-22). Shammpower (60) was rescued "standing off the walkable ground" at (2476,
-4152, 46) in the Eastern Plaguelands, sitting to drink 20 yd under the surface of Blackwood Lake. It had fought Plague
Monstrosities and Blighted Horrors under water; a straight movement under water had left it 1.9 yd inside the lake
bed (the terrain there lies at 48). The core counts water only for a point at most 0.2 yd under the terrain
(`GridTerrainData::GetLiquidData`), so for the bot there was no water at all: the rest's "no rest in the water" rule saw
dry ground and it sat down, and the rescue's exemption for swimmers (round 156 asked half a yard higher) did not hold.
The water checks (`IsSwimming`, `IsDiving`, `Escape::WaterAt`, `Escape::WaterDepth`) ask at the lake bed for a point up
to 3 yd under it now (`WaterProbeZ`); `.ga admin spot` at that point says "in the water (18.2 yd of water there: no place
to rest)" where it said nothing before.

**Round 167: the count from afar and the ways to a zone's givers** (2026-11-22). Mageyo (60) used its hearthstone from
the Eastern Plaguelands to Silithus for "3 quests to take or work on there", found nothing it could do there (a hand-in
at the Bronzebeard Encampment and "Noggle's Lost Satchel", both behind the elite silithids of Hive'Regal, refused as
too dangerous on the spot) and ground. Pewpew's emergency hearthstone of the same round was the rule of round 124 (a
zone written off twice). The count from afar (the zones across the sea, and the capped bot's look at a zone it does
not stand in, round 142) judged a quest's work places by the safest way from the zone's hub (`QuestWorkDanger`, round 119),
but its givers and enders only by the place itself, and the work places only by creatures. The same held for a zone on
the bot's own side it does not stand in: in the run on the gaps instance Priestyo flew from Dustwallow Marsh to Silithus
for "5", three of them behind the same elites. Now, from afar and for a zone the bot does not stand in, a giver and an
ender count only when the safest way from the zone's hub to them passes nothing the bot's walks would refuse
(`PlaceWayDanger`, cached per place, side and level), the quest log's objectives there only when their work is reachable
that way, and the work places of a quest are also its objects to use and the creatures and objects its items come
from. The zone's hub is where a bot that comes from elsewhere arrives; in the zone it stands in the walk gate judges
the ways from where it is.

**Round 164: a run from foes as fast as the getaway** (2026-11-22). Owldudu (60, druid) left two Dust Stormers of
Silithus at 75 % health and died on the run seventeen seconds later. The run was judged with Travel Form as its getaway

foe at the bot's back by the bot's average fight, where Dust Stormers cost it 2.3 times that (they hit back with
Lightning Shield and Lightning Cloud). A getaway that is only speed (Travel Form, Sprint) counts only against foes slower
than it now (`GetawayHelps`), and a foe at the bot's back counts as much more as its kind costs the bot more than its

fights with Barkskin. Also: Pewpew's two "no walk leads from where it stands to the road" at Hive'Zora were round 146's
walk back the way it came, as built (no rescue; it got out and ground on); Duduheal and Wardps waited at the inn of
Cenarion Hold because the grind found no spot, round 163's inn waits.

**Round 163: a pair of one kind; Charge onto a rock; the inn at the level cap** (2026-11-22).

- *Two warriors at one pair of Shadowmages.* Sheesh and Again (60, warriors) died four minutes apart at the same pair
  of Shadowmages (59-60, casters with Shadow Bolt that flee for help) in the Eastern Plaguelands, Sheesh attacked on
  its way to a grind target, Again by its own pull of "2 expected" at 95 % health right after a fight that had taken

  Against a warrior such pairs scatter widely: Again won seven of twelve, left two and died three times, on 2026-11-18
  twice already. A fight against two or three creatures of one kind teaches that kind's cost now, by the estimate's own
  sum (two are 2.5 single fights, three 4.5); a death never lowers it (`Escape::OnFightEnd`, `BotRuntime::Fight::oneKind`).
  A bot that died to a pair counts a pair of that kind as more than it has from then on. And two deaths of the guild's
  characters at one place within six hours set the place aside for the whole guild, whatever was on them (round 142's

  no point movement and no chase asks the ground guard about. Charge, Intercept, Feral Charge and the other charges and
  leaps of an AI-played character are refused now when they would end where the path finder has no walkable ground
  (`GroundGuard::MayLeap`, the spell check).
- *The inn at the level cap.* Since round 162's grind rule the bots at the level cap waited at the inn about three times

  grind looks at, and in the Eastern Plaguelands and Silithus the ten best-placed often stood among elites. The look for

- *Roguecombat's refused quest* ("Into The Maw of Madness", Silithus): its way passes the elite silithids of Hive'Regal,

**Round 162: grinding among elites** (2026-11-22). Buffadin (60) died in Mazthoril of Winterspring for the second time

a hostile elite down to five levels below the bot is passed over, the elites' spawns and the points of their rounds

**Round 161: a pack on a long round; the rock beside Light's Hope once more** (2026-11-22).

- *The Crimson Courier and its bodyguards.* Shamanheal and Lilwar (60) died seven seconds apart grinding Hate Shriekers
  in the Eastern Plaguelands, both "[Crimson Courier (level 60) was near]": they left their fights with one shrieker and

  as too strong, which is right for one creature that seldom passes; so the shriekers on their road were usable spots.
  Patrols whose rounds are as long (within a tenth) and whose nearest points lie within 20 yd of each other count as a
  pack now (`PatrolPacks` in RiskModel.cpp); a pack the bot cannot take together counts as too strong for it, each of

- *The rock.* Lilwar was rescued from the rock beside Light's Hope (round 153) again: its straight step up was refused,
  then a fight with a Noxious Plaguebat took it up by the chase, in short steps, each ending at a point the core counts
  as walkable ground. The path finder takes a polygon within 7 yd of a point for one the point lies on, and the rock's
  face 3 to 6 yd above the slope at its foot is that near; once the bot stood up there, "off the navmesh" no longer held
  for its next step (that rule needs the bot on walkable ground). Walkable ground is a point within 3 yd of the
  navmesh's surface now (the end of the core's probe, `HasNavmeshAt`), and a short step up onto a point without counts
  from half a yard of rise (it was one).

**Round 153: no walk onto a point without navmesh** (2026-11-22). The rock beside Light's Hope of round 151 went on:
four rescues from (2246, -5146, 59-62) in twenty minutes, Retadin found sitting there in a rest, Again and Healerino with

way. Healerino's last walk ran from the hill west of the rock, (2214, -5141, 73), 34 yd down onto it as "a straight line
of 2 points, 0 yd through the air". The cause is the core's path finder: it looks for a polygon of the navmesh within
3 yd across of the walk's end (50 yd up or down), the rock's top has none, and for a character (unlike a creature, which
gets no way) it then builds a straight line from wherever the walk begins (`PathGenerator::BuildPolyPath`: a player
"can fly" there). `.ga admin path` from the rock's foot, the hill and a place 200 yd away all give "normal + not using
a path, 2 points, ends as a STRAIGHT LINE". From afar such a line runs through hills and the air and was refused; from
the hill or the foot it runs on the ground, passed every rule, and put the bot where nothing leads on (the off-navmesh
rescue judged that right). The ground check now refuses a walk from walkable ground to a point the path finder has no
walkable ground at, unless that point is in the water (`GroundGuard::EndsOffTheNavmesh`, in `MayMove` and in
`WouldCancel` for the escape's legs), with its own line: "the path finder has no walkable ground there (a straight line
of N yd onto it)". What the bots wanted on the rock (the bat) is then refused like any target behind a refused step:
the AI lets go of it, a task's target is set aside.

**Round 152: three deaths "during no task"** (2026-11-22). "During no task" says only that no task ran at the moment
of the death: a task ends when a fight is left, a character enters the world without one, and a task that ended for a
pack on its way waits before the planner tries again. What killed them:

  grace (twelve seconds unseen, then out of the place) applied only to a character not in a fight yet, and creatures
  notice a character in the moment it is added to the map, before the planner's first step. That fight is ended now and
  the grace applies.
- *Stormstrikey* (60, shaman) stood at the edge of the Twilight camp of Silithus for the 25 seconds its hand-in waited
  after "a pack on its way", and its AI pulled an Avenger and a Geolord at 59 and 39 % mana; resting at 48 % health and
  18 % mana it was attacked twice and died. Between two tasks a bot starts no fight now (the pull check lets go of a
  creature that is not on it).
- *Hwave* (60, shaman) refused a pull for a Crimson Courier and its four bodyguards (elites on a long round), took a
  grind target 83 yd off six seconds later, met the five at 18 yd on its way, was held fast and died. The pull check
  records such a strong walker now, so the next target and its way keep away from the walker's round (the sights the
  look-out keeps for 90 seconds).
