**Round 148: a mage's opener is no losing fight** (2026-11-22). Bommbang (60, frost mage) died grinding in the Eastern
Plaguelands: a Shadowmage and a Crypt Slayer came at it at a Death Singer of a small Cult of the Damned camp (the risk
model's verdict for the spot, 12 %, was fair: its learned costs of the three kinds are 4 to 7 %); twelve seconds into
the fight it "left a fight against 2 foes at 70 % health [by how the fight went]" with its target at 95 % and died on
the run, the Shadowmages' bolts following it. The same fight, staged on the gaps instance with the fight traces on, was
won at 27 % with a potion, and the traces showed why nothing had happened in those twelve seconds:

- *The fight's own numbers measured the opener.* A level-60 mage casts Frost Nova, steps back to range, then Icy
  Veins, Ice Barrier, Cold Snap and its water elemental (mod-playerbots' cooldowns); its first spell on the target lands
  9 to 13 seconds into a fight. The verdict "by how the fight went" took ten seconds without progress for a fight that
  does not move, and measured how fast the bot takes the foes' health from the fight's start, so it projected a fight
  the bot could not win: five level-60 mages left 25 fights against two ordinary foes at 80 to 100 % health in four
  hours. The kill rate is measured from the moment the foes first lost health now (four seconds of it at least), and a
  fight counts as not moving after twenty seconds without progress.
- *No step back from a caster.* The step back to range after a Frost Nova (`Escape::StepBack`) ran 19 yd from a rooted
  Shadowmage, which casts from where it stands: the run cost the seconds and the cast it broke off, and the bolts went
  on. A creature of the mage class (`unit_class` 8) is no reason for a step back any more; from a rooted melee creature
  beside it the bot still steps back.

Staged again on the new build (two Shadowmages at once): no step back, the first damage after two seconds, won in 20 s
at 77 % (the old build: 31 s, 27 % and a potion). Seven minutes of four level-60 mages after it: 24 fights, none left,
one against two Hate Shriekers won at 32 % with a potion. The run from casters stays as it was (a run's cost is learned
per bot, `runFactor`). With `GuildAdventure.Debug` a line now names every spell an AI-played character casts in a fight
(the trace every two seconds misses every instant spell).

**Round 147: the other side's flight master in Light's Hope; a chase through the ground** (2026-11-21).

- *Bystanders.* Enhancer (60) died to Georgia, the Horde's flight master in the neutral town of Light's Hope: level 65,
  elite, a civilian (she starts no fight) and attackable for the Alliance. The log has five such fights since
  2026-11-20 (Bommbang and Priestyo died with her at full health, Leel pulled her itself: "its own pull (1 expected)").
  mod-playerbots turns to any hostile creature beside its way, and the route node "Lights Hope Chapel flightMaster" is
  right beside her. A creature that does not fight the bot and is a civilian or has a service (flight master, vendor,
  trainer, innkeeper ...) is now let go, before a pull and in a fight, unless a quest of the bot wants it; the bot also
  forgets it as its old target (mod-playerbots went back to her a second later). What is not prevented: a spell that
  hits several creatures (a chain, a nova, a totem) catching her beside a fight; then she fights the bot and its escape
  rules apply.
- *A chase through the ground.* Catdudu (60, a druid in cat form) fought a Putrid Gargoyle, which flies, and ended 18 yd
  under the slope where it stood ("no floor under it"); the rescue put it back ten seconds later. A fight's chase is not
  checked by the ground guard (core patch CP-10 checks point movements only), so this stays the rescue's: nine "under the
  ground" rescues in two days. *Since core patch CP-13* (the maintainers, on the owner's rule that rescues are a
  workaround) a player's chase asks the ground guard too: a chase that would run through the ground is stopped, the
  refusal line says "(its chase in a fight)", and three of them in 45 s in a fight make the bot give up the target.

**Round 146: a pocket in Hive'Ashi** (2026-11-21; e5a9a21 live: no death, at 60 17 characters in the profession mode
and 21 grinding, none at an inn, no standstill rescues). One rescue was left: Mageyo "cut off from every road" 18 yd
under the surface of Silithus. Inside Hive'Ashi, where the ooze-covered deposits lie, the path finder's way towards the
road node above the hive (and towards one ooze-covered vein) is incomplete from some spots and ends in a pocket at
(-6361, 1125, -10) from which no path leads on or back; the bot walked that partial path to its end and stood. Three
changes, each tried on the gaps instance where the case comes again whenever a bot stands there:

- *Gathering nodes the path finder does not lead to* (within 300 yd, for a round, and for a detour in passing) are not
  chosen; such a node waits half an hour. The bot had set out three times for the vein whose path ended 25 yd short.
- *Cut off from every road: the way it came first.* Wherever a bot is found cut off (four places in the planner), it
  walks back along its trail (the last 200 yd it walked out of combat) and plans anew, and what led it there waits half
  an hour; the rescue comes only when it has no trail, or the walk back did not get back where it came from and it is
  still cut off (the owner: rescues are a workaround). A trail-out once per quarter of an hour, as before.
- *A route whose first stretch is a guess, from under the surface* (no node near the bot has a walk the path finder
  proves, and the bot stands more than 8 yd under the surface: a cave, a hive, a building): the way it came first, then
  a route from there. In the open (a lake, a snow field) such a first stretch is walked as before: the first test turned
  two of them into a minute's walk back each.

What is left: from deep in the hive with a trail that does not lead out, the walk back ends inside and the rescue
follows, once per quarter of an hour at most; the navmesh itself is not changed.

**Round 145: rescues after crafting, grinding at the cap, a pack that walks, a hearth for the ship** (2026-11-21; the
first round with the professions and grinding at the cap: of 41 characters at 60, 16 in the profession mode, 13
grinding, none at an inn).

- *Five rescues that were none.* Each came one second after a character in the profession mode set out from the forge,
  anvil or inn it had crafted at for five minutes or more ("has not moved for 5 min ... task travel to Rich Thorium
  Vein"; Wartank twice at Light's Hope, the second time with its hearthstone; Nochnwar, Mageyo twice, Roguecombat, Again
  at Cenarion Hold). The rescue's clock stands still while nothing walks, but that happens in the planner's step, which
  is not called while a character crafts or enchants; the clock ran on. It starts anew now whenever the character
  crafts or enchants.
- *Grinding at the cap fought almost nothing.* The planner chose spots of level 50 to 60, but the step at the spot picks
  its target by the grind settings (three levels below the character: 57 to 60), so at a spot of level-54 Plaguehounds
  it found nothing ("nothing to fight at the spot" every twenty seconds; Magefrost had one fight in four minutes). The
  band of the cap goes with the task now. Two more things the test showed, for every grind: the planner chose spawns
  whose creature the character had just killed (twenty seconds of "nothing to fight" each; it leaves spawns that are
  down alone now, as the objectives do), and a spot where four fights had come of the targets counted as "empty, no fight
  came of its targets" (the grind step does not run during a fight, so it never saw one; a fight resets that clock now).
- *A pack that walks.* Magefrost (60) went around a Crimson Courier and its four Crimson Bodyguards, elites of level 58
  to 60 that walk a round of 421 points through the Eastern Plaguelands, at 45 yd; sixteen seconds later the five were
  on it, its escape found every way past them and it died. The way around a pack is drawn where the pack stands; a
  pack whose nearest creature walks (or half of it) is not walked around any more: the character keeps away from it, as
  from one roamer that walks. A camp is still walked around (one of it may walk a round inside).
- *The hearthstone for the ship.* Priestyo, Owldudu and Pewpew in the south of Silithus picked the Eastern Plaguelands
  across the sea; the walk to Theramore's ship was refused (a town of the other side on the way, level-61 to 64
  creatures around them, no flight master they could walk to), and they hearthed to Cenarion Hold, which is right: no
  way led anywhere from there. But the refusal also wrote the zone off for ten more minutes, so from the inn they did
  not take the flight to Theramore and the ship. A refused walk to a ship followed by the hearthstone leaves the zone
  open; from the inn a second refusal writes it off as before (the stone is not used at the inn). Nochnwar's hearth to
  its inn in the Eastern Plaguelands from Silithus was the travel rule (another continent, L32).

**At the level cap: the professions, then grinding** (2026-11-21; the owner: [quote left out]). A bot at the level cap with no quest left in its zone and no hand-in elsewhere used to wait at an inn. Now:

- *The profession mode first.* A bot on the autopilot whose plan has a primary profession it has not learned, or one
  below the plan's target (300 when the plan names none), gets the order "profession mode" (`CRAFT`), the order the
  owner sees in the addon, with a line and an event ("has no quest left at level 60 and works on its professions now").
  The mode is the one of docs above ("Profession mode"): it learns, crafts, buys, gathers and hunts for its professions.
- *Grinding when the professions have nothing to do.* When the mode finds nothing to craft or gather for two minutes it
  hands back to the autopilot as before; at the cap the autopilot then grinds creatures of ten levels below the bot up
  to its level (50 to 60 at the cap of 60) within 1500 yd in the zone it stands in, by the grind rules (the risk model's
  verdict, beasts before humanoids), and gives the professions another look after 30 minutes (what it grinds brings
  cloth, leather, herbs and ore by its gathering detours).
- *Waiting at the inn* only when there is nothing to grind either; every five minutes it looks again at its quests,
  its professions and grinding.
- A bot with the order `LEVEL_ZONE` grinds too and keeps its order; secondary professions do not hold a bot in the mode.

**Round 143: elites on the way, a rare elite, quest crafting that ran wild, a stall beside a quest area** (2026-11-21).

- *Elites count nine levels higher on the danger map* (four before). A level-60 warrior's route to a hand-in led through
  Tyr's Hand (Scarlet elites of level 55 to 57 among their casters): with four levels the elites stood below the four
  levels from which a way is walked around or refused, and its level-58 squad member died there to three of them,
  "during no task" (it followed). The owner's ruling is a detour or a refusal for elites (§7 L31); with nine every elite down
  to five levels below the walker counts, and the route through Tyr's Hand now names level-64 creatures and a group the
  warrior cannot take, which the gates refuse.
- *A rare elite is no rare.* The risk model and the danger map left rares out or counted them a little ("seldom
  there"). A rare elite (rank 2) is one spawn that is up until somebody kills it, and nobody does on this server: King
  Mosh, a level-60 devilsaur on a round through Un'Goro Crater, killed a level-60 shaman at the plants of its quest. Only
  plain rares (rank 4) are still counted as seldom there; a rare elite counts as an elite, on the danger map and on its
  round.
- *Quest items crafted for another bot, throttled.* Quest 6026 "That's Asking A Lot" asks for Thorium Bars, a Golden Rod
  and Unstable Triggers. From 2026-11-16 the guild's smiths and engineers were set to craft them every 30 s for each of a
  dozen bots that had the quest: 9000 starts in five days, 12,000 Unstable Triggers, 5000 Thorium Bars and 1700 Golden
  Rods "crafted", of which a few hundred really were (most starts stood at no forge or anvil, so the cast failed and the
  next look began it again), and each start ended the crafter's own task ("ends turn-in quest 8285 after 1 s: crafting
  from the guild storage"). What was made went into the guild storage, where crafting for skill used it before the bot
  that needed it looked again. Now a recipe is only started where it can be cast (its anvil, forge or fire in reach, its
  tools in the bags), an item is crafted for one bot's quest at most once in half an hour, and a crafter that crafted for
  another bot is left to its own work for five minutes (`QuestSupply.cpp`).
- *A stall beside a quest area.* A rogue stood five minutes, mounted, 300 yd from the area of "The Twilight Lexicon",
  where NewRpg's walk to the next point of the quest had stopped, until the rescue: the rule for an objective at a quest
  area that gets nowhere asked for the bot within 60 yd of the area, and the way's own stuck rules end once the bot was
  near. It holds for a bot that was near the area too now.

**Round 142: capped bots that stayed at the inn, a member below the cap, a place that kills the guild** (2026-11-21).

- *A zone across the sea counted as from here.* At the level cap a bot with no quest left waits at the inn and looks at
  the zones every five minutes. The look picked Eastern Plaguelands across the sea (five quests, counted from afar) and
  then counted that zone as from where the bot stood, where its quest givers are out of the bot's region: none, so it
  stayed, picked again five minutes later, and stayed (Catdudu at Cenarion Hold, Buffadin at Everlook). A zone that is
  not the bot's own is counted from afar too when the plain count finds nothing, and the zone is picked anew at once.
  Leel at Light's Hope had nothing left: every zone of its level (Eastern Plaguelands, Winterspring, Silithus) counted
  no quest for it.
- *A member below the cap does not follow a capped leader that waits.* A level-58 member stood beside its level-60
  leader at the Cenarion Hold inn for half an hour: the leader waited at the cap with no quest left, and the squad rule
  (a level gap of up to three) kept the member with it. A member below the level cap plays its own order while its
  leader waits so (not a quest partner: its pair's rules part it), and follows again once its leader has quests.
- *A place that kills the guild's characters.* The Twilight camp of Silithus (six Twilight Overlords, eleven Twilight
  Flamereavers and Vyral the Vile, all of level 60 and 61, in a hollow with one way out) killed five level-60 characters
  of one guild on three days (Retadk, Baumi, Mageyo among them), each with up to eight creatures on it and no way to run
  ("of 7 directions 7 had no path"). It is no camp by the open-sides rule (its walls close the sides, its creatures
  stand in a line), and each character came there on its own, with a death place of its own. Now a death with three or
  more creatures on it and another guild character's death within 80 yd in the last two days set the place aside for
  every guild character in the world for eight hours or until it is above the level of what died there
  (`Risk::OnDeath`; `ga_bot_death_place` keeps a death two days).

**Round 126 and 127: the stones of the Blasted Lands, a walk back the way it came, places on their floor, a target let
go, the trainer that teaches most, a capped bot without quests, a quest pair that cannot work its quest** (2026-11-15
and 2026-11-21).

- *Two hearthstones a second after a zone was written off.* A paladin and a hunter of level 53 ground near Dreadmaul Post
  in the Blasted Lands; their ways past the level-60 Dreadmaul ogres were refused, so the zone was "nothing it can safely
  get to" (it waits in `unreachableZones`); the zone picked next (Western Plaguelands) had no way either: the land way
  north leads through Stonard, a Horde town whose Stonard Grunts (level 65) the bots rightly count as enemies, and
  Nethergarde's flight master stands 540 yd away behind the ogres. A refused zone travel used the stone when the bot
  stood in a zone it had set aside for itself, and the zone written off a second before was one. Now only a zone that
  keeps killing the bot (it died there twice) allows the stone at a refused zone travel; anything else is the no-zone
  hold's matter (its three minutes).
- *Back the way it came before the stone.* A level-17 warrior on the Westfall coast and a level-39 rogue in Dustwallow
  Marsh stood beside a camp (12 murlocs, 19 Mirefin) with every route's first node beyond it; the first used its stone at
  the second "the place holds it", the second after eight refused ways in a minute. Now the bot walks back along its
  trail first (the points it walked out of combat, up to 200 yd; `StartTrailOut`, `StepTrailOut`: the core's path from
  point to point, the AI held, at most 90 s, given up in a fight or when it does not get on), once per quarter of an hour,
  and its ways and zone travels are counted anew from there; the stone the next time.
- *Places to craft on their own floor.* A priest in the profession mode went for the nearest Stove of Booty Bay by the
  map, on an upper floor 18 yd above the docks with no stair to it from there; it walked under it, into the bay, and was
  rescued, at the same place in two rounds. A place to craft within 120 yd is taken only when one path of the path finder
  ends at it on its floor (`PathEndsAt`: within 6 yd across and 4 yd up or down).
- *A target let go without stopping the walk.* Two bots in Stranglethorn stood two minutes each 90 and 103 yd from their
  quest's spot, "movement 0; rpg do quest": mod-playerbots picked a creature beside the way (a Venture Co. Geologist, a
  Mosh'Ogg Warmonger) at every look, the check before a pull let it go as off the bot's work, and the letting go
  (`BotDriver::DropTarget`) stopped every movement, four times a second. `BotDriver::LetGo` ends only a chase of that
  creature and a cast at it; the walk to the work goes on.
- *The class trainer that teaches most.* In-place learning of class spells took the list of the nearest friendly class
  trainer, and a start zone's trainer lacks the higher ranks: a bot whose nearest trainer of its class stood in its start
  zone learned nothing more from some level on. `ClassTrainerForLearning` takes the trainer whose list teaches the bot
  the most now, then the one with the longest list, then the nearest on its map. Bots that missed ranks get them at
  their next login or level-up.
- *A bot at the level cap leaves a zone without quests.* A level-60 death knight in Silithus kept Silithus (0 quests)
  over Eastern Plaguelands (7, across the sea; a crossing needs 8) and Winterspring (1; a move needs 3), and waited at
  the inn for good: a bot at the cap does not grind. Such a bot now goes for a zone with quests: on its side one worth a
  move, else across the sea one worth a move, else on its side any with a quest.
- *A quest pair that cannot work its quest parts.* The same death knight was the quest partner of a level-60 warlock for
  "Vyral the Vile"; the leader's walk to Vyral was refused every half hour (a camp of level-61 creatures on the route), so
  the leader waited at the Cenarion Hold inn, its member beside it, until the pair's hour was up, and the two paired
  again half an hour later. After they met, a leader that works no task of the pair's quest for four minutes (out of a
  fight and a rest) parts the pair, and the quest waits two hours before partners pair up for it again
  (`QuestPartners.cpp`, `NoWorkSeconds`).
- *Not built: a "place that leads nowhere" check.* The shop on Booty Bay's eastern docks (Kelsey Yance, Narkk, Haren
  Kanmae) looked like a patch of ground a walker gets into and not out of; the path finder has whole paths in and out of
  it, the live log has one rescue there (the stove case above), and a check of the way from an NPC's spot to the road
  map's node left out quest givers of Lakeshire (their spots lie off the path finder's ground by a hand's breadth).

**A squad member's own vendor visit** (2026-11-14, rounds 125/126: a druid went to a vendor for its squad member every
two minutes, eleven times, and the member stayed at 0 free bag slots: its bags held 25 worn soulbound green pieces, which
only a character's own vendor visit sells (the storage work's `LootService::HandleWornGear`), and the leader's visit made
room only by the loot filter). When the leader's vendor visit is done, every member within 60 yd makes a visit of its own
at that vendor (`OrderService::StepMemberVendorVisit`): it walks within the core's interaction distance (the AI held, 45 s
at most, out of combat), its worn gear goes as on its own visit (`HandleWornGear`), it is repaired at an armorer, and room
is made; a visit that freed nothing in its bags pauses the leader's trips for it for half an hour (`visited V with its
squad leader: N free bag slots (was M)`, `freed nothing in its bags ...: its squad leader's next trip for it waits 30 min`).

**A quest item's vendor: within reach before the purchase** (2026-11-14, round 125: a priest "bought 0 of 1 x Flagon of
Mead" for "The Third Fleet" at Innkeeper Helbrek, and another at Edris Barleybeard, then set out for the next mead vendors
in Dun Morogh, thirteen walks refused for a place it had set aside on the way). The core sells only within its interaction
distance (`Player::GetNPCIfCanInteractWith`, 5 yd), and NewRpg counts a vendor as reached farther off: before a quest
item's purchase the bot steps in (ten seconds at most). And a quest item's vendor trip counts against the quest like a
task of it: two refused or blocked ends leave the quest a quarter of an hour, no walk from vendor to vendor.

**The hearthstone only in the utmost emergency, round 124** (2026-11-14; four emergency hearthstones of the guild in 26
minutes, the owner allows the stone only in the utmost emergency). What they were: a refused travel to the zone it had
picked used the stone at once (a hunter 600 yd from its inn on the Feralas coast, while Tanaris had as much work as
Un'Goro; a death knight in the Blasted Lands); "no zone reachable" used it at once (a paladin went ashore in Rut'theran
for a hand-in in Darnassus, found no zone on that side, and errands are planned only after a zone); and "the place holds
it" used it after one minute (a Shore Strider at the Feathermoon ferry). Now a refused zone travel sets the zone aside
and the autopilot picks another one (the stone only out of a zone that keeps killing the bot); with no zone the
hand-ins it can reach come first and the stone only after the three minutes of the no-zone hold; and a place that holds
the bot makes it wait a minute, the stone only the second time within a quarter of an hour.

**A quest area that gets nowhere** (2026-11-14, a druid stood five minutes at the quest area of "Bloodpetal Poison" in
Un'Goro, NewRpg "doing" the quest, until a rescue): an objective at a quest's point (no spawn) where the bot stands and
the quest gets nowhere for four minutes ends, and the quest waits a quarter of an hour (no rescue).

A squad member with no free bag slot at all sends its leader to a vendor at any distance (the leader's own bags may have
room: Wardps had none, its leader Duduheal 25, the vendor of Marshal's Refuge was beyond the 400 yd of full bags).

**Bags for an empty bag slot** (2026-11-14, the storage work's bag check: one of the owner's new recruits, level 12, had
no bag at all, sixteen slots full of quest items and two Skinning Knives; nothing gave a guild bot a bag). A character
the AI plays that has an empty bag slot puts on the largest plain bag (no profession bag) it can use: out of the guild
storage at its look into the storage (once a minute, above the kind's reserve, straight into the bag slot, so a full
backpack is no obstacle; `put on a bag out of the guild storage: X (N slots)`), else the largest one a vendor it visits
sells, paid from its money and what it lacks from the guild's budget (`bought a bag at V: X (N slots; price)`). A smaller
bag is not swapped for a larger one.

**Two creatures that stand together: the risk model's verdict** (2026-11-14, the maintainers' ruling after round
119). A pair on a way no longer counts two levels higher on the danger map; creatures standing together are a group from
two on, and the walk gate and the route search ask the risk model whether the walker can take that many
(`Risk::CanFight`, the bot's own learned fights). Server settings: `GuildAdventure.Walks.GroupFrom` (2; was 3) and
`GuildAdventure.Roads.PairLevels` (0; was 2, the old bump).

**The way in is judged like the way out** (2026-11-14, the guild leader at level 51 in the Blasted Lands: it walked to a
Redstone Crystalhide 40 yd from the Dreadmaul ogres, levels 58 to 60, and from there every way out was refused for the
ogres; its emergency hearthstone followed). The walk to an objective leaves its last 60 yd out of the way's danger, for
the spot is the risk model's matter; creatures far above the bot in those yards are not, unless they stand right at the
spot (12 yd: the target and its company). Such a walk is refused like the walk out would be.

**A target in the water: the swim first** (2026-11-14, a shaman on a cliff of Feralas had every Sea Spray of quest 7721
set aside one after the other, each "on a level the path finder has no way to", every 30 s: they float in the sea
below, where the navmesh ends). The set-aside of a target on another level waits for the swim (`StepSwim`, once per
task); only a target the swim finds no way to is set aside. And two such ends of one quest's tasks leave the quest for a
quarter of an hour (`no way to its level` counts like a blocked end).

**The last leg of a navmesh path** (2026-11-14, a paladin in Thelgen Rock went for a Tin Vein in the cave's wall: the
navmesh ends 4 yd before the vein, the core ended the "normal" path at the vein's own spot, and its last leg ran into the
rock; the bot stood there "under the ground" until a rescue put it on a road). The ground guard trusted every plain
navmesh path; now it samples the leg from the path's last corner to the destination like any straight line, and a last
leg through solid ground is refused (`PathProbe::ProbeMovement`). (`.ga admin path` from the cave to the vein: "3 yd
through solid ground ... leaves the ground".)

**Waits are no standstill** (2026-11-14, a druid beside Stonard waited 75 s for a patrolling grunt to move on, its task
ended, and one second later it was "rescued" for five minutes without moving). The five minutes of "has not moved"
stand still while the bot waits on purpose: away from a creature (an escape or keep-away) or for a roamer to move on.

**A lift's stops: blocked by height** (2026-11-14, three bots caught on the floor of the Searing Gorge's Cauldron). The
road map has four nodes "Scaffold Cars" one above the other at (-6905, -1207), the stops of the lift from the Cauldron's
floor (z 179) to its rim (z 240); only the floor's stop has walks out of the Cauldron. At 19:17 one refused step towards
the rim's stop took all four out of the road map (`ga_road_block`): nodes went out by their distance on the map alone.
From then on the floor had no node a bot could walk to: bots there were "cut off from every road" and the rescue put
them at the rim's stop in the air, from where they were rescued again. Now a refused step takes out only nodes within
12 yd of its height; blocks of stacked nodes are given back once at startup; and a node with no ground around it at all
is no rescue node.

**A squad member's full bags send its leader to a vendor** (2026-11-14, the storage work's bag check: two squad members
of the guild had no free bag slot and no vendor trip for hours, since 08:23 and since 15:47). A member plans no upkeep of
its own (it follows its leader), so a member within 100 yd with full bags (one free slot or none) makes its leader's
upkeep urgent, and at the leader's vendor visit the bags of every member beside it (60 yd) get the visit's care
(`MakeBagSpace`: the loot filter's junk sold, materials and what it does not use into the guild storage). The log line
says "a squad member's bags full".

**A spot on another level near by: the planner's own steps** (2026-11-14, a druid stood 19 and 6 yd from Scrimshank's
Surveying Gear in the Gaping Chasm of Tanaris, a cave under its feet, for 239 s and 388 s: NewRpg's walk does not get
down). An interaction whose spot lies more than its climb above or below the bot within 80 yd is walked there by the
planner itself along the core's whole path (`walks to the spot of quest N itself: it lies .. yd below it`), when the path
finder has one, hop by hop.

**A long way around is no refused way** (2026-11-14, the maintainers on the owner's ruling: a detour through real terrain is a
route, not a danger). An objective whose road is more than four times the straight line (and longer than 2500 yd) still
takes another spawn at once, but it no longer counts against the quest (the guild leader left "The Corruption of the
Jadefire" for a quarter of an hour after one such spawn and one pack on its way) nor towards "boxed in".

**A zone whose quests lie behind stronger creatures** (2026-11-14, the guild leader at level 51 in the Blasted Lands:
every way from Nethergarde Keep to the quests' creatures passes the Dreadmaul ogres, levels 58 to 60; the walk rule
refused them one after the other, the zone counted 0, its way to the ship passed Stonard's and Grom'gol's Horde guards
(level 65 on the danger map: hostile, rightly counted), no flight master was in reach, and it used its hearthstone).
The zone pick counts a quest, and the planner offers its pickup, only when the way from the zone's hub to the nearest of
its targets (the creatures it asks to be killed, the creatures that drop its items; the four nearest spawns in the
zone) passes no creature more than `Walks.MaxLevelsAbove` above the bot, and no town of the other side
(`OrderService::QuestWorkDanger`, the road map's route for a walker of the bot's level, cached per quest, side and
level). A zone whose quests all lie behind such ways counts 0 and is not picked.

**No blind walks at all** (2026-11-14, the owner's ruling; a warlock "found no route for 2264 yd" from Thorium Point to a
vendor in the Burning Steppes, walked straight, came onto a scaffold of the Cauldron and stood there). A walk the road
map has no route for goes only along a whole way of the path finder (hop by hop, the planner's own steps), else it does
not start (`finds no way to walk to (..): no route of the road map ..., and the path finder has no whole way there`);
the planner's own steps take no straight line the core hands out for want of a path; and the ground guard is never
switched off any more (`the ground check is off for 60 s` was the way out of a dead end: it let the core's straight line
through for a minute). In its place the bot gives up what it was doing there: a fight it cannot get to (the AI lets go
of the creature), a travel (counted as stuck), a walk NewRpg kept starting (it stops), a task (the stuck rule ends it).

**Rescue nodes on the navmesh; the cut-off test** (2026-11-14, the druid in the Cauldron: rescued "cut off" from the
floor, put at the lift node "Scaffold Cars" at (-6900, -1339), which has no polygon, and rescued again 26 s later "off
the walkable ground"). A rescue puts the bot at the nearest road node that stands on the navmesh (a path from it in
some direction), and the cut-off test does not count nodes off the navmesh among the eight it asks.

**A flight when the way on foot is refused** (2026-11-14, a shaman in Feralas: the walk to Tanaris was refused for a group
on the way, the flight had been turned down because the walks to the master and from the landing were most of the way,
and it used its hearthstone). A travel whose way on foot is refused asks for a flight once more without that rule (the
walks are judged as walks of their own) before it gives up (`takes a flight towards X after all: its way on foot is
refused`).

**The hearthstone on travels only to another continent or a capital** (2026-11-14, the owner: [quote left out]; the maintainers' go). The travel hearthstone (a travel to the zone the bot's inn is in, an
errand's ender beside its inn) is used only when the inn is on another continent or in a capital city of the bot's
side (Stormwind, Ironforge, Darnassus, the Exodar; Orgrimmar, Undercity, Thunder Bluff, Silvermoon); else the bot walks
or flies. Bot setting `Travel.Hearthstone` (312): only in an emergency / to another continent or a capital (default) /
whenever it shortens a travel (the old rule). The emergency uses (boxed in, no zone it can get to, a refused way to its
zone or its ship, a zone that killed it) stay whatever the setting says.

**A target on another level** (2026-11-14, the guild leader on the scaffolds of the Searing Gorge's Cauldron: 88 s and
three refused steps for each target, and a restart forgot every one). The ground guard's first refused step towards a
task's target that stands 8 yd or more above or below the bot, when the path finder has no whole way to it from where
the bot stands (and the bot itself stands on the navmesh), sets the target aside at once (`cannot get to X at (..) (..):
it stands N yd above it, on a level the path finder has no way to from where it stands`). When no node of the road map
within 300 yd of the target has a way there either, it is set aside for two hours and kept across a restart
(`ga_bot_wait` kinds 5 to 7: a creature's or an object's spawn, an area); else for the usual 20 minutes.

**No walk goes blindly straight** (2026-11-14, the owner's ruling, relayed by the maintainers for the walk to Theramore's
ship). A short walk (below `Roads.MinDistance`) goes straight only while the path finder has a whole path for it, and
that is asked again from where the bot stands every 40 yd and after a refused step (the walk NewRpg makes is not the
path that was asked for); without one the road map is asked (Theramore's flight master to the ship: 382 yd over the
pier, where the straight walk ran 156 yd through the air beside it and the bot was put at the graveyard). A walk after
a flight asks its way from the landing (a route planned before the flight kept the walk from the landing to the ship
from asking at all). A refused straight step towards a target the path finder has a whole way to makes the planner
walk the bot along that way itself at once (`has its straight step towards X (..) refused: the planner walks it along
the path itself`; the guild leader on the Searing Gorge's rim stood 24 s after its refused drop before the route down).

**The last yards to a fishing spot** are the planner's own point movement along the core's path, and a spot the path
finder has no whole way to from where the bot is gets set aside at once (a priest stood two minutes in the water 12 yd
below its spot on a bank, NewRpg's walk did not set off).

**Refused steps towards the AI's own target** (2026-11-14, a warlock stood ten minutes on the shore east of Booty Bay:
its AI kept going for a Bloodsail Raider in the water below the ledge, and each of its travels and its voyage took the
refused steps as their own, "finds no way on foot", three zones set aside). A refused step towards a creature the AI
goes for that is not the task's target makes the AI let go of it (`lets go of X ... no way on the ground leads there`);
the refusals do not count against the task. And an errand's travel that a pack stops twice within ten minutes gives the
hand-in up for half an hour (the warlock had set out for Bookie Herod's Strongbox at the Kurzen camp five times in two
minutes).

**Walked around or refused only from four levels up** (2026-11-14, the owner's ruling, relayed by the maintainers:
[quote left out]). A single ordinary creature up to three levels above the walker no longer makes a route longer and no
longer closes a walk: `Walks.MaxLevelsAbove` is 3 (a walk is refused past a creature four or more levels above the
bot), `Roads.CostFromLevelsAbove` 4 (a route costs 12 times its length past such a creature, more beyond). Elites count
four levels higher (an elite of the bot's own level is walked around or refused), two creatures that stand together
two higher (a pair two levels up), and groups of three or more and camps are judged by the risk model as before. Both
values are settings (the first a bot setting per guild and per bot). Travels keep their limit of five levels above the
bot; the strong-camp rule (L24) stays. What the behaviour work's keep-aways do in a fight is the behaviour thread's.

**Creatures that walk about meet one another** (2026-11-25, the maintainers from round 222). A group on a way counted
the creatures within 18 yd of a point of it, by their spawns. The Scorpid Terrors of the Shimmering Flats stand 22 to
40 yd apart and wander 30 yd: no group was counted on the ways through them, and a level-31 druid on an errand's travel
was attacked by two of level 34, could not live through a run and died. A creature that walks about now counts within
18 yd plus the share of its walk its reach has (half of it, 10 yd at most): through the Terrors a way has a group of 2
of level 34 (the route for a level-31 walker goes around them, 1053 yd instead of 435).
The start of a route no longer passes every group within 120 yd for a walker that stands outside the reach of all of
them (20 yd then): the 120 yd are for one that stands among them and has to get out. A level-14 tauren on the shore of
Lordamere Lake took a route into the middle of the Vile Fin murlocs' camp 30 yd from it, kept away from it every ten
seconds for a minute and a half, and its voyage ended stuck (`RoadMap::OutsideStartStretch`).

**Rescues that were not needed** (2026-11-14, the owner on the guild leader: [quote left out]; then [quote left out]). Every rescue is a defect now, and its line names the task and its target
(`(task travel to Thorium Point; ...)`). Read on the live log, the guild leader's four rescues of the evening and
what was wrong:
- *The scaffold of the Searing Gorge's Cauldron*: rescued as "off the walkable ground" while it stood on the navmesh.
  The test asked the nearest road nodes, and the Cauldron's lifts are nodes without a polygon of their own: the core
  answers "not using a path" for them. `IsOffNavmesh` asks the ground around the bot first (eight points 4 yd around
  it; a path to one of them means it stands on the navmesh).
- *The Cauldron's floor below Thorium Point*: rescued as "cut off from every road". The three nearest nodes were the
  town's on the rim above; the floor's own node, 360 yd away, is walkable. `IsCutOff` asks the eight nearest.
- *Hearthstone and graveyard*: a rescue within half an hour of the last one took the hearthstone (on cooldown, the
  graveyard), wherever it was: the guild leader was sent home to Tanaris from below Thorium Point, the quest it was
  handing in 124 yd above it, and 41 s later put at Theramore's graveyard on its walk to the ship. Only a rescue
  within 150 yd of the last one on its map counts as "the road node did not help" now.
- *Shore leave*: a ship its owner had left it on (the Moonspray) counted as a crossing the planner had chosen, and
  the hour on its side of the sea held it three minutes in Rut'theran with no zone it could get to. Going ashore from
  a ship it was found on is no crossing.
- *The way into the Cauldron*: the ground guard lets a drop of up to 25 yd through the air pass, and a bot dropped
  over the Cauldron's wall onto its floor, where no path leads out (the lifts are no way for the path finder). A drop
  of 6 yd or more from which the path finder has no way back up to where the bot stands is not taken now (`the way
  drops N yd at (x, y) and no way leads back up from there`); the reaction to a refused movement goes on as before.
Not changed yet: the walk to Theramore's ship (not reproduced on the dev instance); a target on a level the path finder
cannot reach (the Cauldron's scaffold), to be set aside at the first refusal and across a restart; the hearthstone as
a way of travel planning (the owner: only to another continent or back to Stormwind).

**A gather walk ended by a pack** (2026-11-14, round 115: a warrior rode fifteen times in twenty-two minutes for one
Mithril Deposit beside the Bloodsail camp of Stranglethorn and kept away from the camp each time, "its way led into the
middle of their camp"). The reaction to a pack or a strong creature on the way set the target aside for every task but
travels, and the walks of a gather round, a hunt and a fishing trip are travels; the round's look at set-aside places
follows the straight line to the node, which did not cross the camp (the route did). Such a walk now counts with its
place: set aside at once, for 15 minutes, as a grind target (`sets travel (target Mithril Deposit) aside for 15 min`).

**No gathering node among creatures far above the bot** (2026-11-14, the observer: a priest of 38 caught up on its
Herbalism in Stranglethorn after a restart of the server had ended its journey for "Pearl Diving", went for a Wild
Steelbloom beside the Mosh'Ogg ogre mound, level 42 to 44 on their rounds, kept away from them and waited for them for
twenty-five minutes and died there). A node of a gather round or a detour is left out when a hostile creature four
or more levels above the bot stands or walks its round within 60 yd of it (`RoadMap::StrongestNear`, the danger map's
spawns and patrol points, elites higher; `OrderService::StrongNearNode`). The catch-up itself still begins as the owner's
rule says (E19), and a journey a restart has ended is not taken up again by itself.

**Breath as the game counts it** (2026-11-14, the observer: a mage drowned on the floor of a Desolace lake hunting the
crawlers of "Claim Rackmore's Treasure!", 65 s into a dive, a minute after it had come up for air). The dive clock of
`CheckBreath` started anew whenever the bot was at the surface for a moment, but the game gives the breath back only
ten seconds a second (`Player::UpdateMirrorTimers`): a bot that bobbed up now and then in its fights used up its three
minutes while the clock said a minute. `OrderService::TrackBreath` counts the breath as the game does (a second a
second under water, back ten a second above it), every tick; the bot comes up when that and the way up reach a third
of the breath (60 s at most), in a fight at 60 %; at the surface its AI is held until the breath is back (8 to 16 s:
its hunt had taken it down again at once). The line names the breath used: `comes up for air at (..) after 57 s under
water (8 yd deep; 58 s of its 180 s of breath used)`.

**Up for air only when the breath runs short** (2026-11-25, the owner: [quote left out]). The rule above came up after a third of the server's
WaterBreath.Timer whatever was left, so a bot went up with two of its three minutes still in it, and it took the
server's timer for everyone: an undead's Underwater Breathing (a multiplier of the breath) and a Water Breathing aura
or the guild perk Gills (no breath limit at all) were not counted, so those bots came up for nothing.
`OrderService::BreathMs` gives the breath as `Player::getMaxTimer` does (the timer times
`SPELL_AURA_MOD_WATER_BREATHING`, none with a Water Breathing aura or CP-8's breathing hook); `CheckBreath` sends the
bot up when the breath left is no more than the way up (depth at 4 yd/s, counted half again) and 25 s, in a fight
12 s; the way up may take what is left less 8 s (at most 45 s) before the bot is brought up. A character that breathes
under water counts no breath and does not come up.

**Out of a canal whose floor leads nowhere** (2026-11-25, round 226: a level-15 shaman stood an hour in the canal of
the Undercity's War Quarter, its routes, voyages and flights all ending "no way on the ground"). The canal's floor lies
2 yd under the water and is a part of the navmesh of its own (101 polygons from the War Quarter to the east wall); the
water's surface over it belongs to the rest of the city, which a ramp out of the canal at (1747, 375) joins. The core
keeps a swimmer 1.6 yd under the surface (`WorldObject::UpdateAllowedPositionZ`, `GetMinHeightInWater`), half a yard
over that floor, so every path of the bot starts on the floor and none leads out; the bot had come in by a path that
ended in the water (its own steps towards Brill). `OrderService::WadeOut` (from `WalkTo` once per task and from the
cut-off way out): a bot wading in water at least 1 yd deep (its head over the surface; not a diver) whose own path to its destination or to one of the six nearest
road nodes does not leave the water, while the path from the water's surface does within 300 yd, swims out along that
surface path to the shore and 12 yd on, in one movement (`MoveSplinePath`: a new path would start on the floor again);
nothing else moves it meanwhile. Not for a walk to a place in the same water within 400 yd, and not for a bot under the water: there the path finder has straight lines only, and the first live hour sent a warrior fighting naga 24 yd under Desolace's coast "out along the surface" to the shore twice on its way to the next naga. Log line:
`stands on a floor N yd under the water at (..) that leads nowhere (its walk): it swims out along the surface, N yd to
the shore at (..)`. A floor with a whole path to one of the goals on dry ground is no pocket: nothing is done and
nothing written (round 230: in ordinary lakes wading bots wrote "none from the surface leads out" about every five
minutes, their floor reaching three or four of the road nodes asked; their walk lacked a whole path for its
destination).

**Grinding in the water** (2026-11-14, found with the breath test: a warrior farming the Loch's frenzies stood six
minutes on the lake's floor, its target picked every second, until the rescue). A grind target near a bot in the water
is swum to straight (point movements; NewRpg's walk does not start there); targets picked for 60 s with no fight
coming of them make the spot count as empty (`has picked targets at its grind spot for 60 s and no fight came of
them`); a bot in the water whose walk has no way looks for its swim before the off-navmesh rescue puts it on a road,
and a target in the water is its own landing.

**Out of the water to a target on land** (2026-11-14, the observer's "Pearl Diving" test at the Vile Reef: after the
last clam on the sea floor the next target lay ashore and the bot was rescued twice as "cut off from every road").
A bot in the water whose step has no way (the ground guard's refusal) arms the swim too, unless it dives for its own
target there; with no water within 45 yd of the target, the landing is the water near the bot (up to 300 yd, twelve
paths asked for, the nearest towards the target first) from which the path finder leads onto the land, towards the
target; the rest of the way is the walk's.

**A camp's patrols carry it** (2026-11-14, the maintainers' go after the Bloodsail deaths off Booty Bay). A creature
on patrol whose way runs through the middle of a camp carries the camp along its way, up to 40 yd beyond the camp's
farthest creature: a road map node or a link's point within the patrol's reach of such a way counts as in that camp
(for walkers that cannot take it; the camp's middle stands for where the route meets it, so the camp a walker stands
in or walks to stays its own). A Bloodsail mage walks from the middle of its camp 25 yd beyond its tents; a level-44
hunter met it there on a walk to a vendor and had five of the camp on it. On the dev instance: 288 nodes and 4314
links in or through a camp (219 and 4092 before), 1748 patrols carry their camp along 35914 points; the camp part of
loading the road map takes 2.7 s.

**A node the detour does not take** (2026-11-14, the live server). Two miners in the profession mode stood five
minutes beside a vein in Duskwood and Stranglethorn ("rpg idle") until the rescue put them on a road: at the place of
a gather round the planner waited for the detour to take the node, and the detour does not take every node (its own
rules). It waits 15 s now, then the place counts as visited.

**A road beside a camp** (2026-11-14). The road map's camp scan looks 20 yd to either side of a link's path too, not
only at the path itself: a road that passes close beside the middle of a camp counts as one through it (for walkers
that cannot take it). On the dev instance: 4092 links through a camp, were 3298; loading the road map takes about
1.6 s, was 0.9 s.

**No quiet place, no stand-still** (2026-11-14, the observer on the live server). A priest on the profession mode,
its Inscription far behind and so worked on alone, stood 70 minutes on the Westfall coast among murlocs: nothing is
crafted with hostile creatures within 30 yd, the walk to a quiet place found no road node without hostile spawns
within 800 yd, and the branch of a crafting profession in focus returned before anything else could happen (`does not
craft at (-9623, 1464): 3 hostile creatures within 30 yd` every three minutes). Now, with no quiet place in reach, its
other professions have their turns for two minutes (`can do nothing for its Inscription (119) now (no place without
hostile creatures to craft at in reach)`): gathering, fishing, and with nothing at all the way back to the autopilot.

**Orange and yellow recipes before green ones** (2026-11-14; the owner: [quote left out]). In 22 minutes of the live server his guild storage went from 487 Heavy Leather to 6: a hunter in
the profession mode made 66 Heavy Armor Kits in batches of up to 20 while its Leatherworking rose from about 150 to 189,
about half of them green (the kit turns green at 180), while the yellow Guardian Pants could be made from the same
storage. The kit was the cheaper by the materials' worth per point at the chance the core gives (in this core it falls
in a straight line from orange at the yellow threshold to grey, so a green kit at 181 still gives a point in two), and
a batch ran on past the change of colour.
- **The order** (`Professions::CraftForSkill`, `Professions::EnchantForSkill`): an orange or yellow recipe it can make
  now; then one whose lack it can see to by itself (a material it makes, a vendor's, the anvil or forge), which it sees
  to first; a green one only when there is neither (`crafts .. (green: nothing orange or yellow can be made here)`), or
  when what the better recipe lacks cannot be had where it is (a vendor beyond the hub's reach, the hub's walks to an
  anvil used up: `.. (green: what its orange and yellow recipes lack cannot be had here)`); never a grey one. A recipe
  whose material creatures drop does not count as one it can make. Within a colour, the least material's worth per
  expected skill point, as before.
- **Batches up to the change of colour** (`CastsInColour`): an orange or yellow recipe is cast as often as the expected
  points up to green take, a green one up to its next expected point; then the next look decides anew (a recipe learned
  in place at the new skill can be orange).
- **No floor.** The guild storage is there to be used (the owner); a reserve the leader sets on an item in the Storage tab
  holds for this as for every automatic take.

**Tailors, enchanters and scribes that stood still** (2026-11-14; the owner: [quote left out]; his guild's best: Tailoring 149, Enchanting 154, Inscription 113,
the other professions 185 to 302). Three faults, read on the live server:
- **Bolts of cloth counted as bought** (`Buyable`, `WayToCast`, `CraftForSkill`): one clothier sells bolts of linen,
  wool and silk, in Silvermoon, so every recipe that takes a bolt counted it as a vendor's material, the purchase found
  no vendor the bot could get to, and the profession did nothing (a tailor at 120 wrote `can do nothing for its
  Tailoring (120)` every few minutes for hours, beside 776 Wool Cloth in the storage). A material the bot makes itself
  out of the guild storage is made first now (`makes a material first for its Tailoring: .. Bolt of Woolen Cloth`), and
  only a vendor of its own side (or a neutral one) counts.
- **Tools sold** (`OnPlayerCanSellItem` in `CraftOrders.cpp`): mod-playerbots sold the scribes' inking sets and the
  jewelcrafters' kits (white items it had no use for) at its vendor visits, and the profession plan handed out a new one
  half an hour later; in between nothing could be made (17 inking sets and 10 kits that day). A guild character the AI
  plays keeps one of each tool now (`keeps its .. : the tool of its professions is not sold`).
- **The tool its recipes lack comes first** (`CraftForSkill`): every enchanter stood at 150 to 154 with its Runed
  Copper Rod; what gives skill from there asks for the Runed Silver Rod, and the green enchantments the copper rod still
  served gave a point in forty casts, with dust disenchanted out of the storage for each. A recipe that makes a tool the
  bot's orange or yellow recipes lack counts as orange and is made once (`crafts 1 x Runed Silver Rod`).
- **What only another profession makes is ordered** (`SeeToLackedTool`, `Professions::LackedTool`; the owner: [quote left out]). A tool its orange and yellow recipes lack that lies in the guild storage the bot takes out
  (`took 1 x .. from the guild storage: the tool its Enchanting recipes lack`). Else what it cannot make, buy, mill or
  disenchant itself is ordered as a craft order of the guild with the crafters who can make it: a material of the
  tool's recipe it knows (the smith's Silver Rod for the enchanter's Runed Silver Rod), or the tool itself when it
  knows no recipe for it (`orders 1 x Silver Rod from the guild's crafters for its Runed Silver Rod (Startwar can make
  it): its Enchanting recipes lack Runed Silver Rod`). The order is an ordinary one: shown in the Storage tab, made on
  the crafter's town trips or in its profession mode out of the guild storage, the product into the guild storage, from
  where the bot that needs it uses or takes it. One look in ten minutes per bot, no order while one of the item is open,
  and a line when nobody of the guild in the world knows the recipe.
- **A crafter leaves its squad** (`LeaveSquadForCrafting`; the owner: [quote left out]): a bot on the
  profession mode that is a squad member leaves the squad (it followed its leader and crafted nothing: one tailor for
  hours), and the members of a bot on the profession mode go their own ways; not a dungeon group (`.. leaves the squad
  of ..: its order is the profession mode`).
- **A floor for green recipes** (bot setting `Professions.GreenMinChance`, 20 %): a green recipe or enchantment whose
  chance of a point a cast is below it is not made at all, also when nothing orange or yellow can be made.

**A tool is not made twice** (2026-11-13, found by the integration server on the live server). A bot with Jewelcrafting in its
plan got a new Jeweler's Kit about once a minute: the kit is no tool by its item data (the recipes name it as an item,
its TotemCategory is 0), so the loot filter's keep rule did not see it and the bag sweep put it into the guild
storage; the next look of the hand-out (`Professions::LearnPlanned`), which only asked whether the character had
one, made another: 117 kits in a guild's storage after a night. The hand-out now takes the tool out of the guild
storage when one lies there (`took 1 x Jeweler's Kit from the guild storage: the tool of its profession plan`), makes
a new one only when neither the character nor the storage has one, and runs at most once in half an hour per
character and tool. `Professions::IsTool` names the module's tools for whoever decides what a bot keeps (the
planner's bag step and the crafter's rule ask it; the loot filter's two rules in `Storage/LootService.cpp` should).

**Gear made for the guild: green or better, and only for who can put it on** (2026-11-13; the owner: [quote left out]; [quote left out]). `Professions::CraftGearFor` (the bot setting `Professions.CraftGear`) leaves out white and grey pieces, and a
guild character counts as a wearer only when it could put the piece on now (`CanWearCrafted`): the core's own check
for that kind of item (side, class and race, a required profession and its rank, a required spell, the level), the
weapon or armour proficiency, and the reputation the item asks for. mod-playerbots' rating, which decides what is an
upgrade, had asked the core's check already, so no piece was made for somebody who lacked a profession; the
proficiency and the reputation are new, and the rule now stands in the module's own code.
What the owner saw, four Flying Tiger Goggles ("Requires Engineering (100)") in the guild storage, were not made as gear
for anybody: Roguecombat made one per look in the profession mode because the recipe gave it a point of Engineering
(`crafts for its profession (profession mode): Roguecombat crafts 1 x Flying Tiger Goggles`, four times between 07:56
and 08:25), and what a bot makes goes into the storage (the design log §7 E8). Bots that take gear out of the storage
(`StorageSupply`) ask the core's check as well: nobody without Engineering 100 takes the goggles. Gear that crafting
for skill leaves there stays until the leader sells or disenchants it (the Storage tab's buttons).

**Surplus crafted gear is disenchanted** (2026-11-13; the owner, asked what should happen to gear that crafting for skill
leaves in the storage and nobody can wear: [quote left out]). `CraftOrders::SurplusOf` says how far a kind of item in the
guild storage is surplus; it looks at green and blue weapons and armour that a profession recipe makes:
- **nobody of the guild in the world can put it on** (`Professions::CanWear`: a required profession and its rank,
  class, level, armour kind, reputation): every copy is surplus, and these go first;
- **more copies lie there than guild characters would wear it** (mod-playerbots' rating for the levelling gear, the
  dungeon set's for a role): the copies beyond that are surplus; one always stays.
`CraftOrders::DisenchantSurplus` (bot setting `Professions.DisenchantSurplus`, on; per guild and per enchanter): an
enchanter whose skill is enough disenchants such pieces by itself, at its profession looks (at a hub after a hand-in,
in the profession mode), once a minute, at most three pieces a look; the materials go into the guild storage, and
each piece has its line: `disenchanted 1 x Flying Tiger Goggles from the guild storage as surplus (crafted, nobody of
the guild in the world can put it on): 3 x Strange Dust into the guild storage`, `... as surplus (crafted, 6 of it lay
there): ...`. When an enchanter needs dust or essences for a recipe (`DisenchantForMaterials`, E7), surplus pieces
come first as well, the likeliest piece for the missing material within a rank. Loot that is not crafted, grey and
white pieces and epics are not touched; "in the world" means the guild's characters that are logged in at that moment
(a benched engineer does not keep the goggles).

### Recipes from vendors (2026-11-13)

the owner: [quote left out] (to the question whether bots shall buy the recipes of their professions at a
vendor they pass; the fish of his storage stayed raw because the fish recipes are only sold by vendors).

`Professions::BuyRecipesAt` / `RecipeOffers` / `SellsRecipe` (bot settings `Professions.BuyRecipes`, on;
`Professions.RecipeMaxPrice`, 1 gold; `Professions.RecipeYards`, 300; per guild and per bot):

- **Which.** A recipe item of a vendor's list for a profession the character has, planned or not, that it can learn
  now by the item's own rules (`Player::CanUseItem`: the skill and its rank, the level, a reputation) and does not
  know yet; for gold only (no tokens), at most `Professions.RecipeMaxPrice`, and within what the guild's budget
  allows it. Recipes in limited supply count while the vendor has one.
- **Where.** At every vendor the bot visits (selling, repairs, provisions, a quest item), up to five recipes a visit.
  And, looked for once a minute like gear, with a walk to a vendor within `Professions.RecipeYards` that sells one
  (`Buying a recipe for its profession at <vendor>`; after such a trip not again for five minutes). No journeys for
  recipes: the owner's rule for gear (DQ7) holds here too.
- **Who pays.** As with gear and quest items (`GuildBudget::Request`): the bot's own share first, the guild bank the
  rest, within `Budget.ItemPercent` of the bank and the bot's allowance; a purchase that fails gives the money back.
- **Then.** The recipe is learned at once (the item is used up as when a player reads it): `<bot> bought recipes
  from <vendor> and learned them: Recipe: Bristle Whisker Catfish (Cooking 146; 3s 80c, the guild bank paid 1s
  90c)`. Whoever stands at the vendor and can learn it buys it; the rule "the highest skill learns it" is for the
  recipes of the guild storage.

### Cooks make food for the guild (2026-11-13)

the owner: [quote left out] (in the same message: the bots take food, drink,
potions, scrolls and bandages out of the guild storage, one piece at the moment they want to use it; that part is the
behaviour work's).

`Professions::CookForGuild`, called at the top of `OrderService::WorkOnProfessions` (bot settings
`Professions.CookStock`, 40, and `Professions.CookMinutes`, 15; per guild and per bot):

- **Who and when.** Every AI-played guild character that knows Cooking, whether Cooking is in its profession plan or
  not: at its profession looks, which are the three minutes after a hand-in at a hub on the autopilot and every look of
  the profession mode. Food for the guild comes before its recipes for skill.
- **What.** A cooking recipe it knows, grey or not, whose product is food (the item's spell is of the food category)
  that one of the guild's characters eats at its level: the active roster bots and the leader, each with its level; a
  character eats the food with the highest required level it may eat (`StorageSupply`), so a food counts for the
  characters at its required level and up to twelve levels above it. Of the recipes that can be made: food that
  leaves its eater "well fed" first, then the kind more characters eat, then the higher one.
- **How much.** Until the guild storage holds `Professions.CookStock` pieces of that food; then the next kind. A batch
  is what a profession look crafts anyway (`Professions.CraftBatch` at a hub, at most three batches per hand-in; the
  profession mode's batch). When nothing is to cook (the stock is there, or no material), the cook looks again
  `Professions.CookMinutes` later.
- **From what.** Its bags and the guild storage (core patch CP-7): each reagent that comes out of the storage leaves its
  line (`used 1 x Raw Bristle Whisker Catfish from the guild storage as a reagent for ...`), the start of a batch one
  (`cooks for the guild (profession mode): <bot> crafts 5 x Bristle Whisker Catfish. (the guild storage is to hold 40
  of each food its characters eat)`), and what was made goes into the storage with the usual line (`put what it made
  into the guild storage: 5 x ...`). Nothing is bought for it and nothing hunted: only what is there.
- **Where.** At a cooking fire, and only where nothing hostile is around (the looks themselves are behind
  `IsQuietToCraft`). On the autopilot the bot cooks when a fire is where it stands after its hand-in; the profession
  mode walks to a quiet fire (`PlanFocusTrip`).
- The fish recipes are vendor recipes: cooks get them at vendors they pass ("Recipes from vendors").
- Not built: a cook's own campfire (no bot knows Basic Campfire), drink (cooking makes none for the classic levels),
  and the same for alchemists (potions) and First Aid (bandages): the design log section 7 E17.

### Engineers make ammunition for the guild (2026-11-22)

the owner: [quote left out].

`Professions::AmmoForGuild`, called in `OrderService::WorkOnProfessions` after the cooks' food (bot setting
`Professions.AmmoStock`, 5000 rounds, 0 = never; per guild and per bot):

- **Each type.** No profession of this client makes arrows, so it is bullets: for each of the guild's hunters in the
  world whose ranged weapon is a gun (the active roster bots and the leader) the best ammunition of the engineer's
  recipes that the hunter can use (`Ammo::Fits`, `Ammo::Better`) is a kind to keep, when it is no worse than the best
  ammunition a vendor sells the hunter for gold (what it buys anyway, `Ammo::BuyAt`; and a hunter takes ammunition out
  of the storage only when it is no worse than what it carries). A kind nobody shoots is not made. The kind more
  hunters shoot comes first, then the better one. At level 60 no bullet an engineer makes beats Impact Shot, which
  ordinary vendors sell from level 55 (22 damage; Thorium Shells 17.5). An engineer's bullet beats the vendors' for a
  hunter of 5 to 9 (Crafted Light Shot), 15 to 24 (Crafted Heavy Shot), 30 to 39 (Crafted Solid Shot, Hi-Impact Mithril
  Slugs) and 44 to 54 (Mithril Gyro-Shot, Thorium Shells from 52). Round 171 (2026-11-22):
  an engineer with Engineering 63 made 4800 Crafted Light Shot (a level-5 bullet, 2 damage) "for" two level-60 hunters:
  the kind was the best of that engineer's own recipes, whatever the vendors sell.
- **How much.** Until the guild storage holds `Professions.AmmoStock` rounds of the kind (above its reserve), a batch
  at a time; the hunters take it out as they take any ammunition there (docs/storage.md section 9). The storage takes
  ammunition only when a guild character made it, which this is.
- **From what.** Its bags and the guild storage (core patch CP-7), every reagent with its line; what a recipe lacks that
  the engineer makes itself (blasting powder out of stone, bars out of ore) is made first, two steps deep. Nothing is
  bought: a material only vendors sell leaves that kind for later.
- **Where and when.** At a hub after a hand-in and in the profession mode (where it walks to the anvil or forge a recipe
  wants). At the level cap a bot comes to a hub seldom and its professions are mostly done: before it grinds, an
  engineer whose recipes could make what runs low goes into the profession mode for it (a real order change with its
  line and event), and the mode hands back to the autopilot when there is nothing left. It looks every quarter of an
  hour.
- **One engineer at a time.** The first engineer of a guild that sets out for the ammunition makes it for half an hour
  (or until the stock is there); the others go on with what they do. (In the first run three engineers at the cap went
  into the profession mode in the same second for 1040 rounds, each walking to an anvil 1100 to 1700 yd away.)
- **Crafting for skill does not add to a full stock** (round 174, 2026-11-23). Two death knights with Engineering 1 to
  75, Unholymoly and Retadk, crafted for their skill in the profession mode, and the cheapest skill point was Crafted
  Light Shot: 8400 rounds went into the guild storage in one round, on top of the 4800 Bloodyo had made for the
  hunters. `Professions::CraftForSkill` now leaves a recipe whose product is ammunition while the storage holds
  `Professions.AmmoStock` of it, and one whose product is another stackable consumable (a potion, a bandage, food, an
  explosive: in this client explosives are trade goods) while it holds `Professions.SkillCraftStock` of it (919, 200, 0 =
  no cap; per guild and per bot). What the crafter carries of it counts too (what it made goes into the storage when its
  crafting ends, and the next look can come first), and a batch, and the material made for it, is no larger than what
  the storage takes up to the stock (a batch of 20 casts of Crafted Light Shot is 4000 rounds). Another orange or yellow
  recipe gets its turn, or none. Nothing is sold or deleted. Other trade goods (bars, blasting powder) are not capped:
  they are materials.
- Lines: `Roguecombat is level 60 (the level cap): the ammunition of the guild's hunters runs low in the guild storage
  (below 5000 of a kind) and it can make more: its order is the profession mode`, `Roguecombat makes ammunition for the
  guild (profession mode): Roguecombat crafts 6 x Thorium Shells. (2 of the guild's hunters shoot Thorium Shells; the
  guild storage and its bags hold 3960 of it)`, `put what it made into the guild storage: 1200 x Thorium Shells`.

### Endgame consumables for the guild's dungeon runs (2026-11-25)

the owner: [quote left out]. At a dungeon's start his group got a
Solid Sharpening Stone, an Elixir of Ogre's Strength and a Scroll of Stamina IV: the run uses the best the guild storage
holds for each character (stage C, the design log section 7 DC1-DC5), and the storage held no flask, no elixir of the
level-60 recipes, no dense stone and no oil (read in its database: Elixir of Greater Agility was its best elixir, Solid
Sharpening Stone its best stone). Nothing made them: a crafter at 300 gets no skill from a recipe, so its town trips
made nothing, and only cooks (food) and engineers (ammunition) kept a stock for the guild.

`Professions::ConsumablesForGuild`, called in `OrderService::WorkOnProfessions` after the ammunition (bot setting
`Professions.ConsumableStock`, 920, default 20; per guild and per bot):

- **What.** Of the recipes a character knows, those whose product a dungeon run uses: an elixir or flask whose buff a
  fight uses (stats, attack and spell power, healing, armour, health, mana, regeneration, crit, hit, ratings; not
  detection, water breathing or a vision), a scroll of the same kind, a sharpening stone, weightstone or oil, a scope
  (`DungeonSupplies::Classify`), a healing or mana potion. The kind is the effect (agility, strength, a stone for blades,
  a weightstone, a wizard oil, a mana oil, healing potions ...); of each kind the best it can make, the highest item
  level first, nothing more than 15 item levels below the guild's highest level (its active roster and its leader),
  nothing it could not use there. A kind whose best it cannot make (no Black Lotus) falls to the next best; a kind the
  storage holds `ConsumableStock` of at that level or above needs nothing. The kind the storage has least of first.
  What the guild has of a consumable is the guild storage and the crafter's own bags (`GuildStock`): what it made goes
  into the storage only when its crafting has ended, and its next look came before that (Warlockdot made 5 x Gift of
  Arthas three times in 35 s, each look counting the storage's 15, and 30 lay there against a stock of 20,
  2026-11-27). The cooks', engineers', processors' and key makers' stocks are counted the same way.
- **How.** As gear for the guild: what a recipe lacks that the bot makes itself comes first (two steps deep), a
  vendor's material (a Crystal Vial) is bought from the guild's budget (at a hub within 300 yd and three purchases per
  hand-in), a place (an alchemy lab, a forge) is walked to in the profession mode or next to a hub. Batches of the
  usual size; what was made goes into the guild storage as everything a bot makes. A consumable whose casts gave
  nothing twice in a row is left for an hour.
- **When.** After a hand-in at a hub and in the profession mode, a look every quarter of an hour; at the level cap (where
  a bot seldom comes to a hub) the autopilot puts the bot into the profession mode when it can make what runs low,
  before it grinds, and the mode hands back to the autopilot when there is nothing left (as for ammunition). One crafter
  of a guild at a time (half an hour).
- **Use.** A dungeon run's characters use what fits them at its start and after a wipe (DC1-DC5); the levelling bots use
  scrolls by themselves, elixirs only with `Storage.Supply.Elixirs` (B28, off).
- Lines: `makes consumables for the guild's dungeon runs (profession mode): <bot> crafts 5 x Elixir of the Mongoose. (for
  Elixir of the Mongoose; the guild storage and its bags hold 0 of it)`, `buys N x Crystal Vial from .. for consumables for the guild:
  ..`, `walks to .. to make consumables for the guild: ..`, `is level 60 (the level cap): the guild storage holds fewer
  than 20 of .. for the guild's dungeon runs and its recipes make it: its order is the profession mode`.
- Not built: buff food at a run's start (cooks make it, `CookForGuild`, but a run does not eat it), resistance potions.

### Enchantments for the guild's gear (2026-11-25)

*Since 2026-11-26* (the owner: [quote left out]) the item level is the guild bot setting `Professions.EnchantMinItemLevel` (924, default 60,
`GuildAdventure.Professions.EnchantMinItemLevel`); the quality (blue or better) stays.

the owner: [quote left out]. Read
first (read only): his Alliance guild has two enchanters at 300 (Shadow and Magefrost know 96 and 93 enchantments,
Priestyo 208), its level-60 characters wore 1 to 3 pieces of blue quality and item level 60 or more each (the death
knights 14 to 16, their campaign gear) and almost none of them had an enchantment; the guild storage held 326 Armor
Vellums, 6 Weapon Vellums, Illusion Dust, Eternal Essences and Radiant Shards. Nothing of the module put an enchantment on
another character's gear: an enchanter's own skill-ups (`EnchantForSkill`) go on its own pieces.

**How it is done.** The core puts an enchantment on another player's item only through a trade window (`Spell::
CheckCast`, `SpellCastTargets::Update`: an item target is the caster's own, or the trader's "will not be traded"
slot), and mod-playerbots answers trades by itself. The game's other way is the one players use without meeting: the
enchanter writes its recipe on a vellum (`Spell::EffectEnchantItemPerm`: the vellum is used up and the recipe's scroll
is made), and whoever holds the scroll puts it on its own piece (the scroll's use spell is the recipe, without reagents
or rod). A first Armor or Weapon Vellum holds every classic enchantment (their level is 0); the guild's scribes know both
recipes. So: the enchanter makes the scroll, it goes into the guild storage, the wearer takes it out and puts it on.

- **Which pieces.** What a guild character the AI plays wears, of blue quality or better and item level 60 or more
  ([quote left out] read as: characters the AI plays, whatever their order; not the owner's own character while he
  plays it by hand). Pieces in a role store are not worn and wait until they are.
- **The best for the role.** By the stat weights the gear is rated with: the wearer's dungeon role (tank, healer) when
  it has one, else mod-playerbots' weights of its talents (`BotDriver::EnchantScore`, playerbots' reading of an
  enchantment: stats, armour, weapon damage by the weapon's speed, an equip spell, a proc for those who strike).
  Skill, riding and run speed enchantments count nothing. An enchantment goes on only when it is clearly better (5 % and
  half a point of the weights) than the one on the piece.
- **The enchanter** (`Professions::EnchantScrollForGuild`, in `WorkOnProfessions`: after a hand-in at a hub and in the
  profession mode, a look every 10 minutes): of all the pieces, the one its recipes would improve most, with the best
  enchantment it can make now for it (materials in its bags or the guild storage, the rod in its bags), better than what
  is on the piece and than a scroll for it that lies in the guild storage. It takes a vellum out of the guild storage,
  casts the recipe on it (five seconds, `StepEnchanting`), and the scroll goes into the guild storage. A piece a scroll
  is being written for is left to that enchanter for three minutes (two enchanters do not write the same scroll). The
  best it can make now is what the piece gets: when the materials for a better one come in, it writes that one and the
  wearer puts it on over the first.
- **No vellum.** When the best such enchantment lacks only its vellum (neither bags nor storage hold one), it orders
  10 from the guild's scribes as a craft order (`CraftOrders::Add`; the vellum recipe's ink and parchment are theirs).
- **At the level cap** an enchanter on the autopilot that has a scroll to write goes into the profession mode for it
  (as for the endgame consumables), which hands back to the autopilot when there is none left.
- **The wearer** (`Professions::UseEnchantScroll`, in its supply step, a look every 5 minutes): out of a fight, with
  nothing hostile within 30 yd, not in a dungeon or a dungeon run, not on a ship or a flight: the scroll of the guild
  storage that improves one of its pieces most for its role; it takes it out and puts it on (five seconds, it stands
  still; from the saddle it gets off). A scroll that did not take goes back into the guild storage.
- Bot setting `Professions.EnchantScrolls` (921, on; per guild and per bot: off for an enchanter, it writes none; off for
  a bot, it puts none on).
- Lines: `enchants a vellum for the guild (profession mode): Scroll of Enchant Bracer - Superior Stamina for Wartank's
  .. (+9 Stamina instead of none, the best it can make for its role as a tank)`, `made Scroll of
  Enchant .. for the guild: into the guild storage (..)`, `takes a scroll out of the guild storage for its gear: Scroll
  of Enchant .. on its .. (..)`, `put Scroll of Enchant .. of the guild storage on its ..: +9 Stamina (was none)`,
  `orders 10 x Weapon Vellum from the guild's scribes (Priestholy can make it): ..`, `is level 60 (the level cap): it
  can write .. on a vellum for the guild: its order is the profession mode`, and for each vellum out of the storage
  `used 1 x Armor Vellum from the guild storage: it writes Scroll of Enchant .. on it for the guild` (round 232: the
  storage match found 20 vellums gone without a line; the vellum is the spell's target, so no reagent line names it).
- A cast refused because the character was moving (its AI moved it between the stop and the cast, result 51) is tried
  again up to three times with the AI held, instead of ending the job (Healerino's scroll had gone back to the storage).
- No bag sweep while an enchantment is under way (`LootService::SweepBags`): the scroll or vellum lies in the bags
  for the second before the cast, and the half-hourly sweep put Magefrost's Scroll of Enchant Bracer - Greater
  Intellect back into the storage in the second it was taken (round 233; the line said "the scroll is gone", now "the
  scroll left its bags before it was used").
- Not built: enchantments that need materials the guild does not have (Large Brilliant Shards: none in his storage) are
  not gathered or disenchanted for; the head and legs (librams and arcanums, no enchanting recipes).

### Gathering skills keep up with the zone (2026-11-13)

the owner: [quote left out].

`OrderService::CatchUpGathering` (bot setting `Professions.CatchUpGathering`, on; per guild and per bot):

- **When.** On the autopilot (`AUTO`), between two tasks, for the zone the bot quests in or is on its way to (wherever
  it stands), once a minute: for each
  gathering skill of its plan that has work left (Mining, Herbalism, Skinning) what most of the zone asks for is held
  against the bot's skill (`Professions::ZoneGatherUsual`: the middle one of all the zone's mining or herb nodes by the
  skill they need; for Skinning of its skinnable creatures by their level). When the bot's skill is below that, the
  catch-up begins for the skill that is farthest behind: `cannot gather most of what Arathi Highlands has with Mining
  75 (most of it asks for 125): it catches the skill up before it quests on`.
