  **Orange and yellow only** (the owner, 2026-11-14: [quote left out]). The rounds over nodes (a catch-up, the profession mode) take nodes that are orange or yellow for the
  bot's skill: up to 50 points above what a node asks (a point every time up to 25, three times in four up to 50,
  once in four up to 100, then nothing: `Player::UpdateGatherSkill`); the skin hunts likewise for beasts. Green ones
  only where nothing orange or yellow lies within its reach at all; the why line says so. That is Mining 51 to 64:
  copper is green from 51 and tin opens at 65, so a miner there mines green copper or smelts (below). A node beside
  the way while questing (the gather detour) is taken whatever its colour.
  **Smelting.** A miner catching up smelts the guild storage's ore while the smelt is orange or yellow for it (green
  begins halfway between yellow and grey, `Player::UpdateCraftSkill`: Smelt Copper to 46, Tin 65 to 69, Bronze 65 to
  89, Silver to 121, Iron 130 to 144, Gold to 176, Mithril 175 to 201, Thorium 250 to 269), at a forge where it stands,
  else at a forge within 1500 yd it walks to (`smelts for its Mining (catching up)`, `walks to .. to smelt for its
  Mining`); the bars go into the guild storage, where the smiths and engineers take them (gear for the guild makes
  bars from ore as well). The same orange-and-yellow rule holds for smelting at a hub and in the profession mode. The
  storage's reserves hold. New smelts are learned where the bot stands, as the trainer would teach them.
  *Until 2026-11-14 the measure was the zone's lowest node* (`ZoneGatherFloor`, "it can gather nothing there"). A
  Silver Vein (75) stands somewhere in almost every zone up to level 50, so no miner was ever behind: twelve of
  the owner's fourteen miners of level 28 to 45 had a Mining of 44 to 110 (his word on a level-45 warrior with 110 in the
  Searing Gorge, where most ore is Mithril, 175: [quote left out]; to the
  note that about a dozen bots would then go mining for an hour or two before questing on: [quote left out]).
- **What.** The profession mode's gathering for that one skill and nothing else (`RunProfessions` with
  `BotRuntime::catchUp`): rounds over the places of nodes its skill opens and that still teach it, a hunt for skins at
  the place with the most skins to learn from, with journeys (flights) where they are far; vendor trips as usual; its
  goods into the guild storage when the bags fill. No crafting, no quests, no hand-ins meanwhile. The why line reads
  `Catching up on Skinning (27 of 100 for Duskwood): hunting Prowler for skins`.
- **Until.** The skill reaches what most of the zone asks for: `has caught up: <skill> N (was M, T
  min): back to its quests in <zone>`; the bot then picks its zone as usual and quests on. It also ends when the
  bot finds nothing its skill can gather for two minutes (`finds nothing its <skill> N can gather in reach`) or gains
  no point in twenty (`gained no point of ...`): it quests on and the zone is looked at again half an hour later.
  A change of the order ends it.
- **Worth the journey** (the owner, 2026-11-13: [quote left out]). The live server had begun catch-ups for 4 and 6 points (`Skinning 66 (the zone's lowest asks
  for 70)`, `Skinning 94 ... 100`). A catch-up only begins when the skill is at least `Professions.CatchUpMinGap`
  points behind (bot setting 910, default 25); with a smaller gap the bot quests on. A bot that has nothing else to do
  (the hold `Nothing left to do in ..`) catches up any gap.
  Once begun it goes on in one go until what most of the zone asks for is reached, through as many places as that takes. A
  catch-up that was given up is looked at again half an hour later, then one, two and four hours later, since every
  try is a journey there and back; one that succeeded resets that. And because the look is made for the zone the
  bot is on its way to, a bot that was away for a catch-up when the server restarted goes on with it where it
  stands instead of travelling back to its zone first.
- Fishing is not part of it (no node of a zone asks for it; a bot fishes at a hub, and in the profession mode
  travels to water its skill reaches).

### A walk that does not get on: the planner's own steps (2026-11-13)

Live rounds 49 and 50: Warlockdot, then Hunterbm stood at (-3417, -1937, 97.5) in the Wetlands, mounted, "movement 0;
rpg do quest" (and "rpg go camp" on a travel), for five minutes each and again, until the rescue; the second one in
a loop of two and a half minutes. The point is the rim of Whelgar's Excavation. Neither the navmesh nor the mount is
at fault: the core's path finder has a normal path from there to the camp (209 yd), to the raptors in the pit
(125 yd) and so on. The bots come from the camp's quest givers with a target that lies below in the pit or up on the
next hill, and NewRpg's long-distance walk (`MoveFarTo`) heads for the point nearest to its goal and sets that
again every tick; at the rim that point is where the bot stands. A point movement given to a test bot there moved it
half a yard before NewRpg's next tick pulled it back. Routes did not help: their steps were handed to NewRpg too
("has not moved 40 s after taking its route: it walks straight instead").

Now a walk of the planner that has not moved the bot for ten seconds (`WalkTo`: every task walk and every step of a
route; not in a fight, a cast or a flight) is walked by the planner itself from then on (`BotTask::ownSteps`,
`OrderService::OwnStep`): the core's own path to the walk's next point, about 45 yd of it per step as a point
movement, NewRpg resting meanwhile; the ground guard sees each step as before. `does not get on with its walk (N s
at (x, y), D yd to go): the planner walks it along the path itself`. The takeover of an objective walk NewRpg does
not start (above, 25 s) goes straight to this mode. Where the path finder has no way either, the step is refused by
the ground guard or leads nowhere, and the task ends by its stuck rule as before, now within about a minute.
The own steps are a stretch, not the rest of the walk: under them the bot goes on foot (NewRpg rests, and it is
NewRpg that mounts), so after 150 yd NewRpg gets the walk back; a walk that went over to own steps three times keeps
them. The line also shows up in cities (canal bridges and the mage tower of Stormwind), not only at cliffs.
A step waits for the one before it by its spline (`MoveSpline::Finalized`), not by `Player::isMoving`: the stuck lines
of the live test guild (2026-11-25, 20:21 to 20:42: six in 25 minutes, each "moving; movement 0", 31 to 51 own steps begun
and the bot 20 yd on in five minutes) show a bot whose movement flags stayed set with no movement under way, and its
next step waited up to 20 s. The stuck line names the last own step: where to, how long ago, how far the bot is from
it and whether its spline still runs.
mod-playerbots' AI is held while the planner's own steps walk (`BotDriver::PauseAI`, a step's gap at a time, renewed
while the step runs; a fight is not held). On `j5` the debug line of each step (with the setting `GuildAdventure.Debug`:
where from and to, how far along the path, and how the step before ended) showed the own steps of three bots getting 1
to 4 yd each, a step every 2 s (Stonehorn's walk to the tigers of "Tiger Mastery", 21 of 25 steps; Hordeboss's walk past
the Wastewander Bandits of Tanaris, 8 of 15; Priestholy's 5 of 11): the AI went for a creature beside the way, its
movement took the step over a moment after it began, and the check before a pull let the creature go again ("leaves
.. alone on its way"). With the AI held the steps get about 45 yd each.

### Quest items from the guild (2026-11-12, package K2)

A quest that asks for an item the bot does not have was worked only when the planner knew a source in reach (a
creature, an object, a vendor, another quest). Many such items are ordinary goods the guild already owns or can make
(meat for the cooking quests, cloth, bars, an essence): `QuestSupply.cpp`, every 30 s per bot, out of fights
(`GuildAdventure.Quests.ItemsFromGuild`):

1. **Out of the guild storage**: the bot takes what its open quests still miss, where it stands (the storage is
   reached from anywhere, as for the owner). `took 3 x Bear Meat from the guild storage for quest 418 "Thelsamar Blood
   Sausages"`.
2. **From another guild character**: one the AI plays that carries the item, needs it for no quest of its own and
   does not use it itself (playerbots' item usage: its drink, food, ammunition stay) puts it into the storage, and
   step 1 takes it out.
3. **Made by the guild**: when a profession recipe creates the item (3149 items have one), the bot itself or another
   guild character in the world that knows the recipe and has the materials (bags and storage, core patch CP-7)
   crafts what is missing (`CraftService`; the crafter stands still for the casts), and step 2 brings it over on a
   later look.

Only what the storage takes travels this way (no soulbound quest items). **Vendors**: a quest item a vendor sells was
bought "for at most half the bot's money"; it is paid from the guild's budget now (`GuildBudget::Request`, the bot's
own money first, then what the guild hands it within `GuildAdventure.Budget.*`; `Cancel` when nothing was bought).

Seen on the `gaps` instance: three bots took meat and ichor for their cooking quests out of the storage at their first
look; a quest given to a test bot ("Give Gerard a Drink") was served from the storage within a second of the next
look. The first build also took a priest's own drinking water for it, which led to the "does not use it itself"
rule. T1 only: crafting for a quest (no quest with a craftable item was open on the instance) and the vendor purchase
through the budget.

Not built: the auction house (it needs an auctioneer and the mail for the goods), disenchanting for an essence.

### Content lock and the level cap (2026-11-12)

the owner: classic content only while the level cap is 60 (the design log §7 "Levelling gaps", L2). Zones whose level range ends
above the server's `MaxPlayerLevel` are not loaded from `ga_zone_template` (`GuildAdventure.Zones.WithinLevelCap`, default
on; `GuildAdventureMgr::LoadTemplates`): they are missing from AUTO's zone choice, from `LEVEL_ZONE` orders
(`ZONE_INVALID`) and from the addon's zone list. With the cap at 60 that is Hellfire Peninsula (58-63) and the 14 zones
after it; 42 zones stay. Before, a level-59 bot that left the Burning Steppes could pick Hellfire Peninsula through the
Dark Portal (a portal leg counts 6000 yd, the Eastern Plaguelands were farther away). Raising `MaxPlayerLevel` brings the
zones back without any other change.

A bot **at the level cap** gains no experience, so three rules change for it:

- When its zone runs dry it is not bound to the neighbourhood (3000 yd): it goes to the nearest fitting zone with three
  eligible quests, wherever that is.
- It does not grind.
- With no quest left it walks to the nearest inn and waits there ("Level 60 and no quests left for it: Idle at the inn in
  ..."). Every five minutes it checks from the inn whether a zone has a quest to pick up again, and only then leaves.

Professions, dungeons and raids will give capped bots their work later (the owner: [quote left out];
M7, M8).

### Quest planner (port of the wowbot335 WAQ design)

Ported design, not code (the design log §3.3; wowbot335 `TaskRegister`, `QuestTaskRank`, `EligibilityFilter`,
`BlacklistManager`, `WaqTaskState`):

- **Tasks.** Every planning step enumerates: a *turn-in* per completed quest in the log (nearest ender the bot can talk
  to in the target zone, up to 2500 yd, or within 400 yd in any zone; enders farther out are *errands*, below), an
  *objective* per open objective of the quests in the log (nearest spawn of the creature/game object, or of a
  creature/game object that drops the quest item, **inside the target zone**; else the quest POI if it lies in the
  zone; else a spawn up to 1500 yd outside the zone, when it is not more than three levels above the bot: targets just
  across the border), a *purchase* for an objective item nothing in reach drops but a vendor within 3000 yd sells
  (for at most half the bot's money), and a *pickup* per eligible quest of the zone (nearest giver).
- **Item sources** (`WorldIndex::IndexItemSources`): for every item a quest asks for, the creatures and game objects
  whose loot holds it, directly or through one reference table. Rows flagged for the quest (`QuestRequired`) count at
  any chance; ordinary loot (cooking meat, "Flask of Oil", "Murloc Eye") from a 10 % chance on, so the nearest source
  is one worth killing. An item that lies inside another item (`item_loot_template`: Tallonkai's Jewel in the Gnarlpine
  Necklace) has the sources of that container, and the planner opens such a container when it is in the bags
  (`OpenQuestContainers`; locked ones are left). 2615 items have sources on the 3.3.5a world database (2174 with
  quest-flagged direct rows alone).
- **Items another quest rewards** (the chapters of "The Green Hills of Stranglethorn", the antidote of "Need for a
  Cure"): the planner picks that quest up, wherever its giver stands within 2500 yd, before it looks for a vendor.
- What is still without a source is listed in [quest-item-gaps.md](quest-item-gaps.md) with how the game hands each
  item out: 119 objectives of levelling quests, 47 of them made by using an item (the quest interactions), 10 crafted
  with a profession, the rest low drop chances, fishing, skinning and scripts.
- **Eligibility** comes from the core (`Player::CanTakeQuest`: level, class, race, previous quests and chains,
  exclusive groups, skill, reputation, daily/weekly/seasonal) plus `Player::CanAddQuest` (log space) plus NewRpg's own
  rules (`IsQuestWorthDoing`: not grey, not repeatable, not seasonal; `IsQuestCapableDoing`: at most 3 levels above,
  normal type, solo) — the same rules NewRpg applies at the giver, so the bot never walks to a giver that will not hand
  the quest out. Plus the bot's block list.
- **Ranking** (`QuestTaskRank`): nearby pickups (giver within 60 yd, at least 3 free log slots) first; then turn-ins
  and objectives together, nearest first; far pickups last (only with room in the log). Ties: more progress, then the
  lower quest id.
- **Failure rules** (wowbot335 A21, table `ga_bot_quest_block`): a quest fails when NewRpg gives up on it (no progress
  at its spot for 5 minutes), when its giver does not hand it out or its ender does not take it within 45 s at the NPC.
  A giver or ender the bot cannot get to, **or that is not there** (never in sight during those 45 s: dead, respawning,
  on patrol), is no failure: it is skipped for 20 minutes (the quest stays in the log; review H4). A giver or ender
  that was in sight but did not hand out or take the quest is skipped for only 2 minutes (in a start zone one giver
  often holds every quest: a 20-minute break left Hunterbm idle in Shadowglen on 2026-11-12), and in the bot's first
  minute in the world such a miss is no failure at all: the bot tries again at once. The activity log records what the
  bot and the NPC looked like at that moment (§ Activity log). The first failure
  abandons a quest in progress and allows one retry; the second blocks it for that bot for good. **A completed quest is
  never abandoned:** after two failed turn-ins it stays in the log and the planner leaves it alone (the owner can turn it
  in when playing the bot).
- **Death rule** (new, wowbot335 has no counterpart): three deaths at the same quest's objectives within 30 minutes
  set the quest aside until the bot gains a level or 30 minutes pass ("Too dangerous for now: … (3 deaths); doing
  something else first"); the planner works other quests or grinds meanwhile. A quest set aside twice counts as a
  failure (A21: abandoned with one retry, blocked the second time). Three deaths during one grind task set the grind
  spot (100 yd around it) aside the same way; three deaths on the way to an NPC (giver, ender, vendor, trainer, flight
  master) skip that NPC for 30 minutes, and three deaths during a travel count like a stuck travel. A death does not end
  the task: releasing the spirit and walking back
  are not jumps, the bot carries on where it was, and its why line comes back after the revival. `.ga bot plan` shows
  the deaths of the current task and what is set aside.
- **Corpse camping**: a bot that dies a second time within 10 minutes and 40 yd of its last death (it revived among the
  mobs that killed it) takes the spirit healer at the graveyard instead of walking back: the module sends the client's
  `CMSG_SPIRIT_HEALER_ACTIVATE` through the bot's session, so the usual price applies (resurrection sickness, 25 %
  durability loss); below 40 % durability the bot runs back to its corpse instead. The ghost steps across the graveyard to the healer with a short hop. Before: a level-11 Night Elf
  revived at its corpse on the Darkshore beach and died again four times in ten minutes.
- **Grind gaps**: no quest task left → grind at the densest cluster of fitting mobs (level −3…+1, not friendly, not
  elite, drops loot) within 1200 yd inside the zone.

### Quest interactions

NewRpg walks to a quest's spot and lets the grind and loot strategies work; it never uses a quest item, casts a spell on a
quest NPC, uses a quest object or walks into an exploration trigger, so such objectives failed twice and were blocked
(the owner's test run, 2026-11-12: "Rescue the Survivors!", "Inoculation", "Healing the Lake", "Crown of the Earth",
"Garments of the Light"). For those the planner does the work itself: an `interact` task
(`QuestInteraction.cpp` plans it from static data, `OrderInteraction.cpp` carries it out).

| Plan | When (resolved per quest objective and team, cached) | What the bot does |
|---|---|---|
| use item | the quest's start item or a source item (`ItemDrop`) has an on-use spell that names the objective: kill credit for it, a spell condition naming the target creature or object, a "near" condition or a spell focus; for an item objective any item whose on-use spell creates it (the quest's own first, then the rest: handed out by the giver, from a container, from an earlier quest), the first the bot carries with all the spell's reagents | uses the item like a client (`CMSG_USE_ITEM`): on the creature or object the conditions name (Inoculating Crystal on a Nestlewood Owlkin), next to the object of a "near" condition (Neutralizing Agent at the Irradiated Power Crystal; every other try names the object as target), at a spell focus within its range (Crystal Phial at the Shadowglen Moonwell); where it stands when the spell needs no target and no place (binding pages, combining a charm's halves); on a corpse when the spell's conditions want a dead target (capture vessels, ooze jars: it attacks a living one of those creatures first) |
| cast spells | a creature objective that killing cannot credit: friendly or not attackable, with a script (C++ or SmartAI), no quest item | casts its helpful spells that can target another creature (heals first, then buffs, at most a dozen) on it until the credit comes (Gift of the Naaru on a Draenei Survivor; Lesser Heal and Power Word: Fortitude on Guard Roberts) |
| use object | a game object objective without a quest item; an item objective that only game objects hold, with no lock or an "open"-type lock (no lockpicking, herbalism, mining, fishing, inscription, no key) | a locked object with the character's open-lock spell for its lock type ("Opening", instant, as the gathering in passing), any other like a client (`CMSG_GAMEOBJ_USE`; the core's object use does nothing for a chest); takes the loot of a chest and closes it (`DoLootRelease`); a chest that had nothing for the bot although it still lacks the item it came for is set back to `GO_READY`, so its next opening makes the loot anew (an opened chest keeps its loot, and a character that was not there when it was made gets no quest item from it: Hunterbm opened Kerlonian's Chest three times for nothing on the integration server) |
| explore | the quest has the exploration flag and an `areatrigger_involvedrelation` row | walks into the trigger and reports it like a client (`CMSG_AREATRIGGER`; a bot has no client that would) |
| provoke | a friendly objective creature with a SmartAI script that has a gossip choice and, in the script or its timed action lists, a faction hostile to players or an attack; with a follow action and a "distance to creature" event, the place where it turns | talks to it like a client (`QuestEvents::Talk`, the gossip choice of the script), leads it to its place if it follows (Travel profile, `WalkTo`, waits when it falls 20 yd behind), and fights it when it turns; the kill gives the credit. The Threshwackonator 4100 ("Gyromast's Revenge": turn the key, it follows to Gelkak Gyromast and attacks there); the only other script of this kind up to level 60 is the Deserter Agitator ("Traitors Among Us", a talk that turns some of them hostile, no follow) |

The long walk goes like an objective's: `WalkTo` (the road map's route when there is one) and the gate of task walks
(`LeaveDangerousWalk`, the spot's own creatures not counted): a spot behind a group the bot cannot take or creatures far
above it waits `Walks.PostponeMinutes` (Hunterbm swam through five Greymist murlocs off Auberdine on NewRpg's straight
way to the Cliffspring River Waterfall and died; with the change it walked over land and filled the tube). Spell foci
without a spawn are not places to stand ("Bank" shares that focus and named the plan).
The task walks to the nearest spawn of what the plan acts on (else the objective's POI), takes over 25 yd from it (the
*hold* profile: NewRpg stands down, the bot fights back when attacked), steps into range (line of sight only to creatures),
acts, and waits 6 s for the credit (scripts react after the cast). A creature with a gossip menu or quest-giver flag gets no cast-spells plan (that is a "speak with" or escort quest).
A creature or object acted on is not chosen again by the
task; the next spawn comes when nothing is left in sight (a creature is waited for 45 s, an absent object only 5 s:
objects do not walk). The objective's POI is used only when the target has no spawn at all, and a POI spot that did not
work is set aside as an area: with the only spawn set aside (a chest waiting to respawn), the POI next to it sent the
bot straight back every few seconds (Hunterbm and Duduheal at the Chest of the Raven Claw, integration server,
2026-11-12). A use where the bot stands (combine pages) is not ended for a place set aside: its spot is the bot itself,
and the planner chose it again at once (a druid began and ended "The Lost Pages" every 6 s for half an hour in a place
it had set aside, 2026-11-25). Five acts in a row without progress (cast spells: one more than it has spells) are an A21 failure, a
target it cannot get close to in 3 minutes is skipped for 2. Deaths count as at a normal objective. Each act and its
result go into the activity log (`activity: <bot> quest <id>: used item <item> (check <SpellCastResult>) on <target> ... progress before the act`, `cast
<spell> (result ...)`, `used object, looted <n>`, `entered area trigger`, `progress <have>/<need>`, `interaction failed`).
One item for several creature objectives (Umi's Mechanical Yeti on Legacki, Sprinkle and Quixxil, "Are We There,
Yeti?") acts on each objective's own creature; before that every objective listed all three and the one for Sprinkle used
the item on Legacki again (gaps thread's level sweep). Every act gets the bot off its mount first (item spells and casts
fail mounted). A spawn's spot counts as reached only within 10 yd of its height, and a target more than 10 yd above or below is walked to
through NewRpg's path instead of a point movement: Warlockdot stood 23 yd above the crates of "Filthy Paws" in the Silver
Stream Mine and the straight move down was refused by the ground guard until "cannot get close" (integration server,
2026-11-12). A POI spot's height is the surface (`GetHeight` from above), so it has no height rule.

**A follower's aid.** Some NPCs that follow the character for a quest have to be woken or called back with a quest item:
Kerlonian Evershade falls asleep every 25-90 s (Horn of Awakening, "The Sleeper Has Awakened"), Ringo faints (Spraggle's
Canteen, "A Little Help From My Friends"), Shay Leafrunner wanders off every minute (Shay's Bell, "Wandering Shay").
`QuestInteraction::GetFollowerAid` finds the item among the quest's start, source and required items whose on-use spell
names that NPC in its conditions (all three have an implicit-target condition on the NPC's entry); `NeedsAid` says when:
the NPC sleeps (stand state) or no longer follows anyone, outside a fight, for at least 2 s. `OrderService::AidFollower`,
called by the lead step of a quest event (OrderEvents.cpp, the "lead" kind), first opens the chest the item comes from
when the bot lacks it and the chest is in sight (the horn and the bell lie in a chest next to the NPC, as the quest's
item objective: `Resolve`), then walks into the spell's range, gets off its mount (item spells fail mounted), holds the
bot still for the cast (up to 4.5 s) and uses the item, again after 8 s if the NPC did not recover (Shay's Bell has a
cooldown: SPELL_FAILED_NOT_READY once or twice, then it rings), at most six times in a row. Log lines: `quest <id>: opened <chest>
for <item> (...), looted <n>, has it yes`, `quest <id>: used <item> on <npc> (<yd>, asleep|not following; check <result>)`,
`quest <id>: <npc> goes on after <n> use(s) of <item>`.

**Objects at their own interact distance** (2026-11-13, a live finding of the squads thread): an object to open or use counts as in reach only by the core's own test (`Spell::CheckRange` -> `GameObject::IsAtInteractDistance`: the player inside the object's model box grown by the opening spell's range, 5 yd, its height included), not by `GetDistance` against the plan's range. Before, a bot stopped 3 to 4 yd from an object below or above it (an Ancient Statuette on the floor of the Zoram Strand, Sand Pears up in their trees, a Fel Cone, a Sack of Oats) and the open-lock spell failed with `SPELL_FAILED_OUT_OF_RANGE` (97), six times on 2026-11-12/13; Mageyo tried the statuette for six minutes (`OrderInteraction.cpp`, the last-yards step). An object the bot cannot get inside that box of is left after the approach's minute, as before.

**Credit from the kill of other creatures** (2026-11-13, two Dustwallow quests found by the gaps thread in round 85): some objectives name a credit creature that stands nowhere, and the credit comes when other creatures die. The crocolisks of "The Grimtotem Weapon" (11169) cast "Captured Totem Test Credit" (a kill credit for the Captured Totem, 23811) on their killer when they die, the Risen Husks and Spirits of "What's Haunting Witch Hill?" (11180) "Witch Hill Information Credit" (the Restless Apparition, 23861). `QuestInteraction::CreditSources` reads once which creatures give which credit: creature_template KillCredit1/2 and SmartAI death events (and the events linked to them) that call `KILLEDMONSTER` or cast a spell with a kill credit effect. The planner adds those creatures' spawns to the objective's (a kill objective, as for an item they drop), and no interaction plan is made for such a credit creature. Before, Retadin walked "the quest area" of 11169 for eleven minutes with nothing to kill, and the friendly, short-lived Restless Apparition got a "help with spells" plan that two bots waited ten minutes on ("no target in sight").

**A creature to weaken first** (2026-11-13, same round): the Sturdy Rope of "Raptor Captor" (11146) captures only a raptor below 20 % health (its spell's TargetAuraState, `AURA_STATE_HEALTHLESS_20_PERCENT`); Duduheal used it about a hundred times on raptors at full health, `SPELL_FAILED_TARGET_AURASTATE` (check 111). A use-item plan whose spell wants its target below 20 or 35 % health (`InteractionPlan::weakenBelow`) is worked as a fight: the bot attacks the creature, the AI fights it down to the line plus 30 %, then the AI is held and only white blows land (its spells would kill it), and below the line the bot stops attacking and uses the item at once; the AI stays held 6 s for the cast and the credit the creature casts itself (the raptor's "Raptor Capture Credit" takes 4 s). The planner does not run a task in a fight, so this step (`OrderService::StepWeaken`) is called from the fight branch of the bot's update and four times a second beside the pull check: once a second a warrior took a raptor from 40 % to dead between two looks. Log lines: `quest <id>: attacks <creature> to weaken it below <n>% health for ...`, `quest <id>: used item <item> on <creature> at <n>% health (...)`.

**An item that brings the objective's creature** (2026-11-14, the owner's report from Dustwallow Marsh): "Cleansing Witch Hill" (11183) wants the Witchbane Torch lit at the end of the Swamplight dock (spell focus 1464, a send-event); Zelfrax (23864) then comes along a path and is the objective, and he has no spawn. Without a plan the bot stood in "the quest area" for 314 s, NewRpg gave the quest up and the bot took it again (Nochnwar, a loop). The quest's own item whose spell needs a spell focus, sends an event or summons the objective creature, for a creature without a spawn, is a use-item plan (`InteractionPlan::bringsCreature`) where the spell wants it (at the focus, else the quest's POI); the result of the use is waited for a minute (the creature walks up), and the AI fights it.

**Corpse items: the kill first, walked to** (same report): "The Essence of Enmity" (11161) wants Brogg's Totem used on a slain Firemane. The "kill one first" step called `Attack()` without walking to the creature, so Retadin "attacked" a Firemane Ash Tail once a second for four minutes without a fight. It walks up now (`MoveChase`), and a creature no fight comes of within 30 s is passed for the next (`quest <id>: no fight with <creature> after 30 s: the next one`); the weaken step's own attack does the same.

**Keys** (2026-11-14, the owner: [quote left out]): the Grimtotem Key's spell opens a lock on a game object (its explicit target), and the Theramore Prisoner its conditions name is the one set free; used on the prisoner it failed with `SPELL_FAILED_BAD_TARGETS` (12). An item whose spell has an open-lock effect and wants a game object as target goes on a game object whose lock names that key (`QuestInteraction::KeyObjects`: the Blackhoof Cage), from inside its interact distance with the key's spell range. Without the key in the bags the plan is not usable, and when creatures drop it (here a quest drop of the Grimtotems, 20 %) the planner sends the bot to them first (`BotTask::fetchItem`: the task ends with `has the item for its interaction`), then to a cage; each key is used up, so this repeats per prisoner. A key of the quest for an objective creature that has no spawn is a plan of its own with the object's use bringing the creature (`bringsCreature`): "Spirits of Stonemaul Hold" (11159) opens Ogre Remains with the Energized Totem, their trap summons a Stonemaul Spirit, the AI puts it to rest (Retadin had ridden up and down "the quest area", the owner, 2026-11-14). While the result of such a use is waited for, the bot attacks the objective creature once it stands in sight (`quest <id>: attacks <creature> its item brought`): a Stonemaul Spirit stands and talks and attacks nobody, and Retadin stood beside it until the owner took over and hit it.

**Channels** (2026-11-14): some items start a channel whose end gives the credit: the Ooze Buster of "Corrosion Prevention" (11174) casts Ooze Channel on the ooze for 5 s (cancelled by the caster's moving), whose end kills the ooze and gives the credit. A step or another cast of the bot's AI breaks it; Warlockdot fought and walked through every channel after its first one (1 of 10 in 7 minutes on the integration server). While a channel the act started runs, the AI is held and the bot stands, out of a fight and in one (the act's line ends with `it channels`). The Ooze Buster also needs the caster within 40 yd of a Zeppelin Power Core (its script check `spell_ooze_zap`: the aura Energized!, which the cores give for 3 s at a time); out of it the use does nothing, although the core's check of the cast beforehand says yes. Such script rules no data names are a hand list in `QuestInteraction.cpp` (`NearRules`: spell, creature, yards; `InteractionPlan::nearCreature`): only targets near such a creature are taken (spots too), the bot stands on the line from that creature to the target, 8 yd from the creature and within the item's range of the target, and it acts only with the creature's aura on it: without it, it walks up to the creature itself and waits there up to 15 s, else the next target (the cores lie inside the wreck and their periodic spell wants a line of sight).

**Under water** (2026-11-14): "Pearl Diving" (705) opens Giant Clams on the sea floor of Stranglethorn, 12 to 110 yd down, 20 of 80 spawned at a time. Three things kept the bots at 0 of 9 pearls (18 tasks, 24 minutes on the integration server that day): the spot's walk went to NewRpg, which stays at the surface ("is stuck ... 42 yd above the floor", "spot not reached"); the look for a target reached 60 yd from the surface, short of the deep clams; and a chest was taken only when the core activates it for the quest, which it does only for loot flagged as quest loot (the Blue Pearl drops at 100 % without the flag). Now a spot or target under the water the bot swims in, within 60 yd, is dived to straight through the water (a point movement without a path), the look reaches the spot's depth below the bot, and a chest needs no quest activation. Coming up for air is the planner's breath rule (the gaps work).

**Full bags** (2026-11-14): a chest opened for an item objective with no room for the item gives nothing (the loot window opens, nothing is taken) and counts as used, so the task ends "nothing left to act on here" and starts again at the next spawn; Magefrost did that 16 times in a round at the Wyrmtails of "Catch a Dragon by the Tail" with 0 free bag slots (its bags were full of green gear the bag sweep keeps). Before opening such a chest the bot checks room for the quest's item; none: the bag sweep, and still none: the quest waits a quarter of an hour (a level-up lifts it) with the line `no room in its bags for <item> ... the quest waits a quarter of an hour`. The use of an item that makes an item with no room for it waits the same way (it used to restart every 30 s).

**A creature an item brings, an item its use uses up** (2026-11-24, thread "Testgilde spielen"). "Echeyakee" (881)
asks for Echeyakee's Hide; Echeyakee has no spawn, the Horn of Echeyakee summons him beside his lair (its spell sends
event 2980, a summon of 3475 for three minutes). An item objective whose item no creature with a spawn drops looks at
the creatures that drop it; when the quest's own item summons one of them, or needs a spell focus or sends an event and
only one creature drops it, it is a use-item plan "use X next to Y and fight C for I" (`InteractionPlan::brought`), and
the bot attacks what it brought. Before, the quest went to "the quest area" and NewRpg gave up after five minutes. The
horn is used up by its use (charges -1): the minute for the creature runs on without the item (the task had ended
"the quest item is gone"; the bot met Echeyakee anyway at the quest area). Quests whose sort is a dungeon's area
("Trouble at the Docks" (959): Mad Magglish in the Wailing Caverns) get no objective task outside an instance; the
test guild's leader had walked about the Barrens for five minutes for it fourteen times.

**An aura on the target** (2026-11-24, thread "Testgilde spielen"): a spell's conditions can ask for an aura on its target. The Foreman's Blackjack of "Lazy Peons" (5441) wakes a Lazy Peon only while it sleeps (condition: aura 17743 on the target); the bot took the nearest peon, awake or not, its use failed with `SPELL_FAILED_BAD_TARGETS` (check 12), and the test guild's druid needed nine minutes and six ended tasks ("nothing left to act on here") for five peons. The plan keeps the auras the target must have and must not have (`InteractionPlan::targetAuras / targetNoAuras`, from `CONDITION_AURA` with condition target 1), and the bot takes only a creature that fits.

**A creature an object releases** (2026-11-14, the maintainers: death knights stood in undying fights in the Blasted Lands): "The Stones That Bind Us" (2681) counts the Servants of Razelikh, Grol, Allistarj and Sevine. Each is invincible at 1 HP; its SmartAI makes the Stone of Binding of its master selectable within 40 yd when it falls to 5 % (`SMART_EVENT_HEALTH_PCT`, `SMART_ACTION_REMOVE_GO_FLAG` `GO_FLAG_NOT_SELECTABLE` on `SMART_TARGET_GAMEOBJECT_DISTANCE`), and the Stone's own script kills the Servant when used, the credit to the bot that fights it. The bots fought each Servant down to 1 HP and stood there. The plan comes from those script rows, not a hand list (`QuestInteraction::PlanReleaseObject`, `InteractionPlan::beatEntries` and `beatBelow`): out of a fight the bot attacks the nearest free Servant of the objective within sight (the line `attacks <servant> to bring <servant> below 5% health and use Stone of Binding`, 30 s per Servant), a chase that stands still (a bot on a ledge above its Servant, out of its sight) becomes a walk to the Servant's own place after 4 s; in the fight (`StepWeaken`, from the fight branch and the 250 ms loop) a Servant of the plan within 40 yd at or below its line makes the bot stop attacking, walk to the nearest Stone of that entry within 40 yd of the Servant and use it (`uses Stone of Binding on <servant> at 1 health`). The behaviour thread's rule for undying fights (a foe held at 1 HP for 15 s ends the fight) must leave such a Servant alone while the bot's task is that interaction.

### Grey and failed quests (2026-11-13)

the owner, 2026-11-13: [quote left out] (with a quest log of 19 quests, eight of them
grey, one finished and one failed).

Every 20 seconds, alive and out of a fight, whatever its order, an AI-played guild character looks through its quest
log (`OrderService::CareForStaleQuests`):

- **A grey quest is abandoned.** Grey as the client paints it: the quest's level is at or below the level from
  which creatures are grey for the character (level 25: quests up to level 18). A quest without a level of its own
  is never grey. Bot setting `Quests.AbandonGrey` (on; per guild and per bot).
- **A finished grey quest** is kept while one of its enders is within 1000 yd (the planner's turn-in or an errand
  next door hands it in), and abandoned otherwise; never worth a trip.
- **A failed quest** (a timer that ran out, an escort that died while the bot was elsewhere) is given back, grey or
  not and whatever the setting says: it stayed in the log as failed for good. It goes through `FailQuest`, so the
  quest is taken again at its giver once; a second failure blocks it for that bot (the A21 rule).
- Not the quest of the running task or of the errand under way: that ends first.

Each one leaves a line; the game's own rule takes the quest's items. Nothing else is deleted.

```
activity: Hunterbm abandons quest 2459 "Ferocitas the Dream Eater": grey at level 21 (a level-8 quest)
activity: Hunterbm abandons quest 2438 "The Emerald Dreamcatcher": grey at level 21 (a level-6 quest); it was finished, but its hand-in is more than 1000 yd away
activity: Hunterbm abandons quest 5321 "The Sleeper Has Awakened": it failed (a timer, an escort); it is taken again at its giver, once
```

The planner did not work grey quests before either (`CollectLogTasks` skips what mod-playerbots holds not worth
doing: more than four levels below the character, a little wider than grey), nor take them; they only left the log
when it ran short (the quest log care).

### Quests the bots leave alone (2026-11-12)

NewRpg accepts every quest a giver offers that passes `Player::CanTakeQuest`, also the ones the planner has no way to
finish. Each of them used to cost a bot two rounds of five to eight minutes before the A21 rule blocked it for that bot,
and the next bot paid again (the owner's run of 2026-11-12: 11 objectives ended with "NewRpg gave up", 30 % of the logged
task time). `QuestSupport` now says "leave it" up front, from three sources:

| Verdict | Source | Example |
|---|---|---|
| listed | `ga_quest_block_template` in the world database: a hand-checked list with a reason per quest. Add a row to keep bots off a quest, delete one to let them try. A row with a `setting` applies only while that boolean module setting is on (a setting that does not exist counts as off): the 97 class quests whose reward `ClassAbilities` grants directly (pet taming, demons, stances, Bear Form, Redemption, totems) carry `ClassAbilities.Enable` | under water (The Vile Reef), needs bought items (Bartolo's Yeti Fur Cloak), the ender is out of reach (Delivery to Archmage Xylem), the attunement to Naxxramas, a level-80 raid in this client (9121-9123, 9378) |
| scripted event | the quest has the special flag "exploration or event", no area trigger to walk into and no quest item to use: it completes through a script the planner cannot trigger | escorts, defence events, talks with choices |
| learned | the planner blocked the quest with "no progress" for `GuildAdventure.Quests.LearnedBlockBots` (2) different guild bots (`ga_bot_quest_block`) | whatever the bots keep failing at |

The veto sits in the core's `Player::CanTakeQuest` (core patch CP-9, `PlayerScript::OnPlayerCanTakeQuest`) and applies
only to characters the AI plays (a bot, a watched character, a planned leader): NewRpg does not take such a quest, the
planner does not walk to its giver, and the zone choice does not count it. A character its owner plays takes any quest.
A quest that is already in the log stays there; the planner has no task for it and the quest log care (below) drops it
when the log fills up. `GuildAdventure.Quests.Filter = 0` switches the veto off.

`.ga admin quests` prints the counts and the learned quests; `.ga admin quests forget` deletes every learned block
(`ga_bot_quest_block` and the learned verdicts). Run it after the planner got new abilities, so the bots try again.

### Escorts (2026-11-12)

the owner: [quote left out]. An escort quest completes through a script: the quest giver walks a
waypoint path once the quest is taken, and the quest is done when it arrives (and failed when the player falls more
than about 60 yd behind, or the NPC dies).

- **Which quests.** `QuestSupport` takes a pure script-event quest (§ Quests the bots leave alone) for an escort when
  its giver has a waypoint path: an entry in `script_waypoint` (C++ escort scripts) or a SmartAI "waypoint start"
  action (in its script or one of its timed action lists). 84 quests on the 3.3.5a world database, about 40 of them in
  classic zones ("Protecting the Shipment", "Missing In Action", "Free From the Hold", the OOX robots). They are no
  longer vetoed; of the other script events (270 then) those with a plan are played, see the next section.
  `GuildAdventure.Quests.Escorts = 0` puts the escorts back with them.
- **The task.** An escort quest in the log yields a task *escort* that ranks before everything else, nearby pickups
  included: the NPC walks off the moment the quest is taken. NewRpg takes quests in passing, so any other task ends
  when an escort NPC next to the bot starts to move. The bot follows with the core's follow movement (behind the NPC,
  at its speed; NewRpg rests): NewRpg's own walk goes to where the NPC was and falls behind until the script fails the
  quest, which is what happened in the first try. Fights are playerbots'; the follow is set again after each.
- **Ends.** Quest complete: done, the turn-in is ordinary quest work (or an errand). Quest failed, the NPC out of sight
  for 45 s, no start within 90 s (the quest was in the log from an earlier try and the NPC stands at its spot), or 25
  minutes gone: a failure in the sense of the A21 rule, which gives the quest back so it can be taken afresh once, and
  blocks it for that bot the second time. A failed escort quest found in the log is given back the same way.
- **What the event brought and that waits** (the owner, 2026-11-25: [quote left out]). An escort's or a stay or lead event's
  creatures that a script summoned or made hostile (a faction other than their template's), within 30 yd of the NPC
  (or the bot), not in a fight, hostile and in sight: the bot attacks them (`PickWaitingEventFoe`, `DefendWard`;
  activity line `attacks <creature> ..., which its quest's event brought beside <NPC> and which waits to be attacked`).
  They count on a player's coming into their aggro range, which this server halves (`Rate.Creature.Aggro 0.5`). Found
  in the world database (SmartAI summons without "attack the invoker" whose own script has no attack, quests up to
  level 60): "Questioning Reethe" (1273, Ogron's ambush: Paval Reethe makes Private Hallan, two Theramore Skirmishers
  and Lieutenant Caldwell hostile), "The Exorcism", "Mana Surges" and "Cleansing of the Orb of Orahil" (1955, 1957,
  4961, Tabetha's Mana Surges), "This Is Going to Be Hard" (778, Fam'retor Guardian), "Counterattack!" (4021, the
  Kolkar waves), "Get Me Out of Here!" (6132, Maraudine Wranglers), "Wait for Sirra to Finish" (401, the enraged
  mounts). Not counted: summons whose script attacks or walks a path to the players (the Anvilrage of "What Is Going
  On?", Galak Assassins, the Spitelash of "A Crew Under Fire") and C++ escort scripts.
  For these quests the world database is changed too (the owner: [quote left out]; module SQL `ga_quest_aggro.sql`, db-world): each such creature attacks the
  nearest player within 40 yd (60 for the Kolkar waves) when it is summoned, and Ogron's ambush when Paval Reethe's
  script makes it hostile (data 2 2 from his list); so they attack a player who plays by hand as well. Rows with
  ids 50 and up; "Wait for Sirra to Finish" (401) is left as it is (its mounts belong to the sides' factions).
- **The bot stays beside its ward.** While its escort NPC is alive within 30 yd, the bot does not leave a fight above
  35 % health (`WardFightsBeside` in `FightEscape.cpp`: the decision to leave and the keep-away from a creature far
  above it), and the check before a pull lets it attack a creature beside the NPC whatever the count (Ogron's ambush is
  four at once: "does not pull Lieutenant Caldwell ...: the fight would cost it about 165%" had ended the escort). The
  set-off rule of an escort skips a quest that is blocked for the bot (its NPC walking off began the blocked escort
  again and again). On the j5 instance (2026-11-25) a level-38 warrior held the ambush down to 28 % health, Caldwell
  at 3 %, left, came back after its rest, won the fight against the two that were left and finished the escort
  (`ends escort quest 1273 after 15 s: escort done`); before, it left at 84 % health. The same holds for a quest event
  the bot defends at its NPC or leads an NPC through (kinds stay and lead, the plan's NPC): Thrakgar, a level-29 shaman,
  left the first wave of three Galak Assassins at Kanati Greycloud ("Protect Kanati Greycloud", 4966) at 94 % health,
  was netted, could not shake them off and died 9 s after the event had ended (2026-11-26). Whether a bot should take
  such an event at all (its waves judged by the bot's own fights, as `Risk::JudgeSummon` does for an item) is open: the
  quest's waves come from the giver's SmartAI action list on its accept.

### Quest events: talks, events at the giver, NPCs to lead (2026-11-12)

The other script events. For three kinds the world database says what a player has to do, and the planner does it
(`QuestEvents` reads, `OrderEvents.cpp` plays; `GuildAdventure.Quests.Events = 0` leaves them alone again):

- **How credit is traced.** Every SmartAI row that credits a quest ("area explored or event happens", "group event
  happens", "killed monster") is followed back to the events that start it: through its links and the timed action
  lists it sits in, through "set data" (to the rows that set that data on the creature) and through summons (the
  death of a summoned creature leads to whoever summons it), and through what the script itself brings about: "text
  over" back to the row that says the text, "has aura" back to the row that casts it (2026-11-14). Scripts of
  creatures, game objects and area triggers; 53 805 rows, 75 ms at startup.
- **Talk** (109 plans): a gossip choice, or just greeting the NPC or game object, is at the root. For the quest's event
  ("Hidden Enemies": Neeru Fireblade, "The Smoldering Ruins of Thaurissan": the royal historian, the crystal pylons of
  Un'Goro) or for a creature credit of an objective ("Lost in Battle": the corpse; that objective is then not one to
  kill). The bot walks to it, greets it like a client (`CMSG_GOSSIP_HELLO`, a game object is used) and picks options
  until the choice is made: on each menu the option whose action menu leads to the choice (`gossip_menu_option`), so
  conditions and menus the core builds are respected. Then it waits up to two minutes for the credit (scripts hold
  speeches or send enemies first, which the bot fights); three talks without credit are a failure "no progress". A
  talk partner within 500 yd is visited wherever the bot is (the quest giver itself, an NPC in the same city); farther
  ones only as quest work of the target zone, within 2500 yd. *A credit per partner* (the objective counts more than
  one: six Theramore Guards): the wait for a credit is 25 s, the partner that gave it is left alone for three minutes
  and the nearest one not yet asked is next; eight partners in a row with nothing to say are the failure.
- **Stay** (101 plans, 14 in classic zones): the quest giver's own script reacts to "quest accepted" and the quest has
  nothing else to do: "One Shot. One Kill." (three waves on Sentinel Aynasha), "A Rogue's Deal" and "The Missing
  Diplomat" (a brawl with the giver or a man next to it), "Death From Below", "Gerenzo's Orders" (a speech). The bot
  stays within 10 yd of the giver and attacks what attacks either of them, and the giver itself once it turned
  hostile (`BotDriver::Attack`, since playerbots only defends the bot and its group). Six minutes without credit are a
  failure "no progress".
- **Lead** (2 plans): the quest giver follows whoever took the quest until it stands next to another NPC ("Mist":
  SmartAI "follow" with an end creature and an event credit; "Tooga's Quest" from the hand list). The bot walks to that
  NPC, waits when the follower is more than 25 yd behind, fights for it, and stands right next to the end NPC until
  the credit comes.
- **Clear** (1 plan, hand list only): the creature of an objective shows itself once the place around its spawn is
  empty of enemies ("WANTED: Murkdeep!"); the bot clears 80 yd around the spawn, stays and fights what comes
  (§ After the sweep).
- **Enter** (3 plans): an area trigger's script is at the root ("Resupplying the Excavation": the trigger at the
  dwarves on the road sets data on Huldar, who summons the traitor, whose death credits the quest). The bot walks
  into the trigger, sends what a client sends there (`CMSG_AREATRIGGER`), stays and attacks whatever fights next to
  it; six minutes without credit are a failure "no progress".
- **Followers that need help** ("The Sleeper Has Awakened", "A Little Help From My Friends", "Wandering Shay": the
  follower falls asleep, faints or wanders off and wants the quest's item used on it): three rows of the hand list,
  and the lead task calls `OrderService::AidFollower` of the quest interactions when that exists (it compiles with
  and without them). A follower that follows, or has left its spot, shows that its event runs: after a rest, an
  escape, a fight or a jump the lead goes on instead of giving the quest back.
- **Fresh and stale.** Stay and Lead events start the moment the quest is taken, and NewRpg takes quests in passing.
  The planner watches the quest log: a quest of these kinds that appears in it ends the running task ("a quest event
  started") and gets its event task before anything else is planned, also outside the target zone. One that has been
  in the log for longer (taken before a death, a restart, a rescue) has no event running: the bot walks back to the
  giver, gives the quest back and takes it afresh, once; the second time it is a failure.
- **What the trace cannot see** is listed by hand in `ga_quest_event_template` (world database): events of C++ scripts
  ("Pyrewood Ambush": stay; "Tooga's Quest": lead; "WANTED: Murkdeep!": clear), and quests whose script suggests a
  way that is not enough (kind `none`: "Take Down Tethyr!" needs cannons, "Gizelton Caravan" is a caravan escort in
  C++).
- **Verdicts.** A pure script-event quest with a plan is no longer vetoed (92 quests; 183 scripted events are left
  alone, down from 270; of zone quests up to level 60 it is 27, `.ga admin quests scripted` lists them: dungeon
  events, level-60 chains, battleground quests and "Survey Alcaz Island"). A traced talk comes before the guess "the giver walks, so it is an escort" (J.D. Collie walks
  for one of his quests; the three pylon quests are talks).
- **Not covered:** NPCs that follow and need an item used on them on the way ("The Sleeper Has Awakened", "A Little
  Help From My Friends", "Wandering Shay"), credit behind a creature that only appears after a kill ("Screecher
  Spirits"), events started by anything but the accept or a talk (an item used at a place, walking into an NPC's
  sight), talks whose choice gives no credit itself but starts a fight for a drop ("This Is Going to Be Hard").

Containers again: a container a quest hands out (its start item or a source item) is opened too, wherever the bot is
("Seeping Corruption": the box of empty vials), unless a quest wants it back as it is.

### Errands: hand-ins outside the zone (2026-11-12)

The quest planner works one zone, so a completed quest whose ender stands in a capital, in the next zone or across the
sea ("Report to Ironforge", every delivery) used to stay in the log for good, and the chain behind it with it (the
analysis of 2026-11-12 counted 101 such quests in classic content, blocking 65 more). An **errand** is the trip to such
an ender (`OrderErrands.cpp`): the travel code of the zone travel (flight paths, ships, zeppelins, portals) to within
200 yd of the ender, then an ordinary turn-in task.

- **When.** Every hand-in the bot can reach is due when its zone has no quest work left (before it grinds) and when it
  is outside its target zone anyway (before it travels there, and while it is on an errand: the other hand-ins it can
  reach from there follow, nearest first). In its zone and with quest work left it leaves only when three hand-ins wait
  outside or the quest log has fewer than three free slots.
- **Reachable** means: in the bot's region within 3000 yd on foot, or farther with a flight that covers the way
  (`FindFlight`, the same test a zone travel uses); across regions at most two legs (ship, zeppelin, portal), with the
  dock in walking or flying distance and, for a single leg, the ender within 3000 yd of the arrival dock. Never into a
  zone whose level range starts more than five levels above the bot. The cheapest ender wins (yards on foot, a flight
  counts 500, a leg 6000).
- **Failure.** Two stuck travels or deadly ways on one errand give it up for 30 minutes; an ender that cannot be dealt
  with is skipped like any quest NPC (the A21 rule for turn-ins). An order change forgets errands.
- `.ga bot plan` lists the running errand and every completed quest that waits for one, with the reason when it is
  not started ("the zone of the ender is too high", "too far to walk and no flight covers the way", ...). Activity
  log: `starts an errand: hand in quest <id> "<title>" at <NPC> in <zone> (about <n> yd; <k> hand-ins wait outside
  <zone>)`, `gives up the hand-in of quest ...`.

**Quest log care.** NewRpg empties the whole quest log, completed quests included, once fewer than two slots are free
(`NewRpgBaseAction::OrganizeQuestLog`), and it takes quests in passing, so the log fills with quests nobody works on.
Before that happens the planner abandons what is worth least until three slots are free again: quests the bot
out-levelled or failed, quests the planner leaves alone or has blocked for this bot, then quests it has no task for
(other zones' first). Completed quests and quests with a task stay. Activity log: `abandons quest <id> "<title>" to keep
the quest log open (<why>)`.

### Upkeep

Checked every 30 s before quests: the most worn equipped item below 25 % → nearest repairer; two or fewer free bag
slots → nearest vendor (NewRpg sells junk and buys food/water while there). After each level-up: the nearest class
trainer of the bot's class in its region, if it teaches a spell the bot can afford now → walk there and learn every
affordable spell (real cost, `Trainer::TeachSpell`). Food and drink: next section. At every vendor the module also
asks playerbots to buy what else the bot uses (ammo, reagents): playerbots' own buy gets only one kind of consumable
per call, and NewRpg buys only when it also sold something. Services farther than 3000 yd are skipped.

### Rest and provisions (2026-11-12)

Why: in the owner's test run of 2026-11-12 every death of his eight bots (20 in an hour) fell on three bots from level 7
on, and the cause was not the fighting itself. mod-playerbots eats only below 45 % health (`Playerbots.LowHealth`) and
only with food in the bags, drinks only with water in the bags, and its "attack anything" action checks neither health
nor mana, so a bot went from one fight into the next at whatever it had left. The planner bought food only from 10
silver and only when a bot had none, and no bot below level 10 owned that much.

**Where it rests** (`Escape::FindRestSpot`, `GuildAdventure.Rest.SaferPlaceYards`, 40). A player does not sit down in
a camp or on a patrol's way. With a hostile creature (alive now, not far below the bot) or a hostile spawn within 30
yards the bot first walks to a quieter spot: among the points of its trail (the way it came) and three rings around it
(24, 40 and 60 yards away in eight directions) the one with the fewest hostile creatures and spawns within 30 yards,
if that is none at all or at least two fewer than where it stands (a spot with one creature fewer is not worth the
walk). The bot needs a whole path on the navmesh to it and a walk the ground guard would not cancel, and the spot is
the path's own end, so its height is the ground's (the first version kept the bot's height and sat a bot under a
slope twice); then it sits down. Once per rest, at most 12 seconds; a fight on the way ends the rest as always. The rest
line says so: `rested 7 s: ..., walked 38 yd away first (3 hostile creatures near, 0 there), ended by: rested`. Why
line "Resting: walking to a quieter place first". On the dev instance 21 of 27 rests began with such a walk.
The walk never leads into the reach of a hostile creature the bot is not in the reach of already (its aggro range plus
8 yards, at least 14, checked along the whole path): on the integration server a rogue at 39 % health walked 38 yards
"to a quieter place" past a gnoll scout and died to it. A spot with such a way to it is skipped. A bot below half
its health that carries food does not walk at all: it eats where it stands (a few seconds) and goes on.
Right after a run from a fight (an escape mark within 90 s and 120 yd) only a spot with nothing hostile within 30 yd
counts, the eat-in-place rule does not apply, and without such a spot in reach (40 or 100 yd) the bot walks back the
way it came (`StartTrailOut`: `it ran from a fight a moment ago and N hostile creatures stand within 30 yd: it rests
farther back`) and rests at its end; no rest begins while that walk goes on. A shaman had got away from two Venture
Co. creatures in the Barrens at 52 % health, rested 22 yd on "where 2 stood instead of 5", was attacked by three there
8 s later and died on its next run (2026-11-25, round 226).

**In the saddle, and the AI during a rest** (2026-11-12, found with two level-50 casters in Felwood): from level 20
the bots ride everywhere, and a mounted bot was never rested; besides, the AI of a bot that rested without food or
drink was not held, so it mounted up or walked off after a few seconds ("rested 14 s: mana 3% -> 11% ..., ended by:
moved on"). A level-50 priest that spends half its mana on one creature so fought on at 0-16 % mana, lost single
fights against creatures two levels below it and died. Now a bot that needs a rest gets off its mount (a journey,
`Travel` or `Voyage`, goes on: it rests where it arrives), and the AI is held for the whole rest, with or without
provisions (an attack wakes it at once). In the same run afterwards: 27 rests, 25 ended "rested", two by a fight, none
"moved on"; the priest began every fight at 77-83 % mana and lost no health in them.

**Without food and drink** the bot sits and waits for its own regeneration up to the rest's targets; after three times
`Rest.MaxSeconds` it goes on once it is above the values a rest starts at (before 2026-11-12: after `MaxSeconds`; a
mage without money went on at 56-68 % mana, pulled two foes and died without mana).

**Water.** Nobody sits down in the water. The water is asked from the map itself (`Escape::WaterAt`), not from the
character's cached state. A wet bot that needs a rest goes to dry land first (the quietest dry spot within 70 yards,
"went 40 yd ashore first"), or goes on without a rest when there is none. A bot whose head has been under water for
`GuildAdventure.Rest.AirAfterSeconds` (90; the core lets a character drown after `WaterBreath.Timer`, 180 s) goes
ashore to breathe ("ended by: breathed"; why line "Getting out of the water"): a bot that works a quest on the sea
floor does not come up by itself (Hunterbm drowned at the Darkshore shore, 2026-11-12: two minutes without a fight,
then "rested 4 s: health 63% -> 0%"). The death line of the activity log now carries the height and the water:
`died at level 11 in Darkshore at (6222, 633, -4) map 1, under water for 150 s, last fought ...`.

**Rest** (`OrderService::StepRest`, `GuildAdventure.Rest.*`). Every second, for a bot on `AUTO`, `LEVEL_ZONE` or `IDLE`
that is alive, out of combat, not mounted, not in the water and not on a taxi or ship: below 65 % health or, using
mana, below 40 % mana it rests. It stops, gets the *hold* profile (no NewRpg, no "grind": nothing walks or pulls, it
still fights back), eats the best food and drinks the best drink in its bags (the module uses the item itself, as a
client would, so playerbots' thresholds do not matter) and goes on at 85 % health and 75 % mana. While the food or
drink runs the AI is paused so that no buff makes the bot stand up; a change of the combat state wakes it at once
(`PlayerbotAI::UpdateAI`). Without food and drink the bot sits and waits for its own regeneration; that rest ends
after 60 s once it is back above the start values. A fight, a death or mounting up end a rest. The task waits
meanwhile: its time limits and the stuck tracker stand still, the why line says "Resting: eating and drinking" (or
"eating", "drinking", "catching its breath") and comes back afterwards. A bot that came back to life at its corpse
with half health rests before it fights again. `FOLLOW` bots do not rest (they keep up with the owner's character).

**Provisions** (`GuildAdventure.Provisions.*`). A bot of level `MinLevel` (8) or more with at least 100 copper buys
food (and drink, using mana) at every vendor it visits: up to `Stack` (20) pieces of each, the best kind for its
level of which its share of the budget pays at least one bundle, for at most half of its money per visit (the core's
vendor purchase, real price). The owner's rules of 2026-11-12: nothing before level 8 ([quote left out]), and shopping belongs to a hub ([quote left out]; only full bags or a missing essential start a trip at once). So below half a stack a bot goes to a vendor
within `HubYards` (150) that sells what it lacks, looked for every three minutes; the walk to a vendor from the
field when fewer than 4 pieces are left is the option `TripWhenLow` (off: a bot without provisions rests longer until
it comes to a hub; on: at most once per ten minutes, while it still has some only within 400 yards). The vendor is
found by what it sells, among all vendors: the search by the "food vendor" flag missed Brother Danil in Northshire,
who sells bread and water without it, and sent a level-3 leader to Goldshire. Below `MinLevel` only a hunter buys
(its ammunition). A caster stocks `DrinkStack` (40) pieces of drink: it drinks after nearly every fight, and
without drink a level-50 mage rested 70 % of its time (65 to 160 seconds per rest).

A vendor NewRpg does not count as visited although the bot stands in front of it (seen with the innkeepers Belm in
Kharanos and Keldamyr in Dolanaar: 65-160 s there, then "gave up" without a purchase) is served by the module after
8 s within interaction distance: it buys, and repairs when the trip was for a repair and the vendor is an armorer.
`NearestService` no longer offers a vendor, repairer or trainer in a zone that starts more than 2 levels above the bot:
a level-9 priest at the eastern edge of Elwynn Forest walked to Lakeshire for food and died to a level-24 mob.

Limits: the bot rests where it stands, also between the mobs that just killed it (the death rules deal with that
place); a druid in cat or bear form cannot eat and only waits; pets are not looked at; bandages and potions are not
used (playerbots has no bandage action). The self-service at a vendor does not sell loot (NewRpg's visit does).

### Gear and the guild's budget (2026-11-12)

`GearUpkeep.cpp`, `GuildBudget.cpp`. Found on the integration server: the guild's bots of level 15-19 wore items of
average item level 8-15 (the rogue that died most a level-10 and a level-6 weapon), with full durability, their
abilities and their talents. A fight against one foe of their level cost them 25-37 % of their health, so two foes at
once were a lost fight whatever the escape logic did. The owner's rules (2026-11-12): most gear is found or comes from the
guild storage (docs/storage.md §9); a vendor is the exception, only when one near the bot sells an upgrade and it is
within the budget; nothing is bought at a distance; the leader sets the budget.

- **At a vendor** (`Gear::BuyAt`, at every vendor visit beside food and drink): the bot buys the weapon and the
  armour pieces this vendor sells that mod-playerbots rates an upgrade for it (`BotDriver::IsUpgrade`: its class's
  armour kind, a better score for its spec), the best per place on the body, at most three per visit, through the
  core's vendor purchase, and puts them on. Log: `<bot> bought Solstice Robe (18s 69c, the guild paid 14s 31c) from
  Aldren Cordon`.
- **A vendor near it** (`OrderService::PlanUpkeep`, every five minutes): a vendor within `Gear.Buy.NearYards` (300)
  that sells such a piece within the budget (`Gear::SellsUpgrade`) gets a visit; the vendor is chosen by the risk
  rules like any other (`NearestService`). Why line "Buying better gear at <vendor>". `.ga admin gear <character>
  [<yards>]` lists what it would buy where: `Shamanheal (level 17) may spend 1g 27s 83c on one piece now ...`,
  `Hegnar Swiftaxe (287 yd) sells: Tabar (22s 14c), Bearded Axe (53s 5c)`.
- **From its bags** (`Gear::FillEmptySlots`, once a minute): armour the bot carries goes on where it wears nothing,
  whatever its kind. mod-playerbots alone only puts on the armour kind of the class (`RandomItemMgr::CanEquipArmor`:
  mail for a warrior below 40), so a warrior carried cloth shoulders and left its shoulders bare.
- **A warning** (`Gear::Warning`, `GuildAdventure.Gear.WarnGap`, 8): a bot of level 10 or more whose weapon (the main
  hand of a warrior, paladin, rogue, shaman or death knight; the bow or gun of a hunter; the wand of a mage, priest
  or warlock) or whose body armour on average is 8 item levels or more below its level is reported two minutes after
  it entered the world and then at most every half hour: a line in the activity log (`<bot> (level 18) wears gear
  far below its level: main hand Long Bayonet (item level 10), body armour item level 9 on average`) and a `GEAR`
  event in the guild's feed, so the owner sees whom to equip.
- **The budget** (`GuildBudget`; the numbers are bot settings the leader sets): the buyer pays up to
  `Budget.MemberPercent` (50) of its own money, **the guild bank** pays the rest (since 2026-11-13, the owner: [quote left out]; before,
  the other guild characters in the world handed it over, the richest first). The guild bank pays at most
  `Budget.ItemPercent` (10) of its money for one item and at most `Budget.BotAllowance` (1 gold) for one guild
  character over its whole life (table `ga_bot_budget` holds what it has paid for each). An empty guild bank pays
  nothing: a bot then buys only what its own share covers (§7 "Open" GB1). Every purchase the guild bank pays a part of
  is an event of the guild (`GEAR`: "... bought Wise Man's Belt from Franklin Hamar for 12s 54c, the guild bank paid 6s
  80c") and a line of the guild bank in the activity log. The guild bank's gold reaches the buyer untaxed (docs/storage.md
  §10). The helper for other buyers (quest items): `GuildBudget::Request(buyer, price)` hands the buyer the guild bank's
  part and books it, `GuildBudget::Cancel` puts it back when the purchase fails, `GuildBudget::Available(buyer)` is the
  highest price it would accept now.

Limits: gold of characters that are not in the world does not count and cannot be used; vendors only sell white
items, and the vendors of the levelling zones sell hardly any weapon for the levels of those zones (the weapon
merchants stand in the cities), so in practice a bot buys when its way leads through a town; the first build ordered
such pieces "through the guild" from any vendor of the faction, which the owner ruled out the same day.

### Stat weights from wowbot335 (2026-11-26)

the owner asked whether the stat priorities the bots judge items by are those of his wowbot335 research; they were not:
every item choice, mod-playerbots' own (loot, "equip upgrade") and the module's (storage supply, vendor gear, gear made
for the guild, the dungeon set, consumables, enchantment scrolls), went by mod-playerbots' weights, one table per
class and talent tree fixed in its code, and nothing read wowbot335's `profiles/statprio` (198 files, per spec and
phase). The largest differences: stamina 0.1 for every spec that does not tank (wowbot335 0.6 to 1.7), a Blood death
knight levelling by tank weights, intellect of healers and casters far lower, attack power of Retribution,
Enhancement and hunters low, Feral and tank trees weighted towards hit and expertise. On his word ([quote left out]) the bots now judge by wowbot335's weights:

- `tools/gen_stat_weights.py` reads the profiles of the specs the bots play and writes the world table
  `ga_stat_weight` (`data/sql/db-world/base/ga_stat_weight.sql`, 32 profiles x 3 phases): per class, mod-playerbots
  talent tree, variant (0 the tree; 1 the tank of a tree that also deals damage: Blood's bloodtank, Feral's
  feraltank) and phase (0 leveling, 1 preraid, 2 raid), the weights in mod-playerbots' stat types. A healer's spell
  power counts as healing power (mod-playerbots files spell power under both and weighs the one of the spec),
  ranged attack power as attack power, block for a death knight not at all. Run it again when the profiles change.
- mod-playerbots patch 0002 (`patches/mod-playerbots/0002-stat-weights-hook.patch`, docs/core-patches.md) gives
  `StatsWeightCalculator` a hook that runs after its basic weights and before its talent extras (Careful Aim and the
  like) and its hit cap. `BotDriver::LoadStatWeights` (startup) loads the table and puts the hook in.
- The hook takes the profile of the bot's talent tree: the leveling phase below level 60, the preraid phase at 60.
  A Blood death knight and a Feral druid take the tank variant only while their dungeon set as a tank is on
  (`BotDriver::SetRoleMode`, set by `RoleService`); a Protection warrior or paladin is a tank by its tree. The
  dungeon roles' ratings (`RoleScore`, `EnchantScore`, `BuffScore` for a role) take the role's tree: warrior and
  paladin tanks Protection, death knights and druids the tank variant of Blood and Feral; healers Holy (paladin,
  priest) and Restoration.
- A profile speaks for the stats it can list (the primary stats, hit, crit, haste, expertise, armour penetration,
  attack power, spell and healing power, mana regeneration, defense, dodge, parry, block): one it lists gets its
  weight, one it does not list is 0 unless mod-playerbots gave it a negative weight (spell power for a warrior,
  attack power for a priest: what the spec must not wear). Weapon damage, armour, threat, resistance and the bonus
  for stats nobody knows stay mod-playerbots' (wowbot335 has no weapon damage term, and its armour weight is on
  another scale), and so do its rules for armour kinds, weapon kinds and speeds and the hit cap.
- `GuildAdventure.StatWeights.Enable` (1) switches it off. Without patch 0002 the module says so at startup and
  mod-playerbots' weights stay.

### Risk (2026-11-12)

Why: with rest and provisions in place the deaths that were left came from where the planner sent the bots. It took
the nearest spawn of a quest target whatever stood around it, ranked objectives by distance alone (a level-8 priest
began "Protect the Frontier", level 10, because its prowlers were 71 yards away), grinded at the densest cluster, and
its death rule counted deaths per quest id: after "Bounty on Murlocs" was set aside the same bot died on at the same
murlocs under "A Bundle of Trouble" (observer's numbers, 08:22-08:48 on the integration server: ten deaths of one
level-9 priest at one murloc camp).

`RiskModel.h/.cpp` holds the judgement, `OrderService` asks it at four places (`GuildAdventure.Risk.*`):

- **Danger of a spot** (`Risk::SpotDanger`): hostile mob spawns within 22 yards of it count one point each (0.3 when
  more than three levels below the bot, half a point more per level above it), every level of the target above the bot one point, a cave, mine or building
  one and a half (the terrain's indoor flag, remembered per spawn). The mob spawns come from `WorldIndex` through a
  32-yard grid.
- **Objective spot** (`Risk::SaferSpot`, in `CollectLogTasks`): not the nearest spawn of the target but, among up to
  twelve spawns no more than 250 yards farther, the one with the least `distance + 60 yd × danger`. Left out are
  spawns whose creature is more than `MaxFoeLevelAbove` (1) levels above the bot, one more with a pet at its side,
  spawns with a mob more than one level above that standing around them (a quest in level range whose objective lies
  between level-30 mobs: "The Totem of Infliction" for a level-24 hunter), spawns in an area the bot avoids, and
  spawns whose fight would cost the bot too much (next point); when none is left the objective gets no task for now,
  and the planner works something else (so such a quest does not keep the bot in the zone either).
- **The fight a spot means** (`Risk::SpotFightCost`, `GuildAdventure.Risk.MaxFightCostPercent`, 80): the target, if
  it is a creature the bot fights, and every creature that attacks by itself (hostile faction; the yellow ones of a
  starting area are no pack) whose spawn lies within its pull distance of the spot: the core's aggro radius (20
  yards, a yard more or less per level above or below the bot, times `Rate.Creature.Aggro`) plus 6 yards. Each costs
  what the bot's own fights taught it (`Escape::FoeCost`: its cost of a foe of its level, 1.3 times per level above,
  0.92 per level below (0.87 until 2026-11-13); a bot that has fought fewer than four times takes at most its level's prior: 15 % below
  level 6, 25 % below 10, 40 % from there), they die one after the other while the rest keeps hitting, and a pet
  takes 40 % of it. A spot waits while that is more than 80 % of what the bot has. So a healthy bot takes a single
  foe a level above it and two weak ones at once; a bot whose gear is far below its level (cost 40 % and more per
  foe) no pair of its own level. `Risk::CanFight(player, rt, foeLevel, foes)` gives the same answer for a grind.
  Two additions after the live rounds of the evening: hostile spawns beyond the pull distance but within 30 yards
  count a third (they wander, a patrol passes, the fight drifts: a level-18 mage died seven times in the Mo'grosh
  camp, whose ogres stand 20-25 yards apart and were each "alone"), and a fight in the water counted three times
  (a level-17 druid had lost to single level-13 murlocs under water three times; that was its aquatic form, and the
  factor is gone since 2026-11-13, see "Live rounds 47 and 48" below). `.ga admin spot <character> <x> <y> <z>
  [<creature entry>]` spells the verdict out: `Magefrost (level 19; a foe of its level costs it 40%): at (-4923,
  -3899, 301) the target is level 19, 2 hostile spawns within reach: Mo'grosh Ogre 19 at 24 yd (near, counts a
  third), ...; the fight would cost about 100% of what it has (limit 80%, level cap 20): the spot waits`.
  Before (2026-11-12, for some hours): fixed margins, no foe above the bot's level and no pack unless the bot was two
  levels above everything in it, which left a level-3 character in Northshire without any quest work ("Kobold Camp
  Cleanup" stood at 0/8, the Defias thugs of level 3-4 were no target) until it wandered off to grind wolves.
- **Ranking** (`Risk::RankPenalty`): an objective's distance in the ranking grows by 60 yards per danger point of its
  spot and 120 yards per level its quest lies above the bot: quests at the bot's level and lonely targets come first.
- **Grind spot** (`Risk::GrindScore`, in `PlanGrind`): up to six fitting mobs within the cluster radius count for the
  spot, more than eight against it, as do the danger of the spot itself and mobs above the bot's level; before, the
  densest cluster won.
- **A level-up frees a place only when it puts the bot above what killed it there** (2026-11-12: a rogue's caution
  ended with its level-up to 16, it went straight back to the level 15-17 gnolls and died): a place set aside for its
  foes lasts until the bot has their level, a place set aside after two deaths or an escape until the bot is a level
  above the foes there, and "plays it safe" ends after its time or two level-ups, not one.
- **Vendors, repairers, trainers and innkeepers are chosen by the same rules** (`NearestService`, 2026-11-12: four of
  eight deaths of one live window were "during vendor"): not one in a place that is set aside, with creatures too
  strong for the bot around it or behind a straight way through creatures far above it (`Risk::IsSafePlace`); and one
  whose straight way leads back through a place the bot has just died at or run from
  (`BotRuntime::CrossesAvoidedArea`: the way comes within 60 yards of the middle of the place and at least 15 yards
  nearer to it than the bot stands), or whose way passes creatures two or more levels above the bot
  (`Risk::WayDanger`: the straight line for a short way, the road map's route for one over 350 yards; a level-16
