  rogue was sent 520 yards to a fisherman past level-18 creatures and met three of them), is a later choice: the
  least bad of those is taken when no other is left. One behind creatures four or more levels above the bot is not
  taken at all (the trip waits). The way itself is `OrderService::WalkTo`'s matter (routes go around set-aside
  places there).
- **Death places are kept across restarts** (table `ga_bot_death_place`, `Risk::Load` / `RestorePlaces`): deaths
  within 80 yards and six hours count as one place, whatever lies between them. From the second death the place is
  set aside for 30 minutes, twice as long with every further death there (at most eight hours), until the bot is a
  level above what killed it; a death to a foe two or more levels above the bot sets it aside for two hours at once.
  A character that enters the world gets its places back ("still keeps away from 1 place where it died"). Before, the
  count lived in memory for 30 minutes: the camp above killed one bot seven times in three hours, each death more
  than half an hour or a server restart after the one before, so the place was never set aside.
- **Deaths by place and foe** (`Risk::OnDeath`, called from `OnDied`): every death is remembered for 30 minutes with
  its place. A death to a foe two or more levels above the bot sets the place (100 yards around it) aside until the bot
  is within a level of that foe (at most two hours); a second death within 80 yards sets the place aside until the
  next level or for 30 minutes. Objectives and grind spots there are not planned, whatever the quest. The older rules
  stay: three deaths at one quest set the quest aside, a second death at the corpse takes the spirit healer.
- **Playing it safe** (`Risk::IsCautious`): four deaths within 20 minutes, wherever, and the bot works no objectives
  for 15 minutes or until its next level; it still turns quests in and picks them up, and grinds at a safe spot (why
  line "Playing it safe after several deaths: grinding in ...").
- **Rescue from a death loop** (`Risk::Rescue`, `RescueDeaths` / `RescueWindowMinutes`): three deaths within ten minutes
  where the foes are four or more levels above the bot, or in a zone that starts more than two levels above it, and the
  dead bot gives the place up: it takes the spirit healer's resurrection (half health, a quarter of its durability) and
  goes home to its bind point, as a player would with the hearthstone, in one step (a ghost cannot use the stone, and
  alive at that spirit healer it would not finish the cast). Seen on the integration server before: a level-11 rogue
  that strayed into Duskwood died 43 times in half an hour, because the corpse rule resurrected it at the Raven Hill
  spirit healer, which stands between level-25 skeletons.
- A task whose spot lies in a place that was just set aside ends with the death (it would walk back in).

**Objective watchdog** (`OrderService::StepTask`, found while testing this): NewRpg's rule "no progress for five
minutes, give the quest up" only runs once the bot stands at the spot, and the planner's stuck rule only until the bot
was near it once. In between two bots stood 85 yards from a "Timberling Sprouts" spawn for 15 minutes. Now an objective
at a known spawn without a kill, a fight, a rest or an item for three minutes skips that spawn (20 minutes) and takes
another one; after three spawns in a row without progress the quest counts as failed (A21).

Limits: elites are not in `WorldIndex`'s mob list, so an elite next to a spot does not count; patrols count only where
they spawn; the way to a spot is not judged (a bot can still walk through a camp on its way, the gaps thread's travel
work); what the planner sets aside lives in memory and is gone after a restart; quest targets that are game objects
(a chest in a camp) count the mobs around them but have no level of their own.

### Leaving a lost fight (2026-11-12)

`FightEscape.h/.cpp`, called from `OrderService::UpdateBot` right after the fight tracking. Why: over 1034 fights on
the dev instance a fight against one foe was lost in 2.5 % of the cases, against two in 48 %, against three or more in
91 %; these crowded fights were 11 % of all fights and 68 of the 91 deaths. mod-playerbots fights every fight to the
end.

- **Estimate.** Every bot learns what a fight against one foe of its level costs it (`BotRuntime::fightCost`, a running
  average over its own fights: health lost plus half the mana spent; 12 % for the warrior, 44 % for the rogue, 48 % for
  the holy priest on the dev instance; 40 % until it has fought). The rest of a fight costs: the foes die one after the
  other, the weakest first, and everyone still standing hits meanwhile; a foe above the bot weighs 1.3 times per level,
  below it 0.92 times (0.87 until 2026-11-13), an elite 2.5 times. What the bot has: its health, for a mana user times (0.5 + half its mana).
  A foe that hits the bot's pet counts 0.4 of one that hits the bot (a warlock left a fight against two level-17
  mobs, one of them on its voidwalker, ten times in a row before this).
- **A losing fight against one foe** is judged too, but only below 35 % health: one ordinary foe is otherwise fought
  out.
- **When.** Only fights against two or more foes, an elite, or a foe three or more levels above the bot are judged, and
  none against foes five levels below it. When the cost is above what it has times `GuildAdventure.Escape.Margin` on two
  ticks in a row, the bot leaves. A bot that follows its owner never does, and nobody does in an instance.
- **How.** It stops attacking, calls its pet back (passive while it runs), casts what its class has for it (Frost Nova,
  Sprint and Evasion, Psychic Scream and Power Word: Shield, Nature's Grasp, Stoneclaw and Earthbind Totem, Hammer of
  Justice, Hamstring ...: the highest rank it knows, when mana and cooldown allow), and runs in legs of 45 yards: away
  from the foes at first, each leg in the direction (of seven) with the fewest hostile spawns that it has a path to.
  mod-playerbots is paused meanwhile. A creature gives up 30 yards from its home once it has not been damaged for about
  11 seconds (`Creature::CanCreatureAttack`), a foe that was never hit at the 30 yards.
- **End.** Out of combat: "got away"; the place of the fight is set aside for 15 minutes (or until the next level), the
  bot's task ends and NewRpg is put to rest (it would walk on in a straight line from wherever the run ended), so the
  next walk is planned anew; the rest step takes over first. Rooted or stunned ("held fast": a Defias net): it fights on and may
  leave again 8 seconds later. Still chased after `Escape.MaxSeconds` (35): it fights on and does not run again for 90
  seconds.
- **The way out** (2026-11-12, after three bots died on the run among the Stonesplinter troggs of Loch Modan: the run
  led them into more of the camp). The bot keeps a trail of where it walked out of combat (a point every 10 yards, the
  newest 20). The first legs of a run go back along it, the way it came in: the newest point 30 to 80 yards away, if
  no hostile creature stands within 15 yards of it and the bot has a path to it; the escape line then says "the way it
  came". Without a trail, or when it is blocked, the direction is chosen as before, and the score now counts the
  hostile creatures that are alive there (more than the spawns). In a camp (hostile creatures within 25 yards that are
  not in the fight yet) the estimate grows by a fifth per creature, up to five, so the bot leaves when the second foe
  joins, not when its health is half gone. With three or more foes at once of its level or above, one level below
  counted too (`GuildAdventure.Escape.MaxFoes`, 3), the fight counts as lost whatever the estimate says: a warlock had
  stayed with three troggs until 43 % health and died on the run. Foes two or more levels below the bot are left to
  the estimate (a level-16 rogue had run from three level-12 gnolls at 96 % health and died on the run). Foes five or
  more levels below it are fought out only while the bot is above half its health (a level-19 mage ran out of mana
  against two foes of level 13 and 14 and died without a look at the estimate).
- **Stay or run.** A fight that looks lost is not left blindly: the run itself is estimated, and the bot runs only
  when that is better than fighting. On the integration server a level-15/16 rogue left fights against two to four
  gnolls at 66-96 % health and died within 4-10 seconds each time, hit in the back; on the dev instance it ran from two
  level-14 foes at full health and lost half of it on the way.
  - *The run, as measured* (2026-11-12, 125 runs of one evening on the integration server): from one foe a run cost
    19 % of the bot's health on average, from two 22 %, from three 26 %, from four 37 %, and took 11 to 16 seconds;
    2 of 33 runs from one foe ended in a death, 9 of 72 from two, 11 of 32 from three. The foes trail behind one
    another and give up 30 yards from where the fight began (`CreatureLeashRadius`). So the estimate counts the foe
    at the bot's heels for 8 seconds and every further one for 2.5; the first estimate (15 seconds for every foe,
    below) was three times that and made bots stay in fights they could have left ("the run about 93%"). With three
    foes of its level on it a bot now leaves at once, not after a second look.
  - *The run, as first built:* every foe at the bot's back for about 15 seconds, at the rate the bot's own fights taught
    (`BotRuntime::fightHealthRate`: the share of its health one foe of its level takes off it per second, a running
    average beside the full cost, 2 % until it has fought, at least 1 %). A getaway spell that is ready (Vanish,
    Sprint, Blink, Frost Nova, Psychic Scream, Stoneclaw or Earthbind Totem, Divine Shield, Howl of Terror,
    Intimidating Shout, Feign Death, Disengage) leaves 40 % of that. The result is multiplied by what the bot's own
    runs taught it (`BotRuntime::runFactor`, 1.0 at first, 0.4 to 4): after every run the health it really lost is
    set against the estimate, and a death on the run raises the factor by half at least. The first build used a fixed
    1.6 (hits in the back are not dodged or parried and daze the runner, which killed the rogue within ten seconds of
    every run); on the integration server 16 of 18 runs of all bots then got away while bots that stayed because "the
    run would cost 134 %" died in the fight, so the factor is now each bot's own. `.ga bot plan` shows it ("its runs
    cost 1.3 times the estimate").
  - *The fight:* what the estimate says, times 0.75 when a spell that protects the bot is cast now (Evasion, Power
    Word: Shield, Barkskin, Divine Protection, Shield Wall; a spell that does not go out, as a shield without mana,
    does not count).
  - *The decision:* the bot stays when what protects it turns the fight (not when the number of foes alone says it is
    lost), or when it would not live through the run and the run costs more than 60 % of the fight. Staying, it casts
    what protects it and fights; it thinks about running again 12 seconds later. Else it runs, and casts its getaway,
    control and protection spells in the first four seconds as before.
  Log: `<bot> stays in a fight against 3 foes at 78% health: the fight would cost it about 150%, the run about 133%,
  nothing to get away with (used Evasion)`. The escape line names the spells it cast: `... the way it came (used
  Sprint, Evasion): got away ...`. What it does not change: a bot whose gear is far below its level loses a fight
  against two foes of its level whatever it decides (dev instance, 2026-11-12: four runs of ten minutes, six or seven
  deaths each, as before); the decision only stops deaths that the run itself caused.
- **A target fled from twice.** A task that ends with "left a fight" twice within half an hour for the same target
  sets it aside for 15 minutes, and twice as long each further time (at most two hours); the planner takes something
  else. An objective counts by its quest (its foes stand at many spawns; the quest is set aside like after three
  deaths, until the time is over or the bot is two levels on), a quest giver, ender or vendor by the NPC. A druid had
  started one turn-in 15 times in a row and left a fight on the way each time. Log: `<bot> sets turn-in (target ...)
  aside for 15 min: it left a fight there or on the way 2 times`.
- **Not past the rest of the camp, not into the water** (2026-11-12: a warlock ran from murlocs three times and each
  time into further murlocs). A leg is judged along its whole line: every living hostile creature that is not in the
  fight and would have the bot within its reach (its aggro range plus 5 yards, at least 12) on the way costs the
  direction 100 points, a leg that ends in the water 50; a trail point with such a creature on the way, or in the
  water while the bot stands dry, is not used. So such a leg is taken only when nothing else is left.
- **The place afterwards.** It is set aside for 15 minutes, and twice as long for every earlier escape within 100 yards
  of it during the last two hours (30, 60, at most 120 minutes; "got away again (the place is set aside longer)").
  Places that are set aside (after an escape or after deaths, `BotRuntime::IsInAvoidedArea`) hold for objectives,
  grind spots, quest interactions and, since the loop of 2026-11-12, for quest givers and enders too: `PlanQuests`
  drops pickup and turn-in candidates there and a running one ends ("place set aside after deaths or a lost fight"),
  so the bot does something else and comes back rested when the time is over or it has gained a level. On the
  integration server a level-16 warlock had fled from the same mob ten times in 4.5 minutes because its turn-in stood
  70 yards from the fight.
- **Log.** `<bot> left a fight against 2 foes (Defias Trapper level 13) at 95% health: got away after 10 s, health
  84%`; the fight line ends with `left` instead of `won`; the status line counts `left`; `.ga bot plan` shows the
  learned cost. Why line: "Running from a fight it would lose".
- **Keeping away** (`GuildAdventure.Escape.StepAside`): a roaming creature far above the bot is no property of a spot
  (Vultros, a level-26 rare that patrols Westfall, killed a level-13 rogue twice in half an hour). Every two seconds a
  bot looks for one within 35 yards: hostile, four or more levels above it, and a rare, an elite or on a patrol. The
  level is the creature's own plus what its health and damage are worth against an ordinary creature's (a level per
  factor 1.3: Emogg the Crusher, a level-19 rare elite with three times the health and 1.7 times the damage, counts as
  level 26; it killed a level-18 warlock and a level-17 mage that the plain level rule let walk into it). Out of
  combat it steps aside (the same run in legs, mounted too) until the creature is 60 yards away or 20 seconds have
  passed; in a fight it leaves the fight at once. The place is set aside for ten minutes, the task ends (a voyage goes
  on). (Until 2026-11-13 the same creature was not stepped aside for again within three minutes; see "No pass for a
  strong roamer" below.) Log: `<bot> keeps away from Sergeant Brashclaw (level 18 rare), 25 yd away`, then `kept away from
  ...: clear of it after 7 s`. Why line: "Keeping away from a creature far above its level".
- **With the travel work** (where the module has `GroundGuard.h` and `RoadMap.h`; both are used behind
  `__has_include`, so this file also builds without them): a leg is only started when the ground guard would not cancel
  it (`sGroundGuard.WouldCancel`), and the risk model leaves a quest spawn alone when the straight way to it (up to 350
  yards; longer walks are routed along roads) leads through creatures three or more levels above the bot
  (`sRoadMap.DangerAlong`, in `Risk::SaferSpot`).
- **Quest interactions** (use an object or an item, cast, explore; the tasks of PR #33): their spot is chosen like a
  kill objective's (`Risk::SaferSpot`; a creature the bot cannot attack has no level of its own, only what stands
  around it counts: `Risk::ThreatLevel`), a POI or an area to explore is asked about with `Risk::IsSafePlace`, a bot
  that plays it safe starts none, and a running interaction ends when its place was set aside after deaths. Found on
  the integration server: a level-12 rogue died four times in nine minutes at the oat sacks of "Poor Old Blanchy"
  among level-15 Defias Pillagers. The three hooks are in code only the integration branch has.
- Limits: without the road map the way to a task is not judged (a level-13 rogue walked through level-16 gnolls to
  its quest spot and died on the run from two of them); running from foes four
  levels above the bot or out of a cave costs most of its health; the learned cost starts again at every login.
- The one foe it fights (2026-11-25, round 220): a strong creature near makes a bot leave a fight at once, but not when
  that creature is the one ordinary foe on it; then the fight's own estimate decides. A level-30 shaman attacked by
  level-34 Scorpid Terrors in Thousand Needles had left the fight six times in twenty minutes at 87 to 99 % health
  (`[Scorpid Terror (level 34) was near]`) and lost 6 to 50 % of its health on the runs, while the fights it stayed in
  against them it won at 45 to 92 %. Elites and rare elites keep the old rule.

### Casters without drink (2026-11-12)

The gaps thread measured one window of the integration server: three casters without water rested 2019 of 3984
seconds (a mage 51 % of its time, a shaman 64 %, a priest 37 %), about 90 seconds after every fight. Why they held
none: drink is bought at a hub after a hand-in, from a vendor within 150 yards that sells what is missing (the owner's
rule), and these bots worked far from any such vendor for an hour (the mage in the Redridge hills, the shaman handing
in at a quest giver with no innkeeper near); the guild storage gave them a bottle at a time. Their money was not the
reason (48 silver to 1.6 gold). Three changes:

- **Out of drink is urgent** (`GuildAdventure.Provisions.TripWhenOut`, 1): a character that uses mana and holds no
  drink at all walks to the nearest vendor that sells some, like a hunter without ammunition
  (`goes to a vendor (Innkeeper Kimlya, 529 yd): out of drink`), and buys its stack there (`DrinkStack`, 40).
  Food stays a matter of the hub. *Bounded on 2026-11-13* (live round 45: a priest walked 1230 yards for drink,
  152 of the round's 1320 seconds, twice over 1000 yards): only to a vendor within
  `GuildAdventure.Provisions.TripWhenOutYards` (600, straight line; 0 = never), and not while the guild storage
  holds drink the character can use, which the supply step brings within a minute wherever it stands
  (`StorageSupply::HasDrink`). Both are bot settings (per guild and per bot). A mage that knows Conjure Water takes
  no drink out of the storage (one took 37 of 40 bottles a priest of its guild was out of).
- **A mage conjures** its water in a rest when it has none (and its food when it is hurt and has none): `rested 15 s:
  ..., mana 48% -> 78%, no food, drank Conjured Sparkling Water`; the same mage had rested 100 to 128 seconds.
- **Two vendors at a hub**: when nobody near sells both food and drink, the one with the drink is taken, else the
  one with the food (a baker and an innkeeper are two people).

### A character that can heal heals itself (2026-11-12)

the owner: [quote left out] It can: mod-playerbots' damage rotations do
not heal. Its retribution paladin casts Lay on Hands and Divine Shield at critical health and Holy Light only under
the shield; Retadin (level 17, Holy Light rank 3 in its book) ended its fights at 5 to 63 % health with 97-100 % mana,
and sat its wounds out in the rests. Now (`OrderService::StepSelfHeal`, `GuildAdventure.Fight.SelfHealBelow`, 45):

- **In a fight** below 45 % health a character the AI plays casts its heal on itself: a paladin Flash of Light or
  Holy Light, after a Hammer of Justice on what hits it when that is ready (so the cast is not pushed back); a priest
  outside Shadowform Flash Heal, Greater Heal, Heal or Lesser Heal; a shaman Lesser Healing Wave or Healing Wave; a
  druid in no form Regrowth or Healing Touch. mod-playerbots' AI is held for the cast. The fight line counts it:
  `fight 19 s: 1 foe at once (Redridge Brute level 18), health 100% -> 89% (lowest 44%), mana 100% -> 74%, won,
  healed itself 1 time`.
- **In a rest** without food such a character heals itself the same way while it has 30 % mana ("ate nothing
  (healed itself)" in the rest line), and drinks or waits for the mana afterwards.

### Before a pull, and after a death (2026-11-12)

What killed most in the live rounds of that evening were pulls of three and more: a level-19 rogue died five times in
23 minutes at the Redridge gnoll camps ("fight 11 s: 3 foes at once ... died"), a mage with four murlocs at once. The
spot rule had kept the planner away from those packs (`.ga admin spot` says "the spot waits" for the three Brutes that
stand 8 yards apart); but at a spot playerbots picks its targets itself, the nearest one, and that was the pack. And
once three melee foes are on a bot, both answers are a death: creatures run faster than a player, so a run without
a getaway spell ends within ten seconds ("died on the run"), and staying does too.

- **The pull check** (`Escape::CheckPull`, four times a second while the bot is out of combat; once a second came
  too late for a charge or an instant spell, which start the fight within a fraction of a second of the AI's choice;
  not for a bot that follows its owner or its squad leader): when its AI turns to
  a creature, that creature and every living hostile one that would join (the rule of 2026-11-13 is under "Who
  joins a fight" below; at first: everything within 12 yards of the target, or with the bot's way inside its reach) go
  through the fight estimate, at full health, against what the bot has right now and the limit of the spot rule
  (`Risk.MaxFightCostPercent`); three foes of about its level are too many whatever the estimate says
  (`Escape.MaxFoes`). A pull it cannot afford is called off: the AI lets go of the target (no attack, no cast, no
  walk). For a pack, or a single foe too strong even for the rested bot, the place is set aside for ten minutes, the
  task ends, and for a minute, or until it is 70 yards away, the bot pulls nothing by itself (playerbots would turn
  to the same creature again): `does not pull Redridge Brute (level 17): 2 more would join (Redridge Brute 17,
  Redridge Brute 18); the fight would cost it about 186% and it has 100% (limit 80%)`. For a single foe the rested
  bot could afford it rests first: `waits with <creature> ...: it rests first`.
- **The rest follows the next fight.** A rest also starts when the bot has clearly less than a fight against one foe
  of its level needs under that limit (its learned cost divided by the limit, at most 95 %), and lasts until it has
  that much: a level-21 warlock whose fights cost it 80 % went into them at 85 % health and 75 % mana, which is 74 %
  of its strength. For bots whose fights are cheap nothing changes.
- **What a bot learned stays** (`ga_bot_fight_stats`): its cost of a fight, the health a foe takes per second and
  the factor of its runs are kept across restarts. Before, every restart put a bot back to the default of its level
  (40 % per foe) for its first four fights. The share for a pet now only stands in until the cost is learned: the
  learned cost was measured with the pet, and counting the pet again sent a warlock to bears that cost it 80 %.
- **Not back to life among what killed it.** playerbots uses a soulstone (or Reincarnation) at once, where the bot
  lies; a warlock died again 21 seconds after its death, at the same spot. With hostile creatures within 30 yards of
  the corpse the module takes the option away and the bot walks back like everyone else (`does not rise where it
  fell`). playerbots' own walk back already waits for a spot without creatures in reach.
- **A close call counts at once.** A target or NPC the bot got away from with less than 35 % of its health is set
  aside after that one time (a warrior got away from a named level-24 foe with 13 %, rested, walked back and died).
- **A quieter place, farther away.** When no place within the usual 40 yards is quiet enough, the search goes to 100
  yards once (a bot that entered the world inside a camp sat down to eat among the gnolls).
- **The escape line says what the leg rule did**: `[the way it came was closed (2 creatures on it); of 7 directions 5
  led past other creatures, 0 into water, 1 had no path; the one taken passes 0]`.

- **Out of a camp after a login.** A character that enters the world alive with hostile creatures within 30 yards
  (it stood in a camp when the server stopped) looks for a quiet place before anything else, like a rest does, and
  walks there before it eats, whatever its health: `entered the world with 4 hostile creatures within 30 yd: it looks
  for a quiet place first`, then `rested 6 s: ..., walked 22 yd away first (6 hostile creatures near, 0 there)`.

**The spot verdict** (`Risk::JudgeSpot(player, rt, spot)` → `Risk::SpotVerdict`, the one answer every planner
path asks: objectives, interactions, grind spots, gather nodes). A spot is not usable when the place is set aside;
when its target is above the level cap (`Risk.MaxFoeLevelAbove`) or a creature more than a level above the cap stands
within 22 yards; when as many foes of about the bot's level would join as it leaves a fight for (`Escape.MaxFoes`);
or when the fight would cost more than `Risk.MaxFightCostPercent`. What would join (changed on 2026-11-13, "Who
joins a fight" below): hostile spawns within their pull
distance in full, within 30 yards with a third of their cost, and up to 45 yards with a seventh (the spots where a
mage died three times at one gnoll camp had nothing within 30 yards and three creatures between 31 and 39). Elites,
rares and bosses count too (`WorldIndex::GetStrongSpawns`; they were in no list before): an elite as three levels more
and two and a half times the cost. `retryLevel` is the bot's level from which the spot would do (0: none within
eight levels, or the place is only set aside for a time), so a quest whose every spot waits can be left until that
level; a squad standing together raises the limits and gets such quests earlier. `.ga admin spot` prints the
verdict: "the spot waits: a creature far above the bot stands there", "... the fight would cost too much (worth
another look at level 23)".

- **A quest whose pulls keep being called off** is set aside for half an hour after the second one (`sets quest ...
  aside for 30 min: two pulls called off, its targets stand in packs it cannot afford alone`); the bot turns to
  another quest instead of walking from pack to pack. The pull check counts a wandering creature from farther away
  (its wander distance on top of the 12 yards).
- **The fight by its own numbers.** While it fights, the module measures how fast the bot takes the foes' health and
  how fast each foe takes the bot's. Against two or more foes (or one far above it) a fight that clearly goes worse
  than the bot can take (the projection is 1.2 times its health or more) is left early, whatever the learned average
  says (`[by how the fight went]`); a warrior had stayed with two orcs by its average and died with the first at
  9 %. Against one ordinary foe the measurement only replaces the average once the bot is below 35 % health (a foe
  at 5 % is finished; a first build that left single fights early gave up six close ones in ten minutes).
- **What a fleeing foe fetches counts at once**: the creature of its kind it runs to (within 30 yards) and what
  stands within 10 yards of that one are in the estimate while the bot can still walk away from one fleeing foe.
- **A rest moves** when a hostile creature that is not fighting comes within its reach of the resting bot (aggro
  range plus 8 yards, at least 15): `walked 38 yd away when something came near`, twice per rest at most.
- **The spirit healer when the corpse lies badly**: among two or more hostile creatures (30 yards) or under water
  (`will take the spirit healer: its corpse lies among 4 hostile creatures`), at its price, with gear at 40 %
  durability or more; a mage had died twice 50 seconds apart at one camp, a warlock drowned at its corpse.

- **Not into a pack on the way.** A walking bot (not mounted) looks at the next 45 yards of its way every two
  seconds: two or more hostile creatures that are not fighting and would have it within their reach, and that it
  cannot take together by the pull check's rule, end the walk: `keeps away from 4 creatures on its way that it
  cannot take together (the nearest: ...)`; the place is set aside for ten minutes and the planner routes around it.
- **Mana counts in the measurement.** The fight's own numbers are taken in the estimate's measure (health, and mana
  at half weight): a mage behind a Mana Shield lost no health for half a minute, then all of it, and left at 16 %.
- More spells for a bot that leaves or stays: Blind, Lay on Hands, Ice Barrier, Mana Shield.
- **Held fast on a run** (a net, a root): the bot casts what frees it and runs on: the human and gnome racials,
  Hand of Freedom, Blink, a druid's shift into travel or cat form (it keeps a travel form while it runs). Without
  any of them the run ends as before ("held fast, fights on") and is looked at again after eight seconds.
- **Creatures far below the bot count in a pack.** The pull check, the walk's look ahead and what a fleeing foe
  fetches left out everything five or more levels below the bot as trivial. A level-22 mage so pulled "one" level-17
  gnoll of a camp and had five on it within ten seconds, twice in three minutes; a level-16 paladin died to five
  level-13 gnolls. They count down to ten levels below now (at half the cost of a foe of the bot's level), and three
  or more foes far below the bot are judged like any other fight instead of being fought out until half its health
  is gone.

Not solved by this: what three or more melee foes do to a bot once they are on it (a third of the runs from three
end in a death, and staying is worse).

### Who joins a fight; pets; out of the place (2026-11-13)

Live round 38 was the first window without a death, and the weak number became the quests handed in: in half an hour
29 pulls were called off, 18 of them for *one* creature that "would join", and the planner left 26 quests "until
level N". Three things in the counting were wrong, and three in the escape (found in rounds 37 and 39).

**Who joins** (the pull check on the living creatures, the spot verdict on spawn data; one rule):

- *The call for help.* A creature that is attacked calls the creatures **of its own faction** within the core's
  assistance radius (`CreatureFamilyAssistanceRadius`, 10 yards) that would help (`Creature::CanAssistTo`). A spider
  does not come for a wolf. Within that radius plus 2 yards such a creature joins for sure.
- *Its own aggro.* Every other creature joins only when the fight comes into its own aggro radius (the core's: 20
  yards, a yard per level of difference, times `Rate.Creature.Aggro`, here 0.5) plus 3 yards; the fight is somewhere
  on the way between the bot and its target.
- *Perhaps.* A creature that walks about and is its wander distance farther off than that (the spawn data does not
  know the wander distance: 6 yards) may come or not: it counts **half**. Beyond that the camp counts as before, a
  third up to 30 yards and a seventh up to 45.
- *Half a foe is half a foe.* A creature that counts with a share counts with it as a foe to kill and as one that
  hits meanwhile. Before, its cost was reduced but it stood in the fight as a whole attacker: a single creature with
  six others 31 to 45 yards away came out at five times its cost.
- *A rare is seldom there* (hours between its lives, and one of several places holds it): on spawn data it counts
  with 15 % of its place, and not among the foes or as the strongest creature of the spot. When it is alive the pull
  check and the look-out for strong roamers see it. (A level-20 priest was kept from a gnoll camp by a rare the spawn
  data shows at two places 9 and 23 yards from the target.)

Before, everything hostile within 12 yards of the target plus its wander distance (the pull check) or within its
aggro radius plus 6 yards of the spot (the verdict) counted in full, of whatever kind. `.ga admin spot` names each
neighbour's share: `Venom Web Spider 20 at 14 yd (may walk in, counts half)`, `Ribchaser 17 rare at 9 yd (seldom
there, counts little)`; the pull check's line says `1 more would join (Venom Web Spider 19 perhaps)`.
Measured on the dev instance: for a level-22 mage a Rabid Dire Wolf with a spider 14 yards off, another 24 and a
third 42 yards away costs 69 % of what it has and passes (the same kind of pull was refused at 96 to 129 % on the
integration server); a gnoll with a second one 10 yards off and two more at 14 and 18 costs it 144 % and still
waits. A real pack stays a pack: the level-21 priest of the report spends over half its mana on one gnoll five
levels below it (it has no wand), two at once are its limit, and the camps it was kept from hold three and four.

The fight line now carries the pull check's count also when fewer came (`its own pull (3 expected, 1 more
possible)` on a fight against one foe), so the counting can be checked against what happened. With
`GuildAdventure.Debug` a `pull joiner` line says where each further creature of a fight came from. That line showed
that the "1 expected, 3 came" fights of a hunter at the Greymist camp were no miscount: the second and third foe had
their home 58 and 61 yards from the target and were on the bot one second after the pull, the waves of the quest
event "WANTED: Murkdeep!" it had started.

**A pet holds one foe.** A hunter and a warlock learn what a fight costs them with the pet holding the foe; a
hunter's came out at 3 %. A pull of three murlocs was so judged at 30 % and ended at 10 % health. Every foe the pet
does not hold (before the pull: all but the bot's target) now costs at least what a fight costs a bot that has
learned nothing yet (40 % from level 10, times the level factor), in the pull check, in a fight and for the spot
(`Escape::FoeCostAlone`). A fight against one foe is judged as before.

**The warrior's Intimidating Shout** never went out: it needs a foe as its target (the first effect of spell 5246 is
"target enemy"; Psychic Scream, Howl of Terror and Frost Nova are centred on the caster) and was cast on the warrior
itself. In an evening 58 runs of the warriors used a spell 5 times (Hamstring), the Shout never; a level-27 warrior
ran 35 seconds with two orcs at its back and died of it. It is cast on the strongest foe in melee range now. With
`GuildAdventure.Debug` a spell that would have helped and was refused is named once per run (`could not cast ... on
its run: cast result N`).

**Vanish and Feign Death end the fight, not the danger.**
- After one of them nothing is cast on a foe for the rest of the run: a rogue used "Vanish, Gouge", the Gouge put
  it back into the fight, and it died on the run ten seconds later.
- *Out of the fight is not out of the place.* A run used to end the moment the bot was out of combat. After a
  Vanish that is at once, among the foes: a rogue "got away after 1 s", began its rest at 35 % health between four
  orcs and was dead eight seconds later. A bot that is out of combat keeps going while a hostile creature (also one
  on its way home) is within 25 yards, until it is 45 yards from where it left the fight, for twelve seconds at
  most.

**A rider looks ahead too, and a pack gets no pass.** The look at the next 45 yards of the way ("Not into a pack on
the way") left out mounted bots, and from level 20 every bot rides. A level-22 rogue so rode off to its grind target
through three murlocs the pull check had refused seconds before, twice in forty seconds, and died of the second time
(live round 40; the dev instance repeated it at the same place). A rider is checked against what would really have
it in its aggro radius (plus 2 yards; roads lead past camps), a walker as before. After keeping away from one strong
roamer the same creature was not stepped aside for again for three minutes, so the way past it stayed open (gone
since live round 46, below); a pack never got such a pass (the first build was "clear of it after 1 s", started the same task again and rode into the same
murlocs thirteen seconds later). The bot moves until none of the pack is within 30 yards, the task ends (`ends
grind after 7 s: a pack on its way`), and the second time within ten minutes the task's target is set aside for a
quarter of an hour, a grind target at once: `sets grind (target Dire Condor) aside for 15 min: a pack it cannot take
stood on its way there 2 times`. On the dev instance the rogue kept away five times in 40 seconds, went to a condor
on another side and fought seven single fights there in the next three minutes.

**Around a pack, not away from it** (live round 42: 36 tasks in 22 minutes ended on "a pack on its way", and the
quests handed in fell for old and new bots alike). Two changes: the creatures within 30 yards of the place the bot
is going to fight at (an objective, a grind spot, an interaction, an event) are not "on its way", the pull check
decides about them when it is there; and a pack that does stand on the way is walked around, as a player would: a
point beside the pack on the side the way does not lead to, the pack's radius plus its aggro radius plus 8 yards
from its middle, with nothing else hostile on the way there and a path to it (`StartDetour`). The task goes on from
there (`goes around 4 creatures on its way ...`, `went around 4 creatures on its way after 6 s`). Only when there
is no such point on either side, or after three walks around within a minute and a half, the bot keeps away as
described above and the task ends.

**Not staying when the run is clearly cheaper.** A bot with a defensive spell ready stayed in a fight whenever the
spell made it affordable: `stays in a fight against 3 foes at 86% health: the fight would cost it about 74%, the run
about 9% (used Evasion)`; the Evasion ran out, the rogue was at 30 % and died on the run it then tried. It stays that
way only when the run would cost at least 0.6 times the fight.

**A foe that runs for help brings it** (live round 41, the first window with the new counting: of 21 pulls of
their own 18 brought exactly the expected number of foes, 3 more, none fewer). Two of the three were the deaths of
a level-12 warrior, among troggs ("1 expected, 1 more possible", three came) and kobolds ("2 expected", four): both
kinds run for help at 15 % health (SmartAI action "flee for assist"; 823 creature entries have it: troggs, kobolds,
murlocs, gnolls ...) and come back with the nearest creature that would help them within the core's 30 yards.
`WorldIndex::FleesForHelp` knows them from `smart_scripts`. The pull check adds that creature for every sure foe
that flees (two at most): it counts 75 % for a character that fights in melee and 40 % for a hunter, mage, warlock
or priest, who kill most runners on their way (`Escape::FetchedShare`; `2 more would join (Stonesplinter Scout 12
perhaps, Stonesplinter Trogg 12 if one runs for help)`). The spot verdict raises the nearest spawn of the target's
faction within 30 yards to that share. With it both pulls of the warrior come out above its limit.

**A camp is not more than three "may come" per ring.** The shares for the creatures around a spot (a third each
within 30 yards, a seventh each up to 45) stand for creatures that may come into the fight while it lasts; in a
valley with fourteen troggs within 45 yards they added up to more than four further foes, and a level-17 paladin's
fight against one trogg five levels below it came out at 202 % of what it has. Each ring counts for at most three
creatures' worth now (0.9 and 0.45 in all); a ring of three or fewer is judged as before.

**Cost by level difference, measured.** From 3,300 single-foe fights the bots won on the integration server (one
evening): against a foe 2 levels below it a melee character's fight costs 0.77 of one against its own level, 3
below 0.71, 4 below 0.73, 6 below 0.62; for casters 0.91, 0.78, 0.69, 0.75. The model (13 % less per level, at
most five levels) says 0.76, 0.66, 0.57, 0.50: it does not overstate what weaker foes cost, it understates it a
little. Above the bot: one level 1.09 (melee) and 1.35 (casters); the model says 1.3. Nothing was changed for this.

**A druid runs in Travel Form** (from level 16; after Nature's Grasp and Barkskin, which it cannot cast in the
form): a level-23 druid ran from three gnolls on two legs and was dead after eight seconds.

**No run a bot would not live through** (live round 44: six deaths, every one a bot on the run; 23 runs got
away). A rogue left its fights at 46, 36, 32 and 26 % health with two or three creatures in melee and lived five to
nine seconds each time; a level-12 paladin left two troggs at 34 % with `of 7 directions 7 led past other
creatures`. The old rule let a bot run whenever the run cost clearly less than the fight, also when it cost more
than the bot had. Now:
- a bot does not turn its back when the run would cost 90 % or more of the health it has; it stays, casts what
  protects it and fights on (`stays in a fight ...: ... the run about 113% (it would not live through it)`);
- when the first leg of a run leads past further creatures and no spell went out that shakes the foes off (Sprint,
  a nova, a fear, Vanish ...), the run is called off at once: `left a fight ...: no open way, fights on after 0 s`;
- what protects a bot is cast when the second creature is on it, not when it turns to run: Evasion, Barkskin,
  Divine Protection, Shield Wall, Ice Barrier, once per fight (`Escape::StepDefend`; the fight line ends `, used
  Evasion`). The rogue's Evasion used to go out with the run, where it dodges nothing; it is no longer cast for a
  run. Its pulls of two orcs three levels below it had been judged affordable and took all its health twice in two
  minutes;
- a shaman slows the nearest foe with Frost Shock before it runs;
- the look for hostile creatures after a Vanish (see above) left out everything six or more levels below the bot:
  the rogue "got away after 1 s" from level-18 murlocs, sat down among them and died. They count down to ten
  levels below now.
The outcome of every run is in its line (`got away`, `died on the run`, `held fast`, `could not shake them off`,
`no way out`, `no open way`), so the share that ends alive can be counted.

**Home from a place that keeps killing it.** The rogue died five times within sixty yards in eleven minutes; the
place was set aside from the second death on (`5 deaths at this place: it is set aside ... for 240 min`, in
Server.log), but the bot walks back to its corpse, stands up in the middle of the place, and every way out leads
through what killed it. From the third death at one place (within six hours) it goes home instead, like a bot in
a death loop among creatures far above it: resurrected at the price of the spirit healer and moved to its bind
point (`... it gives the place up and goes home`).

**A warlock's pet goes first, and it is a Voidwalker.** The trace of a level-23 warlock showed its pet at 99 to
100 % health through every fight, the creature on the warlock from its first cast. Two causes: mod-playerbots
never sends a pet at a target by itself (its "pet attack" is a chat command; the pet joins when its master is
hit), and its strategy for a demonology warlock is "felguard", whose fallback below level 50 is the Succubus from
level 20 on, which holds nothing. Now a warlock without a Felguard gets the strategy "voidwalker"
(`BotDriver::ResetStrategies` / `SyncStrategies`), and when the pull check lets a pull pass the pet is sent at the
target and the warlock waits until it is there (four seconds at most) before its own first cast. On the dev
instance: `fight 25 s: 1 foe at once (Dragonmaw Raider level 24), health 98% -> 100% ..., mana 92% -> 53%`, the
creature "on something else" in every line of the trace and the pet at 87 % at the end; in the fights before it
the warlock lost 16 to 22 % of its health. A hunter's pet goes with its master's first shot already.

**Attacked in the saddle.** The paladin of the next paragraph, and a shaman a round later (`fight 64 s: 1 foe at
once (Root Thresher level 7) ..., died, its target at 100% health, no damage done in its first 12 s (last action "",
without a target)`), had both just taken "The Kessel Run": the quest puts the character on an elekk (source spell
31973, a mount aura, 15 minutes). mod-playerbots gets off an ordinary mount when it is attacked, but not off this
one, and a mounted character neither fights nor runs. A character that is attacked and still mounted (or in a
vehicle) after four seconds now gets off: `gets off its mount to fight: attacked in the saddle for 4 s`. The quest
is not failed by that (the core casts the source spell on accept and nothing else looks at it; the quest's talks
count on foot). On the dev instance a paladin put on the elekk beside a trogg got off after 4 seconds and won.

**A caster runs to range while its foe is rooted** (`Escape::StepBack`). The fight trace (below) showed what a
frost mage does: it opens at 30 yards, casts Frost Nova when the creature is on it, then walks backwards five
yards at a time (mod-playerbots' "flee", `Playerbots.FleeDistance`) until it is out of melee reach, about ten yards
away, and casts again; the creature is back on it a second and a half after the root ends, and the rest of the
fight is cast in melee. A level-23 mage lost 44 % of its health to one creature a level above it that way, and
19 % in a fight in which it could Blink. Now a mage, warlock, priest, hunter or druid in caster form whose every
attacker in reach is rooted or stunned for three seconds more, one of them within 14 yards, stops its cast and runs
to 24 yards from it, away from it or up to a radian to either side, not past other creatures, not into water, with
a path and in sight of the foe; the fight line says `ran to range 1 time`. Three fights of that mage on the dev
instance against level-23 creatures: with the run it ended at 56 % and 66 % health, in the one in which the root
broke at once at 32 %. A small sample; the learned cost of its fights will show it.

What the traces showed for the other two: a level-20 shadow priest without a wand opens with its instants and a
Mind Blast and then casts Smite until the creature is dead, 65 % of its mana for one creature of its level (its
shield keeps its health at 100 %); a wand would end the fight for nothing. A level-23 demonology warlock's
fights cost it 16 % health and 22 % mana, though its pet stood at full health throughout: the creature was on
the warlock from the first cast.

**The wand in place of a filler** (`OrderService::StepWand`; the owner, 2026-11-13: wands are the guild leader's to put
into the storage, the casters take them from there, which they do). mod-playerbots' casters reach "shoot" last: the
priest above cast its Smites with a wand in its hand. Against one creature, at half health or more:
- a priest that has no Mind Flay yet shoots its wand between its Mind Blasts once its pain is on the target and its
  mana is at 85 % or less; a Smite or Holy Fire that has just begun is stopped for it;
- a priest, mage or warlock finishes a creature at 20 % health or less with the wand when its own mana is below
  60 %.
Not with two creatures on it (every second counts more than the mana there), not in Shadowform, and not while a
Mind Blast, a heal or a shield is being cast. The fight line ends `, used its wand`. Measured on the dev instance
with a level-20 priest: before, 58 to 76 % of its mana for one creature of level 19 to 21 (15 to 18 seconds per
fight); with the wand 14 to 44 % for creatures of level 16 to 20 (14 to 18 seconds), so about half the mana in the
same time. The opening (shield, pain, Mind Blast) is still about a third of its mana.

With `GuildAdventure.Debug` a character that uses mana writes a line every two seconds of a fight: `fight trace
8 s: health 90%, mana 75%, casts nothing, standing; Skeletal Horror at 53% health, 3 yd away, on the bot, rooted`.

**Twelve seconds without damage.** A level-11 paladin stood 62 seconds in a fight against one creature of its
level, its target at full health to the end, never healed itself, never ran, and died; nothing in the log says why.
A fight in which the foes have lost nothing after twelve seconds now notes what the bot was doing at that moment:
`..., died, no damage done in its first 12 s (last action "...", without a target, rooted)`.

**The death line says what the bot died of.** `last fought` named the last creature the bot had ever fought: a druid
died of fatigue on a sea route and its line named a creature of another zone, eight minutes and a voyage earlier.
A fight that ended more than 20 seconds before the death is given with its age (`last fought Dark Strand Fanatic
(level 16) 8 min before`), and the line says `not in a fight`, `of fatigue in deep water (no fight)` (the core's
"dark water") or `drowned (no fight)` (a minute or more under water).

**Live round 46: the level factor, the helper's pack, no pass for a strong roamer.**
- *Creatures below the bot cost more than the estimate said.* Measured on the integration server over about 3,300
  single fights the bots won: against a creature of its own level 1.00, three levels below 0.71 (melee) to 0.78
  (casters), four below 0.69 to 0.73, five below 0.70 to 0.84. The estimate took 0.87 per level (0.66, 0.57, 0.50).
  The same factor divides a fight's cost when the bot learns from it, so a bot that fought creatures below its level
  learned a cost for its own level that was too high: a shaman's went from 0.39 to 0.51 in one round of crocolisks
  one to five levels below it, a tank's to 0.30, and spots of their own level were then refused for them.
  `CostPerLevelBelow` is 0.92 now (0.78, 0.72, 0.66). The learned values correct themselves with the next fights
  (a moving average); nothing is reset.
- *The helper does not come alone.* A foe that runs for help comes back with the nearest of its kind within 30
  yards, and what stands within the assist radius of that one comes too. The fight's own estimate knew that
  (`AddFetched`), the check before a pull and the spot verdict counted the helper only: a level-17 warrior pulled
  "1 expected, 1 more possible" among gnolls twice in ten minutes and had four on it both times, the second its
  death. Both count up to two of the helper's neighbours now, at the helper's share (75 % for a melee character,
  40 % for one that fights at range); the pull line says `..., Riverpaw Bandit 17 with it`, `.ga admin spot` says
  "and so do up to two that stand with that one".
- *No pass for a strong roamer.* A level-14 mage kept away from a level-26 rare beside a quest giver, started the
  same pickup again 26 seconds later, walked into the rare (the three-minute pass) and was dead in two hits. The
  pass is gone: the bot keeps away every time, and the planner counts it against the task's target as it does for a
  pack: the second time within ten minutes the target is set aside for a quarter of an hour (`sets pickup (target
  ...) aside for 15 min: a creature far above its level stood on its way there 2 times`).

**Live rounds 47 and 48: water, a rider's pet, the armour a mage never puts on.**
- *A fight in the water costs what it costs on land.* The factor of three came from a druid that stayed in aquatic
  form; `LeaveTravelForm` ended that. Measured over one night: 83 single fights in or under water of 14 bots, none
  lost, at the cost of their fights on land (a hunter 0.12 against 0.10, a priest 0.35 against 0.29, a rogue 0.16
  against 0.18, a shaman 0.25 against 0.27). The factor is gone from the check before a pull, the spot verdict and
  the decision to leave a fight. It had refused pulls in every pond: `Hunterbm does not pull Young Wetlands
  Crocolisk (level 22): 1 more would join (Fen Dweller 21); the fight would cost it about 147%`, while its fights
  there ended at 94 to 100 % health.
- *A rider's pet counts.* The core puts a pet away when its master mounts and calls it back at the dismount, and
  the check before a pull runs while the bot rides up to its target: the pet counted as absent and every foe as one
  the bot fights alone (at least 40 % each, the cost of a bot that has learned nothing). `FightNeed` takes a pet
  that is put away for the ride as there.
- *The armour a mage never puts on* (`OrderService::StepSelfBuff`). mod-playerbots' mage casts an armour spell
  only once it knows Mage Armor (level 34) or Molten Armor; nothing asks for Frost Armor or Ice Armor alone. All
  three mages of the integration server (levels 16, 24, 25) fought without one (their saved auras: Arcane Intellect
  only; the level-51 mage of the probe guild has its Mage Armor). A mage without any armour spell on casts Ice
  Armor, else Frost Armor, while it does not know Mage Armor. Looked at every five seconds, not mounted, not while
  it casts or runs. Line: `Magefrost puts on Frost Armor (mod-playerbots does not at its level)`. (Paladin auras
  and hunter aspects were looked at too: they are not among the saved auras, so the database cannot say whether
  they are on; the dev instance's paladin had an aura.)
- *What a mage's fight looks like* (the dev instance's trace, a level-24 frost mage against wolves of level 19 to
  21 that came at it): the creature is on the mage at the start, Frost Nova, the run to 24 yards takes four
  seconds, two Frostbolts land while the creature is held, then it is back in melee for the second half of the
  fight, where every hit pushes a cast back. That half is where the 15 to 59 % of its health per creature go.
  Frost Armor slows what hits it; a second step back when the creature arrives again (Blink) is not built.

**Live round 49: creatures the bot cannot beat, patrols, the other side's guards.** A level-25 mage whose single
fights cost it 55 % was sent to lumber piles in the Warsong lumber camp and died to two level-28 Horde Scouts that
walk through it. Three gaps of the spot verdict (`Risk::JudgeSpot`, the same for kill spots, interaction spots and
places, `Risk::IsSafePlace`):
- *A creature the bot cannot beat alone counts in full.* The rings around a spot count a creature with a share (a
  third within 30 yards, a seventh up to 45): a share of the cost of the fights it joins. For a creature whose
  fight alone costs the bot more than it may spend (`Risk.MaxFightCostPercent`), a share of its cost is a share of
  the bot's deaths. Such a creature counts in full within 30 yards and 60 % up to 45 (one far off is a risk worth
  taking, two are not). `.ga admin spot`: `Horde Scout 28 at 23 yd (too strong for it alone, counts in full)`. A bot
  whose fights are cheap is not touched by this: for one that pays 20 % per creature of its level, a creature three
  levels above costs 44 %.
- *Patrols.* The verdict knew where creatures spawn, not where they walk. `WorldIndex::GetPatrolPoints` holds a
  point every 12 yards of every waypoint path of an indexed creature (140,697 points); the nearest point of each
  patrol near a spot counts like a creature that may walk in (half at most, less on a round longer than 400
  yards), and in full when the bot cannot beat it and its round is short. `Warsong Shredder 27 on patrol, its way
  37 yd from here (a round of 213 yd; counts 15%)`.
- *The other side's guards.* The mob index left out creatures without loot, which is what town and camp guards are
  (Horde Guard, Splintertree Guard, Tarren Mill Deathguard, Hammerfall Guardian, level 40 to 50). They are on the
  danger list now (never grind targets); civilians are not. At the Crossroads: `Horde Guard 40 at 23 yd (too strong
  for it alone, counts in full)`. The same for creatures with a service flag that are hostile to a side of players:
  a city's guards answer questions, to their own side (Orgrimmar Grunt, Razor Hill Grunt, Bluffwatcher, Stormwind
  City Guard carry a gossip flag, and every creature with a flag was left out).
The mage's other death of that round was on a ride through a harpy canyon (two casters of its level came at it,
the run from casters does not shake them off); that is not changed here.

**Live round 50: two foes cost 2.5 single fights, and each kind of creature has its own cost.**
- *Two foes.* The estimate let every foe still standing hit for the whole time the one before it is killed: two
  foes of the bot's level were three single fights, three were six. Measured over one night on the integration
  server, 351 fights against two foes: the 291 that were won cost 1.9 times the bot's single fights (per bot 1.1 to
  2.3 for the old nine), 9 were lost, 51 left. The second foe seldom hits from the first second, and part of a
  fight's cost is mana and the way in, which a second foe does not double. Each of the others still standing
  counts half a foe now (`Escape::OthersShare`): two foes are 2.5 single fights, three 4.5. The same in the check
  before a pull, the spot verdict (`NeedOf`), `Risk::CanFight` and the decision to leave. "A pull it cannot afford"
  was 5 to 8 minutes per round for the bots whose single fights cost 27 to 39 %: for them every pair was refused.
- *Each kind of creature has its own cost* (`BotRuntime::foeCost`, table `ga_bot_foe_cost`). A level-17 mage's fights
  cost it 23 % on average: 0 to 8 % against boars, and 66 %, 98 % and twice its life against Black Dragon Whelps of
  its level (they cast, it cannot hold them off). One average for all sent it back to the whelps and kept it from
  pairs of boars. A bot remembers what a fight with each kind of creature costs it, against one of its own level
  (the mean of its first three fights with the kind, then a running average; a death never lowers it). From the
  second fight with a kind on (or the first that took 80 %), the check before a pull and the spot verdict use the
  kind's number, not below half the bot's average. A kind that costs it one and a half times its average and at
  least half its strength no longer raises the average. Lines: `Bommbang has learned that a fight with Black Dragon
  Whelp costs it about 92% (its fights cost 30% on average): it judges that kind by itself from now on`; `.ga bot
  plan` lists `kinds of creature that cost it more`. Per character, not shared: what a kind costs depends on the
  class (creatures with mana cost a druid 1.8 times its other fights and a shaman 0.8 times).
- The fight line of a single fight says `, it was attacked` when the bot had not begun it.

**Live rounds 50 and 51: rested before a walk through hostile ground; out of a camp the way it came.**
- *Rested before the walk.* After a fight a bot rests below 65 % health. A level-17 warrior set out at 80 % for a
  target 211 yards away through the Riverpaw gnolls, was attacked at 65 %, two became four, and neither staying nor
  running would have saved it. When the straight line to the task's target is longer than 60 yards and has hostile
  creatures of about the bot's level along it (the road map's danger; the last 30 yards belong to the target), the
  bot rests first until it has 90 % of its strength. Not in the saddle, once per target, and not while something
  hostile is within 30 yards. On the dev instance six such rests in a minute and a half took 1, 1, 4, 7, 15 and
  35 seconds (the last one a bot at 32 % health without food). Line: `rested 4 s: health 69% -> 94%, ate Stormwind
  Brie, before a walk of 404 yd past level-30 creatures, ended by: rested`.
- *Out of the place the way it came.* A level-20 warrior had fought its way into a gnoll camp, called its next
  pull off ("3 more would join"), was given a task 515 yards away, turned to walk there through the rest of the
  camp and had three gnolls on it four seconds later, with no direction open. After a pull that was called off,
  when hostile creatures stand within 28 yards, the bot goes back the way it came (its trail) until none is within
  30 yards, and only then turns to its next task (`Escape::BackOut`; the keep-away of a pack carries it on). Line:
  `backs out of the place after the pull it called off: 3 creatures within 28 yd (the nearest: Redridge Brute level
  18, 12 yd away)`, then `kept away from ...: clear of it after N s`.

**Live round 52: who really joins, and a creature far above the bot.**
- *The shares of creatures that may join, as counted.* The fight line of an own pull says how many foes the check
  expected and how many more were possible; the integration server's night gives 763 such pulls. A creature
  counted as sure came in 55 of 100 cases ("2 expected": 1.55 foes on average); a creature that "may walk in" or
  that a fleeing foe might fetch came in 11 of 100 (468 pulls of "1 expected, 1 more possible": 1.11 foes). The
  sure ones stay whole: a pull has to be survivable when they all come. The others counted half (wanderers) and
  75 % or 40 % (fetched, for melee and ranged characters); they count a quarter, and 35 % or 20 %. The rings of
  the spot verdict, which stand for the same creatures before the bot is there, go from a third and a seventh to
  a fifth and a tenth. `.ga admin spot` says "counts a quarter / a fifth / a tenth".
- *Four levels above the bot is too strong, whatever the estimate says.* The cost per level is capped at five
  levels, so for a bot whose fights are cheap a boar seven levels above it "cost 48 %": Bellygrub, level 24, wanders
  among the level-16 boars of "Redridge Goulash" and killed a level-19 warrior and a level-17 paladin (twice in 39
  seconds: it stood up at its corpse beside the boar). Three changes: in the spot verdict such a creature counts in
  full within 30 yards and costs at least all the bot has (`the fight would cost about 133%`); the look-out for
  strong roamers also sees an ordinary creature four levels above the bot once the bot is within its aggro range
  plus 8 yards (`keeps away from Bellygrub (level 24), 10 yd away`; rares, elites and patrols are seen from 35
  yards as before); and a bot whose corpse lies within 30 yards of a creature worth three levels more than it
  takes the spirit healer (`will take the spirit healer: its corpse lies beside Bellygrub (level 24)`).
- *Only what can reach the bot.* The Sewer Beast, a level-50 rare, swims in Stormwind's canals below the bridges.
  A level-25 rogue "kept away" from it four times in 70 seconds, 26 to 33 yards above it, on its way to a hand-in
  in the city; the hand-in was set aside and the place avoided, which sent its next walk of 306 yards over
  Goldshire. The look-out now asks for a whole path between the bot and the creature that is at most twice the
  straight line (or 25 yards more): from the streets to each of the canal's spawns the core's path is incomplete.
  A creature in the water to which there is no path counts only at about the bot's own height (it may come
  ashore). Caged creatures and creatures behind a wall are the same case.

**Careful pulls (the owner, 2026-11-13).** His words: [quote left out]. Until then the pull check could only say no: of 521 objective tasks of one live
window 110 ended "a pull it cannot afford". `GuildAdventure.Pull.Careful` (1; a bot setting):
- *Where the fight will be.* Who joins a fight depends on where it is: the creatures of the target's faction within
  the core's 10 yards of it come wherever the fight is; everything else only comes when the bot enters its own aggro
  radius. `JudgePull` counts for a place: the target's own for a class that fights in melee, the place it stands at
  for a caster without a pet (its distance from mod-playerbots, about 25 yards; a pet runs up to the target and
  brings what stands there, so a hunter and a warlock are judged at the target as before).
- *One that stands alone first.* When the target has company (or the fight is not affordable), the bot looks at the
  five nearest creatures of the same kind within 45 yards every two seconds and turns to one that would come alone:
  `turns to a Skeletal Mage that stands alone (34 yd) instead of the one with 2 beside it (Skeletal Warrior 21
  perhaps, Skeletal Warrior 22)`.
- *Else one creature is brought out.* A bot that fights in melee plans a pull to its own side (`PlanPull`) and takes
  it when fewer creatures count there and the fight is affordable there. With a ranged opener: the bow, gun,
  crossbow or thrown weapon in its hands, else a spell of its class (Hand of Reckoning, Avenger's Shield, Exorcism;
  Earth Shock, Lightning Bolt; Faerie Fire (Feral), Moonfire, Wrath; Death Grip, Icy Touch, Death Coil; Heroic Throw,
  Taunt; what its stance or form allows, what it has the power for). It walks to a point at most 28 yards from the
  creature, casts, and waits there until the creature is with it. Without an opener, and only for a creature that
  attacks on sight: it walks to just inside the creature's aggro radius and 10 yards back along the way it came.
  mod-playerbots is held meanwhile and gets the target back when the creature is within 6 yards. Lines: `pulls
  Pygmy Venom Web Spider (level 19) to it by walking into its sight (8 yd) and 10 yd back: 1 fewer would join than
  at its place (Starving Dire Wolf 20 perhaps)`, `pulls ... to it with Throw from 27 yd: ...`, then `pull of ...:
  the creature came to it after 7.3 s, 18 yd from where it stood`. Other ends: `the creature fights from a
  distance, the bot goes to it` (a caster or archer that does not come: after 2.5 seconds without it coming closer),
  `the creature did not come for it`, `called off (something else attacked it / it fights someone else / it did not
  get to its place / it runs)`; a pull that did not work is not tried on that creature for 45 seconds.
- *The same pull for a group* (`Escape::BeginPull(player, rt, target, fightAt)`): the bot opens on the creature the
  caller names and brings it to the place the caller names (a dungeon run's tank and its group's place). While
  `BotRuntime::pull.active` nothing else may move the bot or give it a target; `OrderService::Update` steps every
  pull four times a second; `Escape::CancelPull` hands the bot back.
- Why line of the planner: "Pulling a creature out of its group".

**Rests only below the leader's thresholds (the owner, 2026-11-13).** [quote left out]: of the 646 rests of one live window 285 had begun above both thresholds, every
one of them the rest before a walk through hostile ground of rounds 50 and 51 (to 90 %, 3824 seconds together).
That rest is a setting of its own now, `GuildAdventure.Rest.BeforeWalk` (percent; a bot setting), and off by
default. What still starts a rest above the thresholds: a fight the bot's own fights say it cannot afford with
what it has (`waits with ...: it rests first`; 37 of the 646, mostly a second or two), and going ashore for air.

**Drinking above the mana threshold (the owner, 2026-11-13, a second time: [quote left out]).** Two causes, neither of them a rest that began above the
thresholds:
- *mod-playerbots drinks by itself.* Its grind strategy has "drink" and "food" as default actions, and they judge
  by their own numbers: drink below 85 % mana (a constant in `DrinkAction::isUseful`), food below
  `Playerbots.LowHealth`. A bot working on an objective so drank after nearly every fight without any rest of the
  module: the leader's paladin took ten drinks in five minutes with "0 rests" in its status line. The module puts
  its own versions of the two actions into each bot's AI context (`BotDriver::GuardConsumables`, once a minute and
  after a login): they add the leader's thresholds (`Rest.BelowMana`, `Rest.BelowHealth`) and leave everything
  else to mod-playerbots. No patch of mod-playerbots.
- *A rest of the module ate and drank up to both "until" values once it ran.* A rest begun for health at 60 % drank
  at 80 % mana (170 rests in 94 minutes on the integration server drank although they had begun at 40 % mana or
  more, against 77 below it). Now food is for health below `Rest.BelowHealth` and drink for mana below
  `Rest.BelowMana`, each on its own, at the rest's start or while it runs; the rest ends when what it was for is
  at its "until" value. The rare rest before a fight the bot cannot afford may still use both, the drink only once
  the health is back at its "until" value and the bot is still short (a mage's rest begun for health at 48 % drank
  at 49 % mana three times in one round, because health and mana together were too little; the food alone mended it).

**Consumables out of the guild storage, one piece at a time (the owner, 2026-11-13).** [quote left out] What the rest and the fight do with it (the storage side: docs/storage.md section 9):
- *In a rest.* A character with First Aid bandages itself first when the rest began for its health (its own
  bandage or one out of the storage, the best its skill allows; once per rest). Then food for health and drink for
  mana as before, but from the storage when the bot carries none: one piece, taken out in the second it is used.
  The bags are not filled from the storage any more, and while the storage has food or drink for a bot it buys
  none; what it still carries from a vendor is used up first.
- *In a fight* (`OrderService::StepPotion`, every 1.5 s): below `Fight.PotionBelowHealth` (35 %) a healing potion;
  a mana user below `Fight.PotionBelowMana` (15 %) a mana potion while its target has more than a quarter of its
  health left. The best potion of its bags and the storage. A character that heals itself does that first (it
  begins at 45 %). One potion per fight is the game's rule.
- *On a task with fights*: a scroll of the main stat (and elixirs, when `Storage.Supply.Elixirs` is switched on;
  it is off by default), looked at once a minute with the other supplies (not for every fight: a buff of half an
  hour for the fights of a quest objective, a grind, an escort or a quest event, one scroll per bot per half
  hour; nothing for walks, hand-ins, vendor trips, farm orders or dungeons).
- The pieces of each kind and the two thresholds are bot settings (`Storage.Supply.Provisions`, `.Potions`,
  `.Bandages`, `.Scrolls`, `.Elixirs`, `Fight.PotionBelowHealth`, `Fight.PotionBelowMana`), per guild and per bot.

**A pull the rested bot could afford: it rests first (round 72).** Since the bots drink only below the leader's
mana threshold they stand before their next target at about 80 % of their strength, where mod-playerbots had
topped them up to 85 % mana after every fight. The pull check answered "rest first" only for a single foe and
refused a target with company outright: `does not pull Syndicate Mercenary (level 31): 2 more would join ...; the
fight would cost it about 73% and it has 82% (limit 80%)`, and the task ended. Task endings on a refused pull rose
from 20 in 27 minutes to 51 in 22. Any pull the rested bot could afford now gets `waits with X (level N): 2 more
would join (...); the fight would cost it about 73% and it has 82%: it rests first`, and that rest eats and drinks
at once, also above the leader's thresholds: the pull check has said what the fight needs. It is the one case in
which a bot drinks above `Rest.BelowMana`; without a waiting pull a drink above the threshold comes only once the
health is back and the bot is still short of a fight (section 7 B27). What a pull asked for is served by the one
rest that follows it, and no such drink is taken above the mana a rest ends at (`Rest.UntilMana`): the request
had held for three minutes, and a warlock at 68 % health and 92 % mana drank twice in them (round 74).

**Mages conjure (the owner, 2026-11-13: [quote left out]).**
mod-playerbots has the two actions ("conjure water", "conjure food") and triggers for an empty bag ("no drink",
"no food"), but no strategy joins them, so nothing ever cast them; the module casts the spells itself. A mage that
knows Conjure Water (level 4) and Conjure Food (level 6) buys neither kind and takes neither out of the guild
storage. With fewer than `Provisions.ConjureBelow` (4) pieces of one of them in its bags it stops where it stands,
when nothing hostile is within 25 yards, and casts the highest rank it knows until it carries twice that (`rested
7 s: ..., conjured water and food, ended by: rested`). Not in the saddle (a rider conjures at its next stop on
foot, which is after its next fight), not on a ship, not while it leads or follows a quest's NPC. In a rest for
health or mana it conjures first and drinks then. A cast that does not go out (no mana, no room in the bags) is
tried again after 15 seconds, after two minutes when the mage had stopped only for it. Before level 4 and 6 it
buys like everybody else. Conjured pieces are refused by the guild storage and have no vendor price. Open, not
built: a mage handing its water to the others of a dungeon group (mod-playerbots has "give water" triggers that
no strategy uses either).

**Three findings of the dungeon work (2026-11-13).**
- *A roamer on the way: around it, and no new keep-away while it is not getting nearer.* A squad on a road in
  Westfall kept away from Vultros (a level-26 rare that walks about there) 67 times in a row: each run ended "it is
  still near, goes on" and the next look two seconds later began the next. The look-out remembers the roamer it saw
  last and how far it was: beyond its aggro radius plus 5 yards it only counts while the gap shrinks. And when the
  bot is walking somewhere and the roamer stands on that way, the bot goes around it like around a pack (`goes
  around Samantha Swifthoof (level 40) on its way, 30 yd away; it was riding`), three times in a minute and a half
  at most; only then, or without a way around, it keeps away as before.
- *Rests without food or drink.* A bot that never passes a hub (a recruit, a boosted test bot, a bot back from a
  long dungeon run) has nothing to eat or drink and nothing sent it for some: a paladin rested 37 of 80 minutes,
  39 rests of up to 180 seconds with "no food, no drink". Three rests in a row of 15 seconds or more that had no
  food for the health or no drink for the mana they were for send the bot to a vendor that sells what it lacks,
  wherever one stands in its region (`goes to a vendor (..., 1240 yd): 3 rests in a row without food or drink`),
  unless the guild storage holds drink for it. The provisions level (8) and the least money (1 silver) hold. Inside
  a dungeon the planner's upkeep does not run: a run has to send its bots before it starts.
- *A piece the bot cannot put on* (docs/storage.md section 9).

Not built, and reported instead: a bot whose last stretch to a quest giver is refused ("5 level-24 creatures stand
together on the way") stays where its travel ended, which for the warrior above was inside the camp; and the waves
of a quest event are not known to the pull check.

**Careful pulls after their first live round (round 60, 2026-11-13).** In 23 minutes the live bots began 28 careful
pulls and every one wrote its ending: 19 "the creature came to it" (the fights after them: 28 of 31 against one foe,
none lost), 4 called off because something else attacked the bot, 2 "the creature fights from a distance", 2 "the
opener did not go out". What the round showed, and what changed:
- *The opener from the saddle.* Six of 21 ranged pulls ended `could not open on ... (N tries, the last cast result
  64)`: 64 is `SPELL_FAILED_NOT_MOUNTED`, the bot had ridden up to its place. It gets off its mount before the
  opener and before the step into a creature's sight.
- *Creatures that stand and cast.* A kind whose pull ended "the creature fights from a distance" (Murloc Minor
  Tidecaller, twice for one druid, each a fight against two) is remembered until the next restart and gets no
  careful pull again; the `unit_class` test alone does not know them.
- *A foe that runs for help runs from where the fight is.* The count of the helper it may fetch was taken around
  the creature's own place, so a pull to the bot's side showed no gain among gnolls, kobolds and murlocs and was
  not done. The helper is now looked for within the core's 30 yards of the fight's place: the bot's stand for a
  ranged pull, the few steps back after a walk into the creature's sight.
- *Three or more only with a reserve.* Counted on the integration server over six and a half hours: of 25 fights a
  bot began with three foes expected it left 6 and died in 1 (28 of 100; with two expected 6 of 100, with one 3 of
  100), and of the nine own pulls that ended with four or more on the bot it died in five. A pull that brings three
  or more for certain is only begun when the bot could take one more of the target's kind as well (`does not pull
  ...: the fight would cost it about N% with one more of them (three or more come for certain) ...`); not for a
  squad.
- *Who came that was not expected.* `pull joiner N of M expected after S s: <creature>, its home X yd from where the
  target stood, it wanders W yd, ...; the fight is F yd from where the target stood` is written for every creature
  beyond the expected count (with `GuildAdventure.Debug` for every joiner), so the next rounds say whether the
  surprises walk in, are fetched or stood nearer than counted.

**Dense camps of creatures of the bot's level (round 62, 2026-11-13).** A gnoll field in Westfall (four Riverpaw
that stand together and six that wander around them, level 15 to 17, within sixty yards) killed three bots of level
15 and 16 four times in fifty minutes, and a gnoll camp in Redridge a level-21 warlock twice in two minutes. Read
from the live log, the Riverpaw fights of one morning: 24 own pulls (2 lost) and 44 attacks on bots walking by, 18
of them by three or more at once (2 deaths, 6 fights left). What was wrong, and what changed:
- *The corpse lies among what killed it.* The creatures that kill a bot turn for home the moment it dies, and "on
  its way home" was left out of the count of hostile creatures at the corpse: of 39 deaths of that night with
  three or more creatures on the bot, 31 found nothing hostile there. So a ghost walked back into the field
  (alive again among eight gnolls 44 seconds after its death), and a warlock rose by its soulstone 15 seconds
  after six gnolls had killed it. The killers count now: the spirit healer for a corpse among two or more
  (`will take the spirit healer: its corpse lies among N hostile creatures`), and no soulstone or Reincarnation
  there.
- *A camp is set aside after the first death in it.* A place was set aside from the second death on (or after
  one death to a foe two levels above the bot). A death with three or more creatures on the bot at once sets the
  place aside at once, for half an hour or until the bot is above them (`N creatures were on it at once: the
  place is set aside ...`, Server.log): the planner plans nothing there and routes go around it.
- *Around the whole camp.* The way around a pack went around the creatures on the bot's way only, and led past the
  rest of the field (`went around 3 creatures on its way after 7 s`, and a fight against four two seconds later,
  twice, both deaths). The pack now grows by every creature of its faction that stands within 22 yards of one of
  its creatures, and so on; the bot walks to where a straight line from it touches the camp's circle (a little
