  outside it, the side nearer to its heading first), so the way there stays clear of the whole camp, and the next
  look goes on around it (`goes around 2 creatures on its way that it cannot take together (...) and the 7 that
  stand with them`). Up to 110 yards from the bot; without such a point the bot keeps away as before and its task
  ends "a pack on its way".

**Who came unexpectedly (round 63, the first with `pull joiner` lines).** 39 lines in 25 minutes. Twelve said
nothing about the pull check and are no longer written: creatures ten or more levels below the bot (the check
leaves them out on purpose) and creatures that came after the fight had moved more than 45 yards from where it
began or had lasted more than 45 seconds (a paladin's chain of fights of 219 seconds). Six were skeletons a
creature summons when it is attacked. Of the rest most were creatures counted as "perhaps" (wanderers) that came,
which is what the share is for, and five stood still 13 to 18 yards from the target, just outside its call for
help (the core's 10 yards, measured from middle to middle): a creature of the target's faction that stands still
up to 4 yards outside that reach counts as "perhaps" now, like a wanderer.
The same round showed a waste in the escape: a paladin whose fight a level-32 elite stood near "left" it four
times in five minutes at 92 to 99 % health with one foe or none, cast Divine Protection, Lay on Hands and Hammer
of Justice, found "no open way" each time and fought on. Now the way is looked for first and the spells go out
only when the bot runs; a bot that stays casts what protects it only with two or more on it or below 60 %
health; Lay on Hands only below 35 %; and the line says why it left (`[Stalvan Mistmantle (level 32) was near]`).
(The 295 seconds "in a pull it cannot afford" of that round were two tasks of 183 and 112 seconds that ended on a
refused pull after five and one kills; the bot was not idle.)

**Creatures far below the bot (rounds 65 and 66).** A level-21 shadow priest (453 health, gear of its level)
died to four gnolls of level 14 to 16, and a round later, at level 22, to six murlocs and crawlers of level 17;
a level-27 priest had died three times that morning to murlocs of level 17 at the same shore. Of the night's 79
deaths, 11 were to creatures five or more levels below the bot. Such creatures were left out wherever the
question is what stands around a place: at a login ("entered the world with N hostile creatures"), at a corpse,
at a place to rest, and on the legs of a run (the priest's run led "past 0 other creatures" through the camp
that killed it). They count now down to twelve levels below the bot everywhere (it was five there, and ten for
pulls and packs on the way); what one of them costs in the estimate stays small (0.92 per level below), many
are still a fight. The priest's first death began 12 seconds after a server restart had put it back into the
world between the gnolls; the second while it stood enchanting its bracers 9 to 28 yards from the murlocs.

**Runs that end in a death (the morning of 2026-11-13, counted).** Of about 360 runs since 06:00, 27 ended in a
death. Begun at 80 % health or more: 5 of 244 (2 %). Begun below 60 %: 14 of 47 (30 %), and 10 of the 24 without
a getaway spell. Staying is no general answer: a bot that stayed with three or more creatures on it below 40 %
health died 7 times of 8, and with two on it at 60 % or more 3 times of 7, where a run from there ends in a death
once in a hundred; with one creature on it below 40 % it won 11 of 13. So the rule that changed is a narrow one:
with one or two creatures on it and its own target at 20 % health or less, a bot finishes the target before it
decides about a run (a rogue left two gnolls at 39 % health with its target at 5 % and died on the run ten
seconds later; at 27 % it left a whelp at 8 % and was dead after six).

**A spirit healer inside the camp (round 68).** A level-19 mage died to a level-22 orc in the Blackrock camp of
Redridge, took the spirit healer (its corpse lay beside the orc) and stood at the graveyard 98 yards away, inside
the same camp: every task was refused for its way ("passes level-23 creatures"), the walk out led through the
orcs, and it was dead again 93 seconds after its first death. When the graveyard a corpse's spirit healer stands
at lies in a place the bot keeps away from, or among creatures it cannot take, it goes home instead (the spirit
healer's price, then its bind point, which is the inn of its hub): `will go home instead: the spirit healer of
its corpse (98 yd from it) stands in a place it keeps away from or among creatures it cannot take`.

**An ordinary creature two levels up is no strong roamer (round 70).** A level-32 paladin kept away from a
Highland Thrasher (level 34, an ordinary raptor) four times in 40 seconds, each time ending its task, left its one
fight with it at 95 % health "[Highland Thrasher (level 34) was near]" and lost Arathi as a zone. The look-out
for strong roamers counts a creature's level plus what its health and damage are worth above a plain creature's,
and that surplus was rounded up: 1.1 times the health and 1.2 times the damage (most beasts of that zone) made
"two levels more", so the raptor counted as level 36, four above the bot. The surplus counts in whole levels now,
rounded down (1.32 times the strength is one level; Bellygrub with 1.75 times the health still two). A real
strong roamer is treated as before: around it when it stands on the way, else away from it, and the second time
on the way to one target sets that target aside.

**A strong roamer that turns back from a fight; riders (round 73).** Stitches, a level-35 elite that a finished
quest sends down the Raven Hill road of Duskwood, killed a level-30 warlock and a minute later a level-23 warrior
at nearly the same place. The warlock rode towards it and never looked: the look-out saw 35 yards every two
seconds, which a rider and a patrol that come towards each other cover between two looks. The warrior did keep
away, twice, and each keep-away ended `clear of it after 0 s` with Stitches 26 yards away: a creature that is
walking back from a fight (it had just killed the warlock) was left out of the look, so the bot walked on and was
dead 19 seconds later. Now a creature in that state counts (it is back on its round in seconds), and a rider
looks every second and 63 yards far. Seven minutes later it killed two members of one squad within three seconds,
"during no task": a member beside its leader did not look out at all (its fights and its way are the leader's),
and the one that had ridden ahead "went around" Stitches at 31 yards while it walked towards it. A squad member
looks out for a strong roamer itself now (packs on the way stay the leader's matter), and nobody walks around a
roamer that is coming at it: it keeps away. The look-out runs every second or two for every bot that is alive,
whatever it does (no task, a rest, a vendor, an inn): a resting bot gets up and goes.

**A login among creatures (round 70).** A level-18 warlock entered the world on a murloc shore after a server
restart ("entered the world with 4 hostile creatures within 30 yd: it looks for a quiet place first"), was
attacked within seconds and died on the run twelve seconds later. It had not walked in among them: a restart
respawns every creature at once, around a bot that had cleared the place (and creatures respawn around a bot that
is offline). A bot that enters the world with hostile creatures within 30 yards is not seen by creatures for 12
seconds (the flag a client's character has while it still loads, `UNIT_FLAG_IMMUNE_TO_NPC`; it cannot attack them
either), which is the time of its walk to a quiet place; the character's own timer ends it, whoever plays it by
then. Only at a login, never in play (section 7 B26).

**In the middle of a camp (rounds 71 and 72).** A level-32 rogue hunting panthers beside the Kurzen compound of
Stranglethorn rode into it (`keeps away from 6 creatures on its way ... (the nearest: Kurzen Medicine Man level 33,
2 yd away; it was riding)`), was "clear of it after 12 s" in a gap between the packs, and from there every task
began in the middle of 40 creatures: four escapes in four minutes (`the way it came was closed (3 creatures on
it); of 7 directions 7 led past other creatures`), a rest at 26 % health in another gap, a walk from there, four
of them on it and dead. Three changes:
- *A rider looks beyond the step it is moving on.* The look for a pack on the way measured to the end of the bot's
  current movement, and the long-distance walk moves in short steps: a rider covers one in a second or two. For a
  rider the line goes on along its heading for 15 yards beyond the step's end. (A first build went the whole 45
  yards: where the next step turns, that line ran through camps the road only passes, rider keep-aways rose from
  12 to 34 in a round and tasks ended on packs 25 to 29 yards to the side.)
- *Clear of the pack is not out of the camp.* When a keep-away from a pack ends with nothing within 30 yards, and
  when a run from a fight ends, the bot looks around: four or more creatures that would attack within 55 yards,
  at most three levels below it, half of them or more standing with another one, and on every side (no gap of
  150 degrees between two of them as seen from the bot). Then it is in the middle of a camp and goes on, back
  along its trail or in the direction with the fewest creatures, for up to 40 seconds and 160 yards, until one
  side is open: `stands in the middle of a camp (9 creatures within 55 yd, on every side): it goes on until it
  is out of it`, `kept away from ...: out of the camp after 21 s`. A field of single creatures (where a bot
  works, one at a time) is no camp.
- The place is set aside as after every keep-away, so the next task does not lead back in.
- *A camp is worked from its edge* (round 75: a druid and its quest partner were sent to a Kurzen Jungle Fighter
  two rings of packs inside the compound: two walks around, a keep-away five yards from a pack, the task ended,
  the next spawn of the same camp, the same again). The spot choice (`Risk::SaferSpot`) leaves a spawn alone
  when the straight approach to it, from 10 yards after the bot to 30 yards before the spawn, leads into the
  middle of a camp the bot (or its squad) cannot take (`Risk::EntersCamp`, "A camp as an area" below; spawns
  from 35 yards on, and for a bot inside such a camp every spawn in its middle: "Out of a camp first" below). A quest
  whose every spawn lies behind such a camp waits like any quest whose spots are too much. (The first build,
  round 79, asked the road map for any two creatures within 18 yards of the approach. No bot died at the Kurzen
  compound or the Blackrock camp any more, but in a field of beasts two stand within 18 yards of every approach:
  "Tiger Mastery", "Panther Mastery", "Raptor Mastery" and the basilisks of "Singing Blue Shards" waited for one
  to five levels, 66 "every spot of it near is too much" lines in one window. A camp is now what the camp query
  calls one; beasts and single creatures are none.)

- *The spawns count for "in the middle"* (round 78: the fifth death at that compound; the rogue stood where it
  had just killed two Kurzen, the keep-away from the next pack ended "clear", and the respawns and the packs
  beside them had it). The creatures alive around the bot and the places of the hostile spawns around it are
  looked at together; at least one of them has to be alive.

**An opener that the core calls out of range (round 78).** `could not open on Crystal Spine Basilisk with Throw
(8 tries, the last cast result 97): it walks into its sight instead`: the careful pull chose its place by the
distance on the map, the core measures in three dimensions (a creature up or down a slope is further than the map
says), and a creature that wanders has walked on by the time the bot stands there. Eight tries from the same
place, then the walk into the pack's sight that the careful pull was meant to avoid. After a try that fails for
the range the bot now steps a few yards nearer (to three yards inside the spell's range by the core's measure),
twice at most and never into the creature's sight, and tries again. For a bow, gun or thrown weapon the least
distance of the plan also includes the melee range the core adds to it.

Not covered by this: a bot that is attacked by several while it works inside a camp its quest sends it into
(a mage at the Thandol Span: three Syndicate on it during the interaction; the healing potion of the new
consumables rule is what it has there).

**A camp as an area (rounds 76 to 79).** The look for packs on the way sees creatures: two or more that would have
the bot in their aggro radius on the next 45 yards. In a camp that is too late: the way threads between the first
ones, and when the look fires the bot stands among them (a warrior walked to its quest objects through the Mosshide
camp of the Wetlands and had five on it; a shaman on a travel three minutes later, three; a rogue's route led over
a road map node inside Stonewatch Keep). The risk model now knows camps as areas, from the spawn data
(`Risk::CampAtPoint`, RiskModel.h):

- A point lies **in the middle of a camp** when four or more spawns of creatures hostile to the team stand within
  55 yards of it, two of them within 30, half of them or more with another one within 12 yards, and on every side
  of the point (no gap of 150 degrees between two of them). A field of single creatures is no camp (nothing stands
  together), and a point at a camp's edge is outside (one side is open). Patrols, rares and beasts make no camp
  (a first build took the panthers of northern Stranglethorn, 25 around one point, for one: beasts that stand
  thick are a field to hunt in, and the look for packs on the way sees two of them together). Spawns, not
  creatures: a camp whose creatures are dead for the moment is still one.
- The camp holds **for walkers up to a level** (`CampAt::walkerLevel`): its creatures are at most three levels
  below such a walker. The level is the highest from which the creatures still make a camp, so a single strong
  creature beside a camp of weak ones makes no camp of its own level. `CampAt` also carries the middle, lowest and
  highest level of those creatures, their number, their middle and radius.
- A character **cannot take** a camp when the fight model says no to three of its creatures at once, four for
  a camp with ten or more spawns around the point (`Risk::CanFight` with the camp's middle level; a squad that
  stands together counts as for spots).
- Answers are kept per map, team, 12-yard cell and height band (30 yards), so a leg costs a table look per 10
  yards.

The question for a leg of a walk is `Risk::EntersCamp(player, rt, mapId, fromX, fromY, toX, toY, &camp, &atYards,
skipStart, stopBefore)`: does this straight leg lead into the middle of a camp the character cannot take, and where.
`Risk::LegEntersCamp(mapId, fromX, fromY, toX, toY, team, walkerLevel, ...)` asks the same without a character (the
road map's links; a node: `Risk::CampAtPoint`), `Risk::InCampItCannotTake` for one point.

Where the bot quality code uses it:

- **On a walk** (`FindCampAhead`, with the look for packs, four times a second for a rider): along the movement to
  its end and up to 30 yards further along the heading, 90 yards at most. When that leads into the middle of a camp
  the bot cannot take and two or more of its creatures are alive around the place where the way enters it, the bot
  goes around them as around a pack (`goes around N creatures on its way ... [its way led into the middle of their
  camp]`), and when there is no way around, or after three walks around in 90 seconds, it keeps away and the task
  ends as for a pack (the second time within ten minutes its target is set aside). Not for the camp the task's own
  fight is in (an objective, a grind, an interaction or an event whose spot lies in that camp or within 80 yards of
  where the way enters it: the spot's verdict and the check before a pull decide there), and not while the bot
  stands in a camp already.
- **A rest** is not taken at a quiet spot in the middle of a camp (nothing within 30 yards, and everything around
  it).
- **`Risk::IsSafePlace`** says no to a place in the middle of a camp the character cannot take: the graveyard of a
  spirit healer (the bot goes home instead), a vendor, the place of a quest giver or ender, an area to explore.

What it does not do: change routes. A route leg or a road map node inside a camp is the routes' matter (the
function above is there for them); a bot whose only way leads through a camp it cannot take ends its task before the
camp and, the second time, sets the target aside.

**A fight in which nothing happens.** A warlock stood beside Manor Mistmantle for over half an hour, "in combat" at
45 % health: no fight line, no step, no task start or end. The game counts a character as fighting for as long as
any creature holds a combat reference to it, also a creature that does not attack it, that it cannot see or that
cannot reach it; mod-playerbots' AI finds no target and does nothing; and the planner leaves a fighting bot to its
AI with the task's clock stopped, so neither the stuck rule nor the rescue ends it. `TrackFight` now watches the
fight by the clock on the wall: when for 45 seconds the bot has lost no health (two points below the most seen
since), its foes have lost nothing, nobody has joined or left, it has not moved three yards and casts nothing, the
module writes who holds the fight and ends it (`CombatStop` for the bot and its pet):

`<bot> has been in a fight for N s in which nothing has happened for 45 s (health .., N on it, at (..), last action
".."): in combat with <creature> (level .., entry .., N yd away, N yd higher, health ..%, on <its target> / on
nobody, evading, cannot reach its target, the bot cannot see it); its pet .. with ..: the module ends the fight`

After that the bot walks away from the creature that held the fight, as from a roamer it keeps away from (60
yards; `Escape::WalkAway`): where it stood the same thing would begin again.

The fight line of such a fight ends with "ended by the module (nothing happened in it)", and it teaches the bot
nothing about what a foe costs. Not in a dungeon (a boss that talks), on a flight or a ship, during an escape, or
while the bot is stunned, feared or confused. The line is also the diagnosis: it names the creature that held the
fight, so the cause behind it (a creature that does not evade, an invisible one) can be dealt with where it is.

**A foe that does not die.** Bloodyo, a death knight recruited that day, stood 297 seconds in a fight with a Servant of
Grol (Blasted Lands, quest 2681 "The Stones That Bind Us") whose health bar stood at 0 %. The creature's SmartAI sets
"invincibility at 1 HP" when it resets, and at 0 to 5 % it casts Spirit Shock, says a line and makes the Stone of
Binding selectable; the credit comes from the Stone's spell hitting it (spell 10834). A kill objective never uses the
Stone, so the creature cannot die. The rule above took 297 seconds instead of 45 because the Servant kept hitting the
bot and the bot kept casting: both count as something happening, and each reset the quiet clock (Retadk, another new
death knight, had the same fight at the same place, 53 s). The death knights themselves fight as they should
(Unholymoly won 27 fights that evening, Retadk 4; the Servant was Bloodyo's only fight). Now `TrackFight` also
watches how the foes' health goes: when no foe on the bot or its target has reached a new low (one point of health
percent below the lowest seen) for 60 seconds, or one of them has stood at one health point for 15 seconds (30 in an
interaction task, whose plan may bring a creature low and then walk to an object to use on it), the fight
goes nowhere, whatever the bot does or suffers meanwhile (the 60 seconds not while another character of its group
fights within 100 yards: a healer beside its squad's fight has no foe of its own):

`<bot> has been in a fight for N s in which its foes have lost nothing for N s: <creature> (level ..) stays at one
health point (a script holds it there) / stays at N% health (immune, or a script holds it) (health ..%, last action
".."): the module ends the fight and the bot leaves that creature alone for 15 min`

The module ends the fight, the bot walks away from the creature, the pull check leaves that creature alone for 15
minutes (unless it is on the bot) and the planner does not choose its spawn for a task in that time; a task that was
about it (an objective, an interaction, a grind) ends with "a foe that does not die", and two such ends of a quest
within ten minutes set the quest aside for a quarter of an hour, like a pack on the way (`IsBlockedEnd`). Not in a
dungeon (a boss with an invulnerable phase), on a flight or during an escape. Doing the quest itself (the Stone of
Binding used on the weakened Servant) is a matter of the quest interactions.

Two more holes the same evening showed. After the module's `CombatStop` the Servant, aggressive and two yards away,
attacked again in the same moment, so the fight never ended, and the walk away from it turned into "attacked on its
way, it fights after 0 s" (the rule that a bot caught on a keep-away fights what it can take): the same fight again.
A creature the module left alone for not dying is now no creature to fight on the way: the bot runs on from it, as
from one far above it. And Retadk, the other death knight, stood "in combat" for over a quarter of an hour 14 yards
from the Servant of Sevine (rooted and stunned by its own Spirit Shock, the same script), nothing counted on it, its
travel task's clock standing still as for any fighting bot, and lost a few points of health a minute: the quiet
rule's "the bot lost two points of health" began the quiet anew each time. Health lost while nothing is on the bot
(no attacker, no target) is no fight going on any more, so that rule ends such a fight after its 45 seconds.

The walk away from what held such a fight (`Escape::WalkAway`, for this rule and the quiet rule) uses the keep-away's
legs, and with them its rules for a strong creature on a round: on bq the bot then waited 61 yards from the Servant
"until it has moved on", and its voyage waited for it as "on its way" (a creature at one health point that had just
chased it). A walk away ends once the creature is 60 yards off or the time is over, with no wait and no sight of a
roamer, and the task goes on from where the bot stands.

Asked by the maintainers after the quest interactions' test of the Stone of Binding (a level-55 bot died at the Servant
of Sevine to four Voidwalker Minions and the Servant): the Shadowsworn Warlocks around the Servants summon a Voidwalker
Minion out of combat (SmartAI, spell 5108), so the minions have no spawns. The spot verdict counts them since
"minions a camp's casters summon" (`WorldIndex::MinionOf`), and the Servant of Sevine's spawn lies in the middle of
the Shadowsworn camp, which `Risk::SaferSpot` refuses at any distance for a bot that cannot take the camp; `.ga admin
spot` for a level-55 mage there: "Shadowsworn Warlock 54 at 27 yd (near, counts a fifth), Voidwalker Minion 54 at 27
yd (near, counts a fifth) ...; the point is in the middle of a camp (14 spawns of level 54-56 ...): it cannot take it
and keeps out". The test build of the quest interactions did not have those two changes yet.

Then the same live: Lilwar (47) pulled two Wastewander Shadow Mages in Tanaris for quest 3362, "its own pull (2
expected)", four came (two Voidwalker Minions), it left at 57 % and died on the run; Shammpower the same on quest 1691.
Two holes: the Shadow Mages (and nine more casters: Dark Strand Voidcallers and Adepts, Burning Blade Apprentices,
Twilight Shadowmages, Searing Blade Warlocks ...) cast "Summon Voidwalker" 12746, which summons a pet, not a plain
creature, and `WorldIndex::MinionOf` only knew the summon effect (369 kinds of creature with a minion now, 326
before); and the check before a pull, which looks at the live creatures, did not count a minion at all: it answers no
call for help (it has an owner) and stands beside its owner, not on the bot's way, but it fights as soon as its owner
does. Every creature the pull check counts now brings its minions at its own share: "Freshone does not pull
Wastewander Shadow Mage (level 43): 3 more would join (Voidwalker Minion 43, Wastewander Shadow Mage 42 perhaps,
Voidwalker Minion 42 with Wastewander Shadow Mage); the fight would cost it about 115% and it has 99% (limit 80%)".
`.ga admin spot` now also lists the target's own minion (the verdict counted it already).

**A strong creature on its way: wait until it has moved on, and keep off its way.** Stitches again, six deaths in a
day: four bots around Darkshire kept away from him fifteen times in a quarter of an hour, "clear of it after 0-10 s"
each time, and two of them died. Read from the log: a rider is sixty yards off after a second, so the keep-away was
over at once, the task ended, the planner's next task led back onto the road (a grind spot beside it, a route along
it), and he was there; and a warrior "went around" him at 49, 19 and 12 yards within twelve seconds (the circle
around a roamer is drawn where it stands at that moment, with eight yards to spare) and was dead fifteen seconds
later. Three changes:

- **No walk around a roamer that walks or fights, or that is within 40 yards.** From such a one the bot keeps away.
- **Clear of it is not enough while it is on its way.** Sixty yards off, the bot stands and waits (`<bot> waits N yd
  from Stitches (level 35) until it has moved on`) while the roamer walks or fights within 110 yards, for 75 seconds
  at most; when it comes within sixty yards again the bot runs again (three times at most). Then the keep-away ends
  as before (`kept away from ...: clear of it after N s`).
- **Its way is no place to work or rest.** Every strong roamer on its way that a guild character sees (a patrol, a
  summoned creature, one more than 40 yards from its home) is noted with where it was and how it walks
  (`Escape::RoamerNear`, kept for 90 seconds after the last sight). For a character it is four or more levels above
  (by its health and damage, as for the look-out), a spot within 80 yards of where it was seen last, or within 60
  yards of where it walks in the next 45 seconds, waits: `Risk::JudgeSpot` says "a strong creature is walking there
  right now" (quest spots, grind spots, gather nodes, the places of quest givers, vendors and graveyards through
  `Risk::IsSafePlace`), and a rest is not taken there. Stitches comes with a quest and has no spawn and no waypoints
  in the world database, so no verdict from the spawn data could know him; this one comes from what the bots see.

For a leg of a walk there is `Escape::RoamerOnLeg(mapId, fromX, fromY, toX, toY, level, &who)` (the first 300 yards
of the leg); the routes do not ask it yet.

**Out of a camp first; the last yards on foot (rounds 81 to 83).** The Kurzen compound killed three more bots in one
night in spite of the camp rules, and two bots died "during no task". Read from the log, four mechanisms:

- A level-36 warrior rode 509 yards to the first Kurzen at the compound's northern edge, a spawn the verdict rightly
  called usable, arrived in the saddle among its neighbours and had four on it ("it was attacked").
- A pair of quest partners pulled the compound's outer Kurzen one by one, each next spawn 30 to 60 yards further in
  (the edge rule held from 70 yards on only), and stood in its middle a minute later. The leader went out ("stands
  in the middle of a camp ... out of the camp after 26 s"); its member, which follows and decides nothing, stayed in
  a fight against three and died "during no task"; the leader went back in for it and then stood four yards from
  the corpse, "Squad: waiting", and its next task, 505 yards away, began there.
- A level-36 paladin entered the world inside Stromgarde after a restart. Creatures do not see a bot for twelve
  seconds after such a login; it found no place to rest, its rest ended at once, its objective task began in the
  same second, and it used the twelve seconds to walk 50 yards to its target. When they saw it, it stood on a
  Syndicate Conjuror with five around it ("does not pull ...", "backs out ...: the nearest ... 0 yd away"), and died.
- A level-42 warrior rode to a hand-in at an object inside the Bloodsail camp of the Stranglethorn coast; the look
  for packs fired at 8 yards, a Frost Nova held it, six were on it.

Five rules:

- **The last yards are walked** (`Escape::WalksLastYards`). mod-playerbots rides a melee character up to five yards
  from its target, at twice the speed every look-out here was made for. Within 60 yards of a task's target that has
  spawns of creatures which are no friends of the bot within 40 yards, the bot goes on foot (`gets off its mount N yd
  before <target> and walks the rest`), and stays on foot while it is within 100 yards of that target. On foot the
  AI picks its target from a distance, the check before a pull runs before the bot stands among the neighbours, the
  careful pull has room, and the look for packs on the way sees them at 28 to 45 yards. Objectives, grind spots,
  interactions, quest events, pickups, hand-ins, vendors, trainers, flight masters and fishing places; not a travel
  or a voyage, not a squad member, not in a dungeon; off with `Pull.Careful`. At a hub nothing hostile has its
  spawn, and the bot rides up to the NPC as before.
- **Out of a camp first** (`Escape::Step`). A bot that stands in the middle of a camp it cannot take and has no
  fight there goes out of it before anything else: with no task (a task ended there, it waits, it entered the world
  there), while it waits for its squad, and when a new task begins whose target is more than 70 yards away. Along
  the way it came, else to the emptiest side, until one side is open (40 seconds and 160 yards at most), and its
  task, if it has one, goes on from there: `<bot> stands in the middle of a camp it cannot take (N creatures within
  55 yd; the nearest: ..) with nothing to do there / while it waits for its squad / and its next task lies
  elsewhere: it goes out of it first`, then `kept away from ..: out of the camp after N s`. The camp: by the creatures
  alive around it when four of them at once are more than it can take, or by the spawn data with one of them alive
  within 55 yards. Looked at every two seconds while idle and once per new task; after a leave not again for half a
  minute.
- **A camp is worked from its edge, also from near, also from inside.** The spot choice now refuses a spawn from 35
  yards on (was 70) when the approach, from 10 yards after the bot to 30 yards before the spawn, leads into the
  middle of a camp the bot cannot take; and a bot that stands in the middle of such a camp gets no spawn that lies
  in the middle too (so it has nothing to do there, and goes out).
- **A big camp is four at once.** "Cannot take" asked the fight model about three of the camp's creatures; for a camp
  with ten or more spawns around the point it asks about four (three bots had four Kurzen on them that night; their
  Medicine Men heal, the fight lasts, the next ones come).
- **A login among creatures.** The bot backs away from what stands within 28 yards at once (`backs out of the place
  it entered the world in: ..`), and no task starts before the twelve seconds are over ("Waiting a moment after its
  login among creatures").

And a squad member runs with its leader also when the leader keeps away from a pack or goes out of a camp
(`StepSquadFlee`; before, only when the leader ran from a fight), not when the leader steps aside for one roaming
creature. The legs of a keep-away or a run count a direction that ends in the middle of a camp the bot cannot take
as closed while another is open (a hunter that kept away from three Kurzen at the east side of the compound was led
127 yards west by its legs, each free of living creatures, into the compound's middle).

What this does not do: a leader still helps a member that fights within 30 yards, also at a camp's edge; and a spot
at the edge of a dense cluster stays usable (the check before a pull and the careful pull decide there).

**Out of drink (the owner, 2026-11-14).** [quote left out]; and: [quote left out]. Read from the live log: the guild leader, a level-39 paladin
with 37 gold, carried no drink; thirty bots drank the storage dry one piece at a time ("0 left there" after almost
every take); at a town it bought none, because a bot bought drink only while the storage had none for it and a few
pieces lay there at that moment; and the trip for a bot out of drink was bounded to vendors within 600 yards, of
which the middle of Dustwallow has none. It rested 180, 93 and 106 seconds in ten minutes. Two rules:

- **At a town it buys.** A character that uses mana and carries fewer than half a stack of drink
  (`Provisions.DrinkStack`, 40) buys up to the stack at a vendor that stands within `Provisions.HubYards` of it, and
  at any vendor it visits, whatever the guild storage holds: the storage bridges the way to the next town, a piece
  at a time, it is not the supply. (Food is as before: what the storage holds first, the cooks make it for that.)
- **With none in its bags and none in the storage it goes to a vendor at once.** The rest that finds nothing to
  drink (no piece in the bags, none in the storage, no mage in its group) ends, its task ends ("out of drink"), and
  the planner's next look sends it to the nearest vendor that sells drink, as far as it takes
  (`Provisions.TripWhenOutYards`, now 0 = no bound, up to 3000 yards; the vendor is chosen by the risk rules as any
  other): `<bot> has nothing to drink at N% mana (none in its bags, none in the guild storage): it goes to a vendor
  now`, `goes to a vendor (.., N yd): out of drink`. On the way it does not sit down for its mana (a rest for its
  health runs as always and ends when the health is back). A hand-in or pickup it was at is finished first. When no
  vendor is in reach it rests as before and does not ask again for ten minutes. Not a squad member (it follows; its
  leader's mage gives it water), not in a dungeon or on a dungeon order, not on a ship, not with a quest's NPC in
  tow; a mage conjures.

**A hunter's Auto Shot that outlives its fight; a dry member does not hold its dungeon group (the owner, 2026-11-14:
[quote left out]).** In his Scarlet Monastery Cathedral run
Hunterbm (43) rested 40 s at 37 % mana with no drink and then 155 s from 35 % mana, taking its first Moonberry Juice
in the last five seconds, with 97 of them in the guild storage, while Wartank waited 120 s "for its squad (Hunterbm
rests)". Three of its five rests in those twelve minutes had no drink, each right after a fight; the ones that
drank began after a bandage. The rest eats and drinks only while the character casts nothing
(`IsNonMeleeSpellCast`), and that counts an auto-repeat spell. The core ends a wand's Shoot when its target dies
but never a hunter's Auto Shot (`Unit::_UpdateAutoRepeatSpell` leaves spell 75 running). A player's client cancels
it, a bot has none, so the hunter stayed "casting" after its fight until something else ended the Auto Shot.

- `OrderService::StopLeftoverAutoShot` (every tick, after the fight tracking) ends Auto Shot when its target is dead,
  gone or out of the world, or when for 4 s neither the hunter nor its target fought and no pull of the module runs.
  mod-playerbots opens a fight with Auto Shot out of combat, and the first shot comes a moment later. A rest ends any
  auto-repeat spell before it eats or drinks.
- In a dungeon a group member that uses mana and has nothing to drink (none in its bags, none in the guild storage,
  no mage in its group) rests no more for its mana. It keeps up, its mana comes back as it walks, and its rests for
  health run as always. A rest only for mana ends with `nothing to drink: it keeps up with its group`. The group's
  healer is the exception: the group waits for its mana. A member with a drink drinks, and its mana from 35 % to 75 %
  takes 15 to 20 seconds.

**In a dungeon a bot rests where it stands (the owner, 2026-11-14: [quote left out]sicheres[quote left out]).** Inside an instance a rest
starts where the bot stands, beside its group: no walk to a quieter place first and no move when something comes near
(the group of his Cathedral runs had walked 22 to 58 yards away before its rests). The rest line says so:
`where it stood in the dungeon (6 hostile creatures within 30 yd)`. No rest in deep water and the end of a rest at a
fight stay as they are.

**No rest in the water (the owner, 2026-11-14).** [quote left out]. Two causes. (1) Whether a bot stands in water was asked by its feet
(`Escape::WaterAt`: the water's level against the bot's height). The path finder keeps a bot at the surface of deep
water, and there the answer flips between "in the water" and "dry" by centimetres: the guild leader began a rest
floating on 1.7 yards of swamp water (the take-over line of that second: height 30.25, floor 28.52; his client then
showed it swimming), and the "quieter place" a rest walks to could lie on the water as well. (2) With no dry spot
within 70 yards the module did not rest at all, and mod-playerbots' own drink and food actions tried in the water,
where the core takes the drink off a swimmer at once, and waited out their ten to twenty-seven seconds each time.
Now:

- `Escape::WaterDepth` gives the water's level above the floor under the bot (0 on dry ground, on a pier or bridge),
  and a place is no place to rest in water deeper than 0.6 yards (`Escape::TooWetToRest`): for the rest's start, the
  spot it walks to (`Escape::FindRestSpot`) and the look after the walk. Shallow water is ground.
- A bot in such water whose rest is due (to drink, eat, bandage itself, conjure) goes to dry ground first: the
  quietest dry spot the path finder has a whole way to, within 70 yards and then up to 150 (`Getting out of the water
  to rest`; the walk has the time the way takes swimming), and rests there: `.. went N yd ashore first`.
- With none in reach it does not rest in the water and goes on with its task; it looks again every five seconds
  (`<bot> needs a rest (health H%, mana M%) in D yd of water at (..) and finds no dry ground within 150 yd: it does
  not rest in the water and goes on`, once in two minutes).
- mod-playerbots' drink and food actions are not useful in such water (`BotDriver::GuardConsumables`), and the guard
  is put on every tick: an AI that is new (a hand-over from its owner, the end of watch mode) had mod-playerbots' own
  actions again for up to a minute and drank below 85 % mana.
- A rest the AI had begun ends when the owner takes the character over (it stayed open while he played and was
  logged as "rested 425 s").

`.ga admin spot` names the water at its point by depth ("1.7 yd of water there: no place to rest").

**Food only below the health threshold (the owner, 2026-11-14).** [quote left out]. No fix was lost (the rest code of the live head
was the branch's). It was the rest a pull asks for ("waits with ..: it rests first", round 72): in it "not enough for
the fight" was a reason to eat at any health below 100 %, and the guild leader ate at 77 % health and 51 % mana (61
of the day's 2916 rests ate at 65 % health or more). Now food is for health below `Rest.BelowHealth` in every rest;
the rest for a fight drinks (up to `Rest.UntilMana`) and ends when the bot has enough or has all a rest gives by the
leader's rules. The check before a pull waits for a rest only when such a rest makes the pull affordable (what the
bot has after it: its health as it is, or `Rest.UntilHealth` when it is below the threshold, and its mana at
`Rest.UntilMana`); else it is "does not pull", as for any pull the bot cannot afford. A rest for a fight starts only
when it can give something.

**A pull from the side away from the others (the owner, 2026-11-14).** [quote left out] The live
lines: "turns to a Mirefin Murloc that stands alone (29 yd) instead of the one with 3 beside it", "pulls Mirefin
Murloc (level 36) to it with Hand of Reckoning from 27 yd", and three to five seconds later three more were on the
bot, their homes 15, 17 and 24 yards from where the target had stood: on its way to the paladin. Two causes:

- *The count looked around the creature's own place only.* The core does not make a creature's call for help once:
  it repeats it every `CreatureFamilyAssistancePeriod` (3 s) for as long as the creature fights, within
  `CreatureFamilyAssistanceRadius` (10 yd) of wherever it is then. What a pulled creature runs past, and what stands
  where the fight is, comes with it. `JudgePull` now counts a creature that would help the target as sure when it
  stands within the call's reach (10 + 2 yd) of the target **or of its way to the fight's place**, and as "perhaps"
  a few yards beyond.
- *The bot pulled from where it happened to come from.* `PlanPull` put the pull place on the line from the creature
  to the bot. When that run would bring company, `BestVerdict` now also looks at the places on the far side of the
  creature (`AwaySides`: straight away from where the others of its camp stand, the ones within 30 yards that would
  help it, and 45 degrees to either side of that), at the opener's reach less two yards (28 at most), and takes the
  place with the cheapest fight that the bot has a whole way to, a way that passes nobody's sight (the creature's
  own included): `pulls <creature> to it with Exorcism from 28 yd, from the side away from the others`. With no such
  place the pull is not made, as before ("does not pull").

A paladin opens with Exorcism (then Hand of Reckoning, Avenger's Shield); the other classes' openers are as they
were (the bow, gun or thrown weapon first). The creature is waited for where the bot stands, as before.

**No Consecration against a single target (the owner, 2026-11-14: [quote left out]).**
mod-playerbots' paladin strategies (retribution, protection, holy) cast Consecration in every fight. The module puts
its own version of the action into a paladin's AI context (as with food and drink, `BotDriver::GuardConsumables`): it
is cast only when at least `Fight.ConsecrationMinFoes` foes in a fight stand within its eight yards (a bot setting,
2), in the open world and in dungeons, whatever the talents; a tank holding several keeps it. Under
`GuildAdventure.Debug` a refusal is a line, once per half minute: `Palatest does not cast Consecration: 1 foe(s) in a
fight within 8 yd (from 2)`.

**Interrupts (the owner, 2026-11-23: [quote left out]).** What
mod-playerbots does: each class has an interrupt trigger ("kick", "pummel", "counterspell", ...) that fires when the
bot's current target casts, but only the strategies that list it use it. Rogues (Kick), shamans (Wind Shear), death
knights (Mind Freeze), shadow priests (Silence), marksmanship hunters (Silencing Shot), bear druids (Bash) and
paladins (Hammer of Justice) have it. Mages do not: their strategies list Counterspell only against an enemy healer,
and in two days of the gaps clone's debug log (about 13,000 fights of four mages) one Counterspell was cast. Arms
warriors, every warrior of the guild by its default template, have none: Pummel is in the fury strategy, Shield Bash
in the tank strategy, and Pummel wants Berserker Stance while arms fights in Battle Stance; Pummel and Shield Bash were
cast 0 times in that log. And the trigger looks at the bot's current target only, and not at whether the foe's spell
can be interrupted at all.

`Escape::StepInterrupt` (FightEscape.cpp), four times a second for every character the AI plays, in a fight: the foes
of its fight (what it attacks and what attacks it) are looked at for a spell the game lets be interrupted (the core's
own test in `Spell::EffectInterruptCast`: a cast with a cast time or a channel of the "silence" prevention type with the
interrupt flag, with at least 0.3 s of the cast left). Its class's interrupt is cast on the first such foe in its reach
when it is ready: Kick, Counterspell, Wind Shear, Mind Freeze, Silence, Silencing Shot, a bear's Bash, Shield Bash
(with a shield, in Battle or Defensive Stance), Pummel. For Pummel an arms warrior changes to Berserker Stance first,
when the rage it keeps through the change (Stance Mastery and Tactical Mastery, as the core counts it) pays for the
Pummel and it has that rage; the rest of its rage is lost, as for a player who does the same, and its rotation changes
back to Battle Stance a moment later. A spell of its own that it is casting gives way. A paladin's Hammer of Justice
and a warlock's felhunter stay mod-playerbots' (a stun of a minute's cooldown; the guild's warlocks fight with a
voidwalker). Bot setting `Fight.Interrupt` (135, on; per guild and per bot). The fight line counts them (`, interrupted
N casts`), and under `GuildAdventure.Debug` each is a line: `Wardps interrupts Noxious Plaguebat's Slowing Poison with
Pummel (1 yd away)`. In a test on the gaps instance (the clone of the owner's guild at level 60, 16 minutes, 458 fights): 62 casts interrupted, Pummel 24, Wind Shear 22, Kick 6, Counterspell 5, Mind Freeze 5 ("Mageyo interrupts Cursed Mage's Arcane Bolt with Counterspell (21 yd away)", "Warriorio interrupts Monstrous Plaguebat's Sonic Burst with Pummel (3 yd away)"); each Pummel of an arms warrior followed its change to Berserker Stance in the same second, and its rotation was back in Battle Stance one or two seconds later; one death (a mage that took a pack of three it had judged at 51 %), no rescue.

**A paladin's cooldowns and heals (the owner, 2026-11-14).** [quote left out]. (1) The decision to leave
a fight counts what a paladin can give itself back with a cooldown that is ready (`EmergencyReserve`: Lay on Hands
as 90 % of its health, else Divine Shield with 30 % mana as 50 %; neither with Forbearance on it), and the module
presses them itself below 25 % health (`StepSelfHeal`: `<bot> casts Lay on Hands at N% health`; mod-playerbots has
both on its "critical health" trigger, but a level-40 test paladin among four murlocs went down to 9 % with both
ready and neither on cooldown afterwards). Not before a pull: no pull is planned on a cooldown of twenty minutes. (2) The
module's own heal (`SelfHealSpell`): in a fight Holy Light, and Flash of Light only while The Art of War makes it
instant; out of a fight, in a rest without food, Flash of Light for the last quarter of the health and Holy Light
for more.

**A melee bot that does not get under way to its target.** the owner, 2026-11-14 07:02: Retadin stood with "You are too
far away!" (the client's line for a melee swing out of reach). A quest interaction that wants a corpse set a
creature 42 yards off as his target once a second, for 205 seconds; mod-playerbots' approach did not run between
the calls, and the pull check had let the lone creature pass. Now a melee bot that the pull check let at a target
and that has not moved for three seconds while the target stands beyond its reach is pulled to it
(`Escape::CheckPull`, `BotRuntime::pullOkSince`): its opener from range when it has one, else a walk into the
creature's sight (`has not got under way to <creature> (level N, D yd) for S s: it pulls it`). Such a bot is looked
at every check, not every two seconds. Not while it rests or casts.

**The why line after a walk around a pack.** The status line read "Keeping away from creatures it cannot take
together" for as long as the task ran after a walk around a pack (268 s in one case; 9 of a round's status lines,
which looked like bots standing in keep-aways: the keep-aways of rounds 88 to 90 took 395, 309 and 156 s in all,
49, 49 and 46 of them, median 2 to 4 s). The task's own line comes back when the task goes on.

**A swimmer's run.** A bot that leaves a fight in water too deep to stand in swims its legs in a straight line
through the water, at its depth or just above the floor where that rises (the path finder has no ways under water:
a level-39 warrior that a level-46 Coral Shark came for had "of 7 directions .. 7 had no path; none left" and
"fights on").

**A strong creature that keeps to its place; one creature on the way does not end the task; what an item summons
(round 93).** the owner watched Retadin (level 43) walk to and fro at Sandsorrow Watch in Tanaris. His task was the
water hole of "Gadgetzan Water Survey"; 72 yards from it stands Jin'Zallah the Sandbringer, a level-46 rare elite
(worth 53 levels by its health and damage) that never moves (no waypoints, no script). The look-out treated it as
one on a round: every way that led within 40 yards of it was "a way into it", so the bot went around it, came within
24 yards of it on the way back to its line, kept away, was "clear of it after 3 s", and its task ended ("kept away
from a creature far above its level"); 100 yards around the place were set aside for ten minutes, the water hole
with them; Tanaris had "nothing it can safely get to", the bot chose Stranglethorn across the sea and its voyage
waited, went around and kept away twelve more times in five minutes.

- *A creature that keeps to its place* (a spawn, a random walk or a waypoint path that stays within 30 yards of its
  spawn, not fighting or on its way home: `KeepsToItsPlace`; 15 yards of random walk until the bronze drakes at the
  Caverns of Time, which walk 16 to 18 yards about, held a warrior on its way to a vendor in there for twelve
  minutes, waiting for them "to pass") is no danger to a way that stays out of its reach:
  its aggro range for the bot, how far it walks about and 6 yards (`StandReach`). The look-out asks how near the
  next 70 yards of the bot's path come to it (`WayClosest`); a way that stays out is ridden; one into its reach goes
  around it (up to eight times in a minute and a half, the circle drawn with its reach and 8 yards: `[it keeps to
  its place: the way keeps N yd from it]`); inside its reach the bot steps out of it (`out of its reach`) and its
  task goes on; the third step-out from the same creature within three minutes counts as a way that ends inside its
  reach (`[it keeps to its place, and the bot's task led it into its reach the third time in three minutes]`: Mahiri,
  a level-23 shaman, stepped out of a Scorched Basilisk's reach 23 times in five minutes in Stonetalon while its own
  steps to the spot of "New Life", 17 yd below it, led back past it, 2026-11-26). Only a way that ends inside its reach, or finds no way around it, ends the task, and then its target
  counts as one it cannot get to, without a wait for the creature to pass (`asideStood`): it is set aside for a
  quarter of an hour at once (`sets vendor (target Yarley) aside for 15 min: a creature far above its level keeps to
  its place on its way there`), where a pack sets it aside the second time. In a fight it counts only
  once the fight has drawn the bot into its reach: a level-47 warrior left a fight against one Sandfury troll at full
  health beside the water hole because Jin'Zallah "was near", 40 yards off, and its quest task ended.
- *One creature on the way does not end a task* (the maintainers' ruling): after a keep-away from one creature on a
  round, every task waits where the bot got to (20 s at a time, four minutes per task: `waits with its <task> at
  <target>: <creature> is on its way`) and goes on when the creature's sights are off its way; journeys did so
  before. And no place is set aside after one creature (a pack or a camp still sets theirs aside): its sights keep
  spots and ways on its round out for a minute and a half (`RoamerNear`), and one that keeps to its place reaches
  only so far.
- *What an item summons* counts like a target (`Risk::JudgeSummon`, for the interaction planner before the item is
  used): the Untapped Dowsing Widget's spell summons a Centipaar Tunneler (level 47-48) out of the water hole, four
  levels above Retadin. A summon that will fight the bot (a wild summon of a creature hostile to it; pets, totems,
  guardians and vehicles are the bot's own) is too much when it is above the level cap, four levels or more above
  the bot (an elite three more) or its fight costs more than `Risk.MaxFightCostPercent`; the objective then waits
  until the level from which it would do (`leaves quest 992 "Gadgetzan Water Survey" until level 47: using Untapped
  Dowsing Widget summons Centipaar Tunneler (level 48), too much for it at level 43`).
  The same holds for an object whose use springs a linked trap (2026-11-24): each kind of object of the objective is
  judged by its trap's spell, and what the summons call in by their script counts too (`WorldIndex::MinionOf`). One
  kind of the Deepmoss Eggs of "Deepmoss Spider Eggs" (1069) springs two Deepmoss Hatchlings of level 14, and each calls
  a Deepmoss Matriarch of 22 at 30 % health: a level-19 warrior opened two and died with four on it. Now `leaves quest
  1069 "Deepmoss Spider Eggs" until level 23: its objects spring a trap that summons Deepmoss Hatchling (level 14),
  Deepmoss Hatchling (level 14), Deepmoss Matriarch (level 22), Deepmoss Matriarch (level 22), too much for it at level 19`.
  Once brought, the quest's own creature is not judged again at the pull check (`QuestBroughtIt`: a summon without a
  spawn, of the bot's item or of the trap of an object its quest key opened, that an incomplete quest in its log wants
  killed, and less than four levels above it, an elite three): refusing it left it standing where it came (the
  observer's "Spirits of Stonemaul Hold": the Stonemaul Spirit attacks nobody by itself).
  The objects the bot opens at the spot are judged too (2026-11-25, `OrderService::TrapRefused`): the planner chose a
  spawn without such a trap, but the interaction step took the nearest object in sight, and mod-playerbots' loot opens
  quest objects beside the way. Of the Kodo Bones of "Bone Collector" (5501) one kind (176751) springs a Kodo Apparition
  of level 38; a level-31 shaman opened such bones twice beside the untrapped ones it was sent to, fled from the
  Apparition both times and went home by hearthstone. Now the step passes such an object, and the loot beside the way
  leaves it (`leaves Kodo Bones beside its way alone: its trap summons what it cannot take`).

**An object in the middle of a camp is no place to use (round 102).** Wartank (48) opened the Stolen Cargo of
"Stoley's Shipment" in the middle of the Southsea camp of Tanaris, was attacked three times on its way in and died at
the crates with four on it. Reproduced on the dev instance with its learned costs, today's verdict refuses the crates
(105 to 114 %, "the place is guarded"), and without its cost for Southsea Swashbucklers still "every spot of it near is
too much" (so the quest waits for a partner). Live it had never fought a Swashbuckler before it set out, so the verdict
took its average cost for the five of them and the pull share counted the camp's outer ones at a fifth. A fight's
verdict hangs on such costs; a camp's does not (`CannotTake`: three of its creatures at once, four in a camp of ten
spawns or more, at the bot's cost per level, its squad counted). So an object to use in the middle of a camp the bot
cannot take is not used at all (`Risk::SaferSpot`): the bot stands there for the seconds of the use, among the camp,
and no careful pull draws the creatures off first. A partner or a squad can make it workable.

**Backing away from a melee foe (round 108).** mod-playerbots' ranged combat strategy has a character that fights at
range back off five yards ("flee", `Playerbots.FleeDistance`) whenever its foe is in melee reach, straight away from
the foe and again while the foe follows, and it looks at nothing behind it; a mage's "blink back" does the same with
twenty yards. Mageyo (37) pulled one Kurzen Commando at the edge of their camp (the pull check: one), and 22 to 29
seconds into the fight three more were on it: the fight had drifted 22 to 27 yards from where the Commando stood,
into the next ones (the Commandos stand 10 to 20 yards apart, in stealth). It ran at 43 % with three on it and died.
The module's own versions of the two actions (`BotDriver::GuardConsumables`) take the same steps at the same angles,
but a step that comes nearer to a hostile creature not in the fight yet and into its reach (its aggro range and six
yards, at least twelve: `Escape::StepWakes`) is not taken; with no step open the character fights on where it stands
(`does not back away from ...: every way back leads toward ...`, at most once per half minute).

**What comes to help the creatures on the way (round 108).** The look for a pack on the way counted the creatures
within their reach of the bot's way (a rider: within their aggro range), not what the core's call for help brings when
one of them is attacked (CreatureFamilyAssistanceRadius, repeated every few seconds while a creature fights). Shammpower
(40) walked along the north edge of the Bloodsail camp by Booty Bay to a Stranglekelp node 69 yards from the camp's
middle; two raiders lay within reach of its way, two were within its means, and three, then six were on it (the
camp's five stand 8 to 12 yards apart, the raiders net, the run was held fast). The look now adds every creature that
stands within the assistance radius (and two yards) of one in reach and would help it (`CanAssistTo`), as the check
before a pull does, and judges the walk by all of them.

**No herb behind a camp it has just kept away from (round 108).** In the profession mode Shammpower (40) set out for
three Stranglekelp beside the Bloodsail camp of the Southern Savage Coast within 45 seconds: the first two travels ended
"a pack on its way", the third was caught. A keep-away from a pack or a camp sets the place aside for ten minutes;
the herb search left out nodes inside such a place, not nodes whose straight way leads into one. It leaves those out
now too (`BotRuntime::CrossesAvoidedArea` in `PlanGatherRound`).

**A fight that never ends because creatures come and go (round 108).** Shamanheal stood "in combat" for 480 seconds at the
Ogre Remains of Dustwallow Marsh, two creatures in the count, not a step in five minutes. The rule that ends a fight in
which nothing happens began its 45 seconds anew whenever the number of creatures on the bot changed, and one that
cannot reach the bot leaves and comes back again and again. What counts now: the bot loses health, a foe reaches a new
low of its own health, a creature joins the fight for the first time, the bot moves or casts.

**Packs two characters could take: a quest for a partner (round 108).** Quest 604 "The Bloodsail Buccaneers" (ten
swashbucklers, who stand with warlocks and their imps and succubi) sat in the logs of five of the guild's characters
without progress: each pull was refused ("the fight would cost it about 155% and it has 78%"), and after two the quest
was set aside for half an hour, again and again. The check before a pull now notes whether one more guild character
beside the bot would make the pull affordable (its budget, rested, added to the bot's rested one; never for a creature
the bot cannot beat), and when the second refused pull sets the quest aside with that note, the quest becomes a hard
quest for the guild (`QuestPartnerService::OnTooHard`, the owner's rule: quest partners for hard, elite and group quests),
so two characters that carry it pair up for it. A pack that two characters could not take either (362 %) gets no
such mark.

**The place of a keep-away is set aside when it begins (round 112).** Task endings on "a pack on its way" doubled in
round 112 (40 in 22 minutes); 18 of them came from the camp look on the spawn data, and one mage alone ended seven
tasks in a minute and a half beside the Undead Ravager camp of Desolace. A keep-away from a pack or a camp set its
place aside only when it ended, and the planner chooses the next task the moment the old one ends: with nothing set
aside yet the next way led into the same camp. The place is now set aside when the keep-away begins, at the middle of
the creatures it keeps away from, so the spot check of the next objective (`CrossesAvoidedArea`) sees a way into the
camp as one.

**The looks on the way follow the path, not the straight line (round 113).** The look for a pack on the way and the
look for a camp took the straight line from the bot to the end of its movement. A long walk's movement ends hundreds
of yards off while its path curves: Shammpower's sixth death at the Bloodsail camp of the Southern Savage Coast was a
zone travel whose movement ended 392 yards to the south-east, its path first curving through the camp ("8 hostile
within 60 yards, none on its way"), and it rode within six yards of a warlock and its succubus. Staged on the dev
instance the bot was attacked there three times in a row. Both looks now take the next yards along the movement's own
path points (`WayAhead`: 45 yards for packs, 90 for camps, a rider's 15 more beyond a short step's end). On the next
run the bot went around the warlock group twice, kept out of the camp's middle and reached Booty Bay.

**Who comes with the ones who come (round 113).** The check before a pull counted who would help the target and who
stands on the way; every creature that joins a fight calls for help itself as it engages, and what stands beside a
sure joiner comes as well. A level-43 warrior pulled a Mosh'Ogg Warmonger on its round ("2 expected": a Shaman beside
its way), the Mauler 9.5 yards from the Shaman was on it three seconds later, and it died where another guild
character had died half an hour before. The check now adds, for every sure joiner, what stands within the assistance
radius of it and would help it.

With the debug setting two more lines say what a fight or a look was about: `attacked, foe N ...` for a fight the bot
did not begin (where it stood, each attacker's home, a round it walks, who summoned it), and `pack look: ... it takes
them` when the look let a way past two or more creatures be.

**The same task ended the same way, again and again (round 114).** Catdudu began the escort of "Suntara Stones"
(Dorius Stonetender, Searing Gorge) again every few seconds for twenty minutes, each time ended by "a pack on its way":
31 of the round's 67 such endings. The rule that leaves a quest alone for a quarter of an hour after two of its tasks
in a row ended for what stood in their way, with no progress in between, counted objectives and interactions only, and
setting the escort's spawn aside does not stop an escort while its NPC stands in sight. Now every kind of quest work
counts (`ClearTask`): an escort, a quest event, a pickup and a journey to a far spot of a task, and a refused way
("way too dangerous", "route too dangerous", "objective too far around", "no way on the ground" ...) counts like a pack
or a pull it cannot afford. A hand-in keeps its own rule (it waits for its way to clear and then sets its ender aside),
an errand's travel its own (it is dropped). An escort whose quest is left alone fails when its NPC walks on without the
bot, and the failed quest is taken again once, as every failed quest.

**Four or more creatures far below the bot (round 115).** Three deaths in half an hour, each against four or five
creatures seven to eight levels below the bot: a level-44 warrior on its way up the Bloodscalp ruins to Nezzliok the
Dire ("left a fight against 4 foes ...: no open way", then five), a level-42 shaman at The Emperor's Tomb of "Kurzen's
Mystery" in the same ruins (five, held fast on its run), a level-40 frost mage at Dalinda Malem's side in Thunder Axe
Fortress (four Burning Blade of level 32). Measured over the day's fights on the integration server: against creatures
five to eight levels below the bot a single foe cost 7-8% of the bot's health, two 17-18%, three 25-31% (none of 146
lost), four or more 43-46% on average with 9 deaths in 105 and 30 runs; more than eight below, none of 100 such fights
was lost. The estimate's mean for four (seven single fights) is about right; its spread is not, and the limit of 80%
let fights in whose mean was near it. Three changes:

- `Escape::CrowdTail`: from three foes to four the need of a fight counts up to twice, for what the bot would not
  begin for its work: the look for a group on its way (`FindPackAhead`), and everything that asks `Risk::NeedOf`: the
  spot verdict, `Risk::CanFight` (camps, guarded places, the groups on a route). The pull check and the decision to
  leave a fight keep their own rules.
- `Risk::GuardsNear` counts creatures down to eight levels below the bot (were three), so Thunder Axe Fortress is a
  guarded place for a level-40 mage (`.ga admin spot`: "the spot waits: the place is guarded", where it said "it would
  work there").
- An object to use is a place to walk up to as well: the guarded-place verdict holds for the objects of
  interactions too (it held for places without a spawn only: quest NPCs, vendors, gathering nodes). On bq a level-42 shaman with "Kurzen's Mystery" opened
  Gri'lek the Wanderer, as the live shaman did, and then "leaves quest 207 ... for a quarter of an hour: every spot of
  it near is too much for it at level 42" instead of walking to the tomb.

**A detour or a refusal only for elites, creatures four levels above and groups (the owner, 2026-11-14).** [quote left out]; and
[quote left out], [quote left out]. Measured over the day's single fights on the integration server: a foe two or three
levels above the bot cost 21-22% of its health (12 deaths in 1743), four levels above 26% (6 in 71), five 39% (4 in
34), six and more 69% (32 in 58). The rules of the risk model and the look-outs now draw the line there:

- `Escape::StrengthOf`: an elite counts by its health and damage (`ThreatLevelOf`), every other creature (a rare that
  is no elite included) by its level alone. The look-out for strong creatures (keep away, walk around, the waits for
  one on the way), the strong creature that stops a pull, the sights of roamers and the "caught on its way" rule use
  it; an ordinary creature with a little more health than its level no longer counts as one four levels higher.
- The pull check pulls a single ordinary creature less than four levels above the bot whatever the estimate says: no
  refusal and no rest first for it (the rest between fights keeps the leader's thresholds).
- The spot verdict: `Risk.MaxFoeLevelAbove` is 3 by default (was 1), so a target four levels above the bot waits, a
  target two or three above does not; a creature beside a spot waits it from four levels above (was three); a single
  ordinary target with less than one more foe to be expected beside it is never "too much".
- A wait for a strong creature on the way lasts a minute per task at most (was four).

Groups the bot cannot take (the pack look, camps, guarded places, the crowd tail) keep their rules.

**On its way it fights what its work wants, what attacks it and what stands in its way (round 117).** A level-47 rogue
on its way to the Dark Iron Slavers of "Culling the Competition" fought six Greater Lava Spiders in a row, one by a
careful pull with Throw from 28 yards: mod-playerbots picks targets near the bot whatever its task, and the rogue
never got nearer until the stuck rule ended the task. The pull check (four times a second, on the target the AI has
chosen) now leaves a creature alone on the bot's way to an objective, an interaction, a hand-in, a pickup, a vendor, a
trainer, a journey, a ship, a flight master, water to fish at or a safe place when no quest in its log needs it (a
kill, a kill credit, an item it drops), it does not attack the bot, and its reach (its aggro range and five yards,
twelve at least) covers neither where the bot stands nor the next 45 yards of its way: `leaves ... alone on its way:
nothing its work wants, and it does not stand in its way`, once per creature in ten minutes (mod-playerbots picks the
same creature again at every look while the bot does something else beside it). A grind, an escort, a quest event, a
squad member and a dungeon keep their own rules. In its first live round (round 120) no creature a quest of the bot
wanted was left alone, and the old nine fought as often as in the round before (201 fights against 204).

**Groups far below the bot are no group it cannot take.** A level-46 warlock kept away from packs of three and four
level-35 Kurzen Commandos, which cost it 10-20% a fight, until it used its hearthstone. Over the day's live fights
none of 100 against four or more creatures more than eight levels below the bot was lost (19-35% of its health on
average). `Escape::GroupLevelsBelow` (8): the look for a group on its way counts creatures down to eight levels below
the bot, the crowd tail counts only those (in `Risk::NeedOf` by each part's level, in `Risk::CanFight` by the foes'
level); what stands around a place keeps counting further down (`PackLevelsBelow`, 12).

**A creature that stands and casts after a careful pull is made to come.** The careful pull's last phase used to end
with "the creature fights from a distance, the bot goes to it", also when its place was in its group (a level-44
warrior pulled a Skullsplitter Mystic with Throw, went to it, had its three neighbours on it and died). Now the bot
goes to it only when the fight at its place is one it can take (`JudgePull` there); else it steps out of the creature's
line of sight within 26 yards (`FindLureSpot`: not nearer to it, not past or into other creatures' reach, not into deep
water, a whole path), and if the creature still stands, out of the reach of its spells, 44 yards from it; a creature
that comes for neither is left alone and the bot walks away from it (`... among its group: left alone`).

**No wait for a creature that stays about the place (round 121).** A bot waited 75 seconds beside Stonard for a
level-65 Stonard Grunt to move on; the grunts there walk loops of four points some forty yards across and never leave,
the task ended, and the rescue then took the bot for one that had not moved for five minutes. `Escape::StaysAround`: a
guard, a creature in a town of the other side, and one whose waypoint round is short (every point within 60 yards of
its middle) or lies wholly within 150 yards of the bot stays about the place. For such a creature the keep-away does
not wait for it to move on; the task's target counts as one behind it and is set aside at once (as for a strong
creature that keeps to its place), the place around the creature is kept out of the next ways for ten minutes, and a
journey does not wait for it on its way (`StepRoamerWait`): `does not wait for ... to move on: it stays about the
place (...); the bot turns to other work`.

**No spawn in the middle of a camp, however near (round 122).** A paladin of level 52 worked the Jaedenar Cultists,
Adepts and Guardians of "Forces of Jaedenar" one spawn after the other into the middle of their camp, each next one
less than 35 yards on, while the spot choice refused a spawn in a camp's middle only from 35 yards on (its approach
had to enter the camp). In the middle, "it goes out of it first" began, every way out had creatures on it, and it died
against four. `Risk::SaferSpot` now leaves a spawn alone that lies in the middle of a camp the bot cannot take at any
distance; and the single-target exemption of the spot verdict (below four levels, no group) holds only outside such
a camp and with less than half a foe more to be expected (it was a whole one: in a camp the shares of the creatures
around stay small). Of the other deaths of that check, Catdudu (49) died to a careful pull of a Dunemaul Enforcer for
which one Brute "may still come" and two came (the pull check's estimate, not the new thresholds), Cleaveyo (47)
thirty seconds after entering the world among Centipaar silithids, with no task, Leel (39) on a travel through Badlands
hyenas after four gather detours.

**Minions a camp's casters summon (round 102).** Duduheal (43) died opening the Bloodsail Charts of "The Bloodsail
Buccaneers" in the Bloodsail camp of Stranglethorn: "left a fight against 4 foes (Succubus Minion level 41) at 71%:
died on the run". The spot had passed `Risk::SaferSpot`, but the Bloodsail Warlocks' succubi and imps have no
spawns: each warlock's SmartAI script casts Summon Succubus or Summon Imp out of combat. So the spot verdict counted
half the creatures that stand there. `WorldIndex::MinionOf` reads from the SmartAI scripts which creature a creature
summons in a fight or around one: a spell with a summon effect or a summon action, in combat, out of combat, at a
health, on aggro, in range, at a respawn or a reset. It leaves out summons for a quest's item, a talk, a death or an
event step, and critters and totems. The risk model's look at the spawns around a place
(`ForEachMobNear`: the spot verdict, the camp verdict, guarded places, a rest's quiet place, hostiles around) counts
such a minion beside its summoner, at its level and on its side. At the charts, for a level-40 priest, the verdict
went from 6 warlocks and 67 % to 12 creatures and 149 % (`Imp Minion 41 at 24 yd (near, counts a fifth)`). The pull
check counts the minions that are alive anyway.

**A guarded place; a squad's water; a levelling shaman's totems (round 85).**

- *A guarded place.* A priest rode 355 seconds to Dalinda Malem inside Thunder Axe Fortress and 229 seconds to a
  chest among the naga, turned round at the gate both times ("a pack on its way"), and would have set out again
  half an hour later; a warrior died at the Bloodsail Correspondence. The verdict on a quest giver or an ender
  asked who would join a fight at the place itself (one or two of the eight Burning Blade around Dalinda), not
  whether the bot gets there. A place to walk up to (a giver, an ender, a vendor: `Risk::JudgeSpot` for a spot
  without a creature or an object of its own) is now also judged by what has its spawn around it: three or more
  creatures that would attack the bot, not more than three levels below it, within 30 yards, and more than it can
  take together (four at most are counted): `the spot waits: the place is guarded` (`Risk::GuardsNear`). Hubs have
  no such spawns. And what the spawn data does not show is learned once: when a pickup or a hand-in ends for a
  pack on the last 250 yards and creatures have their place within 40 yards of the target, the place is set aside
  until the bot has a level more or for two hours, across restarts (`Risk::SetPlaceAside`, kept like a place it
  died at): `sets the place of turn-in (target ..) aside until level N or for 120 min: a pack it cannot take stood
  on the last N yd of its way there, and creatures have their place around it`. (Elsewhere a hand-in still waits
  25 seconds and tries again, four times: a pair of raptors beside a hub wanders off.)
- *A squad's water.* A shaman that led a mage through Dustwallow drank the guild storage dry, one piece at a time,
  and then sat out its mana for 100 to 190 seconds in every five minutes beside a mage that carried twelve
  drinks. A character that rests for mana and finds no drink in its bags or the storage gets four from the mage
  of its group within 40 yards (what the mage conjured first, else what it bought; the mage keeps two and conjures
  its own again): `<bot> got 4 x Sweet Nectar from Magefrost, the mage of its squad, to drink (20 left with the
  mage)`. Only from a character the AI plays.
- *A levelling shaman's totems.* mod-playerbots gives an enhancement shaman four totems (Strength of Earth, Magma,
  Healing Stream, Windfury; other talents four others) and sets them again whenever the last ones are out of
  reach: about a third of a levelling shaman's mana every 30 yards. In the open world a guild shaman sets one
  Searing Totem and nothing else (`BotDriver::KeepTotems`, looked at every 20 seconds and whenever its strategies
  are reset); in a dungeon it has the set of its talents again. `<bot> sets one Searing Totem per fight while it
  levels`. Its shocks still cost it 16 to 31 % of its mana per creature at level 36 (three fights on the dev
  instance): the totems were part of the cost, not all of it.

**Not "on its way" when the way leads away (round 86).** A level-38 hunter stood in the Kurzen compound, creatures
27 to 37 yards away on several sides. Eight pickups at a camp 600 yards away and then its own retreat ended "a pack
on its way" within 6 to 69 seconds, 350 seconds in all, and each target was set aside for a quarter of an hour.
Two things were wrong. The look for a pack on the way counted every creature whose reach covers the next 45 yards,
also one the bot stands beside and walks away from; now the way has to bring the bot at least three yards nearer
to a creature than it is. And the compound was no camp for that hunter (its creatures are five levels below it, a
camp counts down to three), so "out of a camp first" did not fire, while four of them had just taken it from 100
to 58 %: for the question whether a bot should get out of where it stands, creatures down to six levels below it
count, when four of them at once are more than it can take. (The camps a bot keeps out of, and the spots it is
refused, still count three levels: nothing more waits for it.)

And the other way round, for a rider: the group of a pull the bot has just called off is known to be too much, so
for a minute its way keeps 20 yards off every creature within 30 yards of that pull's place, whether it rides or
walks (a rider's look counts only what would have it in its aggro radius, because roads lead past camps). A
level-44 hunter called a pull at the Bloodsail camp off ("6 more would join"), was given a vendor 203 yards away,
rode off past the same camp, and five were on it 25 seconds later.

**Caught on the way out.** A keep-away or a back-out that was attacked became a run from a fight, whatever had
attacked: a level-30 rogue that backed out of the Raven Hill cemetery after a pull it had called off was attacked by
one skeleton three levels below it, "left" that fight at 93 % health with Vanish and Sprint, ran for 35 seconds
through the cemetery and died with four on it, "during no task". Now the usual rule decides (`ShouldLeave`): what it
can take, it fights (`kept away from ..: attacked on its way, it fights`); a creature far above it, or a fight it
would leave anyway, is a run as before. And the line of such a run counts what is on the bot, not the camp it was
leaving.

**A creature the bot cannot beat, in the water and on its round.** the owner's leader, a level-37 paladin, died twice
in one night to a Coral Shark (level 46, elite) on "Thresher Oil": the sharks swim rounds of 800 yards through the
water of the Young Murk Threshers. The spot verdict knows such a round and refuses the spawns beside it; three
other places did not:

- **The look-out under water.** `FindThreat` asks whether the creature can get to the bot: a whole path, or, for a
  creature in the water, at most five yards above or below it (a walker on a shore is out of a swimmer's reach).
  Under water the path finder has no paths and the shark was more than five yards off in height: unseen. When the
  bot itself is in the water, a creature in the water reaches it (`keeps away from Coral Shark (level 46 elite), 32
  yd away`).
- **The check before a pull.** It weighed a creature that "may walk in" at a quarter, whatever it was; the bot
  "turned to a Young Murk Thresher that stands alone", "1 expected", and the shark was 16 yards from the thresher
