  four seconds later. A creature four levels above the bot (by level, health and damage, as for the look-out) is not
  weighed: when it may come at all the pull is not made, and one that is on its way (a patrol, anything that moves)
  may come from 30 yards farther off than its aggro radius (`does not pull Young Murk Thresher: 1 more would join
  (Coral Shark 46 too strong for it)`). No rest "for" such a pull either.
- **After the death.** The place was set aside for two hours ("until the level of those foes") and the quest for
  half an hour. When what killed the bot is four or more levels above it, the place is kept for eight hours (`what
  killed it there is level 46, far above it: the place is set aside until level 46 or for 8 h`) and the quest
  rests two hours (`leaves quest .. for 120 min: it died on it to a creature far above it (Coral Shark, level 46)`).

And a strong creature that only swims is no matter for a point on dry land: `Escape::RoamerNear` / `RoamerOnLeg`
(the notes of strong creatures on their way) leave it out unless the point is water (the water's level above the
ground there; a pier is ground). The sharks off Theramore had closed the pier for walkers.

What this does not cover: a bot that fights one creature at the edge of such a field and has others wander in
(the shares for "may walk in" are measured over all places, a quarter; the new `pull joiner` lines will say what
they are in a camp), and a bot already inside a camp when its pull is called off (`backs out of the place ...: 6
creatures within 28 yd (the nearest ... 7 yd away)`, attacked on the way out).

### Fights in the water, travel forms (2026-11-12)

The live server's water deaths were read as "swimming bots deal almost no damage". Measured on the dev instance with
a detail line per three seconds of a fight in the water (`water fight`, `GuildAdventure.Debug`): a warlock, a hunter,
a druid casting and a druid in bear form fight under water as they do on land (a level-17 druid killed a level-14
Greymist Seer 41 yards down in 18 to 31 seconds). Two things were wrong, neither of them the water:

- **A druid in aquatic form does nothing.** playerbots shifts a druid that is under water and out of combat into
  aquatic form, and its combat strategies do not take it out again: attacked in that form it stood 8 yards from its
  foe for the whole fight, cast nothing and hit nothing (live: 93 seconds against one murloc four levels below it,
  dead, three times in a row). Now an AI-played character that is in combat in aquatic form, travel form or as a
  ghost wolf leaves the form (`leaves its aquatic form to fight`); not while it runs from a fight, where the form is
  the faster way out.
- **Two of eight bots played the wrong rotation**, in the water and everywhere else: docs/specs.md "Stored
  strategies".

A fight against two or more foes also says how it began: `its own pull (1 expected)` (the pull check had let the
target pass and expected that many foes; more came) or `it was attacked` (the bot had chosen no target: it stood or
walked within the reach of creatures). On the dev instance, eight minutes with 12 bots after the pull check: 14 such
fights, 5 the bot's own pull (four of them with one foe expected and one more that came), 9 attacks; all three
fights against three and more were attacks, on a bot working inside an orc camp.

The fight line says where a fight took place and how far the bot got: `fight 93 s under water, begun in aquatic
form: 1 foe at once (...), ..., died, its target at 97% health` (`in the water` = it stood in water, `under water` =
its head was under; the target's health only for fights it lost or left). What is left of the water: a bot pulls
more than it sees there (creatures above and below it), which the spot rule and the escape count three times.

### Out of ground effects (2026-11-14)

the owner, 2026-11-14: [quote left out]. Read in his Maraudon run (Pristine Waters, 15:31 to 16:00): the Noxious Slimes
cast Noxious Cloud (spell 21070) in every fight, and two wipes and two deaths right after a revival ("not in a fight,
last fought nothing") were characters standing in it; his screenshot shows Retadin brought back in the cloud.

- **Cause.** mod-playerbots has a strategy "avoid aoe" (its action steps out of a hostile area aura of a dynamic
  object, a damaging trap and a trigger creature with a damaging aura, up to `Playerbots.MaxAoeAvoidRadius`, 15 yd, its
  `AoeAvoidSpellWhitelist` left alone). Its switch `Playerbots.AutoAvoidAoe` is read by no code in our pin, and no
  default strategy list has it: no guild bot ever had it on.
- **Built.** Every AI-played guild character carries "avoid aoe" in and out of combat (`BotDriver::KeepAvoidAoe`,
  asserted every 5 s: a change of talents or a login resets the strategies). Four times a second the module looks
  whether it stands in a hostile ground effect (`BotDriver::GroundEffectOn`: a negative aura of a dynamic object whose
  caster is hostile); then it steps out at once with mod-playerbots' own action (`BotDriver::StepOutOfGroundEffect`,
  the AI released from whatever the module holds it for: a rest, the hold while the tank pulls, a pull); when that
  action finds nothing (in the first test 6 of 17 times: its value of the aura is a second old, or its flee point had
  no way), a step straight out of the effect's circle, 3 yd past its edge, away from its middle or to either side of
  that. A rest in it ends (`a ground effect`). `OrderService::StepGroundEffect`; an activity line every 10 s at most:
  `Dmmage stands in Flamestrike at 85% health in a fight: it steps out` (or `no way out of it found`).
- **Not yet:** a revival waits while a ground effect lies on the corpse (comes with the dungeon files, §7 GE1).
- **Around it, not in and out** (the owner, 2026-11-25: [quote left out]). The step out did nothing about the walk that led in: its mover (the follow of the
  group's tank, the planner's walk, NewRpg) set it again at once (a hunter in a Cloud of Disease in Scholomance stepped
  out every few seconds for half a minute out of any fight, its rest ended by it). Out of a fight the module looks twice
  a second at the next 25 yd of the bot's movement (`OrderService::StepGroundEffectAhead`, the hostile dynamic objects
  within 40 yd): a way that leads into an effect is walked around it instead, the shorter arc at its radius plus 3 yd,
  each point on the ground and in sight of the one before (`walks around Cloud of Disease (10 yd across) on its way: 12
  yd instead of through it`); a movement that ends in it (the place beside its tank) stops at its edge until the effect
  is gone or the movement leads elsewhere (`waits at the edge of ... : its walk ends in it`); with no way around, an
  effect that ends within 15 s is waited for at its edge, one that lasts is gone through quickly, with no step out on the
  way (`goes through ... quickly: no way leads around it`). In a fight the fight's own places count (the step out).

### Class abilities (2026-11-12)

In 3.3.5a some abilities come only from class quests, and in this world database no class trainer teaches them: the
hunter's pet handling (Tame Beast, Call Pet, Dismiss Pet, Feed Pet, Revive Pet), the warlock's voidwalker, succubus
and felhunter, the warrior's Defensive Stance, Taunt, Sunder Armor and Berserker Stance, the druid's Bear Form (with
Growl and Maul) and Cure Poison, the paladin's Redemption, and the shaman's totems: the four totem items (every totem
spell needs its element's item, and no vendor sells them) and the first totem spell of each quest. The order planner
does not plan class quests (their `QuestSortID` is negative, so they belong to no zone, and most need "use this item
on that creature"), and mod-playerbots gives their rewards only to random bots
(`AutoMaintenanceOnLevelupAction::LearnSpells`). So a guild hunter had no pet at level 20.

the owner (2026-11-12, the design log §7 DQ2): they are given automatically, like the class spells of D22, and the hunter
gets a standard pet at level 10. As built (`ClassAbilities.h/.cpp`, `GuildAdventure.ClassAbilities.*`): the world
table `ga_class_ability` (class, race or 0, level, a spell, an item or the creature of the hunter's first pet; its own
file `data/sql/db-world/base/ga_class_ability.sql`) lists them; `ClassAbilities::Grant` gives a bot every row of its
class and race up to its level that it lacks. `OrderService::UpdateBot` calls it on the first tick after a login,
after a level-up and every five minutes (a totem that found no room in the bags, a pet that could not be made while
the hunter was flying or mounted). The hunter's first pet is a beast of its start zone at the hunter's own level (the
row of its race wins over the row for every race: Ice Claw Bear for dwarves, Nightsaber Stalker for night elves, Dire
Mottled Boar for orcs, Armored Scorpid for trolls, Prairie Stalker for tauren, Elder Springpaw for blood elves,
Nightstalker for draenei), made the way the core makes a tamed pet (`Unit::CreateTamedPetFrom`); a hunter that has a
pet, also a stabled or dismissed one, gets none. mod-playerbots' hunter strategies then call, feed, mend and revive
it. The leader gets nothing: he plays his class quests himself.

**The good pet at 60** (the owner, same message: [quote left out]). Rows of `ga_class_ability` with `pet_kind` 1 (the good pet: a Bloodaxe Worg, a wolf) and 2 (the exotic pet: a
Devilsaur), both at level 60. Once per hunter (`ga_bot_pet_upgrade` in the characters database, so a pet the guild
leader chose afterwards is left alone): a hunter with the Beast Mastery talent (`Player::HasTalent(53270)`; a talent is
no entry of the spell book) gets the exotic pet; a hunter whose talent template takes that talent with the points of
the server's level cap waits for it; every other hunter gets the good pet. The built-in Beast Mastery templates take
the talent at point 51 = level 60 (docs/specs.md). The new pet replaces the hunter's pet, wherever it is: at its side,
put away while the hunter rides (a level-60 bot rides nearly all the time; it is taken off its mount for the moment),
dismissed or dead; stabled pets stay. Not in a fight, on a flight or a ship; a hunter that is due its pet is looked at
every 30 seconds.

**Pet talents** (the owner, 2026-11-13: [quote left out]; his hunter's cat had 3 unspent
points). mod-playerbots spends pet talent points only in its level-up auto pick
(`AutoMaintenanceOnLevelupAction::AutoPickTalents` -> `PlayerbotFactory::InitPetTalents`), behind
`Playerbots.AutoPickTalentsForPlayerControlledBots`, which is 0 for guild bots since their talents follow the talent
templates (docs/specs.md); its premade pet builds (`Playerbots.PremadeHunterPetLink.<tree>.16/20`) are endgame lists that
it sorts with an unstable sort over equal keys, so they give no reliable order. As built
(`ClassAbilities::SpendPetTalents`, bot setting `ClassAbilities.PetTalents`, on): the order planner looks every 10 seconds
at the pet of a hunter it plays, out of combat, and spends free points along a fixed build of the pet's tree, in an order
that keeps the tree's rules at every step (3 points per row above, dependencies at the rank they ask for):

| Tree | Build (points 1-16; 17-20 with the hunter's Beast Mastery talent) |
|---|---|
| Ferocity (damage) | Cobra Reflexes 2, Dash 1, Spiked Collar 3, Culling the Herd 3, Spider's Bite 3, Call of the Wild, Rabid, Bloodthirsty 1, Wild Hunt 1; Bloodthirsty 2, Heart of the Phoenix, Shark Attack 2 |
| Tenacity (tanking) | Great Stamina 3, Natural Armor 2, Blood of the Rhino 2, Guard Dog 2, Thunderstomp, Cobra Reflexes 2, Taunt, Last Stand, Pet Barding 1; Silverback 2, Pet Barding 2, Great Resistance 2 |
| Cunning (damage) | Cobra Reflexes 2, Dash 1, Spiked Collar 3, Culling the Herd 3, Feeding Frenzy 2, Mobility 1, Wolverine Bite, Roar of Recovery, Mobility 2, Wild Hunt 1; Wild Hunt 2, Cornered 2, Bullheaded |

A pet has its first point at level 20 and one more every four levels (11 at level 60). Diving pets (bats, birds of prey,
carrion birds, wind serpents, dragonhawks, nether rays, sporebats, chimaeras, moths, wasps: the families Talent.dbc's pet
mask allows Dive for, the core does not read that mask) take Dive and the diving Mobility in place of Dash and its
Mobility. Each list also names, after its twentieth point, what mod-playerbots' premade builds take, so a pet tamed
through mod-playerbots counts as one of the build. A pet with a talent outside its build is the owner's choice and is left
alone (said once per pet: `leaves the talents of its pet ... as they are`); nothing is touched while the owner plays the
hunter himself (the planner does not run for it), and the leader's pet only while the AI plays him. Log line
(`GuildAdventure.log`): `<hunter> (level N) spent N talent points of its pet <name> (level N, <tree>): <talent> <rank>,
...; N left`. Who chooses pet builds is an open point for the owner (the design log §7 "Open" PT1).

**Rogue poisons** (the owner, 2026-11-13: [quote left out]). In 3.3.5a there is nothing to learn: since patch 3.1 poisons are items that poison vendors sell from level 20
(Instant Poison at 20, Deadly Poison at 30, a new rank every eight levels), used on a weapon; the items ask for a level
only, and the old Poisons skill (spell 2842) opens an empty crafting window. mod-playerbots puts them on by itself
(`GenericRogueNonCombatStrategy`, `GenericRogueStrategy`: Instant Poison on the main hand and Deadly Poison on the off
hand, the one it carries on both hands when it carries one kind) whenever a weapon has no temporary enchantment; but
it gives poisons only to random bots (`PlayerbotFactory::InitReagents`) and nothing bought any: on the integration
server neither guild rogue (Roguecombat 30, Stealth 21) carried one, and the guild storage held none. As built
(`RoguePoisons.h/.cpp`, bot settings `Poisons.Enable`, `.Stock`, `.Pair`):

- From level 20 a rogue the AI plays keeps `Poisons.Stock` doses (10; one dose lasts an hour) per weapon hand of the
  kinds of its pair (`Poisons.Pair`: Instant on the main hand and Deadly on the off hand, Instant on both, or Deadly on
  both; Deadly from level 30, Instant on both before that; the pairs are the ones mod-playerbots plays), every rank it
  can use counted.
- The guild storage first: below its stock it takes what the storage holds of its kinds, the best rank first, once a
  minute with the other supplies (`Poisons::TakeFromStorage`; a line per take: `<rogue> (level N) took N x <poison> out
  of the guild storage for its weapons (N doses of <kind> now, it keeps N; N left there)`).
- Otherwise it buys at a poison vendor on its normal shopping stop: at any vendor it visits that sells them, and at a
  hub after a hand-in a poison vendor within 200 yd when it carries less than half its stock and the storage holds
  none (`OrderService::PlanUpkeep`; the owner's rule: shopping at a hub, no trips from the field). Only the visit itself
  (or a hub without such a vendor) starts the 10-minute pause before the next look; a trip something else cut short
  (round 71: a rogue set out for Malissa 152 yd away and teamed up with a quest partner 15 s later) is taken up again at
  the next plan while the bot is within 400 yd of that vendor, for up to 20 minutes. The poison vendor comes before
  the ordinary vendor trip of the same hub stop, and that visit sells and repairs too when it is due (round 73: a rogue
  with bare weapons handed in twice 66 yd from Malissa in Darkshire and went 171 yd to another vendor to sell).
- A rogue that carries no poison of its kinds at all and has a bare weapon (`Poisons::Bare`) takes the poison vendor
  of the town it stands in at any stop between two tasks, not only after a hand-in (`OrderService::PlanPoisonStop`,
  every 15 s at most): a vendor within 300 yd of it with an innkeeper or a flight master within 250 yd of the vendor.
  Line: `<rogue> goes to a vendor (<vendor>, N yd): it carries no poison and a weapon is bare, a poison vendor stands in
  this town; ...` (round 74: a rogue went through Lakeshire and Darkshire with bare weapons for hours, its hub stops
  taken by crafting and selling). The best rank the vendor sells that its level allows, up to the stock; its own money first, the guild's
  budget (`GuildBudget`) for what it cannot pay. Line: `<rogue> bought poisons for its weapons from <vendor>: ...`.
- The module never puts a poison on or takes one off: mod-playerbots applies them, and the dungeon preparation
  (`DungeonSupplies`) coats a weapon only when it has no temporary enchantment either, so the two never fight over a
  weapon; a run's storage poisons and these stocks are separate.
- `.ga admin poisons <character> [take | buy]` (administrator, console, SOAP): what the rogue uses, carries, finds in
  the storage and has on its weapons; `take` and `buy` are test aids (the storage now; the poison vendor it stands at).

Not built: Crippling, Mind-numbing, Wound and Anesthetic Poison (mod-playerbots applies only Instant and Deadly); the
owner's own rogue is not stocked while he plays it.

Not built: pets do not learn new ranks by themselves beyond what the core gives a pet on level-up; the quests
themselves stay undone (their XP and reward items are not given).

### Death knights (2026-11-14)

the owner (2026-11-14): [quote left out].

**Before.** The Death Knight unlock is a guild member (the leader or a roster bot) at level 55
(`ProgressionService::IsDeathKnightUnlocked`). The core's own death knight rules (`HeroicCharactersPerRealm = 1`, a
level-55 character on the account, `CharacterCreating.MinLevelForHeroicCharacter`) live in the character screen's
create handler, which recruitment does not use (`RosterService::Recruit` calls `Player::Create`), so a guild can have
several. `Player::Create` makes a death knight at `StartHeroicPlayerLevel` (55) in Acherus (map 609, the
`playercreateinfo` row), with the green Acherus starting gear (item level 60), 20 silver, no hearthstone, no Death Gate.
There the core gives it the talent points of its rewarded campaign quests only (`Player::CalculateTalentsPoints`: 0 for
a fresh one), and `Player::TeleportTo` refuses every far teleport out of Acherus to a death knight without Death Gate
(50977). The order planner has no zone in Acherus (`GetRegionAt` returns none for map 609), so the bot stood there; the
campaign (the Eye of Acherus, the stolen horse, the duels, the battle at Light's Hope) is vehicles and script events the
planner does not play.

**mod-skip-dk-starting-area** (read 2026-11-14, `src/SkipDK.cpp`): a `PlayerScript::OnPlayerFirstLogin` for any
character in area 4342 with player security; it adds the hearthstone and three reward items, adds and rewards the 33
campaign quests (`AddQuest` + `RewardQuest`: their experience, gold, item choice 0 and scripts), raises the level to
`Skip.Deathknight.Start.Level` (58), teaches nine spells, saves, teleports to Stormwind or Orgrimmar and binds the
hearthstone there, sets the gold to `StartHeroicPlayerMoney` and puts Rune of Cinderglacier on the reward weapons. It
would act on our recruits (their first login goes through `HandlePlayerLoginFromDB` with the first-login flag), but its
experience, its gold (taxed by the guild tax, then taken away again), its fixed item choice and its teleport during the
login do not fit, so its effect is built into the module instead (`DeathKnights.h/.cpp`), no further module.

**As built.** The guild's bot setting `DeathKnights.SkipStart` (guild-wide, default 1):

- *Recruitment:* `DeathKnights::PlaceRecruit` appends two statements to the new character's save transaction: its
  position in its side's capital (Stormwind's trade district, Orgrimmar's valley of strength; the places the module
  above uses) and its hearthstone row at the inn there (without a row `Player::_LoadHomeBind` binds it in Acherus). No
  teleport: it enters the world in the capital.
- *First plan* (`OrderService::UpdateBot`, roster bots the AI plays, alive and out of a fight):
  `DeathKnights::FinishStart` counts the campaign as done. The 31 quests of the chain plus "The Scarlet Apocalypse",
  "The Lich King's Command", the race's "A Special Surprise" and the side's "Where Kings Walk" / "Warchief's Blessing"
  are marked rewarded (`Player::SetRewardedQuest`: no experience, so it stays at the core's level, no gold, no quest
  scripts or source spells), their reputation is given (`RewardReputation`), and what their reward spells teach is
  learned (the "learn spell" effects of each quest's reward spell: Death Gate, the Acherus Deathcharger, runeforging);
  Death Gate and Runeforging are learned in any case. With 1 the campaign's item rewards follow (blue, item level 65-70:
  the fixed ones and, of a quest with a choice, the one the bot's playerbots rating prefers), best item level first:
  each piece goes on where it beats what is worn by that rating (rings and trinkets against the weaker of the two), the
  Acherus starting piece it replaces is destroyed (soulbound, a few copper), anything else goes into the bags (by mail
  when they are full). With 2 it keeps the starting gear. A hearthstone if it has none. Outside Acherus the core counts
  the talent points of its level (46 at 55), which its talent template spends at once (`SpecService::Maintain`). An
  activity line names it all, the owner gets an `INFO` event ("... skipped the death knight starting area and begins in
  Stormwind").
- With 0 the death knight begins in Acherus as the core makes it and does not get out: 0 talent points, and the
  autopilot picks a zone "across the sea" whose travel from map 609 leads nowhere (seen on the `dk` instance: "starts
  voyage on (target Ironforge)" and a walk inside Acherus).

**Runes.** A death knight enchants its weapons at a runeforge (Acherus, Ebon Hold), which bots never visit. Every five
minutes, after a login and right after `FinishStart`, a death knight the AI plays puts the best rune it knows on a
weapon it wears that has no permanent enchantment (`DeathKnights::Runeforge`, bot setting `ClassAbilities.Runeforging`,
per guild and per bot), the way `Spell::EffectEnchantItemPerm` does: Fallen Crusader, Razorice, Cinderglacier, Lichbane
in that order, and while its dungeon set as a tank is on Stoneskin Gargoyle, Nerubian Carapace, Swordshattering or
Swordbreaking first; a rune a weapon cannot take (the spell's item requirements) is passed over, a weapon with any
enchantment is left alone.

### Squads (2026-11-12)

Two or three guild bots level together (`Squads.h`, `OrderSquads.cpp`). The bot quality work found that a single bot
loses about every second fight against two foes of its level and almost every fight against three, and that the gear it
finds keeps it below its level; a squad turns those fights into fights it wins.

- **What a squad is.** One **leader**, a roster bot that plays its own order (any order; normally `AUTO` or
  `LEVEL_ZONE`), and up to `GuildAdventure.Squads.MaxSize - 1` **members** that follow it: playerbots master = the
  leader (another bot, not the owner's character), strategy profile *follow*, all in the leader's party. Table
  `ga_bot_squad` (member -> leader; the leader has no row). A member's own order stays stored and waits; it plays it
  again when it leaves the squad, while its leader is benched or not in the world, and while their levels are more than
  `MaxLevelGap` apart (BOT `sqs` says which). A leader follows nobody and a member leads nobody (no chains). The owner
  playing the leader himself is fine: the members then follow the character he plays.
- **Who forms them.** The owner, per bot, in the addon's Orders sub-tab ("Squad: follow ...", GADV `SQUAD_SET g l`,
  applied at once); `.ga admin squad <bot> <leader | none>` for tests. With `GuildAdventure.Squads.Auto = 1` bots
  without a squad on `AUTO` / `LEVEL_ZONE` that stand in the same zone within 400 yards and two levels of each other
  form squads by themselves once a minute (the highest level leads); such automatic links (`automatic` = 1) end by
  themselves when the bots are in different zones and far apart.
- **XP, kills, loot.** By the core's party rules: XP is shared, kill credit goes to every member in reach. The party
  loots free for all (the member sets it while the AI plays the leader), so the module's auto loot of every member
  empties the squad's kills; quest items drop for each member that needs them, whatever the loot method. On a dungeon
  run of its leader the party rolls instead (group loot from uncommon up, "Dungeon runs" above).
- **Quests.** A member plans no quests. Every two seconds it looks at its leader's quest log: a quest the leader has
  and it has not, whose giver (creature or object) stands within 15 yards of the member, it takes too
  (`CanTakeQuest` / `CanAddQuest`, so the quests AI-played characters leave alone stay left alone, core patch CP-9,
  then `AddQuestAndCheckCompletion` with the giver, as the client's accept does, scripts included). A completed quest
  in its log whose ender stands within 15 yards it hands in (the reward playerbots rates best for it, else the one that
  sells for most; the ender's scripts run as for a client). A shared quest the leader abandoned it abandons too; one
  the leader handed in while the member's part is not done stays, unless fewer than four quest log slots are free.
  Lines: `took quest ... with its squad leader ...`, `turned in quest ... beside its squad leader ...`,
  `gave up quest ...`.
- **The leader waits** (its task clocks stand still, profile *hold*, why line "Squad: waiting (...)") while a member
  within `WaitYards` (80) rests, is dead and its corpse lies within that distance (it runs back), or fights within 40
  yards (the leader joins that fight), and while a member lags more than 50 yards behind (but not farther than
  `CatchUpYards`). A wait ends after `MaxWaitSeconds` (120); then the leader goes on for a minute before it waits
  again. Never during a voyage. Lines: `waits for its squad: ...`, `waited N s for its squad (...): goes on`.
- **Why the leader waits, shown on its members** (2026-11-27; the owner, watching a member in a Zul'Gurub raid: [quote left out]). A member's why line was "Squad: following <leader>" whenever
  the leader's own line began with "Squad:", which its wait line "Squad: waiting (...)" does, so the reason never reached
  the member (the watch bar and the Details window show the member's line). Now the member's line is "Squad: following
  <leader>; <leader>: <what the leader does>" (`OrderService::LeaderWhyForMember`): the leader's line without "In
  <dungeon>: ", its "Squad: waiting (...)" as "waiting for its squad (...)"; nothing for the leader's other squad lines.
  Inside a dungeon run the leader's own wait line reads "In <dungeon>: waiting for its squad (...)". The Details window
  (GADV `GET what=plan`) of a member has a line of the kind `wait` with the same text and, when its leader is on a run,
  "Dungeon run: <dungeon> (inside), led by <leader>" (docs/protocol.md "The plan of a guild character").
- **No rest while the squad fights** (2026-11-25): a leader or member out of a fight, at 30 % health or more, starts no
  rest (and ends one, `ended by: its squad fights`) while one of its squad within 40 yd is in a fight with attackers on
  it; it helps instead. A leader rested twice in half a minute, walking 59 and 44 yd away to a quieter place, while its
  member fought two Razormane centaurs alone, could not get away and died.
- **Catching up.** A member more than `CatchUpYards` (250) behind its leader, or on another map (the leader took a
  flight, a ship, a portal, or revived at a spirit healer), travels after it after 15 seconds as a player would
  (the owner, 2026-11-25: bots move like players, no teleports; `OrderService::StepRejoinTravel`): on another land mass
  the next ship, zeppelin or portal of its side towards the leader's (`NextTravelLink`, a voyage), on the same one a
  travel to where the leader stands with its flights, the last 300 yd a walk to it, until it is within 60 yd and
  follows again. Not while the leader flies, rides a ship, is dead or fights, nor while the member fights. Lines: `is
  N yd behind its squad leader ...: it travels after it as a player would`, `travels after its squad leader ... to
  <land>: <ship> from .. to ..`, `is back near its squad leader`. A way that finds nothing (no link for its side, a
  refused route, stuck, the ship that did not come) first gets a meeting point (round 226): the flight master of its side
  nearest to its leader, within 3000 yd of it and nearer to it than the member is; the member travels there and waits
  (up to 15 min), and its leader comes to fetch it, by flight when far, the last 250 yd on foot (`OrderService::
  ChooseMeetingPoint`, the leader's task `fetchSquad`; ten minutes at most). Lines: `finds no way of its own to its squad
  leader .. it goes to <the flight master> and waits there for its leader to fetch it`, `waits at .. for its squad leader
  .. to fetch it`, `goes to fetch its squad member ..`, `is back near its squad leader .., which fetched it at ..`. When
  that finds nothing either it waits two minutes; only then, with the bot setting
  `Squads.CatchUpFallback` (313, guild-wide, on), is the member put beside its leader (`found no way to its squad
  leader ... by road, flight, ship, zeppelin or portal: it is put beside it`); off, it waits and tries again. In a
  dungeon run the run's own rules hold (its teleports in and out, a member with no way on foot inside put beside its
  leader). A member 8 yd or more above or below its leader, 20 yd and more from it, with no way on foot to it walks to
  it along the roads, a lift included (round 223); not while it or its leader swims or dives (round 230: a member at a
  lake's surface with its leader 10 yd below it set out along the roads).
- **Fights.** A member fights beside its leader (playerbots' group combat; the planner also points an idle member at
  its leader's foe and an idle leader at a member's foe). `FightEscape` counts the squad: the foes of the squad
  characters within 30 yards are the bot's foes, their health and mana count beside its own, and the "this many foes
  and it leaves" rule (`Escape.MaxFoes`) is multiplied by the characters that stand together. Members do not judge a
  fight themselves; when the leader runs they stop fighting and run at its heels. A member's death counts for the
  leader's risk model as if the leader had died there (places set aside, playing it safe).
- **Spots.** The fight-cost limit of a quest spot and of a grind target (`Risk.MaxFightCostPercent`, in
  `Risk::SaferSpot` and `Risk::CanFight`) is multiplied by the characters of the squad within 120 yards of the
  leader: a squad of three works packs and grinds foes a lone bot leaves for later.
- **Ground, roads, rescue.** A member that follows close moves with the core's follow movement, which CP-10's ground
  guard does not see; a member far behind walks with playerbots' point movement, which the guard checks. The leader's
  routes over the road map become the members' way as they walk behind it. The rescue of a bot under the ground works
  for members as for any bot; a member that is stranded (it has no task that walks) is caught by the wait and the
  catch-up.

Settings (`GuildAdventure.Squads.*`): `Enable` (1), `MaxSize` (5, the leader included: a squad is also the group of a
dungeon run), `MaxLevelGap` (3), `Auto` (0), `WaitYards` (80), `MaxWaitSeconds` (120), `CatchUpYards` (250). Commands:
`.ga squad [character]` (the squads of that character's guild; GM, also console), `.ga admin squad <bot> <leader | none>`;
`.ga bot plan` has a `squad:` line.

### Quest partners (2026-11-13)

Guild bots that have the same hard quest team up to finish it (`QuestPartners.h/.cpp`, the squad links of `Squads.h`,
`OrderSquads.cpp`). The owner, 2026-11-13: bots with the same quest may join up to finish it, but only for hard quests
(where guild members die several times) and for elite and group quests; when nobody else has the same quest it is kept
for now, but skipped for as long.

- **Hard.** (a) An elite or group quest by its data: quest type *Group* (1), more than one suggested player, or a kill
  objective that is an elite, rare elite or boss creature. Dungeon and raid quests (types 62, 81, 85, 88, 89) are the
  dungeon runs' and do not count. (b) A quest guild characters died on (the planner's task was its objective, an
  interaction or its event, or a quest partner died while its leader worked it) `PartnerDeaths` (2) times within
  `PartnerHours` (6). (c) With `PartnerTooHard` (1): a quest whose every spot near was too much for a guild character
  at its level (the line `leaves quest ... every spot of it near is too much for it`), and only when a second
  character beside it would make one of the nearest spots workable and the straight way there passes no creature the
  walk gate would refuse for it (`Walks.MaxLevelsAbove`; the gate judges the way for the bot alone, partner or not) (the risk model judged with one more squad
  character: a partner raises what a fight may cost and how many foes may come, not the level cap or the creatures far
  above the bot; in the first live round 12 of 14 pairs parted within 20 seconds of meeting, their targets above the
  level cap for both). (b) and (c) count for guild
  characters up to the level they happened at, as the planner's death rest does; the guild's marks live in memory (a
  restart forgets them). *The developers' choice:* (c) belongs to it (the design log section 7 "Open" QP1). Line: `quest N "..."
  is hard for the guild now (...): guild bots up to that level do it with a partner`.
- **Without a partner** the quest stays in the log and the planner skips it: no objective task (`CollectLogTasks`), not
  counted as work that keeps the bot in a zone; it is not given back for its deaths or for no progress while it waits
  (`FailQuest`'s reasons `deaths` and `no_progress`: line `keeps quest ... instead of giving it back (...)`); the quest
  log care gives it up only when nothing else without progress is left; the grey rule (`Quests.AbandonGrey`) still
  applies. A bot that has partners beside it (two or more of its squad within 120 yards, a quest partner squad or the
  owner's) does not skip it. Line, once per quest: `keeps quest N "..." (why) until another guild member has it too`.
- **Pickups.** The planner does not walk to a quest giver for a hard quest, unless the bot is in a squad of two or more,
  or the giver stands within 150 yards and another guild character that could be its partner (on `AUTO` /
  `LEVEL_ZONE`, within `MaxLevelGap` levels, in the same zone within `PartnerYards`) keeps that quest. Quests NewRpg takes in
  passing at a giver it visits are kept as above.
- **Pairing** (every 20 seconds per guild): AI-played roster bots on `AUTO` or `LEVEL_ZONE`, in no squad, not on a
  dungeon run, with the same hard quest unfinished, within `Squads.MaxLevelGap` levels of each other, in one zone within
  `PartnerYards` (400, was 1500: before the cap up to four members walked 1260 to 1416 yards to one leader, and walks
  to a partner took 11 % of all task time on the integration server; a quest hard only because it was too much for
  one: one member, at most one level below the leader, since the verdict was that level's with one more character),
  and only when the quest's zone is the one the leader plans for (its order's or the
  autopilot's target zone; the zone it stands in only while it has none: the planner leaves the quests of a zone it
  passes through alone): the higher level leads, the others (up to `Squads.MaxSize`) follow it. The link is a squad
  link held in memory only (never in `ga_bot_squad`; after a restart the pairing forms it again). Both look at the
  quest anew (a "too much" set-aside of either ends, so the risk model judges it with both). Line: `M (level a) and L
  (level b) team up for quest N "..." (why): M walks to L (d yd)`.
- **Meeting.** The member walks to its leader along the road map (a travel task, `StepPartnerMeet`), not with
  playerbots' follow and not with the squad's catch-up teleport (that one is for a way the leader has just taken); the
  leader stands and waits for it (why line `Squad: waiting (M comes to team up for "..." (d yd))`, without the usual
  two-minute limit). Within 30 yards they have met (line `met its quest partner ...`) and the member follows as in any
  squad. Partners that have not met within `PartnerMeetMinutes` (8), or whose member finds no way (a stuck walk),
  part.
- **Together.** The leader's planner works the partner quest first (its tasks before any other); the member follows,
  fights beside it, takes the quests its leader takes at a giver they stand at and hands in beside it, as any squad
  member (why line `Squad: following L, its quest partner for "..."`). When the leader's part is finished (complete,
  or handed in) and its only member's is not, the roles turn round at once, before the leader walks off to its hand-ins
  and errands with its member in tow: the member leads and the other helps it (line `... is done with
  quest ... and ... is not: ... leads now and ... helps it`); a member whose quest is complete but not handed in hands
  it in by itself.
- **Parting.** The link goes when the quest is done for both, when one of them is not in the world, has another order
  or was benched, when quest partners are switched off for one of them, after `PartnerMaxMinutes` (60), and when the
  leader sets the quest aside although both stand together (deaths, every spot too much even for both). In the last
  three cases, and when they did not meet, the quest is not paired again for `PartnerRetryMinutes` (30); also when the
  owner takes a partner out of its squad. When the leader left the quest until a level (`leaves quest ... until level
  N`), the quest is not paired again before one of its holders is that level (at most two hours: `..., and it waits
  until one of them is level N`). Line: `M and L part after quest N "...": why`. Neither is left standing in a place it
  cannot take alone: with hostile creatures within 28 yards both go back the way they came first (line `... backs out
  of the place as its quest pair parts: ...`); a level-19 partner left in the Blackrock orc camp of Redridge had died
  twice within 93 seconds.
- **The switch.** The bot setting `Squads.QuestPartners` (category "Questing and travel"; per guild and per bot): off,
  or `Squads.Enable = 0`, and the bot tries hard quests alone as before. The guild leader (no roster bot, no squad takes
  it in) keeps the old ways.
- **What the owner sees.** BOT `sqq` / `sqqn` (the quest of the partner squad) and `qw` / `qwn` (the quests kept for a
  partner, docs/protocol.md section 6); the Orders sub-tab's squad line says "Quest partner of L for "..."" or "Leads a
  quest partner squad for "..."" and "Waits for a guild partner: ...". `.ga squad` lists the guild's hard quests and
  what its bots keep for a partner, `.ga bot plan` has a `quest partners:` line.

Settings (`GuildAdventure.Squads.*`): `QuestPartners` (1, a bot setting), `PartnerDeaths` (2), `PartnerHours` (6),
`PartnerTooHard` (1), `PartnerYards` (400), `PartnerMeetMinutes` (8), `PartnerMaxMinutes` (60), `PartnerRetryMinutes`
(30).

### Why line, events, rates

The roster's `why` field is the planner's line ("Travelling to Westfall (1240 yd)", "Questing in Elwynn Forest: \"Kobold
Camp Cleanup\" (Kobold Vermin)", "Picking up … from …", "Turning in … at …", "Grinding in …", "On the way to …: 2 new
spells", "Idle at the inn in Goldshire", "Following Probeguild", "Cannot reach …", "Dead: running back to the corpse").
Events: `ZONE_CHANGE` (arrived in the target zone), `ZONE_DONE` (out-levelled the ordered zone), `ORDER` (auto-advance);
`LEVEL_UP`, `QUEST_DONE`, `DEATH` come from the hooks of M2 and feed the "while you were away" summary. `xph` and `gph`
are rolling one-hour rates from one sample a minute (0 during the first five minutes).

### Activity log

What each guild bot did, for reading afterwards (a test run, a night of offline play): its own logger
`module.ga.activity`, which `tools\configure-server.ps1` sends to `logs\GuildAdventure.log` only (appended, every line
with a timestamp). Without that logger line in `worldserver.conf` the lines go to the `module` logger (Server.log and
the console). Lines, all starting with `activity: <bot>`:

| Line | When | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `entered the world` | the planner first sees the bot after a login | level, zone, position, order |
| `starts <task>` | every task but holds (pickup, objective, turn-in, travel, voyage, vendor, train, discover, grind, safe spot) | quest id and title, objective, target, distance, zone |
| `ends <task>` | when the task ends | quest id, seconds, deaths during it, whether the target was reached, the outcome ("quest in the log", "objective done", "turned in", "NewRpg left the quest", "stuck", "jumped", "order changed", ...) |
| `quest <id> "<title>" not_offered` / `cannot_turn_in` | a quest NPC in sight did not give or take the quest within 45 s | NPC in sight, distance, reached (NewRpg's visit), whether the NPC has the quest, can take / can add / worth doing (or can reward), NewRpg status, in combat, quest status, seconds since the login |
| `died` | the bot died | level, zone, position, in or under water, what it died of when no fight did (`not in a fight`, `of fatigue in deep water`, `drowned`), the creature it last fought (name and level, with `N s / min before` when that fight ended more than 20 s earlier), the task and quest, durability |
| `fight` | a fight ended (`GuildAdventure.ActivityLog.Fights`) | seconds, the most foes on the bot at the same time, the highest-level foe, health at its start (the last value seen out of combat) and end and the lowest in between, mana at start and end, won or died; for its own pull what the pull check expected (`its own pull (2 expected, 1 more possible)`), also when fewer came |
| `does not pull <creature>` / `waits with <creature>` | the bot's AI turned to a creature it cannot afford now (the pull check) | the creatures that would join, the estimate, what the bot has, the limit; "waits": one foe, it rests first |
| `does not rise where it fell` | the bot died with a soulstone or Reincarnation and hostile creatures at its corpse | how many within 30 yards |
| `plays a healing / tank spec` | with the gear warning (two minutes after a login, then every half hour), for a bot outside a squad | what a fight costs it |
| `leaves its <form> to fight` | an AI-played character was attacked in aquatic form, travel form or as a ghost wolf | the form |
| `plays by its talents again` | at a login or after a level-up the combat strategies playerbots had stored did not fit the talents (docs/specs.md "Stored strategies") | the strategies that went and those that came |
| `water fight` | every three seconds of a fight in the water, only with `GuildAdventure.Debug` | form, power, depth, movement, the spell being cast; the target with its health, distance (flat and up), melee range, line of sight, whom it attacks |
| `rested` | a rest ended (same setting) | seconds, health and mana before and after, what it ate and drank ("no food", "no drink"), what ended it (rested, time over, a fight, died, moved on) |
| `status` | every five minutes | level and xp %, zone, position, how far it moved in those five minutes, hp, durability, free bag slots, money, xp/h, since the last status line: fights (how many against two or more foes at once, how many begun below half health), rests and their seconds, deaths; pieces of food and drink in the bags; how active it was (below); task and its age, alive / in combat / dead, the why line |

The reason lines the planner already wrote (failed quests, stuck travels, set-asides, spirit healer) stay in Server.log.
A bot whose status lines show the same position for several five-minute steps stands still; `ends` lines with
"NewRpg left the quest" every few seconds show a loop.

**How active a bot is** (the owner, 2026-11-25: [quote left out]). The status line carries, for its five
minutes (`OrderService::TrackActivity`, at every step of the planner): `stood still N s` (no step of half a yard since
the last look, out of a fight, a rest and a cast; a bot that crafts or enchants counts as busy), `(N s with a walk to do)`
(of that, with a task that walks, its target more than 10 yd away and nothing it waits for on purpose: away from a
creature, for one on its way, the planner's own wait), `walked N yd` (the yards it went on its own, teleports, flights
and ships left out; against `moved`, which is a straight line, a ratio far above 1 is a walk to and fro), `N turns back`
(stretches of 15 yd out of a fight that turned back more than 150 degrees on the one before), `N tasks begun (N ended
within 10 s)` (a task begun again and again), `N target switches` (in a fight it turned to another creature while the
one before was alive and fighting) and, since 2026-11-27, `stood most while: hold 40 s, turn-in 12 s` (the tasks it
stood still with, the longest first, up to three of 5 s or more; `waiting on purpose` for the waits named above).
`tools/analysis/bot_activity.py <log> [--since ..] [--who a,b] [--sort ..]` sums
them per bot over a window, with the lines of walks that did not work (`is stuck`, `does not get on with its walk`,
refused ways, keep-aways, rescues, hearthstones), tasks that ended within 2 s, quests handed in and deaths; on a log
from before the counters it reports those lines alone.

## Playerbots settings

Written by `tools\configure-server.ps1`; the module warns at startup when they differ:

| Setting | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `Playerbots.RpgStatusProbWeight.*` | 0 (all nine) | NewRpg executes, the module plans |
| `Playerbots.BotCheats` | `""` | legitimate progress (the design log §1): no free food/water, no known flight paths, no raid cheats |
| `Playerbots.SummonWhenGroup` | 0 | a bot that joins the owner's party is not teleported to them |
| `Playerbots.AutoPickTalentsForPlayerControlledBots` | 0 (since the talent templates, docs/specs.md; 1 before) | the module spends the talent points along the bot's template; with 1 playerbots' premade specs would spend them first |

## Commands

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `.ga bot plan <bot>` | planner state: order, why, task, zone, region, NewRpg status, master, party, quest log, bags, durability, money, rates, blocked quests (GM, also console) |
| `.ga admin login <leader>` | log in the leader's active guild bots without a master (tests without a client) |
| `.ga admin logout <leader>` | log out the leader's AI-driven guild bots |
| `.ga admin order <bot> <order> [zone]` | set a bot's order; for the leader also `HOLD` (its default, no order) |
| `.ga admin offline <leader> <minutes>` | set the offline window |
| `.ga admin recruit <leader> <race> <class> <gender> <name>` | recruit a bot for that leader's guild (result in `Server.log`) |
| `.ga admin kill <bot>` | kill an AI-driven guild bot where it stands (tests of the death rules) |
| `.ga admin hub <zone id>` | both teams' hubs of a zone, with the zone and region their spot lies in |
| `.ga admin order <bot> FARM <item id> [<target stock>]` | the farm order for that item (§ Farm orders), with a target stock it ends at; refused for an item no creature bots grind drops |
| `.ga admin farm <character> <item id>` | where that character would farm the item: the creatures that drop it, the ones at or below its level limit, the best hunting grounds with the risk model's verdict, or why it has none (reads only) |
| `.ga admin path <character> <x> <y> <z> [<from x> <from y> [<from z>]]` | the path the core would move that character along to the point (from where it stands, or from the given spot; without a height from the surface there), and how much of it leaves the ground |
| `.ga admin walk <character> <x> <y> <z>` | starts the point movement playerbots uses for a walk, for an AI-played character (test aid for the ground guard) |
| `.ga admin route <character> <x> <y> <z> [<level>] [<from x> <from y>]` | the route of the road map that character would walk to the point (from where it stands or from the given spot, at its own or the given level): length, nodes, strongest hostile creatures on it and on the straight line |
| `.ga admin quests [forget \| scripted \| <quest id>]` | the quests AI-played characters leave alone (counts, the learned ones) and the quest events the planner plays; `forget` deletes every block the planner learned; `scripted` lists the zone quests up to level 60 left alone as script events; with a quest id: its event plans, its verdict, its escort NPC |
| `.ga admin questscan <character> [min] [max]` | how the planner would work every quest of the level range (default 1-60) for that character's race, class and side: per objective kill, loot, given with the quest, an interaction kind, explore, or a gap with its reason; the quests of each kind and gap go to Server.log (`questscan`). The character must be in the world |
| `.ga admin takequest <character> <quest id>` | test aid for quest events: with a giver of the quest within 100 yd the character accepts it there like a client (first call puts it next to the giver, second call accepts, with every script that reacts to the accept); else the quest is put into its log directly |
| `.ga squad [character]` | the squads of that character's guild: leader, members with level and squad state (GM, also console) |
| `.ga admin squad <bot> <leader \| none>` | the bot follows that guild bot of its guild as a squad member, or leaves its squad (§ Squads) |
| `.ga admin boost <character> <level>` | test aid for runs at levels no test bot has reached: sets the level of an AI-played character and gives it bags, uncommon gear of that level, ammunition and some money (playerbots' factory); spells, skills and talents follow from the level-up as in play. Never for a guild bot in play |

The `admin` commands are administrator-only and run from the console / SOAP.

## Tests

- **Development server** (`GA_INSTANCE=m4`, tools\ga-env.ps1): own build `_work\build-m4`, runtime `_work\server-m4`,
  ports 3727/8088/7881, databases `GA_m4_*` (seeded with a copy of the integration server's auth, characters and
  playerbots data). Bot behaviour is tested there over SOAP (`.ga admin login`, `.ga admin order`, `.ga bot plan`) and
  the database, without a client.
- **Client** (ga-probe on the integration server): scenario `orders` (in the default run: orders from the addon,
  why lines, parties) and `away-summary` (optional, about 8 minutes: closes the client for 6 minutes, then checks the
  "while you were away" summary): `GA_PROBE_OWNER=<thread> python -X utf8 tools/ga-probe/gaprobe.py test orders`.

## Open points

- Teleporters that are objects, not area triggers: the Silvermoon-Undercity orb and the city portals of Shattrath and
  Dalaran. Ships, zeppelins, area-trigger portals and flight paths are built (§ Travel).
- Blood Elf bots leave the Eversong Isles through the Ghostlands-Eastern Plaguelands pass (an area trigger) until the
  Silvermoon-Undercity orb is used: at level 20 that is a walk through a level-55 zone.

- Quest types the planner cannot finish yet (escort, "speak with" in gossip, item uses the quest data does not tie to the
  objective, spells scripts check in C++ beyond "a helpful spell") are left alone up front where the module can tell
  (§ Quests the bots leave alone); the rest is still learned the hard way: such a quest fails twice and is blocked for
  that bot, and after two bots for all. Using items, casting helpful spells on quest NPCs, using quest objects and
  "open"-lock chests, and exploration are built (§ Quest interactions). Escorts and gossip quests belong to the thread
  [quote left out] (2026-11-12).
- Death Knights recruited with `DeathKnights.SkipStart = 0` start in Acherus (region none): no zone there, they hold.
  With the default they begin in the capital (§ "Death knights").
- playerbots' ghost handling teleports a ghost to a graveyard when it has not reached its corpse within 10 minutes, and
  to a *start-zone* graveyard when its durability is below 10 % (`SpiritHealerAction`, `GetGrave(startZone)`); seen
  once: a level-58 hunter with starting gear and broken equipment went from Honor Hold to a graveyard in the Eastern
  Kingdoms and walked back through the Dark Portal. The module does not hold this one off yet (it would need a
  playerbots change or the module driving the ghost itself).
- The AUTO zone choice counts a pickup as work without checking that its giver can be reached (other region, avoided
  spawn); only the quests in the log are checked against what the planner can build a task for (review H5 follow-up).
- `nd` / `gcap` limits become meaningful with dungeons (M8) and bigger spending (M7); until then the addon offers them
  but the planner does not read them (review, the design log §2.4).
- Routes: the Deeprun Tram and the walking links of other kinds in playerbots' graph (teleporters, transports) are
  not used; the walk to the first node and from the last one is a straight navmesh walk whose danger only enters the
  cost; the zone choice of AUTO does not know routes yet, it learns that a zone is out of reach when the travel is
  refused; objective and grind walks inside a zone are NewRpg's and take no route.
- Ground guard: NPCs behind a teleporter (the trainers and quest NPCs in the sanctum of Stormwind's wizard tower) are
  not reached: the walk ends on the tower above them, the turn-in is given up. Leaving through the teleporter works.
  Chase and follow movements (`MoveChase`, `MoveFollow`) are not checked, only point movements, which is what
  playerbots uses for walking and for closing in on a target.
- Errands: objectives are still worked in the bot's own region only (no voyage for an objective); an errand with two
  legs is not checked for the walk at its far end before the bot sets out; quest items given by an NPC in a talk, by
  another quest or by a script have no source the planner knows (82 classic quests).
- Alliance bots in Feralas: the hub is Feathermoon Stronghold on Sardor Isle, most objectives are on the mainland, and
  the planner only works objectives in the bot's own region; the zone counts as having quests while the island's
  quests are open. Working objectives across a ferry needs voyages for objectives, not only for zone changes.
- Deadlines compare `getMSTime()` values directly; after 49.7 days of uptime the counter wraps and the planner's waits
  and set-asides are off for one cycle (review N2).
- Portals use `TeleportTo` (the area trigger's own checks do not run) and `LEVEL_ZONE` does not check the bot's level
  against the zone: a low-level bot ordered to Hellfire Peninsula walks through the Dark Portal (review N1; the design log §7
  "Open").
